updates.question_text: Regarding Barrett oesophagus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a precursor to adenocarcinoma in the source
It is classically shown as a low smooth stricture without hiatal hernia
The classic imaging pattern is a low stricture with no associated hiatal hernia
It is primarily a precursor to squamous carcinoma of the mid oesophagus
It develops secondary to chronic reflux
options_after: It is a precursor to adenocarcinoma in the source
It is classically shown as a low smooth stricture without hiatal hernia
The classic imaging pattern is a low stricture without associated hiatal hernia
It is primarily a precursor to squamous carcinoma of the mid oesophagus
It develops secondary to chronic reflux
updates.explanation: Barrett oesophagus is described as a reflux-related precursor to adenocarcinoma. The classic imaging clue in the source is high stricture with associated hiatal hernia, and a reticular mucosal pattern is also highlighted. Squamous carcinoma is linked to different risk factors and more often mid-oesophageal disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding oesophageal carcinoma on barium and staging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Irregular contour and abrupt shouldered edges are suspicious contrast-study features
Squamous carcinoma is classically mid-oesophageal in the source
T1 versus T2 staging is the main radiologist-facing CT distinction in the source
Adenocarcinoma is classically a cervical oesophageal web complication only
Adenocarcinoma is linked with chronic reflux and Barrett oesophagus
options_after: Irregular contour and abrupt shouldered edges are suspicious contrast-study features
Squamous carcinoma is classically mid-oesophageal in the source
T1 versus T2 staging is the main radiologist-facing CT distinction in the source
Adenocarcinoma is classically a cervical oesophageal web complication
Adenocarcinoma is linked with chronic reflux and Barrett oesophagus
updates.explanation: On barium, malignancy is suggested by irregular contour and abrupt shouldered edges. The source links squamous carcinoma with mid-oesophageal disease and adenocarcinoma with chronic reflux, PPI history, and Barrett oesophagus, usually lower oesophagus. The CT distinction emphasised for radiologists is T3 adventitial involvement versus T4 adjacent-structure invasion.

updates.question_text: Regarding hiatal hernia types, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Para-oesophageal type 2 has the GE junction above the diaphragm
Type 2 has no increased risk of incarceration in the source
Sliding type 1 hernia is the most common type in the source
Type 1 is defined by the GE junction above the diaphragm
The distinction is based on gastric ulcer depth rather than GE-junction position
options_after: Para-oesophageal type 2 has the GE junction above the diaphragm
Type 2 lacks increased risk of incarceration in the source
Sliding type 1 hernia is the most common type in the source
Type 1 is defined by the GE junction above the diaphragm
The distinction is based on gastric ulcer depth rather than GE-junction position
updates.explanation: The source states that type 1 sliding hernia is most common and has the GE junction above the diaphragm. Type 2 para-oesophageal hernia has the GE junction below the diaphragm and a higher reported incarceration risk. The classification depends on GE-junction position.

updates.question_text: Regarding oesophageal ulcer patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Herpes ulcers are small and multiple with a halo of oedema
CMV and HIV ulcers are described as large, flat, and ovoid
Herpes ulcers are classically large flat ovoid ulcers identical to CMV
Crohn oesophagitis is the most common Crohn manifestation in the source
Crohn oesophageal involvement is rare and associated with aphthous ulcers
options_after: Herpes ulcers are small and multiple with a halo of oedema
CMV and HIV ulcers are described as large, flat, and ovoid
Herpes ulcers are classically large flat ovoid ulcers closely comparable to CMV
Crohn oesophagitis is the most common Crohn manifestation in the source
Crohn oesophageal involvement is rare and associated with aphthous ulcers
updates.explanation: Herpes produces small multiple ulcers with an oedematous halo. CMV and HIV ulcers are described as large, flat, and ovoid. Crohn oesophageal involvement is rare and severe-disease associated, with aphthous ulcers surrounded by oedematous mounds.

updates.question_text: Regarding oesophageal diverticula, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Zenker diverticulum arises from the hypopharynx through Killian dehiscence
Traction diverticula are round pulsion diverticula that never empty
Zenker diverticulum arises from the abdominal oesophagus below the diaphragm
Killian-Jamieson diverticulum is anterior/lateral and arises below the cricopharyngeus
Epiphrenic diverticula are just above the diaphragm and usually right-sided in the source
options_after: Zenker diverticulum arises from the hypopharynx through Killian dehiscence
Traction diverticula are round pulsion diverticula that will not empty
Zenker diverticulum arises from the abdominal oesophagus below the diaphragm
Killian-Jamieson diverticulum is anterior/lateral and arises below the cricopharyngeus
Epiphrenic diverticula are just above the diaphragm and usually right-sided in the source
updates.explanation: Zenker diverticulum is a posterior pulsion diverticulum from the hypopharynx through Killian dehiscence. Killian-Jamieson diverticulum arises from the cervical oesophagus below the cricopharyngeus and is anterior/lateral. Epiphrenic diverticula are just above the diaphragm, usually on the right. Traction diverticula are mid-oesophageal, often triangular, related to scarring, and empty because they contain muscle.

updates.question_text: Regarding oesophageal pseudodiverticulosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is best demonstrated by avoiding contrast and using only CT angiography
It represents dilated submucosal or excretory mucosal ducts
It causes multiple tiny outpouchings rather than true diverticula
It is associated with oesophageal strictures, reflux, and candidiasis in the source
It is caused by a para-oesophageal hernia in nearly all cases
options_after: It is best demonstrated by avoiding contrast and using primarily CT angiography
It represents dilated submucosal or excretory mucosal ducts
It causes multiple tiny outpouchings rather than true diverticula
It is associated with oesophageal strictures, reflux, and candidiasis in the source
It is caused by a para-oesophageal hernia in the large majority of cases
updates.explanation: Pseudodiverticulosis is due to dilated submucosal glands or mucosal ducts, giving multiple tiny outpouchings that are not true diverticula. The source lists associations with strictures, reflux, and candidiasis, and notes that a single-contrast phase can show it well.

updates.question_text: Regarding oesophageal web and Plummer-Vinson syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Oesophageal web is most commonly in the cervical oesophagus near the cricopharyngeus
A web is a posterior-only muscular ring at the GE junction
Oesophageal webs protect against oesophageal and hypopharyngeal carcinoma
A web is caused by a thick muscular membrane in the distal thoracic oesophagus
Plummer-Vinson syndrome includes iron deficiency anaemia and dysphagia in the source
options_after: Oesophageal web is most commonly in the cervical oesophagus near the cricopharyngeus
A web is a posterior-predominant muscular ring at the GE junction
Oesophageal webs protect against oesophageal and hypopharyngeal carcinoma
A web is caused by a thick muscular membrane in the distal thoracic oesophagus
Plummer-Vinson syndrome includes iron deficiency anaemia and dysphagia in the source
updates.explanation: Oesophageal web is a thin mucosal membrane most commonly located in the cervical oesophagus near the cricopharyngeus. Plummer-Vinson syndrome includes iron deficiency anaemia and dysphagia, with additional source-listed associations. Webs are a risk factor for oesophageal and hypopharyngeal carcinoma rather than protective.

updates.question_text: Regarding dysphagia lusoria and oesophageal spasm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Nutcracker oesophagus is diagnosed by barium appearance alone in the source
Dysphagia lusoria is due to a left gastric artery aneurysm compressing the stomach
Dysphagia lusoria is due to compression from an aberrant right subclavian artery
Oesophageal spasm may show corkscrew tertiary contractions favouring the distal oesophagus
Oesophageal spasm always produces a fixed malignant stricture
options_after: Nutcracker oesophagus is diagnosed by barium appearance alone in the source
Dysphagia lusoria is due to a left gastric artery aneurysm compressing the stomach
Dysphagia lusoria is due to compression from an aberrant right subclavian artery
Oesophageal spasm may show corkscrew tertiary contractions favouring the distal oesophagus
Oesophageal spasm characteristically produces a fixed malignant stricture
updates.explanation: Dysphagia lusoria is swallowing difficulty due to compression by an aberrant right subclavian artery. Oesophageal spasm may have a normal exam, but the testable barium pattern is corkscrew tertiary contractions in the distal oesophagus. Nutcracker oesophagus requires manometry rather than barium alone.

updates.question_text: Regarding pseudoachalasia and scleroderma oesophagus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Scleroderma typically has competent LES with no reflux sequelae
Scleroderma never involves the oesophagus in the source
Pseudoachalasia is secondary to cancer at the GE junction
Failure of the GE junction to relax or a visible mass should prompt concern for pseudoachalasia
Pseudoachalasia has no role for CT or upper GI evaluation
options_after: Scleroderma typically has competent LES without reflux sequelae
Scleroderma will not involve the oesophagus in the source
Pseudoachalasia is secondary to cancer at the GE junction
Failure of the GE junction to relax or a visible mass should prompt concern for pseudoachalasia
Pseudoachalasia has negligible role for CT or upper GI evaluation
updates.explanation: Pseudoachalasia mimics achalasia but is caused by malignancy at the GE junction; a fixed non-relaxing obstruction, mass, or cancer risk factors should raise suspicion, with CT or upper GI evaluation. Scleroderma commonly involves the oesophagus, causing lower oesophageal dysmotility, incompetent LES, reflux, stricture, Barrett oesophagus, and adenocarcinoma risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding oesophageal high-yield table patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Medication-induced oesophagitis causes ulcers, often at the arch level or distal oesophagus
Long stricture differential includes prolonged nasogastric tube, radiation, and caustic ingestion
Glycogenic acanthosis mimics Candida in an asymptomatic elderly patient
Achalasia is a fixed malignant GE-junction obstruction that never relaxes
Severe Candida can be described as shaggy
options_after: Medication-induced oesophagitis causes ulcers, often at the arch level or distal oesophagus
Long stricture differential includes prolonged nasogastric tube, radiation, and caustic ingestion
Glycogenic acanthosis mimics Candida in an asymptomatic elderly patient
Achalasia is a fixed malignant GE-junction obstruction that will not relax
Severe Candida can be described as shaggy
updates.explanation: The high-yield table links medication-induced oesophagitis with ulcers at the arch level or distal oesophagus, long strictures with prolonged nasogastric tube, radiation, or caustic ingestion, glycogenic acanthosis with Candida mimic in an asymptomatic older patient, and severe Candida with a shaggy appearance. Fixed malignant GE-junction obstruction is pseudoachalasia, not idiopathic achalasia.

updates.question_text: Regarding diverticulum pattern recognition, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Zenker is posterior and above the cricopharyngeus
Traction diverticula are round blind sacs that do not empty because they contain no muscle
Killian-Jamieson is lateral and below the cricopharyngeus
Traction diverticulum is mid-oesophageal and often triangular
Epiphrenic diverticulum is just above the diaphragm and associated with motor abnormality
options_after: Zenker is posterior and above the cricopharyngeus
Traction diverticula are round blind sacs that do not empty because they lack muscle
Killian-Jamieson is lateral and below the cricopharyngeus
Traction diverticulum is mid-oesophageal and often triangular
Epiphrenic diverticulum is just above the diaphragm and associated with motor abnormality
updates.explanation: Zenker is posterior and above the cricopharyngeus, arising from the hypopharynx. Killian-Jamieson is lateral and below the cricopharyngeus, arising from the cervical oesophagus. Traction diverticula are mid-oesophageal, triangular, and related to scarring. Epiphrenic diverticula are just above the diaphragm and are pulsion diverticula associated with motor abnormality. Round non-emptying diverticula without muscle are pulsion-type features.

updates.question_text: Regarding the imaging appearance of gastric adenocarcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Benign gastritis is more likely focal nodular wall thickening than diffuse stratified thickening
Gastric adenocarcinoma classically shows absence of adjacent fat-plane involvement in advanced disease
It never causes gastric outlet obstruction in the source
It may appear as asymmetric focal nodular wall thickening greater than 12 mm
It is usually a large ulcerated heterogeneous mass rather than a smooth exophytic GIST-like mass
options_after: Benign gastritis is more likely focal nodular wall thickening than diffuse stratified thickening
Gastric adenocarcinoma classically shows absence of adjacent fat-plane involvement in advanced disease
It will not cause gastric outlet obstruction in the source
It may appear as asymmetric focal nodular wall thickening greater than 12 mm
It is usually a large ulcerated heterogeneous mass rather than a smooth exophytic GIST-like mass
updates.explanation: Gastric adenocarcinoma is described as a large ulcerated heterogeneous mass or focal nodular asymmetric wall thickening greater than 12 mm. Benign gastritis is more diffuse and stratified. Gastric cancer is more likely than lymphoma to cause gastric outlet obstruction, be distal, and extend beyond the serosa with fat-plane obliteration.

updates.question_text: Regarding gastric lymphoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The stomach is the most common extranodal site for non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the source
Gastric lymphoma can be primary MALT or secondary systemic lymphoma
Even extensive gastric lymphoma commonly causes gastric outlet obstruction
Its appearance is always a single smooth exophytic submucosal mass
H. pylori is a risk factor
options_after: The stomach is the most common extranodal site for non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the source
Gastric lymphoma can be primary MALT or secondary systemic lymphoma
Even extensive gastric lymphoma commonly causes gastric outlet obstruction
Its appearance is characteristically a single smooth exophytic submucosal mass
H. pylori is a risk factor
updates.explanation: Gastric lymphoma can be primary MALT or secondary systemic disease, and the stomach is described as the commonest extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma site. H. pylori is a risk factor. Lymphoma can look variable and may be extensive, but rarely causes gastric outlet obstruction compared with adenocarcinoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding Menetrier disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It causes regular rugal thickening involving the fundus
It is a focal antral scarring deformity identical to ram-horn stomach
It causes high albumin from increased gastric protein absorption
It is always an adult-only disease without a childhood form
It classically spares the antrum
options_after: It causes regular rugal thickening involving the fundus
It is a focal antral scarring deformity closely comparable to ram-horn stomach
It causes high albumin from increased gastric protein absorption
It is characteristically an adult-predominant disease without a childhood form
It classically spares the antrum
updates.explanation: Menetrier disease is an idiopathic gastropathy with regular rugal thickening, classically involving the fundus and sparing the antrum. It can have a childhood form thought to be CMV related. Protein loss into the gastric lumen can cause hypoalbuminaemia.

updates.question_text: Regarding ram-horn deformity, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the classic imaging sign of gastric diverticulum in the posterior fundus
It is a tapering/tubular conical deformity of the distal stomach or antrum
Causes include peptic-ulcer scarring, granulomatous disease, and scirrhous carcinoma
It is caused only by Menetrier disease involving the fundus
The source states that sarcoid never involves the stomach
options_after: It is the classic imaging sign of gastric diverticulum in the posterior fundus
It is a tapering/tubular conical deformity of the distal stomach or antrum
Causes include peptic-ulcer scarring, granulomatous disease, and scirrhous carcinoma
It is caused primarily by Menetrier disease involving the fundus
The source states that sarcoid will not involve the stomach
updates.explanation: Ram-horn deformity is a tapering tubular/conical distal stomach shape. The differential includes peptic-ulcer scarring, granulomatous disease such as Crohn disease, sarcoid, TB, or syphilis, and scirrhous carcinoma. The source notes that the stomach is the commonest GI location for sarcoid.

updates.question_text: Regarding Roux-en-Y anatomy and complications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The stomach is divided to create a gastric pouch attached to jejunum
A jejunojejunal anastomosis forms the lower part of the Y
Roux-en-Y eliminates the risk of leaks and internal hernias
The excluded stomach is removed in all Roux-en-Y procedures in the source
Roux-en-Y can be used for obesity or as an alternative operation in selected gastric cancer cases
options_after: The stomach is divided to create a gastric pouch attached to jejunum
A jejunojejunal anastomosis forms the lower part of the Y
Roux-en-Y eliminates the risk of leaks and internal hernias
The excluded stomach is removed in most Roux-en-Y procedures in the source
Roux-en-Y can be used for obesity or as an alternative operation in selected gastric cancer cases
updates.explanation: Roux-en-Y divides the stomach to create a pouch, attaches it to jejunum, and connects jejunum to jejunum to form the Y. It is used for bariatric surgery and can be used for gastric cancer in selected contexts. The source notes risks including leaks, gallstones, fistulas, and internal hernias; the excluded stomach remains attached to the duodenum.

updates.question_text: Regarding early post-operative leak evaluation after upper GI surgery, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Leaks usually occur early, within about 10 days
They often occur at the gastrojejunal anastomosis
Water-soluble oral contrast fluoroscopy 1-2 days post-op is the source-listed test
Contrast outside the stomach or bowel lumen, including in drains, is positive for leak
Barium is always the first contrast agent before water-soluble contrast in suspected leak
options_after: Leaks usually occur early, within about 10 days
They often occur at the gastrojejunal anastomosis
Water-soluble oral contrast fluoroscopy 1-2 days post-op is the source-listed test
Contrast outside the stomach or bowel lumen, including in drains, is positive for leak
Barium is characteristically the first contrast agent before water-soluble contrast in suspected leak
updates.explanation: Post-operative leaks are early, often at the gastrojejunal anastomosis. The source recommends water-soluble oral contrast fluoroscopy 1-2 days post-op and obtaining a scout first. Extravasated contrast outside bowel or stomach, or contrast in drains, indicates leak. Barium may increase sensitivity after a negative water-soluble study but is not first-line because barium peritonitis is a risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding simple mechanical bowel obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is defined by two adjacent points of obstruction enclosing a segment
It is primarily treated by immediate surgery in all cases because ischaemia is the rule
It has a single point of obstruction in the source description
Upstream gas and fluid accumulation contribute to distension and air-fluid levels
It has no role for decompression of retained secretions
options_after: It is defined by two adjacent points of obstruction enclosing a segment
It is primarily treated by immediate surgery in most cases because ischaemia is the rule
It has a single point of obstruction in the source description
Upstream gas and fluid accumulation contribute to distension and air-fluid levels
It has negligible role for decompression of retained secretions
updates.explanation: Simple mechanical obstruction has one obstructing point. Upstream gas initially distends bowel, followed by retained fluid from reduced absorption and increased secretion, producing air-fluid levels. This explains why decompression with an NG tube is central. Two adjacent obstruction points define closed-loop obstruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding closed-loop obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is defined by two or more points of obstruction
It has a higher risk of ischaemia than simple mechanical obstruction
It can show C- or U-shaped fluid-filled distended loops
It is usually a benign ileus with no mechanical transition points
Coronal CT images are useful for recognising the morphology
options_after: It is defined by two or more points of obstruction
It has a higher risk of ischaemia than simple mechanical obstruction
It can show C- or U-shaped fluid-filled distended loops
It is usually a benign ileus without mechanical transition points
Coronal CT images are useful for recognising the morphology
updates.explanation: Closed-loop obstruction has two or more points of obstruction and is higher risk for ischaemia, often requiring surgery. Helpful morphologic clues include multiple transition points, C- or U-shaped fluid-filled loops, radial layout with converging loops/vessels, and sometimes pneumatosis. Coronal images are especially useful.

updates.question_text: Regarding causes of SBO after Roux-en-Y, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Greater weight gain after surgery promotes internal hernia by adding protective mesenteric fat
Adhesions are the most common cause after open surgery in the source
Laparoscopic procedures create fewer adhesions and allow more mobility
More mesenteric mobility is protective against twisting or herniation
Internal hernia is impossible after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y
options_after: Greater weight gain after surgery promotes internal hernia by adding protective mesenteric fat
Adhesions are the most common cause after open surgery in the source
Laparoscopic procedures create fewer adhesions and allow more mobility
More mesenteric mobility is protective against twisting or herniation
Internal hernia is not a recognised complication after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y reconstruction
updates.explanation: After open Roux-en-Y surgery, adhesions are the commonest SBO cause. Laparoscopic surgery creates fewer adhesions and more mobility, which can permit twisting or herniation through defects. Marked weight loss, not weight gain, reduces protective mesenteric fat and can increase internal hernia risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding internal hernia sites after Roux-en-Y, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A transverse mesocolon defect is relevant in retrocolic Roux limb routing
Antecolic routing requires a transverse mesocolon defect in all cases
Internal hernias occur only at the gastrojejunal anastomosis
A mesenteric defect at the enteroenterostomy is a potential site
Petersen hernia occurs behind the Roux limb mesentery
options_after: A transverse mesocolon defect is relevant in retrocolic Roux limb routing
Antecolic routing requires a transverse mesocolon defect in most cases
Internal hernias occur primarily at the gastrojejunal anastomosis
A mesenteric defect at the enteroenterostomy is a potential site
Petersen hernia occurs behind the Roux limb mesentery
updates.explanation: The source lists three internal hernia sites: transverse mesocolon defect for retrocolic Roux routing, mesenteric defect at the enteroenterostomy or jejunojejunal anastomosis, and Petersen space behind the Roux limb mesentery. Antecolic routing avoids the transverse mesocolon defect, though other defects remain possible.

updates.question_text: Regarding thick nodular small-bowel folds, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Segmental thick nodular folds suggest Crohn disease in the source
Diffuse nodularity with uniform 2-4 mm nodules can reflect lymphoid hyperplasia
Variable larger nodules can reflect lymphoma or metastases
Diffuse nodularity is specific for benign transient ileus and has no tumour differential
Intestinal lymphangiectasia is listed in the diffuse nodular differential
options_after: Segmental thick nodular folds suggest Crohn disease in the source
Diffuse nodularity with uniform 2-4 mm nodules can reflect lymphoid hyperplasia
Variable larger nodules can reflect lymphoma or metastases
Diffuse nodularity is specific for benign transient ileus and lacks tumour differential
Intestinal lymphangiectasia is listed in the diffuse nodular differential
updates.explanation: The source links segmental thick folds with nodularity to Crohn disease. Diffuse thick nodular folds include Whipple disease, lymphoid hyperplasia with uniform 2-4 mm nodules, lymphoma or metastases with larger variable nodules, and intestinal lymphangiectasia. Tumour is therefore part of the differential.

updates.question_text: Regarding loop separation and tethering on small-bowel studies, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Loop separation without tethering can be due to ascites
Tethering means loops are pushed apart but remain freely mobile without convergence
Intrinsic mucosal disease always spares the mucosa in the source
Loop separation without tethering can be due to wall thickening, adenopathy, or mesenteric tumours
Loop separation with tethering suggests carcinoid in the source
options_after: Loop separation without tethering can be due to ascites
Tethering means loops are pushed apart but remain freely mobile without convergence
Intrinsic mucosal disease characteristically spares the mucosa in the source
Loop separation without tethering can be due to wall thickening, adenopathy, or mesenteric tumours
Loop separation with tethering suggests carcinoid in the source
updates.explanation: Loop separation without tethering can result from ascites, wall thickening such as Crohn disease or lymphoma, adenopathy, or mesenteric tumour. Tethering implies loops being pinched and pulled toward a displacing mass, with carcinoid highlighted. The source states that extrinsic processes spare mucosa, while intrinsic processes alter it.

updates.question_text: What is the key mucosal clue distinguishing extrinsic from intrinsic small-bowel processes in the source?
options_before: Extrinsic processes alter mucosa more than intrinsic processes
Extrinsic processes spare the mucosa, while intrinsic processes alter the mucosa
Both always produce identical mucosal ulceration
Intrinsic disease never affects mucosa on barium studies
Only CT angiography can assess mucosal alteration
options_after: Extrinsic processes alter mucosa more than intrinsic processes
Extrinsic processes spare the mucosa, while intrinsic processes alter the mucosa
Both characteristically produce closely comparable mucosal ulceration
Intrinsic disease will not affect mucosa on barium studies
Primarily CT angiography can assess mucosal alteration
updates.explanation: The source gives a useful principle: extrinsic processes spare the mucosa, while intrinsic processes alter the mucosa. This helps distinguish loop displacement from mucosal or mural disease on contrast studies.

updates.question_text: Regarding Meckel diverticulum, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a congenital true diverticulum of the distal ileum
It is a false diverticulum of the proximal jejunum
It never acts as a lead point for intussusception
It is unrelated to the omphalomesenteric duct in the source
Bleeding Meckel diverticula with gastric mucosa can take up Tc-pertechnetate
options_after: It is a congenital true diverticulum of the distal ileum
It is a false diverticulum of the proximal jejunum
It will not act as a lead point for intussusception
It is unrelated to the omphalomesenteric duct in the source
Bleeding Meckel diverticula with gastric mucosa can take up Tc-pertechnetate
updates.explanation: Meckel diverticulum is a true congenital diverticulum of the distal ileum, related to persistence of the omphalomesenteric duct. Gastric mucosa explains bleeding and uptake on a Meckel scan. It can mimic appendicitis when inflamed, cause bleeding, act as a lead point for intussusception, or cause obstruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding inflammatory and diverticular small-bowel disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chronic dialysis patients cannot mimic pancreatitis on barium studies
Adjacent pancreatic or gallbladder inflammation can thicken duodenal folds
Primary duodenal Crohn disease can occur but is rare in the source
Jejunal diverticula occur along the mesenteric border and are associated with bacterial overgrowth/malabsorption
Jejunal diverticulosis is more common than colonic diverticulosis
options_after: Chronic dialysis patients will not mimic pancreatitis on barium studies
Adjacent pancreatic or gallbladder inflammation can thicken duodenal folds
Primary duodenal Crohn disease can occur but is rare in the source
Jejunal diverticula occur along the mesenteric border and are associated with bacterial overgrowth/malabsorption
Jejunal diverticulosis is more common than colonic diverticulosis
updates.explanation: Duodenal fold thickening can result from adjacent pancreatic or gallbladder inflammation, Crohn disease, or chronic dialysis-related changes that mimic pancreatitis on barium. Primary duodenal Crohn disease is rare. Jejunal diverticulosis is less common than colonic diverticulosis, occurs along the mesenteric border, and is associated with bacterial overgrowth and malabsorption.

updates.question_text: Regarding bowel trauma versus shock bowel, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Shock bowel is diagnosed by focal leaked oral contrast alone
Bowel trauma always has brighter adrenal enhancement as the dominant clue
Bowel trauma is more focal, while shock bowel is more diffuse
Traumatic wall thickening can reflect high-attenuation submucosal blood
Shock bowel has near-water attenuation oedema with intense mucosal enhancement
options_after: Shock bowel is diagnosed by focal leaked oral contrast alone
Bowel trauma characteristically has brighter adrenal enhancement as the dominant clue
Bowel trauma is more focal, while shock bowel is more diffuse
Traumatic wall thickening can reflect high-attenuation submucosal blood
Shock bowel has near-water attenuation oedema with intense mucosal enhancement
updates.explanation: Bowel trauma is typically focal and may have high-attenuation submucosal blood plus direct or indirect injury signs. Shock bowel is diffuse, with near-water oedema, intense mucosal enhancement, and systemic signs such as bright adrenals or flat IVC.

updates.question_text: Regarding small-bowel metastatic disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Prostate carcinoma is the classic source described for multiple small-bowel target lesions
Small-bowel metastases are limited to direct peritoneal spread and never haematogenous seeding
Melanoma is highlighted as a classic small-bowel metastasis source
Melanoma can produce multiple target lesions in the source
Ovarian dermoid is the typical primary source in the passage
options_after: Prostate carcinoma is the classic source described for multiple small-bowel target lesions
Small-bowel metastases are limited to direct peritoneal spread rather than haematogenous seeding
Melanoma is highlighted as a classic small-bowel metastasis source
Melanoma can produce multiple target lesions in the source
Ovarian dermoid is the typical primary source in the passage
updates.explanation: Melanoma is highlighted as a classic small-bowel metastatic tumour source and can produce multiple target lesions. Breast, lung, and Kaposi sarcoma can also seed the small bowel haematogenously, but melanoma is the key source in this passage.

updates.question_text: Regarding obturator hernia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is classically seen in older women in the source
It can produce Howship-Romberg sign from obturator nerve compression
It herniates between obturator and pectineus muscles
It always causes early complete bowel obstruction before strangulation
It occurs through the semilunar line above the arcuate line
options_after: It is classically seen in older women in the source
It can produce Howship-Romberg sign from obturator nerve compression
It herniates between obturator and pectineus muscles
It characteristically causes early complete bowel obstruction before strangulation
It occurs through the semilunar line above the arcuate line
updates.explanation: Obturator hernia is the classic older-woman hernia, often in settings of increased intra-abdominal pressure. Bowel herniates between obturator and pectineus muscles and may compress the obturator nerve, causing medial thigh-to-knee paraesthesia known as Howship-Romberg sign. It may be asymptomatic but can strangulate.

updates.question_text: Regarding internal hernias and paraduodenal hernias, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Internal hernia is herniation through the skin and abdominal wall muscles only
Internal hernia commonly presents as closed-loop obstruction and may strangulate
Paraduodenal hernias are the most common type of internal hernia in the source
Left paraduodenal hernia is more common than right paraduodenal hernia
Paraduodenal hernias are unrelated to congenital recesses or fossae
options_after: Internal hernia is herniation through the skin and abdominal wall muscles
Internal hernia commonly presents as closed-loop obstruction and may strangulate
Paraduodenal hernias are the most common type of internal hernia in the source
Left paraduodenal hernia is more common than right paraduodenal hernia
Paraduodenal hernias are unrelated to congenital recesses or fossae
updates.explanation: Internal hernia is herniation of viscera through peritoneal or mesenteric defects and often manifests as closed-loop obstruction with strangulation risk. Paraduodenal hernias are the most common type, and the left-sided form is much more common than the right-sided form.

updates.question_text: Regarding generalized and focal ileus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ileus is defined by a fixed transition point and decompressed distal bowel only
A central sentinel loop excludes pancreatitis in the source
Generalized ileus has large and small bowel extensively air-filled but not necessarily focally obstructed
Sentinel loop is focal bowel dilatation adjacent to local inflammation
Mechanical obstruction and ileus have identical symmetric bowel-gas patterns in the source
options_after: Ileus is defined by a fixed transition point and decompressed distal bowel
A central sentinel loop excludes pancreatitis in the source
Generalized ileus has large and small bowel extensively air-filled but not necessarily focally obstructed
Sentinel loop is focal bowel dilatation adjacent to local inflammation
Mechanical obstruction and ileus have closely comparable symmetric bowel-gas patterns in the source
updates.explanation: Ileus is paralysed bowel. Generalized ileus makes large and small bowel appear similarly air-filled, whereas obstruction is more asymmetric. Focal reactive ileus produces a sentinel loop adjacent to local inflammation, such as right lower quadrant appendicitis, central pancreatitis, or left lower quadrant diverticulitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding appendiceal mucocele, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mucinous cystadenoma is the most common mucinous appendiceal tumour in the source
Layering within a cystic mass on ultrasound is described as an onion sign
Mucocele perforation can lead to pseudomyxoma peritonei
Mucinous cystadenoma and cystadenocarcinoma are always easily distinguished by imaging
Appendiceal mucocele is a solid hypervascular liver lesion
options_after: Mucinous cystadenoma is the most common mucinous appendiceal tumour in the source
Layering within a cystic mass on ultrasound is described as an onion sign
Mucocele perforation can lead to pseudomyxoma peritonei
Mucinous cystadenoma and cystadenocarcinoma are characteristically easily distinguished by imaging
Appendiceal mucocele is a solid hypervascular liver lesion
updates.explanation: Mucinous cystadenoma is described as the commonest mucinous tumour of the appendix and can markedly dilate the appendix. Imaging may not reliably separate cystadenoma from cystadenocarcinoma. Perforation can cause pseudomyxoma peritonei, and the onion sign on ultrasound suggests mucocele.

updates.question_text: Regarding sigmoid and caecal volvulus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Sigmoid volvulus usually points to the left upper quadrant and maintains haustra in the source
Caecal volvulus is the common nursing-home constipation volvulus and points to the right upper quadrant
Caecal volvulus is more common than sigmoid volvulus in adults
Sigmoid volvulus is the most common adult colonic volvulus
Sigmoid volvulus has no recurrence after decompression in the source
options_after: Sigmoid volvulus usually points to the left upper quadrant and maintains haustra in the source
Caecal volvulus is the common nursing-home constipation volvulus and points to the right upper quadrant
Caecal volvulus is more common than sigmoid volvulus in adults
Sigmoid volvulus is the most common adult colonic volvulus
Sigmoid volvulus lacks recurrence after decompression in the source
updates.explanation: Sigmoid volvulus is the common adult form, associated with chronic constipation in older or institutionalised patients, and can show a coffee-bean or inverted-3 sign pointing to the right upper quadrant. Caecal volvulus is less common, seen in younger patients with mobile mesentery or predisposing factors, and more often points left upper quadrant. Sigmoid recurrence after decompression is high.

updates.question_text: Regarding caecal bascule and colonic pseudo-obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Caecal bascule is anterior folding of the caecum without twisting
The terminal ileum is not involved in caecal bascule, so small-bowel dilatation is not expected in the source
Colonic pseudo-obstruction is always due to a mechanical obstructing mass
Caecal bascule is defined by a mesenteric twist with distal ileal obstruction
Ogilvie syndrome shows marked diffuse large-bowel dilatation without a discrete transition point
options_after: Caecal bascule is anterior folding of the caecum without twisting
The terminal ileum is not involved in caecal bascule, so small-bowel dilatation is not expected in the source
Colonic pseudo-obstruction is characteristically due to a mechanical obstructing mass
Caecal bascule is defined by a mesenteric twist with distal ileal obstruction
Ogilvie syndrome shows marked diffuse large-bowel dilatation without a discrete transition point
updates.explanation: Caecal bascule is described as anterior folding of the caecum without torsion, with ectopic mid-abdominal caecal dilatation and no terminal ileal involvement. Ogilvie syndrome or colonic pseudo-obstruction occurs after serious illness or in nursing-home patients and shows diffuse large-bowel dilatation without a discrete transition point.

updates.question_text: Regarding diversion colitis, colitis cystica, rectal cavernous haemangioma, and gossypiboma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Rectal cavernous haemangioma is never associated with pelvic phleboliths or vascular syndromes
Gossypiboma is a primary mucinous appendiceal tumour rather than a retained surgical material mimic
Diversion colitis or pouchitis occurs in a surgically diverted blind loop with bacterial overgrowth
Colitis cystica profunda involves larger cysts in the pelvic colon and rectum
Colitis cystica superficialis is limited to the appendix and never affects the colon
options_after: Rectal cavernous haemangioma is not associated with pelvic phleboliths or vascular syndromes
Gossypiboma is a primary mucinous appendiceal tumour rather than a retained surgical material mimic
Diversion colitis or pouchitis occurs in a surgically diverted blind loop with bacterial overgrowth
Colitis cystica profunda involves larger cysts in the pelvic colon and rectum
Colitis cystica superficialis is limited to the appendix and will not affect the colon
updates.explanation: Diversion colitis or pouchitis occurs when a blind loop no longer receives faecal stream, especially with inflammatory bowel disease. Colitis cystica superficialis has small cysts throughout the colon, while profunda involves larger pelvic colonic or rectal cysts. Rectal cavernous haemangioma may show many phleboliths and is linked with vascular syndromes. Gossypiboma is a retained surgical sponge or cotton product and can mimic abscess.

updates.question_text: Regarding liver metastases from colon cancer, which of the following MRI features are source-consistent?
options_before: T1 dark signal
Homogeneous progressive enhancement like a typical haemangioma
Uniform marked T1 hyperintensity from fat as the classic pattern
No target-like morphology is ever described in the source
Mildly bright T2 signal
options_after: T1 dark signal
Homogeneous progressive enhancement like a typical haemangioma
Uniform marked T1 hyperintensity from fat as the classic pattern
Target-like morphology is not described as a feature in the source
Mildly bright T2 signal
updates.explanation: The source describes colon liver metastases as classically T1 dark, mildly T2 bright, heterogeneously and non-progressively enhancing, and sometimes target-like. Uniform marked T1 fat signal or progressive haemangioma-like enhancement are not the classic metastatic patterns described here.

updates.question_text: Regarding surgical treatment of rectal cancer, which of the following statements are correct?

options_after: Tumour position relative to the anorectal angle helps determine operation type
A 5 cm threshold above the anorectal angle is used to separate high from low in the source
High rectal cancer can be treated with low anterior resection with continence preservation
Low rectal cancer is treated with abdominoperineal resection and colostomy in the source
Primarily low rectal cancer is treated with total mesorectal excision
updates.explanation: The source uses tumour position relative to the anorectal angle, with about 5 cm separating high from low rectal cancer. High rectal cancer can be treated with low anterior resection and continence preservation. Low rectal cancer is treated with abdominoperineal resection and colostomy. Both approaches include total mesorectal excision.

updates.question_text: Regarding peritoneal disease spread, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Intraperitoneal seeding is unrelated to normal fluid flow
Natural peritoneal fluid flow is mainly downward from the upper abdomen to pelvis through the left gutter only
The gastrohepatic ligament allows spread from stomach, oesophagus, and liver in the source
The gastrosplenic ligament can allow spread from stomach to splenic hilum
The duodenocolic ligament can allow spread from right colon to nodes near duodenum or pancreas
options_after: Intraperitoneal seeding is unrelated to normal fluid flow
Natural peritoneal fluid flow is mainly downward from the upper abdomen to pelvis through the left gutter
The gastrohepatic ligament allows spread from stomach, oesophagus, and liver in the source
The gastrosplenic ligament can allow spread from stomach to splenic hilum
The duodenocolic ligament can allow spread from right colon to nodes near duodenum or pancreas
updates.explanation: Disease can spread haematogenously, through lymphatics, by direct invasion along ligaments and mesenteries, and by intraperitoneal seeding. The source highlights gastrohepatic, gastrosplenic, and duodenocolic ligaments as spread pathways. Intraperitoneal seeding follows normal peritoneal fluid flow, largely upward from pelvis through the right more than left paracolic gutter.

updates.question_text: Regarding peritoneal carcinomatosis and omental caking, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Natural ascites flow helps determine implant location
Retrovesical space is described as the most common dependent implant site
Omental caking can posteriorly displace bowel away from the anterior abdominal wall
Peritoneal implants always spare dependent pelvic recesses
Omental caking is defined as air in the biliary tree
options_after: Natural ascites flow helps determine implant location
Retrovesical space is described as the most common dependent implant site
Omental caking can posteriorly displace bowel away from the anterior abdominal wall
Peritoneal implants characteristically spare dependent pelvic recesses
Omental caking is defined as air in the biliary tree
updates.explanation: Peritoneal implants follow the natural flow and dependent pooling of intraperitoneal fluid. The retrovesical space is highlighted as the most common site because it is dependent. Omental seeding or caking thickens the omentum and can posteriorly displace bowel from the anterior abdominal wall.

updates.question_text: Regarding carcinoid, desmoid, and sclerosing mesenteritis in the mesenteric mass scheme, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Smooth single solid mesenteric masses with no fat are limited to pseudocyst in the source scheme

Desmoid is a unilocular cystic lesion by definition
options_after: Smooth single solid mesenteric masses without fat are limited to pseudocyst in the source scheme
Ileal location with arterial enhancement and infiltrative margins suggests carcinoid
Distorting margins with delayed hyperenhancement suggest desmoid or sclerosing mesenteritis in the source
Carcinoid is excluded if a mesenteric mass is near the ileum
Desmoid is a unilocular cystic lesion by definition
updates.explanation: The source scheme points toward carcinoid when a mesenteric mass has infiltrative margins, ileal location, and arterial enhancement. Distorting margins with delayed hyperenhancement suggest desmoid or sclerosing mesenteritis. Smooth single solid lesions without fat have other differentials such as GIST or solitary fibrous tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding mesenteric lymphoma and misty mesentery, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mesenteric lymphoma is usually non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the source
The sandwich sign is a confluent soft-tissue mass encasing mesenteric vessels
Misty mesentery is never followed up because lymphoma is impossible

Bulky retroperitoneal nodes and a soft-tissue sandwich sign favour lymphoma over simple mesenteric panniculitis
options_after: Mesenteric lymphoma is usually non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the source
The sandwich sign is a confluent soft-tissue mass encasing mesenteric vessels
Misty mesentery is managed without interval imaging when lymphoma is excluded clinically
Misty mesentery is increased mesenteric fat density centred around the jejunal root with small nodes
Bulky retroperitoneal nodes and a soft-tissue sandwich sign favour lymphoma over simple mesenteric panniculitis
updates.explanation: Mesenteric lymphoma is usually non-Hodgkin lymphoma and can produce the sandwich sign, where lobulated confluent soft tissue encases mesenteric vessels. Misty mesentery is increased mesenteric fat density near the jejunal root, often due to mesenteric panniculitis but lymphoma remains a differential. Bulky retroperitoneal nodes or a soft-tissue sandwich sign increase suspicion for lymphoma, and follow-up may establish stability.

updates.question_text: Regarding liver surface anatomy and Couinaud segmentation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The caudate lobe is segment 8 and drains only through the right hepatic vein
Cantlie line runs from the spleen to the umbilicus in the source
The liver lacks visceral peritoneal covering at the porta hepatis, bare area, and gallbladder fossa
Injury to the bare area can result in retroperitoneal bleeding
Couinaud segments are functional divisions with their own biliary drainage, inflow, and outflow
options_after: The caudate lobe is segment 8 and drains primarily through the right hepatic vein
Cantlie line runs from the spleen to the umbilicus in the source
The liver lacks visceral peritoneal covering at the porta hepatis, bare area, and gallbladder fossa
Injury to the bare area can result in retroperitoneal bleeding
Couinaud segments are functional divisions with their own biliary drainage, inflow, and outflow
updates.explanation: The liver is peritonealised except at the porta hepatis, bare area, and gallbladder fossa; bare-area injury can bleed retroperitoneally. Couinaud segmentation is functional, with each segment having its own biliary drainage, inflow, and outflow. The caudate lobe is segment 1 and drains directly to the IVC. Cantlie line runs from the IVC to the middle of the gallbladder fossa.

updates.question_text: Regarding hepatic veins and segmental anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The right hepatic vein divides segments 7/8 from 6/5 in the source

The left hepatic vein divides the right anterior and right posterior sector in the source
The portal vein divides the liver into anterior and posterior segments rather than upper and lower segments
The caudate lobe drains through the main hepatic veins only
options_after: The right hepatic vein divides segments 7/8 from 6/5 in the source
The middle hepatic vein divides segments 4a/8 and 4b/5
The left hepatic vein divides the right anterior and right posterior sector in the source
The portal vein divides the liver into anterior and posterior segments rather than upper and lower segments
The caudate lobe drains through the main hepatic veins
updates.explanation: The source lists hepatic vein landmarks: right hepatic vein divides 7/8 from 6/5, middle hepatic vein divides 4a/8 and 4b/5, and left hepatic vein or ligamentum teres fissure divides 4a/2 and 4b/3. The portal vein separates upper and lower segments. The caudate lobe drains directly to the IVC.

updates.question_text: Regarding hepatic anatomic variants and MRI signal, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The most common biliary variant listed is left hepatic duct draining into the cystic duct
The pancreas is described as T1 dark because it contains no enzymes
The most common vascular variant listed is replaced right hepatic artery from the SMA
The spleen is T2 bright and T1 dark in the source memory model
The liver is normally much brighter than pancreas on T1 in the source memory model
options_after: The most common biliary variant listed is left hepatic duct draining into the cystic duct
The pancreas is described as T1 dark because it lacks enzymes
The most common vascular variant listed is replaced right hepatic artery from the SMA
The spleen is T2 bright and T1 dark in the source memory model
The liver is normally much brighter than pancreas on T1 in the source memory model
updates.explanation: The source lists replaced right hepatic artery from the SMA as the common vascular variant and right posterior segmental duct into the left hepatic duct as the common biliary variant. Its MRI memory model treats spleen as water/blood-like (T2 bright, T1 dark), pancreas as very T1 bright from enzymes, and liver as T1 brighter/T2 darker but not as T1 bright as pancreas.

updates.question_text: Regarding cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and THADs, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fibrosis first causes symmetric enlargement of all liver segments with no caudate change in the source
Portal hypertension is only post-hepatic by definition in the source
THADs persist unchanged on equilibrium and delayed phases by definition
THADs are transient arterial/early portal phase enhancement differences related to altered portal and arterial flow
Caudate to right lobe ratio greater than 0.75 is described as nonspecific and never useful
options_after: Fibrosis first causes symmetric enlargement of most liver segments without caudate change in the source
Portal hypertension is primarily post-hepatic by definition in the source
THADs persist unchanged on equilibrium and delayed phases by definition
THADs are transient arterial/early portal phase enhancement differences related to altered portal and arterial flow
A caudate-to-right-lobe ratio greater than 0.75 is too nonspecific to aid diagnosis
updates.explanation: Hepatic fibrosis can preferentially affect the longer right portal venous course, leading to right-lobe atrophy and caudate/left-lobe hypertrophy. Portal hypertension can be pre-hepatic, hepatic, or post-hepatic. THADs are focal arterial buffer responses seen in arterial or early portal phases and not delayed phases.

updates.question_text: Regarding cirrhosis-related perfusion and portal hypertensive bowel changes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The central-peripheral phenomenon reflects peripheral subcapsular enhancement with relative central/perihilar hypodensity
Portal hypertensive colopathy can mimic colitis and is worse on the right in the source
Portal hypertensive colopathy is fixed after transplant and never resolves
Portal hypertensive gastropathy can cause gastric wall thickening and upper GI bleeding without varices
The central-peripheral phenomenon is primarily caused by acute appendicitis
options_after: The central-peripheral phenomenon reflects peripheral subcapsular enhancement with relative central/perihilar hypodensity
Portal hypertensive colopathy can mimic colitis and is worse on the right in the source
Portal hypertensive colopathy is fixed after transplant and will not resolve
Portal hypertensive gastropathy can cause gastric wall thickening and upper GI bleeding without varices
The central-peripheral phenomenon is primarily caused by acute appendicitis
updates.explanation: Cirrhosis can produce global perfusion changes, with arterial response in peripheral subcapsular liver and relative central hypodensity: the central-peripheral phenomenon. Portal hypertensive colopathy can mimic colitis and is worse on the right because left-sided collaterals decompress the left colon more effectively. The source states it resolves after transplant. Portal hypertensive gastropathy can produce thickened gastric wall and upper GI bleeding even without varices.

updates.question_text: What is the direction of hepatofugal portal venous flow?
options_before: Toward the liver
Only from hepatic vein to IVC
Away from the liver
Only through the cystic duct
From bile duct to portal vein
options_after: Toward the liver
Primarily from hepatic vein to IVC
Away from the liver
Primarily through the cystic duct
From bile duct to portal vein
updates.explanation: Hepatofugal flow means flow directed away from the liver. In cirrhosis, severe resistance and arterioportal shunting can contribute to reversed portal venous flow.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI liver contrast agents, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Extracellular agents behave like CT iodine contrast in that they are blood-flow dependent
Extracellular liver MRI phases resemble arterial, portal venous, and interstitial timing
Multihance has no biliary excretion and cannot ever be used for bile leak assessment
Hepatocyte-specific agents make every benign and malignant lesion bright at 20 minutes
Gd-EOB-DTPA/Eovist has hepatocyte-specific uptake and biliary excretion
options_after: Extracellular agents behave like CT iodine contrast in that they are blood-flow dependent
Extracellular liver MRI phases resemble arterial, portal venous, and interstitial timing
Multihance lacks biliary excretion and will not ever be used for bile leak assessment
Hepatocyte-specific agents make most benign and malignant lesions bright at 20 minutes
Gd-EOB-DTPA/Eovist has hepatocyte-specific uptake and biliary excretion
updates.explanation: Extracellular gadolinium agents stay outside cells and behave like CT contrast in lesion enhancement timing. Hepatocyte-specific agents are taken up by hepatocytes and excreted into bile, with Eovist as the classic example. Multihance is mostly extracellular but has a small biliary-excretion component, so delayed imaging can be used for bile leak assessment. Hepatobiliary phase darkness is nonspecific because many lesions lack functioning hepatocytes.

updates.question_text: Regarding hepatic adenoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is usually solitary and seen in women using oral contraceptives in the source
Anabolic steroid use is an alternative association in men
Multiple adenomas suggest glycogen storage disease or liver adenomatosis
Imaging reliably separates hepatic adenoma from HCC in all cases
Adenomas never regress after stopping oral contraceptives
options_after: It is usually solitary and seen in women using oral contraceptives in the source
Anabolic steroid use is an alternative association in men
Multiple adenomas suggest glycogen storage disease or liver adenomatosis
Imaging reliably separates hepatic adenoma from HCC in most cases
Adenomas will not regress after stopping oral contraceptives
updates.explanation: Hepatic adenoma is typically solitary in a woman using oral contraceptives, with anabolic steroid use as an alternative risk factor. Multiple lesions suggest glycogen storage disease or adenomatosis. Imaging cannot reliably distinguish adenoma from HCC in all cases; adenomas may regress after stopping oral contraceptives, but can bleed and rarely transform.

updates.question_text: Regarding conventional HCC, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It usually occurs in cirrhosis or chronic liver disease
Risk factors include hepatitis B, hepatitis C, haemochromatosis, glycogen storage disease, and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency in the source
Portal vein invasion can occur, with hepatic vein invasion considered more specific in the source
AFP is always normal in conventional HCC
Spontaneous hepatic bleeding is specifically excluded as an HCC behaviour
options_after: It usually occurs in cirrhosis or chronic liver disease
Risk factors include hepatitis B, hepatitis C, haemochromatosis, glycogen storage disease, and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency in the source
Portal vein invasion can occur, with hepatic vein invasion considered more specific in the source
AFP is characteristically normal in conventional HCC
Spontaneous hepatic bleeding is specifically excluded as an HCC behaviour
updates.explanation: HCC typically arises in cirrhosis or chronic liver disease, with multiple risk factors listed in the source. AFP is elevated in many cases but not universally. HCC often invades portal vein, while hepatic vein invasion is considered more specific. The source also notes that HCC can rupture and cause spontaneous hepatic bleeding.

updates.question_text: Regarding hepatic metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Liver metastases are much more common than primary liver cancer in the source
Colon should be considered first when liver metastases are seen
Hyperechoic metastases are always hypovascular colon metastases
Calcified metastases usually suggest mucinous neoplasm such as colon, ovary, or pancreas
Tiny indeterminate hypodensities in breast cancer patients without definite liver metastases are often benign in the source
options_after: Liver metastases are much more common than primary liver cancer in the source
Colon should be considered first when liver metastases are seen
Hyperechoic metastases are characteristically hypovascular colon metastases
Calcified metastases usually suggest mucinous neoplasm such as colon, ovary, or pancreas
Tiny indeterminate hypodensities in breast cancer patients without definite liver metastases are often benign in the source
updates.explanation: Liver metastases are far more common than primary liver cancer, and colon is the first source to consider. Calcified metastases suggest mucinous tumours such as colon, ovary, or pancreas. Hypervascular metastases can be hyperechoic, whereas colon, lung, and pancreas metastases are often hypoechoic. Very small indeterminate hypodensities, even in breast cancer patients without definite liver metastases, are often benign.

updates.question_text: Regarding focal liver lesions on ultrasound, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: FNH can be isoechoic and difficult to see unless it bulges the liver, has a scar, or shows spoke-wheel Doppler
Hepatic adenoma appearance is variable because of haemorrhage, fat, calcification, and necrosis
Metastases are especially suspicious when multiple lesions have a target halo
Internal or peripheral Doppler flow outside a classic FNH spoke-wheel pattern is never concerning
HCC can show a hypoechoic halo or target-like capsule in the source
options_after: FNH can be isoechoic and difficult to see unless it bulges the liver, has a scar, or shows spoke-wheel Doppler
Hepatic adenoma appearance is variable because of haemorrhage, fat, calcification, and necrosis
Metastases are especially suspicious when multiple lesions have a target halo
Internal or peripheral Doppler flow outside a classic FNH spoke-wheel pattern is not concerning
HCC can show a hypoechoic halo or target-like capsule in the source
updates.explanation: FNH may be sonographically subtle and is recognised by mass effect, central scar, or spoke-wheel Doppler. Adenoma is variable because of blood products, fat, calcification, and necrosis. HCC can show a hypoechoic halo/fibrous capsule. Multiple lesions with target halo are concerning for metastases, and flow patterns other than classic FNH spoke-wheel can raise concern.

updates.question_text: Regarding incidental liver lesion CT algorithm concepts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Suspicious features include blurry margins, thick septa, nodularity, heterogeneity, or portal venous density over 20 HU
A lesion under 1 cm in a low-risk patient requires no follow-up in the source algorithm
Benign features include sharp margins, density under 20 HU, or characteristic benign enhancement

All low-risk lesions over 1 cm require biopsy regardless of imaging features
options_after: Suspicious features include blurry margins, thick septa, nodularity, heterogeneity, or portal venous density over 20 HU
A lesion under 1 cm in a low-risk patient requires no follow-up in the source algorithm
Benign features include sharp margins, density under 20 HU, or characteristic benign enhancement
High-risk patients include cancer or chronic liver-risk contexts and often proceed to MRI
Most low-risk lesions over 1 cm require biopsy despite variation in imaging features
updates.explanation: The algorithm treats subcentimetre lesions in low-risk patients as no follow-up. Benign features include sharp margins, low density under 20 HU, and characteristic benign enhancement. Suspicious features include blurry margins, thick septa, nodularity, heterogeneity, or portal venous density over 20 HU; high-risk clinical context usually pushes toward MRI.

updates.question_text: Regarding primary versus secondary haemochromatosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Primary haemochromatosis involves liver and pancreas with splenic sparing in the source
Primary haemochromatosis is acquired from multiple transfusions with reticuloendothelial uptake
Secondary haemochromatosis is genetic increased GI absorption affecting pancreas first
Both forms always spare the liver
Secondary haemochromatosis involves liver and spleen with pancreatic sparing in the source
options_after: Primary haemochromatosis involves liver and pancreas with splenic sparing in the source
Primary haemochromatosis is acquired from multiple transfusions with reticuloendothelial uptake
Secondary haemochromatosis is genetic increased GI absorption affecting pancreas first
Both forms characteristically spare the liver
Secondary haemochromatosis involves liver and spleen with pancreatic sparing in the source
updates.explanation: Primary haemochromatosis is inherited increased absorption and involves liver and pancreas, with splenic sparing. Secondary haemochromatosis is acquired from chronic inflammation or transfusions, with reticuloendothelial uptake involving liver and spleen while sparing pancreas.

updates.question_text: Regarding nutmeg liver and massive caudate hypertrophy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Nutmeg liver can be seen with Budd-Chiari syndrome
Massive caudate hypertrophy is listed with Budd-Chiari, PSC, and primary biliary cirrhosis
Nutmeg liver is a specific sign of appendiceal mucocele only
Massive caudate hypertrophy excludes Budd-Chiari in the source
Nutmeg liver can be seen with right heart failure or constrictive pericarditis
options_after: Nutmeg liver can be seen with Budd-Chiari syndrome
Massive caudate hypertrophy is listed with Budd-Chiari, PSC, and primary biliary cirrhosis
Nutmeg liver is a specific sign of appendiceal mucocele
Massive caudate hypertrophy excludes Budd-Chiari in the source
Nutmeg liver can be seen with right heart failure or constrictive pericarditis
updates.explanation: Nutmeg liver describes mottled hepatic enhancement and can occur with Budd-Chiari, hepatic veno-occlusive disease, right heart failure, and constrictive pericarditis. The source lists massive caudate hypertrophy with Budd-Chiari, primary sclerosing cholangitis, and primary biliary cirrhosis.

updates.question_text: What is the normal hepatic artery resistive index range after liver transplant in the source?
options_before: Below 0.1 only
options_after: Below 0.1
updates.explanation: The source lists a normal hepatic artery resistive index after transplant as 0.5-0.7. It also expects rapid systolic upstroke and hepatic artery peak velocity under 200 cm/s.

updates.question_text: Which branching gas pattern is most consistent with portal venous gas rather than pneumobilia?
options_before: Central gas near the porta hepatis only
Gas confined to the gallbladder lumen
Gas limited to the common bile duct after sphincterotomy
Gas in the stomach
Gas within 2 cm of the liver capsule
options_after: Central gas near the porta hepatis
Gas confined to the gallbladder lumen
Gas limited to the common bile duct after sphincterotomy
Gas in the stomach
Gas within 2 cm of the liver capsule
updates.explanation: Portal venous gas travels toward the hepatic periphery and can extend within 2 cm of the liver capsule. Pneumobilia is more central because bile drains toward the porta hepatis.

updates.question_text: Regarding pneumobilia and portal venous gas, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pneumobilia is usually central
Portal venous gas is peripheral and can be associated with bowel necrosis and pneumatosis
Pneumobilia always indicates bowel necrosis
Portal venous gas is expected only after manipulation of the sphincter of Oddi
Portal venous gas is always benign COPD-related gas in the source
options_after: Pneumobilia is usually central
Portal venous gas is peripheral and can be associated with bowel necrosis and pneumatosis
Pneumobilia characteristically indicates bowel necrosis
Portal venous gas is expected primarily after manipulation of the sphincter of Oddi
Portal venous gas is characteristically benign COPD-related gas in the source
updates.explanation: Pneumobilia is central because bile flows toward the porta hepatis and is often related to prior procedures affecting the sphincter of Oddi. Portal venous gas travels peripherally and has a broad differential, including benign causes and severe causes such as bowel necrosis, often with pneumatosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding jaundice, bacterial cholangitis, and PSC, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: PSC is unrelated to cholangiocarcinoma in the source
Dilated intrahepatic bile ducts are common in all cirrhosis types except PSC
Benign stricture after surgery or biliary intervention is described as the most common jaundice cause in the source
Bacterial cholangitis classically presents with jaundice, fever, and right upper quadrant pain

options_after: PSC is unrelated to cholangiocarcinoma in the source
Dilated intrahepatic bile ducts are common in most cirrhosis types except PSC
Benign stricture after surgery or biliary intervention is described as the most common jaundice cause in the source
Bacterial cholangitis classically presents with jaundice, fever, and right upper quadrant pain
PSC produces progressive multifocal strictures of intrahepatic and/or extrahepatic bile ducts
updates.explanation: The source notes that benign strictures after surgery or intervention are a common jaundice cause. Bacterial cholangitis has Charcot-type triad of jaundice, fever, and right upper quadrant pain and can cause abscess. PSC is chronic cholestatic duct inflammation with multifocal strictures, cirrhosis, strong cholangiocarcinoma association, and unusual intrahepatic duct dilatation among cirrhosis causes.

updates.question_text: Regarding choledochal cyst classification, which of the following statements are correct?

Type 4 involves only extrahepatic ducts by definition
Type 2 is a bile duct diverticulum

Type 3 is Caroli disease in the source
Type 4 involves primarily extrahepatic ducts by definition
Type 2 is a bile duct diverticulum
Type 5 is Caroli disease and is intrahepatic only
updates.explanation: Todani type 1 choledochal cyst is focal CBD dilatation and is by far the commonest. Type 2 is a bile duct diverticulum, type 3 is choledochocele, type 4 has both intra- and extrahepatic involvement, and type 5 is Caroli disease with intrahepatic disease only.

updates.question_text: Regarding ductal high-yield comparisons, which of the following statements are correct?

options_after: Caroli disease is associated with polycystic kidney disease, medullary sponge kidney, and cholangiocarcinoma
AIDS cholangiopathy can show PSC-like ducts plus papillary stenosis
Recurrent pyogenic cholangitis favours the right ductal system and lacks stones in the source summary
Malignant biliary strictures tend to be short and abrupt compared with benign strictures
PSC is strongly associated with ulcerative colitis but not cholangiocarcinoma
updates.explanation: The summary links Caroli disease with kidney associations and cholangiocarcinoma; AIDS cholangiopathy with PSC-like strictures and papillary stenosis; recurrent pyogenic cholangitis with stones, left duct predominance, and cholangiocarcinoma risk; and PSC with UC and cholangiocarcinoma. Malignant strictures tend to be long with shouldering, while benign strictures tend to be abrupt and short.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal gallbladder anatomy and measurements, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Width greater than 4 cm is always normal regardless of symptoms or fasting state

The gallbladder lies inferior to the interlobar fissure between right and left lobes

A mildly distended gallbladder is always obstructed regardless of fasting state
options_after: Width greater than 4 cm is characteristically normal despite variation in symptoms or fasting state
Normal wall thickness should be greater than 8 mm
The gallbladder lies inferior to the interlobar fissure between right and left lobes
It distends when fasting and empties after eating
A mildly distended gallbladder is characteristically obstructed despite variation in fasting state
updates.explanation: The normal gallbladder lies inferior to the interlobar fissure. It distends when fasting and contracts after eating, so mild fasting distension may be normal. Width over 4 cm suggests dilatation, and normal wall thickness is under 3 mm. Wall thickening is nonspecific and may be biliary, hepatic, or systemic oedema-related.

updates.question_text: Regarding gallbladder variants, which of the following statements are correct?

Duplicated gallbladder cannot occur
Duct of Luschka is the main pancreatic duct entering the duodenum
options_after: Duct of Luschka is an accessory cystic/subvesicular duct that can cause persistent bile leak after cholecystectomy
Phrygian cap is a fold of the gallbladder on itself and is clinically insignificant in the source
Intrahepatic gallbladder is a recognised location variant often above the interlobar fissure
Duplicated gallbladder will not occur
Duct of Luschka is the main pancreatic duct entering the duodenum
updates.explanation: Duct of Luschka is an accessory subvesicular/cystic duct variant that can lead to persistent bile leak after cholecystectomy. Phrygian cap is a benign fold of the gallbladder. Intrahepatic gallbladder is a recognised location variant, often above the interlobar fissure, and duplication can occur.

updates.question_text: Regarding gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Gallstones in children should raise sickle cell disease consideration in the source
Stones smaller than 3 mm always cast a clean acoustic shadow
Gallbladder wall thickening over 3 mm is nonspecific
Non-biliary causes of gallbladder wall thickening include hepatitis, heart failure, and cirrhosis in the source
Most gallstones are cholesterol stones in the source
options_after: Gallstones in children should raise sickle cell disease consideration in the source
Stones smaller than 3 mm characteristically cast a clean acoustic shadow
Gallbladder wall thickening over 3 mm is nonspecific
Non-biliary causes of gallbladder wall thickening include hepatitis, heart failure, and cirrhosis in the source
Most gallstones are cholesterol stones in the source
updates.explanation: Gallbladder wall thickening is nonspecific and can come from cholecystitis or non-biliary causes such as hepatitis, heart failure, or cirrhosis. Most stones are cholesterol stones, with pigmented stones making up the remainder. In children, sickle cell disease should be considered. Very small stones may fail to shadow.

updates.question_text: Regarding gallbladder shadowing and acute cholecystitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A gallbladder full of stones gives clean shadowing
Emphysematous cholecystitis gives dirty shadowing from gas
Sonographic Murphy sign and cholelithiasis are highly sensitive ultrasound findings in the source
Most acute cholecystitis is due to a stone obstructing the cystic duct
Porcelain gallbladder always gives clean shadowing identical to gallstones
options_after: A gallbladder full of stones gives clean shadowing
Emphysematous cholecystitis gives dirty shadowing from gas
Sonographic Murphy sign and cholelithiasis are highly sensitive ultrasound findings in the source
Most acute cholecystitis is due to a stone obstructing the cystic duct
Porcelain gallbladder characteristically gives clean shadowing closely comparable to gallstones
updates.explanation: Clean gallbladder shadowing suggests stones, dirty shadowing suggests gas in emphysematous cholecystitis, and porcelain gallbladder has variable shadowing. Acute cholecystitis is usually calculous from cystic duct obstruction; sensitive ultrasound findings include sonographic Murphy sign and cholelithiasis.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute acalculous cholecystitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: HIDA scan will show normal gallbladder visualisation
It occurs in severely ill or post-operative patients rather than routine biliary colic patients
The classic scenario in the source is after heart valve replacement surgery
Thick wall and adjacent fluid are more important than gallbladder dilatation in the source
The absence of stones makes acalculous cholecystitis impossible
options_after: HIDA scan will show normal gallbladder visualisation
It occurs in severely ill or post-operative patients rather than routine biliary colic patients
The classic scenario in the source is after heart valve replacement surgery
Thick wall and adjacent fluid are more important than gallbladder dilatation in the source
The absence of stones excludes acalculous cholecystitis
updates.explanation: Acalculous cholecystitis is the important exception to stone-driven cholecystitis and occurs in very ill or post-operative patients, with a classic post-heart-valve-replacement scenario. Wall thickening and adjacent fluid are emphasised more than dilatation. HIDA behaves like obstructive cholecystitis, with non-visualisation of the gallbladder.

updates.question_text: Regarding porcelain gallbladder, polyps, and gallbladder cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Porcelain gallbladder is treated by reassurance only in the source
Porcelain gallbladder is extensive wall calcification and has increased cancer risk
Gallbladder polyps over 1 cm are generally removed
Most gallbladder cancers are unrelated to gallstones in the source
Porcelain gallbladder protects against gallbladder cancer
options_after: Porcelain gallbladder is treated by reassurance primarily in the source
Porcelain gallbladder is extensive wall calcification and has increased cancer risk
Gallbladder polyps over 1 cm are generally removed
Most gallbladder cancers are unrelated to gallstones in the source
Porcelain gallbladder protects against gallbladder cancer
updates.explanation: Porcelain gallbladder is extensive wall calcification, increases gallbladder cancer risk, and is surgically removed. Polyps over 1 cm are concerning enough for removal. Gallbladder cancer is strongly associated with gallstones and other chronic inflammatory risks, including PSC, chronic cholecystitis, porcelain gallbladder, Mirizzi syndrome, and large polyps.

updates.question_text: Regarding gallbladder cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
