options_before: Classic presentation is an elderly woman with nonspecific right upper quadrant pain, weight loss, anorexia, and long-standing gallstones or risk factors
Most gallbladder cancers are associated with gallstones in the source
PSC, chronic cholecystitis, porcelain gallbladder, Mirizzi syndrome, and large polyps are source-listed risk factors
Gallbladder cancer often presents late with liver invasion or portal nodes
Fundal gallbladder cancer is the only location that never causes obstruction or late presentation
options_after: Classic presentation is an elderly woman with nonspecific right upper quadrant pain, weight loss, anorexia, and long-standing gallstones or risk factors
Most gallbladder cancers are associated with gallstones in the source
PSC, chronic cholecystitis, porcelain gallbladder, Mirizzi syndrome, and large polyps are source-listed risk factors
Gallbladder cancer often presents late with liver invasion or portal nodes
Fundal gallbladder cancer is the principal location that will not cause obstruction or late presentation
updates.explanation: Gallbladder cancer is associated with chronic inflammatory and stone-related risk factors, including gallstones in most cases, PSC, chronic cholecystitis, porcelain gallbladder, Mirizzi syndrome, and large polyps. It often presents late, with direct liver invasion or portal nodes. The source notes poor outcomes and nonspecific symptoms.

updates.question_text: Regarding hepatic vein Doppler, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal hepatic venous flow is mainly antegrade from liver toward heart
Right-heart pressure changes can alter hepatic venous waveform morphology
All flow above the baseline is antegrade toward the heart in the source diagram
Cirrhosis cannot alter hepatic venous pulsatility
Absent hepatic venous waveform is the normal expected pattern
options_after: Normal hepatic venous flow is mainly antegrade from liver toward heart
Right-heart pressure changes can alter hepatic venous waveform morphology
Most flow above the baseline is antegrade toward the heart in the source diagram
Cirrhosis will not alter hepatic venous pulsatility
Absent hepatic venous waveform is the normal expected pattern
updates.explanation: Hepatic venous flow is complex and phasic, but the bulk should be antegrade toward the heart. Right-sided cardiac pressure changes and direct venous compression from cirrhosis can alter waveforms. In the source diagram, retrograde flow is above baseline and antegrade flow below baseline.

updates.question_text: What is the normal direction of portal venous flow?
options_before: Toward the liver
Away from the liver
Toward the right atrium through hepatic veins
Into the cystic duct
Only into the splenic vein
options_after: Toward the liver
Away from the liver
Toward the right atrium through hepatic veins
Into the cystic duct
Primarily into the splenic vein
updates.explanation: Normal portal venous flow is hepatopetal, directed toward the liver. Reversed hepatofugal flow is abnormal and most importantly associated with portal hypertension.

updates.question_text: Regarding portal vein Doppler, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal portal venous flow should be strongly pulsatile and reverse each cardiac cycle
Normal portal vein velocity is between 20 and 40 cm/s in the source
The normal waveform is gently undulating and remains above the baseline
Slow portal flow is defined as less than 60 cm/s in the source
Absent portal flow is always benign respiratory variation
options_after: Normal portal venous flow should be strongly pulsatile and reverse each cardiac cycle
Normal portal vein velocity is between 20 and 40 cm/s in the source
The normal waveform is gently undulating and remains above the baseline
Slow portal flow is defined as less than 60 cm/s in the source
Absent portal flow is characteristically benign respiratory variation
updates.explanation: Normal portal venous flow is toward the liver with a gentle undulating waveform remaining above baseline, and velocity around 20-40 cm/s. Slow flow is less than 15 cm/s, most commonly from portal hypertension. Absent flow can reflect thrombosis, tumour invasion, or stagnant flow from severe portal hypertension.

updates.question_text: What Doppler angle should generally be used for velocity measurement according to the source?
options_before: Exactly 90 degrees
Greater than 80 degrees
Any angle is acceptable
Less than 60 degrees
Only 120 degrees
options_after: Exactly 90 degrees
Greater than 80 degrees
Any angle is acceptable
Less than 60 degrees
Primarily 120 degrees
updates.explanation: Doppler strength follows the cosine of the angle, so velocity measurements should use an angle less than 60 degrees. A 90-degree angle gives no Doppler shift.

updates.question_text: Regarding portal venous pulsatility, reversed flow, and slow flow, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pulsatile portal flow can be caused by right-sided CHF, tricuspid regurgitation, or cirrhosis with arterioportal shunting
Reversed portal flow is most importantly caused by portal hypertension
Post-hepatic causes of slow flow include isolated gallstones only
Portal vein thrombosis is excluded if no colour flow is seen
Slow portal flow is velocity below 15 cm/s in the source
options_after: Pulsatile portal flow can be caused by right-sided CHF, tricuspid regurgitation, or cirrhosis with arterioportal shunting
Reversed portal flow is most importantly caused by portal hypertension
Post-hepatic causes of slow flow include isolated gallstones
Portal vein thrombosis is excluded if colour flow is absent
Slow portal flow is velocity below 15 cm/s in the source
updates.explanation: Portal pulsatility can result from right-sided CHF, tricuspid regurgitation, or cirrhosis with vascular arterioportal shunting. Reversed flow is most importantly portal hypertension. Slow flow is below 15 cm/s and may be pre-hepatic, intrahepatic, or post-hepatic. Absent colour flow may be thrombosis, tumour invasion, or severe stagnant portal hypertension.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal pancreas imaging and cystic fibrosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The entire pancreas is intraperitoneal in the source
Cystic fibrosis never involves the pancreas
The pancreas should be more echogenic than normal liver on ultrasound
The pancreas should be the brightest non-contrast T1 abdominal organ in the source
Fibrosis in cystic fibrosis increases both T1 and T2 pancreatic signal
options_after: The entire pancreas is intraperitoneal in the source
Cystic fibrosis will not involve the pancreas
The pancreas should be more echogenic than normal liver on ultrasound
The pancreas should be the brightest non-contrast T1 abdominal organ in the source
Fibrosis in cystic fibrosis increases both T1 and T2 pancreatic signal
updates.explanation: The source states that pancreas is normally more echogenic than liver and is the brightest non-contrast T1 organ. The pancreas is retroperitoneal except the tail may be intraperitoneal. Cystic fibrosis frequently involves the pancreas, producing fibrosis with decreased T1/T2 signal or more commonly fatty replacement with increased T1 signal.

updates.question_text: Regarding pancreatic trauma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pancreatic duct integrity is the key management issue in the source
Suspected duct injury should be evaluated with MRCP or ERCP
Low-attenuation fluid separating enhancing pancreatic parenchymal portions indicates laceration rather than contusion
Peripancreatic fluid is specific for pancreatic injury and cannot reflect aggressive resuscitation
Traumatic pancreatitis in a child too young for the mechanism should never raise non-accidental trauma concern
options_after: Pancreatic duct integrity is the key management issue in the source
Suspected duct injury should be evaluated with MRCP or ERCP
Low-attenuation fluid separating enhancing pancreatic parenchymal portions indicates laceration rather than contusion
Peripancreatic fluid is specific for pancreatic injury and will not reflect aggressive resuscitation
Traumatic pancreatitis in a child too young for the mechanism should not raise non-accidental trauma concern
updates.explanation: In pancreatic trauma, duct integrity is the crucial question because duct injury changes management. Subtle signs include focal enlargement or adjacent fluid. A low-attenuation cleft separating enhancing pancreatic tissue is laceration, not contusion. Peripancreatic fluid is nonspecific and can reflect resuscitation; suspicious mechanism in a very young child should raise non-accidental trauma concern.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute pancreatitis collections, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Before 4 weeks with necrosis, the term is walled-off necrosis
After 4 weeks with necrosis, the term is acute necrotic collection
Before 4 weeks without necrosis, the term is acute peripancreatic fluid collection
After 4 weeks without necrosis, the term is pseudocyst
All collections are called pseudocysts regardless of time and necrosis
options_after: Before 4 weeks with necrosis, the term is walled-off necrosis
After 4 weeks with necrosis, the term is acute necrotic collection
Before 4 weeks without necrosis, the term is acute peripancreatic fluid collection
After 4 weeks without necrosis, the term is pseudocyst
Most collections are called pseudocysts despite variation in time and necrosis
updates.explanation: The source vocabulary separates collections by time and necrosis. Without necrosis, an early collection under 4 weeks is acute peripancreatic fluid collection and after 4 weeks is pseudocyst. With necrosis, under 4 weeks is acute necrotic collection and after 4 weeks is walled-off necrosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding pancreatitis complications and ultrasound findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Splenic vein and portal vein thrombosis are vascular complications
Isolated gastric varices can occur secondary to splenic vein occlusion
Gas is present in all pancreatic abscesses
An inflamed pancreas becomes hyperechoic relative to liver on ultrasound
GDA and splenic artery pseudoaneurysms are vascular complications
options_after: Splenic vein and portal vein thrombosis are vascular complications
Isolated gastric varices can occur secondary to splenic vein occlusion
Gas is present in most pancreatic abscesses
An inflamed pancreas becomes hyperechoic relative to liver on ultrasound
GDA and splenic artery pseudoaneurysms are vascular complications
updates.explanation: Pancreatitis vascular complications include splenic or portal vein thrombosis and pseudoaneurysm of the GDA or splenic artery. Splenic vein occlusion can cause isolated gastric varices. Gas is characteristic for infected collections but detected in only a minority of pancreatic abscesses. An inflamed oedematous pancreas is hypoechoic relative to liver, opposite of normal.

updates.question_text: Regarding pancreatic pseudocyst and simple cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Simple cysts are more common than pseudocysts after pancreatitis
Inflammatory pseudocyst is the most common pancreatic cystic lesion in the source
True epithelial-lined simple pancreatic cysts are rare and associated with syndromes such as VHL, polycystic kidney disease, and cystic fibrosis
Pseudocysts are mucin-producing premalignant tumours by definition
Pseudocysts communicate with the main duct in all cases and are always main-branch IPMNs
options_after: Simple cysts are more common than pseudocysts after pancreatitis
Inflammatory pseudocyst is the most common pancreatic cystic lesion in the source
True epithelial-lined simple pancreatic cysts are rare and associated with syndromes such as VHL, polycystic kidney disease, and cystic fibrosis
Pseudocysts are mucin-producing premalignant tumours by definition
Pseudocysts communicate with the main duct in most cases and are characteristically main-branch IPMNs
updates.explanation: When a cystic pancreatic lesion is seen, inflammatory pseudocyst from acute or chronic pancreatitis is the most common cause. True epithelial-lined simple cysts are rare and associated with syndromes including VHL, polycystic kidney disease, and cystic fibrosis. Pseudocyst is inflammatory rather than a mucin-producing neoplasm.

updates.question_text: Regarding IPMN, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: IPMN is a mucin-producing tumour arising from duct epithelium
Side-branch IPMN commonly appears as a small cystic mass in the head or uncinate process
Side-branch lesions under 3 cm are usually benign in the source
IPMN never communicates with the pancreatic duct
It can be side-branch, main-branch, or mixed
options_after: IPMN is a mucin-producing tumour arising from duct epithelium
Side-branch IPMN commonly appears as a small cystic mass in the head or uncinate process
Side-branch lesions under 3 cm are usually benign in the source
IPMN will not communicate with the pancreatic duct
It can be side-branch, main-branch, or mixed
updates.explanation: IPMN is a mucin-producing duct epithelial neoplasm and may involve side branches, main duct, or both. Side-branch lesions are common, often head/uncinate cystic masses that communicate with duct and are usually benign if under 3 cm. Communication with the duct distinguishes IPMN from serous and mucinous cystic neoplasms.

updates.question_text: Regarding main-branch IPMN and malignant features, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Main-branch IPMN has no malignant potential and is always ignored
Main-branch IPMN causes diffuse main duct dilatation
Main-branch IPMN has higher malignant potential than side-branch IPMN
All main-duct IPMNs are considered malignant enough that resection should be considered in the source
Concerning features include main duct over 10 mm, enhancing nodules, diffuse/multifocal involvement, or solid hypovascular mass
options_after: Main-branch IPMN lacks malignant potential and is characteristically ignored
Main-branch IPMN causes diffuse main duct dilatation
Main-branch IPMN has higher malignant potential than side-branch IPMN
All main-duct IPMNs are considered malignant enough that resection should be considered in the source
Concerning features include main duct over 10 mm, enhancing nodules, diffuse/multifocal involvement, or solid hypovascular mass
updates.explanation: Main-branch IPMN produces diffuse main duct dilatation, can mimic chronic pancreatitis with atrophy and calcification, and has much higher malignant potential than side-branch IPMN. The source says all main-duct IPMNs are considered malignant and resection should be considered. Concerning features include large main duct, enhancing nodules, diffuse/multifocal disease, and solid hypovascular mass.

updates.question_text: Regarding periampullary tumours, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They originate within 2 cm of the major papilla
They can arise from distal CBD, pancreas, or duodenum
MRI/MRCP helps assess the periampullary region
They are impossible to treat surgically and have worse prognosis than pancreatic adenocarcinoma in all cases
Gardner syndrome is protective against ampullary carcinoma in the source
options_after: They originate within 2 cm of the major papilla
They can arise from distal CBD, pancreas, or duodenum
MRI/MRCP helps assess the periampullary region
These lesions are unsuitable for surgical treatment and have a poorer prognosis than pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Gardner syndrome is protective against ampullary carcinoma in the source
updates.explanation: Periampullary tumours originate within 2 cm of the major papilla and may arise from distal CBD, pancreas, or duodenum. MRI/MRCP is useful for evaluating this region, and they can be treated with Whipple in selected cases, generally with better prognosis than conventional pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Gardner syndrome is associated with increased ampullary carcinoma incidence.

updates.question_text: What is the classic arterial-phase clue for intrapancreatic accessory spleen/splenosis?
options_before: Complete lack of enhancement on all phases
Peripheral nodular discontinuous enhancement with 15-minute fill-in
Double duct sign
Tiger-striped enhancement like spleen
Central dot sign
options_after: Complete lack of enhancement on most phases
Peripheral nodular discontinuous enhancement with 15-minute fill-in
Double duct sign
Tiger-striped enhancement like spleen
Central dot sign
updates.explanation: Intrapancreatic accessory spleen or splenosis follows spleen on imaging, including dark T1, bright T2 relative to liver, diffusion restriction, and tiger-striped arterial enhancement like the spleen. Heat-treated red blood cell or sulfur colloid nuclear medicine studies can confirm splenic tissue.

updates.question_text: Which structure is resected in a standard Whipple procedure according to the source?
options_before: Pancreatic head
Splenic hilum only
Entire colon
Both kidneys
Distal oesophagus only
options_after: Pancreatic head
Splenic hilum
Entire colon
Both kidneys
Distal oesophagus
updates.explanation: The standard Whipple procedure involves resection of the pancreatic head, duodenum, gastric antrum, and almost always the gallbladder. Reconstruction includes jejunal loop anastomoses to stomach, biliary tree, and pancreas.

updates.question_text: Regarding standard and pylorus-preserving Whipple procedures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Standard Whipple removes the whole pancreas and spleen in all cases
Standard Whipple resects pancreatic head, duodenum, gastric antrum, and usually gallbladder
Pylorus-preserving pancreatoduodenectomy leaves the stomach intact and uses duodenojejunal anastomosis
Pylorus-preserving Whipple always removes the proximal stomach
Whipple reconstruction avoids pancreatic and biliary anastomoses
options_after: Standard Whipple removes the whole pancreas and spleen in most cases
Standard Whipple resects pancreatic head, duodenum, gastric antrum, and usually gallbladder
Pylorus-preserving pancreatoduodenectomy leaves the stomach intact and uses duodenojejunal anastomosis
Pylorus-preserving Whipple characteristically removes the proximal stomach
Whipple reconstruction avoids pancreatic and biliary anastomoses
updates.explanation: The standard Whipple removes pancreatic head, duodenum, gastric antrum, and usually gallbladder, with gastrojejunal, biliary-enteric, and pancreatojejunal anastomoses. Pylorus-preserving pancreatoduodenectomy preserves the stomach and uses a proximal duodenojejunal anastomosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding pancreas transplant anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Modern exocrine drainage is always into the bladder only
It is an established therapy for severe type 1 diabetes, often with renal transplant
Arterial inflow comes from donor SMA and donor splenic artery in the source
Venous drainage is via donor portal vein and recipient SMV
The graft receives arterial inflow from the cystic artery only
options_after: Modern exocrine drainage is characteristically into the bladder
It is an established therapy for severe type 1 diabetes, often with renal transplant
Arterial inflow comes from donor SMA and donor splenic artery in the source
Venous drainage is via donor portal vein and recipient SMV
The graft receives arterial inflow from the cystic artery
updates.explanation: Pancreas transplant is used for severe type 1 diabetes, often with renal transplant. Arterial supply is dual, via donor SMA to the head and donor splenic artery to body/tail. Venous drainage is via donor portal vein and recipient SMV. Exocrine drainage is usually bowel, with older transplants using bladder drainage.

updates.question_text: Regarding pancreas transplant failure and Doppler, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute rejection is the number one cause of graft failure in the source
Arterial thrombosis is more common than venous thrombosis because the pancreas has no dual supply
Resistive indices are highly reliable in pancreas transplant because the organ has a capsule
Shrinking transplant is a buzzword for acute pancreatitis in week 1
Donor splenic vein thrombosis is the second cause and usually occurs within the first 6 weeks
options_after: Acute rejection is the number one cause of graft failure in the source
Arterial thrombosis is more common than venous thrombosis because the pancreas lacks dual supply
Resistive indices are highly reliable in pancreas transplant because the organ has a capsule
Shrinking transplant is a buzzword for acute pancreatitis in week 1
Donor splenic vein thrombosis is the second cause and usually occurs within the first 6 weeks
updates.explanation: Acute rejection is the leading cause of pancreas graft failure, followed by donor splenic vein thrombosis, usually within 6 weeks. Venous thrombosis is more common than arterial thrombosis; arterial thrombosis is less dominant because of dual Y-graft supply. RI is not useful because the pancreas lacks a capsule. Shrinking transplant suggests chronic rejection.

updates.question_text: Regarding accessory spleens, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Accessory spleens can mimic pancreatic tail masses or lymph nodes
They follow splenic enhancement across CT phases and may stripe arterially
Sulfur colloid cannot help distinguish accessory spleen from tumour
Accessory spleens cannot hypertrophy after splenectomy
They never contribute to recurrence of haematologic disease after splenectomy
options_after: Accessory spleens can mimic pancreatic tail masses or lymph nodes
They follow splenic enhancement across CT phases and may stripe arterially
Sulfur colloid cannot help distinguish accessory spleen from tumour
Accessory spleens will not hypertrophy after splenectomy
They will not contribute to recurrence of haematologic disease after splenectomy
updates.explanation: Accessory spleens are common and can mimic pancreatic tail mass or lymph node. They follow the spleen across imaging phases, including arterial striping, and sulfur colloid can help confirm splenic tissue. After splenectomy they may hypertrophy and cause recurrence of the original haematologic disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It occurs after splenic trauma with implantation and recruited blood supply
Heat-treated red blood cell or sulfur colloid studies can confirm splenic tissue
It should be suspected when multiple soft tissue masses coexist with absent or abnormal spleen and trauma history
It is always ovarian metastatic disease by definition
It cannot occur in the thorax even after diaphragmatic rupture
options_after: It occurs after splenic trauma with implantation and recruited blood supply
Heat-treated red blood cell or sulfur colloid studies can confirm splenic tissue
It should be suspected when multiple soft tissue masses coexist with absent or abnormal spleen and trauma history
It is characteristically ovarian metastatic disease by definition
It will not occur in the thorax even after diaphragmatic rupture
updates.explanation: Splenosis occurs after traumatic splenic disruption with implantation and recruited vascular supply. Nuclear medicine with heat-treated red blood cells or sulfur colloid can prove splenic tissue. Multiple soft tissue nodules with absent or abnormal spleen and trauma history should suggest splenosis; thoracic implants can occur after diaphragmatic rupture.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic sarcoidosis, Gamna-Gandy bodies, and peliosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Peliosis is defined by gas in the splenic vein
Peliosis isolated to spleen is common and never occurs with liver involvement
Sarcoidosis commonly involves the spleen, with splenomegaly often the only sign
Splenic sarcoid can appear as multiple hypodense 1-2 cm nodules on CT
Gamna-Gandy bodies are T2-dark siderotic nodules associated with portal hypertension
options_after: Peliosis is defined by gas in the splenic vein
Peliosis isolated to spleen is common and will not occur with liver involvement
Sarcoidosis commonly involves the spleen, with splenomegaly often the only sign
Splenic sarcoid can appear as multiple hypodense 1-2 cm nodules on CT
Gamna-Gandy bodies are T2-dark siderotic nodules associated with portal hypertension
updates.explanation: Sarcoidosis can involve spleen frequently, often only causing splenomegaly, but granulomatous aggregates may appear as multiple hypodense nodules. Gamna-Gandy bodies are small haemorrhagic/siderotic foci associated with portal hypertension and are T2 dark, with gradient echo being sensitive. Peliosis is multiple blood-filled cyst-like spaces, usually hepatic too; isolated splenic peliosis is very rare.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic peliosis associations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It can be associated with oral contraceptive use or anabolic steroid use in the source
It can occur in AIDS, renal transplant patients, and Hodgkin lymphoma patients
It is usually symptomatic with fixed obstructive jaundice
It is a calcified granuloma from healed histoplasmosis by definition
It cannot rupture spontaneously in the source
options_after: It can be associated with oral contraceptive use or anabolic steroid use in the source
It can occur in AIDS, renal transplant patients, and Hodgkin lymphoma patients
It is usually symptomatic with fixed obstructive jaundice
It is a calcified granuloma from healed histoplasmosis by definition
It will not rupture spontaneously in the source
updates.explanation: Peliosis is rare and consists of blood-filled cyst-like spaces in solid organs, usually liver as well as spleen. The source lists associations with oral contraceptives, anabolic steroids, AIDS, renal transplant, and Hodgkin lymphoma. It is usually asymptomatic but can rupture spontaneously.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic infections, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Histoplasmosis is the most common radiologically detected splenic infection in the source and can produce multiple round calcifications
Splenic TB can have a similar calcified appearance but is less common in the US source framing
Brucellosis granuloma is often solitary, 2 cm or larger, and may have a bullseye calcified appearance
In immunocompetent patients, splenic abscess is usually aerobic, with Salmonella classic in damaged spleen
Fungal microabscesses occur only in immunocompetent patients and never show bullseye ultrasound appearance
options_after: Histoplasmosis is the most common radiologically detected splenic infection in the source and can produce multiple round calcifications
Splenic TB can have a similar calcified appearance but is less common in the US source framing
Brucellosis granuloma is often solitary, 2 cm or larger, and may have a bullseye calcified appearance
In immunocompetent patients, splenic abscess is usually aerobic, with Salmonella classic in damaged spleen
Fungal microabscesses occur primarily in immunocompetent patients and will not show bullseye ultrasound appearance
updates.explanation: Histoplasmosis is described as the most common radiologically detected splenic infection, often with multiple round calcifications. TB can look similar but is less common in the US. Brucellosis may be solitary and larger with bullseye calcification. Immunocompetent abscesses are usually aerobic, classically Salmonella in damaged spleen, while immunocompromised patients can have fungi, TB, MAI, or PCP microabscesses, sometimes bullseye on ultrasound.

updates.question_text: Regarding small and enlarged spleen differentials, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Small spleen causes include sickle cell, post-radiation, and post-Thorotrast in the source table
Malabsorption syndromes are listed among small spleen causes
Felty syndrome consists of splenomegaly, rheumatoid arthritis, and neutropenia
Splenic vein thrombosis is listed only as a cause of small spleen
Large spleen causes include passive congestion, lymphoma, leukaemia, and Gaucher disease
options_after: Small spleen causes include sickle cell, post-radiation, and post-Thorotrast in the source table
Malabsorption syndromes are listed among small spleen causes
Felty syndrome consists of splenomegaly, rheumatoid arthritis, and neutropenia
Splenic vein thrombosis is listed primarily as a cause of small spleen
Large spleen causes include passive congestion, lymphoma, leukaemia, and Gaucher disease
updates.explanation: The source table lists small spleen causes including sickle cell, post-radiation, post-Thorotrast, and malabsorption syndromes. Enlarged spleen causes include passive congestion from heart failure, portal hypertension or splenic vein thrombosis, lymphoma, leukaemia, Gaucher disease, and Felty syndrome. Felty syndrome is splenomegaly, rheumatoid arthritis, and neutropenia.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic haemangioma, lymphangioma, and hamartoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Splenic lymphangiomas are common adult malignant tumours
Splenic haemangioma is the most common benign neoplasm of the spleen
Small splenic haemangiomas may lack the classic hepatic peripheral nodular discontinuous enhancement pattern
Hamartomas are usually PET-hot malignant lesions by definition
Splenic haemangioma never enhances
options_after: Splenic lymphangiomas are common adult malignant tumours
Splenic haemangioma is the most common benign neoplasm of the spleen
Small splenic haemangiomas may lack the classic hepatic peripheral nodular discontinuous enhancement pattern
Hamartomas are usually PET-hot malignant lesions by definition
Splenic haemangioma will not enhance
updates.explanation: Splenic haemangioma is the commonest benign splenic neoplasm and is typically smooth, well-marginated, enhances, and washes out later; the classic hepatic enhancement pattern may not occur, especially under 2 cm. Lymphangiomas are rare, often childhood/subcapsular lesions. Hamartomas are rare incidental lesions with heterogeneous enhancement and may be dense if hemosiderin is present.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic angiosarcoma and splenic metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Angiosarcoma is the most common primary splenic malignancy for academic purposes in the source
Melanoma is never associated with splenic metastasis in the source
It may appear as heterogeneity or low density in an enlarged spleen and can rupture spontaneously
Prior Thorotrast exposure is a source-listed association
Splenic metastases are rare, but breast, lung, and melanoma are listed sources
options_after: Angiosarcoma is the most common primary splenic malignancy for academic purposes in the source
Melanoma is not associated with splenic metastasis in the source
It may appear as heterogeneity or low density in an enlarged spleen and can rupture spontaneously
Prior Thorotrast exposure is a source-listed association
Splenic metastases are rare, but breast, lung, and melanoma are listed sources
updates.explanation: Primary splenic malignancy is rare; angiosarcoma is the main primary malignant entity discussed, with poor prognosis, heterogeneous/low-density enlarged spleen, necrosis, poor enhancement, and spontaneous rupture risk. Prior Thorotrast is an association. Splenic metastases are rare; breast, lung, and melanoma are listed, with melanoma the commonest primary neoplasm metastasising to spleen in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding pancreas transplant pancreatitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pancreas transplant pancreatitis is never seen before 6 months
Graft pancreatitis is common within 4 weeks after transplant and usually mild
Older bladder-drained transplants had increased pancreatitis rates in the source
Pancreatitis proves arterial thrombosis rather than rejection or venous thrombosis
Bowel drainage was the older drainage method associated with higher pancreatitis rates in the source
options_after: Pancreas transplant pancreatitis is not seen before 6 months
Graft pancreatitis is common within 4 weeks after transplant and usually mild
Older bladder-drained transplants had increased pancreatitis rates in the source
Pancreatitis proves arterial thrombosis rather than rejection or venous thrombosis
Bowel drainage was the older drainage method associated with higher pancreatitis rates in the source
updates.explanation: The source states that the graft is susceptible to pancreatitis, which is common under 4 weeks after transplant and usually mild. Increased pancreatitis rates were seen with older bladder-drained transplants.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic trauma and splenosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The spleen is the most common solid organ injured in trauma in the source
Splenic trauma can be life-threatening because the spleen contains substantial blood volume
Trauma CT should be portal venous phase rather than arterial phase for routine assessment
Splenosis can occur in the peritoneal cavity or pleura depending on diaphragm injury
Splenosis implants cannot recruit blood supply
options_after: The spleen is the most common solid organ injured in trauma in the source
Splenic trauma can be life-threatening because the spleen contains substantial blood volume
Trauma CT should be portal venous phase rather than arterial phase for routine assessment
Splenosis can occur in the peritoneal cavity or pleura depending on diaphragm injury
Splenosis implants will not recruit blood supply
updates.explanation: The spleen is the commonest solid organ injured in trauma and contains substantial blood, so injury can be life-threatening. Trauma CT is performed in portal venous phase to avoid confusing normal arterial striping with laceration. Splenosis implants recruit blood supply and usually occur in the upper abdominal peritoneal cavity, but can be pleural after diaphragmatic rupture.

updates.question_text: Regarding accessory spleen and splenosis confirmation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Sulfur colloid can help confirm accessory splenic tissue
Both accessory spleen and splenosis should have absolutely no tracer uptake
Accessory spleen always enhances differently from the spleen on all CT phases
Splenosis is excluded by prior trauma history
Heat-treated red blood cell imaging can confirm splenosis
options_after: Sulfur colloid can help confirm accessory splenic tissue
Accessory spleen and splenosis are expected to lack tracer uptake
Accessory spleen characteristically enhances differently from the spleen on most CT phases
Splenosis is excluded by prior trauma history
Heat-treated red blood cell imaging can confirm splenosis
updates.explanation: Splenic tissue can be confirmed with sulfur colloid or heat-treated red blood cell studies because accessory spleens and splenosis take up tracer like spleen. Accessory spleens follow splenic enhancement across CT phases, and splenosis is supported by trauma history.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic infection in different host states, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In immunocompetent patients, splenic abscess is usually due to aerobic organisms
Salmonella is a classic organism in damaged spleen such as trauma or sickle cell disease
In immunocompromised patients, fungi, TB, MAI, and PCP can cause multiple microabscesses
Histoplasmosis causes only non-calcified solitary lesions by definition
Fungal infection may show a bullseye appearance on ultrasound
options_after: In immunocompetent patients, splenic abscess is usually due to aerobic organisms
Salmonella is a classic organism in damaged spleen such as trauma or sickle cell disease
In immunocompromised patients, fungi, TB, MAI, and PCP can cause multiple microabscesses
Histoplasmosis causes primarily non-calcified solitary lesions by definition
Fungal infection may show a bullseye appearance on ultrasound
updates.explanation: Immunocompetent splenic abscess is usually aerobic, with Salmonella classic in an already damaged spleen. Immunocompromised patients may develop unusual infections such as fungi, TB, MAI, or PCP with multiple microabscesses, and fungal lesions can show a bullseye ultrasound appearance. Histoplasmosis commonly produces multiple round calcifications.

updates.question_text: Regarding splenic lymphoma imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Low-grade splenic lymphoma may present only with splenomegaly
High-grade lymphoma or Hodgkin disease may show discrete splenic tumour nodules
Splenic lymphoma is PET cold and T1 bright in the source
Splenic lymphoma is always an isolated primary splenic malignancy without systemic disease
Splenic lymphoma is less common than splenic angiosarcoma as a malignant splenic tumour
options_after: Low-grade splenic lymphoma may present only with splenomegaly
High-grade lymphoma or Hodgkin disease may show discrete splenic tumour nodules
Splenic lymphoma is PET cold and T1 bright in the source
Splenic lymphoma is characteristically an isolated primary splenic malignancy without systemic disease
Splenic lymphoma is less common than splenic angiosarcoma as a malignant splenic tumour
updates.explanation: Lymphoma is the most common malignant splenic tumour and is usually systemic. Low-grade disease may show only splenomegaly, while Hodgkin and high-grade lymphoma can produce discrete nodules. Imaging is low density on CT, T1 dark, and PET avid.

updates.question_text: Regarding the suspicious mass scenario in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fibrocystic change is always concordant with a spiculated high-density mass
A new mass on a screening mammogram is still recalled as BI-RADS 0 before diagnostic work-up
Spiculated irregular high-density mammographic morphology is suspicious
Suspicious ultrasound features include irregular hypoechoic mass, non-parallel orientation, posterior shadowing and echogenic halo
Discordant benign biopsy results after highly suspicious imaging should prompt surgical excision
options_after: Fibrocystic change is characteristically concordant with a spiculated high-density mass
A new mass on a screening mammogram is still recalled as BI-RADS 0 before diagnostic work-up
Spiculated irregular high-density mammographic morphology is suspicious
Suspicious ultrasound features include irregular hypoechoic mass, non-parallel orientation, posterior shadowing and echogenic halo
Discordant benign biopsy results after highly suspicious imaging should prompt surgical excision
updates.explanation: The source highlights that screening abnormalities still receive BI-RADS 0 until diagnostic work-up. A spiculated, irregular, high-density mass with suspicious ultrasound morphology is BI-RADS 5 in the scenario. Benign pathology that does not explain those findings is discordant and should lead to surgical excision.

updates.question_text: Regarding the nipple on breast imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chronic nipple inversion or retraction can be normal
Normal nipple enhancement on contrast-enhanced breast MRI should be called Paget disease
The nipple should never be positioned in profile because it obscures masses
New nipple inversion or retraction should raise concern for underlying malignancy
The areola should not change with puberty or parity
options_after: Chronic nipple inversion or retraction can be normal
Normal nipple enhancement on contrast-enhanced breast MRI should be called Paget disease
The nipple should not be positioned in profile because it obscures masses
New nipple inversion or retraction should raise concern for underlying malignancy
The areola should not change with puberty or parity
updates.explanation: The source states that chronic inversion or retraction can be normal, but new distortion should raise concern for underlying cancer. The nipple should be in profile to avoid calling it a mass. Nipple enhancement on contrast MRI can be normal and should not automatically be called Paget disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding fibroglandular tissue, danger zones and Cooper's ligaments, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The medial inferior breast and retroglandular region normally contain the densest fibroglandular tissue
The axillary extension of breast tissue is the tail of Spence
The upper outer quadrant has more fibroglandular tissue and is a common cancer location
Architectural distortion occurs only with benign cysts
Straightening or tethering of Cooper's ligaments can manifest as architectural distortion
options_after: The medial inferior breast and retroglandular region normally contain the densest fibroglandular tissue
The axillary extension of breast tissue is the tail of Spence
The upper outer quadrant has more fibroglandular tissue and is a common cancer location
Architectural distortion occurs primarily with benign cysts
Straightening or tethering of Cooper's ligaments can manifest as architectural distortion
updates.explanation: The source identifies the axillary extension as the tail of Spence and notes the upper outer quadrant as more densely populated with fibroglandular tissue. Regions with little dense tissue, such as medial/inferior and retroglandular areas, are danger zones where cancers can hide. Cooper's ligament tethering produces architectural distortion in settings including surgical scar, radial scar and invasive ductal carcinoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast blood supply and lymphatic drainage, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The internal mammary nodes receive the majority of breast lymphatic drainage
The majority of breast blood flow is via the internal mammary artery
The lateral thoracic and intercostal perforators provide no breast blood supply
Axillary drainage is irrelevant in breast cancer staging
Nearly all lymphatic drainage goes to the axilla
options_after: The internal mammary nodes receive the majority of breast lymphatic drainage
The majority of breast blood flow is via the internal mammary artery
The lateral thoracic and intercostal perforators make a negligible contribution to breast blood supply
Axillary drainage is irrelevant in breast cancer staging
Nearly all lymphatic drainage goes to the axilla
updates.explanation: The source gives most breast blood supply as internal mammary, with the remainder from lateral thoracic and intercostal perforators. It also states that nearly all lymphatic drainage goes to the axilla, with only a small remainder to internal mammary nodes. Axillary lymphatic drainage is therefore central to breast cancer spread.

updates.question_text: Regarding internal mammary nodal metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Internal mammary nodal metastases are the commonest initial nodal spread pattern
Internal mammary nodal disease is never seen once axillary disease is present
Visible internal mammary nodes on ultrasound are abnormal in the source
Internal mammary nodes drain nearly all breast lymph
Isolated internal mammary metastases are uncommon and are linked with medial cancers
options_after: Internal mammary nodal metastases are the commonest initial nodal spread pattern
Internal mammary nodal disease is not seen once axillary disease is present
Visible internal mammary nodes on ultrasound are abnormal in the source
Internal mammary nodes drain the large majority of breast lymph
Isolated internal mammary metastases are uncommon and are linked with medial cancers
updates.explanation: The source states that if internal mammary nodes are seen on ultrasound they are abnormal. Isolated metastasis there is uncommon and is associated with medial cancers. More commonly, internal mammary disease appears after axillary spread, not as the dominant initial route.

updates.question_text: Regarding the sternalis muscle, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is always bilateral and therefore never mimics a mass
It is best confirmed by biopsy rather than prior imaging
It can simulate a mass and is seen only on the CC view, not on MLO
It is a normal lymph node between pectoralis minor and major
It is a calcification distribution pattern
options_after: It is characteristically bilateral and therefore will not mimic a mass
It is best confirmed by biopsy rather than prior imaging
It can simulate a mass and is seen only on the CC view, not on MLO
It is a normal lymph node between pectoralis minor and major
It is a calcification distribution pattern
updates.explanation: The source presents sternalis as an Aunt Minnie mimic of a mass, typically unilateral and visible only on the CC view. Prior mammograms or CT can help confirm it. It is a muscle variant, not a nodal station or calcification pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast development and ectopic breast tissue, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The milk streak explains the location of normal and ectopic breast tissue
The axilla is the commonest location for ectopic breast tissue
Extra nipples cannot occur along the milk streak
Biopsy of a prepubescent breast bud can damage development
Ectopic breast tissue is most common in the kidney
options_after: The milk streak explains the location of normal and ectopic breast tissue
The axilla is the commonest location for ectopic breast tissue
Extra nipples will not occur along the milk streak
Biopsy of a prepubescent breast bud can damage development
Ectopic breast tissue is most common in the kidney
updates.explanation: The source links the milk streak to normal and ectopic breast tissue. The axilla is described as the most common site for ectopic breast tissue, with the inframammary fold second. Biopsy of a breast bud can damage breast development, so it should be avoided.

updates.question_text: Regarding lactation-related breast imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The breast becomes denser in the third trimester and lactation
Biopsy is impossible during lactation under any circumstances
Ultrasound has greater sensitivity than mammography in lactating patients in the source
Galactocele is a benign fat-containing lesion that can show a fat-fluid level
A lactating adenoma always requires mastectomy
options_after: The breast becomes denser in the third trimester and lactation
Lactation is a contraindication to breast biopsy
Ultrasound has greater sensitivity than mammography in lactating patients in the source
Galactocele is a benign fat-containing lesion that can show a fat-fluid level
A lactating adenoma characteristically requires mastectomy
updates.explanation: The source emphasises increased density in late pregnancy/lactation, making ultrasound more sensitive than mammography for a mass. Galactocele is a benign fat-containing lesion, often subareolar and sometimes showing a fat-fluid level. Biopsy can be done in lactating patients but carries milk fistula risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding MLO positioning and technical adequacy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The inframammary fold should ideally be visualised
Camel-nose positioning indicates ideal up-and-out positioning
A convex relaxed pectoralis muscle is preferred over a concave pectoralis
The MLO view contains the most breast tissue of the standard views
A concave pectoralis always proves excellent coverage
options_after: The inframammary fold should ideally be visualised
Camel-nose positioning indicates ideal up-and-out positioning
A convex relaxed pectoralis muscle is preferred over a concave pectoralis
The MLO view contains the most breast tissue of the standard views
A concave pectoralis characteristically proves excellent coverage
updates.explanation: The source describes inframammary fold visualisation and relaxed convex pectoralis as desirable. MLO contains the most breast tissue of the standard views. Camel-nose positioning is a bad sign of inadequate up-and-out positioning.

updates.question_text: Regarding LMO views and MLO trivia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: LMO replaces MLO as the standard screening view in all patients
LMO may be used in kyphosis or pectus excavatum
MLO contains less breast tissue than every other view
LMO is specifically used to characterise milk of calcium
LMO may be used to avoid a medial pacemaker or central line
options_after: LMO replaces MLO as the standard screening view in most patients
LMO may be used in kyphosis or pectus excavatum
MLO contains less breast tissue than most other views
LMO is specifically used to characterise milk of calcium
LMO may be used to avoid a medial pacemaker or central line
updates.explanation: The source gives kyphosis, pectus excavatum and avoiding a medial pacemaker or central line as reasons for an LMO view. MLO remains the standard oblique screening view and contains the most breast tissue. Magnification true lateral views, not LMO, are used for milk of calcium.

updates.question_text: Regarding choosing ML or LM for a finding seen on the CC view, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A medial finding on the screening view should be worked up with ML because all medial lesions rise
If a finding is seen only on MLO, LM is always chosen because most cancers are medial
A lateral finding on the screening view should be worked up with ML to bring it closer to the detector
ML and LM are interchangeable because receptor distance is irrelevant
LM is used for every finding favoured to be milk of calcium
options_after: A medial finding on the screening view should be worked up with ML because most medial lesions rise
If a finding is seen primarily on MLO, LM is characteristically chosen because most cancers are medial
A lateral finding on the screening view should be worked up with ML to bring it closer to the detector
ML and LM are interchangeable because receptor distance is irrelevant
LM is used for a finding favoured to be milk of calcium
updates.explanation: The source gives a practical localisation rule: if the finding is lateral on screening, use ML; if it is medial, use LM, moving the area closer to the receptor. If seen only on MLO and not CC, ML is favoured because most breast cancers are lateral. Milk of calcium is evaluated with true lateral magnification, not by a blanket LM rule.

updates.question_text: Regarding screening performance expectations and comparison studies, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Prior mammograms from about 2 years earlier should be reviewed when available
The target cancer detection range is zero cancers per 1000 mammograms
Any BI-RADS category on screening has the same positive predictive value
Prior comparison is discouraged because early change cannot be assessed
A screening BI-RADS 1 or 2 is counted as a positive screen in the source
options_after: Prior mammograms from about 2 years earlier should be reviewed when available
The target cancer detection range is zero cancers per 1000 mammograms
Any BI-RADS category on screening has the same positive predictive value
Prior comparison is discouraged because early change will not be assessed
A screening BI-RADS 1 or 2 is counted as a positive screen in the source
updates.explanation: The source recommends comparison with mammograms from 2 years earlier when available, because early changes are easier to detect. It gives an expected cancer detection range and a PPV1 benchmark rather than zero detection. BI-RADS 1 and 2 are not positive screening outcomes in that metric.

updates.question_text: Regarding MLO and CC view coverage, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The MLO view should deliberately exclude the pectoralis muscle
MLO maximises axillary and posterior tissue
The CC view should show no medial skin
CC ideally maximises posterior medial tissue
Inadequate posterior lateral or axillary-tail coverage can prompt an exaggerated lateral CC view
options_after: The MLO view should deliberately exclude the pectoralis muscle
MLO maximises axillary and posterior tissue
The CC view should fail to show medial skin
CC ideally maximises posterior medial tissue
Inadequate posterior lateral or axillary-tail coverage can prompt an exaggerated lateral CC view
updates.explanation: The source summarises MLO as maximising axillary and posterior tissue, and CC as covering posterior medial tissue. If posterior lateral or axillary-tail coverage is inadequate, an exaggerated lateral CC can be used. The pectoralis is expected on MLO, and some medial skin confirms adequate CC coverage.

updates.question_text: Regarding true lateral localisation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: True lateral views are never used for single-view findings
Medial lesions rise on true lateral views in the source's mnemonic
The source states that all cancers are medial
Tangential views replace all true lateral views
True lateral views can help triangulate lesions seen on a single view
options_after: True lateral views are not used for single-view findings
Medial lesions rise on true lateral views in the source's mnemonic
The source states that most cancers are medial
Tangential views replace most true lateral views
True lateral views can help triangulate lesions seen on a single view
updates.explanation: The source uses the mnemonic that medial lesions rise on the true lateral view. True lateral imaging helps localise findings seen on one view. It does not replace tangential views for skin findings, and the source notes that many cancers are lateral rather than all medial.

updates.question_text: Regarding blur artefact on mammography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Blur can be due to patient motion
Blur occurs only when exposure is exactly correct
Blur can occur with inadequate compression
Thick or fuzzy Cooper's ligaments can suggest blur
Skin thickening with fuzzy Cooper's ligaments should never suggest oedema
options_after: Blur can be due to patient motion
Blur occurs primarily when exposure is exactly correct
Blur can occur with inadequate compression
Thick or fuzzy Cooper's ligaments can suggest blur
Skin thickening with fuzzy Cooper's ligaments should not suggest oedema
updates.explanation: The source lists patient motion, inadequate compression and exposure problems as blur causes. Cooper's ligaments should be thin white lines; thick or fuzzy appearance suggests blur or oedema. If skin thickening is present, oedema should be considered.

updates.question_text: Regarding grid use in mammography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All mammographic views, including magnification, must use a grid
Grid lines prove that the nipple is in profile
Magnification views are performed without a grid
Grid use determines whether a lesion is medial or lateral
Grid lines are a BI-RADS malignancy descriptor
options_after: Most mammographic views, including magnification, must use a grid
Grid lines prove that the nipple is in profile
Magnification views are performed without a grid
Grid use determines whether a lesion is medial or lateral
Grid lines are a BI-RADS malignancy descriptor
updates.explanation: The source states that mammograms generally use a grid except for magnification views. Grid lines are artefacts, not malignancy descriptors, nipple-position markers or localisation tools.

updates.question_text: Regarding biopsy considerations in developing or lactating breasts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A milk fistula is impossible to infect
Biopsy of a prepubescent breast bud can damage breast development
Lactating breast biopsy is absolutely impossible under all circumstances
Prepubescent breast buds should be biopsied routinely to prove normal development
Biopsy during lactation can create a milk fistula
options_after: A milk fistula is regarded as a sterile complication
Biopsy of a prepubescent breast bud can damage breast development
Active lactation is an absolute contraindication to breast biopsy
Prepubescent breast buds should be biopsied routinely to prove normal development
Biopsy during lactation can create a milk fistula
updates.explanation: The source warns against biopsy of a prepubescent breast bud because it can affect development. Breast biopsy during lactation can be performed when needed but carries risk of a milk fistula, which can become infected. It is not an absolute impossibility, but the risk must be recognised.

updates.question_text: Regarding biopsy route selection and pathology correlation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Calcifications not seen by ultrasound are biopsied stereotactically rather than by ultrasound guidance
Concordance means the pathology result contradicts the imaging findings
Discordant benign pathology after BI-RADS 5 imaging should be accepted as final without action
A benign biopsy result that does not explain highly suspicious imaging is discordant
Ultrasound guidance is preferred even when the target cannot be seen sonographically
options_after: Calcifications not seen by ultrasound are biopsied stereotactically rather than by ultrasound guidance
Concordance means the pathology result contradicts the imaging findings
Discordant benign pathology after BI-RADS 5 imaging should be accepted as final without action
A benign biopsy result that does not explain highly suspicious imaging is discordant
Ultrasound guidance is preferred even when the target will not be seen sonographically
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes stereotactic biopsy for calcifications invisible on ultrasound from ultrasound-guided biopsy for sonographically visible masses. Concordance means pathology fits the imaging and clinical picture. Discordant benign pathology after highly suspicious imaging should prompt further action such as surgical excision.

updates.question_text: Regarding localisation of a lesion seen only on the MLO view, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A medial lesion rises on the true lateral view
A lesion seen only on MLO is always central
A lateral lesion falls on the true lateral view
The mnemonic used is that lead sinks and muffins rise
True lateral imaging cannot help localise single-view findings
options_after: A medial lesion rises on the true lateral view
A lesion seen primarily on MLO is characteristically central
A lateral lesion falls on the true lateral view
The mnemonic used is that lead sinks and muffins rise
True lateral imaging will not help localise single-view findings
updates.explanation: The source teaches the MLO-only localisation rule with the mnemonic that lateral lesions sink and medial lesions rise on the true lateral view. This is needed because projection on MLO can be counterintuitive. True lateral views are specifically used to help localise such findings.

updates.question_text: Regarding high-risk blind spots on standard mammographic views, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The axillary tail is always completely visualised on CC
Medial breast tissue seen on CC may be excluded from MLO
The inferior posterior breast is always completely included on CC
The medial breast is never seen on CC
Single-view findings are automatically artefacts
options_after: The axillary tail is characteristically completely visualised on CC
Medial breast tissue seen on CC may be excluded from MLO
The inferior posterior breast is characteristically completely included on CC
The medial breast is not seen on CC
Single-view findings are ordinarily artefacts
updates.explanation: The source warns that some regions may be visible only on one view. Medial breast tissue seen on CC may be excluded from MLO, and inferior posterior tissue on MLO may be excluded from CC. Therefore single-view findings require localisation rather than automatic dismissal.

updates.question_text: Regarding the systematic clock-face approach to mammographic localisation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The posterior nipple line is ignored because only the nipple position matters
The CC view is not used in the clock-face method
The lesion is first related to the posterior nipple line on MLO
Central versus peripheral position cannot be estimated
The distance from the posterior nipple line can be transferred to a clock-face diagram
options_after: The posterior nipple line is ignored because primarily the nipple position matters
The CC view is not used in the clock-face method
The lesion is first related to the posterior nipple line on MLO
Central versus peripheral position will not be estimated
The distance from the posterior nipple line can be transferred to a clock-face diagram
updates.explanation: The source describes first locating the lesion above or below the posterior nipple line on MLO, then drawing a parallel line through the lesion and transferring that relationship onto the clock-face model. The CC view is then used to determine medial/lateral and central/peripheral position.

updates.question_text: Regarding rolled CC views, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They can help localise a finding seen only on the CC view
A superior lesion moves in the direction of the roll
Rolled CC views are used only for lesions already visible on both views
An inferior lesion moves opposite the direction of the roll
The top of the breast is the reference point for the roll
options_after: They can help localise a finding seen only on the CC view
A superior lesion moves in the direction of the roll
Rolled CC views are used primarily for lesions already visible on both views
An inferior lesion moves opposite the direction of the roll
The top of the breast is the reference point for the roll
updates.explanation: Rolled CC views are used to infer superior versus inferior location for a finding seen only on CC. The breast is rolled around the nipple axis using the top of the breast as reference. Superior lesions move with the roll and inferior lesions move opposite the roll.

updates.question_text: Regarding BI-RADS 4, 5 and 6, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: BI-RADS 4 findings are biopsied but a benign result may be accepted if concordant
BI-RADS 4 is used only for normal screening mammograms
BI-RADS 5 means benign pathology would not be accepted as concordant
BI-RADS 6 means path-proven cancer
BI-RADS 5 has less than 2% malignancy probability
options_after: BI-RADS 4 findings are biopsied but a benign result may be accepted if concordant
BI-RADS 4 is used primarily for normal screening mammograms
BI-RADS 5 means benign pathology would not be accepted as concordant
BI-RADS 6 means path-proven cancer
BI-RADS 5 has less than 2% malignancy probability
updates.explanation: The source describes BI-RADS 4 as suspicious and requiring biopsy, but with the possibility of accepting a benign concordant result. BI-RADS 5 is highly suggestive of malignancy, so benign pathology is discordant. BI-RADS 6 is path-proven cancer.

updates.question_text: Regarding the basic BI-RADS flow in work-up, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A screening technical repeat is always BI-RADS 5
Screening mammograms can be BI-RADS 0 for suspicious findings needing diagnostic work-up
Diagnostic work-up proving a benign fat-containing lesion or cyst can return the patient to screening
BI-RADS 3 is the correct category for every symptomatic palpable mass
BI-RADS 4 and 5 findings both get biopsy
options_after: A screening technical repeat is characteristically BI-RADS 5
Screening mammograms can be BI-RADS 0 for suspicious findings needing diagnostic work-up
Diagnostic work-up proving a benign fat-containing lesion or cyst can return the patient to screening
BI-RADS 3 is the correct category for most symptomatic palpable masses
BI-RADS 4 and 5 findings both get biopsy
updates.explanation: The flow chart uses BI-RADS 0 for screening recall or technical repeat. Diagnostic work-up that proves a benign cyst or fat-containing lesion can return to screening. Suspicious BI-RADS 4 and BI-RADS 5 findings both proceed to biopsy, with different expectations about pathology concordance.

updates.question_text: Regarding mammographic mass descriptors, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A mass is a space-occupying lesion seen in two different projections
Margin is the most reliable descriptor for benign versus malignant assessment in the source
Mass density is described relative to the spleen
Mass description includes shape, margin and density
A lesion seen in one projection only is automatically a mass
options_after: A mass is a space-occupying lesion seen in two different projections
Margin is the most reliable descriptor for benign versus malignant assessment in the source
Mass density is described relative to the spleen
Mass description includes shape, margin and density
A lesion seen in one projection primarily is ordinarily a mass
updates.explanation: The source defines a mammographic mass as a space-occupying lesion seen in two projections, described by shape, margin and density relative to breast parenchyma. It highlights margin as the most reliable feature for benign-versus-malignant assessment. One-view density is an asymmetry rather than automatically a mass.

updates.question_text: Regarding mammographic asymmetry terms, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Developing asymmetry is new or larger than prior
Asymmetry is a density seen in one view that may or may not represent a mass
Global asymmetry involves a greater volume of breast tissue than the contralateral side, around a quadrant or more
Developing asymmetry is always BI-RADS 2 without work-up
Focal asymmetry is seen in two projections and may need spot compression
options_after: Developing asymmetry is new or larger than prior
Asymmetry is a density seen in one view that may or may not represent a mass
Global asymmetry involves a greater volume of breast tissue than the contralateral side, around a quadrant or more
Developing asymmetry is characteristically BI-RADS 2 without work-up
Focal asymmetry is seen in two projections and may need spot compression
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes one-view asymmetry, global asymmetry, focal asymmetry and developing asymmetry. Focal asymmetry is seen on two projections and may need spot compression, while developing asymmetry is new or larger than prior. Developing asymmetry is not automatically benign.

updates.question_text: Regarding BI-RADS ultrasound mass lexicon, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Shape includes round, oval and irregular
Orientation includes parallel and not-parallel
Ultrasound masses are described only by calcification distribution
Margin descriptors include circumscribed, indistinct, angular, microlobulated and spiculated
Echo pattern and posterior acoustic features are part of the description
options_after: Shape includes round, oval and irregular
Orientation includes parallel and not-parallel
Ultrasound masses are described primarily by calcification distribution
Margin descriptors include circumscribed, indistinct, angular, microlobulated and spiculated
Echo pattern and posterior acoustic features are part of the description
updates.explanation: The source lists ultrasound descriptors as shape, orientation, margin, echo pattern and posterior acoustic features. Shape includes round/oval/irregular, and orientation includes parallel/not-parallel. Calcification distribution is not the only descriptor for ultrasound masses.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI background parenchymal enhancement and lesion categories, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Background parenchymal enhancement is described on the first post-contrast sequence
Masses greater than 5 mm are described by shape, margin, internal enhancement and T2 signal
Foci are defined as lesions over 5 cm
Foci are less than 5 mm and do not require shape and margin description
Background enhancement has only two categories: present or absent
options_after: Background parenchymal enhancement is described on the first post-contrast sequence
Masses greater than 5 mm are described by shape, margin, internal enhancement and T2 signal
Foci are defined as lesions over 5 cm
Foci are less than 5 mm and do not require shape and margin description
Background enhancement has primarily two categories: present or absent
updates.explanation: The source states that background parenchymal enhancement is described from the first post-contrast sequence, with categories ranging from none to marked. Foci are less than 5 mm and too small for shape/margin description. Masses greater than 5 mm are described in more detail, including T2 signal.

updates.question_text: Regarding calcification categories in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All calcifications are malignant until proven otherwise
Calcifications are discussed as artefact, benign or suspicious
Artefacts cannot simulate calcifications
Benign calcifications always have segmental distribution
Suspicious calcifications are defined only by patient age
options_after: Most calcifications are malignant until proven otherwise
Calcifications are discussed as artefact, benign or suspicious
Artefacts will not simulate calcifications
Benign calcifications characteristically have segmental distribution
Suspicious calcifications are defined primarily by patient age
updates.explanation: The source frames calcifications as artefact, benign or suspicious. Artefacts can mimic calcifications, and benign versus suspicious assessment depends on morphology and distribution rather than age alone. Segmental distribution is concerning because it can follow ductal anatomy.

updates.question_text: Regarding dermal calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They occur in skin folds, cleavage or axilla
They always require stereotactic biopsy
They are typically deep ductal segmental calcifications
They may remain in the same place on CC and MLO views, producing the tattoo sign
Tangential view can help confirm dermal location
options_after: They occur in skin folds, cleavage or axilla
They characteristically require stereotactic biopsy
They are typically deep ductal segmental calcifications
They may remain in the same place on CC and MLO views, producing the tattoo sign
Tangential view can help confirm dermal location
updates.explanation: The source describes dermal calcifications in sweaty skin-fold regions and notes that they can stay in the same place on CC and MLO, the tattoo sign. Tangential view is used to confirm the dermal location. They are not by definition ductal segmental calcifications.

updates.question_text: Regarding eggshell and dystrophic calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Eggshell calcifications are linked with fat necrosis
Eggshell calcifications are the classic finding of DCIS in a single duct
Dystrophic calcifications are always tiny and uniform
Dystrophic calcifications can occur after radiation, trauma or surgery
Lucent-centred calcifications prove invasive lobular carcinoma
options_after: Eggshell calcifications are linked with fat necrosis
Eggshell calcifications are the classic finding of DCIS in a single duct
Dystrophic calcifications are characteristically tiny and uniform
Dystrophic calcifications can occur after radiation, trauma or surgery
Lucent-centred calcifications prove invasive lobular carcinoma
updates.explanation: The source links eggshell calcifications with fat necrosis and dystrophic calcifications with radiation, trauma or surgery. Dystrophic calcifications are often large and irregular. Lucent-centred morphology can be benign in these contexts rather than proof of invasive cancer.

updates.question_text: Regarding round breast calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Grouped round calcifications on a first mammogram are always BI-RADS 5
They often develop in lobules
Round calcifications are always malignant even when bilateral and symmetric
Round calcifications are managed exactly like a spiculated mass in every case
When bilateral, symmetric and scattered, they are usually benign
options_after: Grouped round calcifications on a first mammogram are characteristically BI-RADS 5
They often develop in lobules
Round calcifications are characteristically malignant even when bilateral and symmetric
Round calcifications are managed exactly like a spiculated mass in most cases
When bilateral, symmetric and scattered, they are usually benign
updates.explanation: The source explains round calcifications as often lobular and usually benign when bilateral and symmetric. If grouped, isolated or new, they may need work-up; grouped round calcifications on a baseline study can be BI-RADS 3 rather than automatically BI-RADS 5.

updates.question_text: Regarding a biopsy specimen with suspected milk of calcium but no visible calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The correct conclusion is always specimen mix-up
Milk of calcium is invisible on mammography
The target must be a metallic artefact if calcifications are absent on routine pathology
Polarised light is used only for silicone implant rupture
Milk of calcium may require polarised light to assess birefringence
options_after: The correct conclusion is characteristically specimen mix-up
Milk of calcium is invisible on mammography
The target must be a metallic artefact if calcifications are absent on routine pathology
Polarised light is used primarily for silicone implant rupture
Milk of calcium may require polarised light to assess birefringence
updates.explanation: The source notes that milk of calcium may not be seen unless assessed with polarised light for birefringence. Absence of routine visible calcifications in the specimen does not automatically mean the target was missed or that the finding was metallic artefact.

updates.question_text: Regarding BI-RADS 3 follow-up, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Some places follow BI-RADS 3 findings for 2 years at 6-month intervals
BI-RADS 3 never requires follow-up imaging
Any change during follow-up upgrades the finding to BI-RADS 4 and biopsy
A new lesion can be assigned BI-RADS 3 to avoid biopsy
BI-RADS 3 findings are treated with immediate mastectomy
options_after: Some places follow BI-RADS 3 findings for 2 years at 6-month intervals
BI-RADS 3 will not require follow-up imaging
Any change during follow-up upgrades the finding to BI-RADS 4 and biopsy
A new lesion can be assigned BI-RADS 3 to avoid biopsy
BI-RADS 3 findings are treated with immediate mastectomy
updates.explanation: The source describes BI-RADS 3 as a follow-up category, often followed for 2 years at 6-month intervals. Change during that interval upgrades the lesion to BI-RADS 4 with biopsy. BI-RADS 3 is not a way to dismiss a new lesion without follow-up.

updates.question_text: Regarding palpable lesions and BI-RADS 3 in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Every palpable lesion must be BI-RADS 5
Every palpable lesion is BI-RADS 2 if it resembles a fibroadenoma
The source says this controversy is certain to be the main exam question
The source presents palpable BI-RADS 3 use as controversial rather than a clean exam rule
Palpability eliminates the need for diagnostic work-up
options_after: Most palpable lesions must be BI-RADS 5
Most palpable lesions is BI-RADS 2 if it resembles a fibroadenoma
The source says this controversy is certain to be the main exam question
The source presents palpable BI-RADS 3 use as controversial rather than a clean exam rule
Palpability eliminates the need for diagnostic work-up
updates.explanation: The source notes the classic teaching that palpable lesions should not be BI-RADS 3, but also mentions newer data suggesting palpable fibroadenoma-like lesions can still have very low malignancy risk. It therefore frames the issue as controversial and unlikely to be tested in a forced corner.

updates.question_text: Regarding asymmetry subtypes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Global asymmetry is always BI-RADS 5 on baseline work-up
Global asymmetry is a larger volume of tissue than the contralateral side, roughly a quadrant or more
Focal asymmetry is seen in two projections and may represent a mass
Focal asymmetry is defined as tissue seen only on one view
Developing asymmetry is new or larger than prior
options_after: Global asymmetry is characteristically BI-RADS 5 on baseline work-up
Global asymmetry is a larger volume of tissue than the contralateral side, roughly a quadrant or more
Focal asymmetry is seen in two projections and may represent a mass
Focal asymmetry is defined as tissue seen primarily on one view
Developing asymmetry is new or larger than prior
updates.explanation: The source defines global asymmetry as greater volume than the contralateral side, focal asymmetry as two-view density that may be a mass, and developing asymmetry as new or increased compared with prior. A one-view density is simple asymmetry, and global asymmetry is not automatically BI-RADS 5.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI associated findings and implant description, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Associated findings can include nipple retraction, skin thickening, oedema and pectoralis invasion
Implants are described only by patient age
Pre-contrast signal and artefacts are forbidden associated findings
Implant description includes type and location
Implant luminal features such as radial folds or linguine are never described
options_after: Associated findings can include nipple retraction, skin thickening, oedema and pectoralis invasion
Implants are described primarily by patient age
Pre-contrast signal and artefacts are forbidden associated findings
Implant description includes type and location
Implant luminal features such as radial folds or linguine are not described
updates.explanation: The source allows associated findings such as nipple retraction, skin thickening, oedema, pectoralis invasion, pre-contrast signal and artefacts. Implant reporting includes type, location and luminal features. It is not reduced to patient age alone.

updates.question_text: Regarding calcification work-up views, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Tangential views cannot help confirm dermal calcifications
MLO alone is sufficient to prove all calcifications are benign
True lateral magnification helps show milk of calcium layering
Grouped new calcifications never need magnification views
Dermal calcifications are confirmed by renal angiography
options_after: Tangential views will not help confirm dermal calcifications
MLO alone is sufficient to prove most calcifications are benign
True lateral magnification helps show milk of calcium layering
Grouped new calcifications will not need magnification views
Dermal calcifications are confirmed by renal angiography
