For cyclical breast pain over age 40, no imaging is appropriate in the source
Cyclical breast pain is characteristically BI-RADS 5
updates.explanation: The source's ACR section lists no imaging as appropriate for cyclical unilateral or bilateral breast pain both under and over age 40. Other modalities are low-rated or inappropriate rather than mandatory high-level tests.

updates.question_text: Regarding ACR appropriateness for non-cyclical breast pain and stage 1 breast cancer staging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Routine metastatic imaging is indicated for every asymptomatic initial stage 1 case
Non-cyclical pain under 40 requires whole-body PET/CT as first-line
For non-cyclical pain under 40, ultrasound might be appropriate
All stage 1 breast cancer patients require brain MRI before local treatment
Newly diagnosed asymptomatic stage 1 breast cancer does not require CT, MRI or PET to rule out metastases in the source
options_after: Routine metastatic imaging is indicated for routine asymptomatic initial stage 1 case
Non-cyclical pain under 40 requires whole-body PET/CT as first-line
For non-cyclical pain under 40, ultrasound might be appropriate
Most stage 1 breast cancer patients require brain MRI before local treatment
Newly diagnosed asymptomatic stage 1 breast cancer does not require CT, MRI or PET to rule out metastases in the source
updates.explanation: The source says ultrasound might be appropriate for non-cyclical breast pain in patients under 40. It also states that in newly diagnosed asymptomatic stage 1 breast cancer, metastatic imaging such as CT, MRI or PET is not appropriate. Whole-body staging and brain MRI are not routine in this setting.

updates.question_text: Regarding asymptomatic initial stage 1 breast cancer work-up, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: No metastatic imaging is appropriate in the source
PET/CT is mandatory before treating all stage 1 cancers
Brain MRI is mandatory before treating all stage 1 cancers
Bone scan is mandatory before treating all stage 1 cancers
CT chest abdomen pelvis is rated highly appropriate for all asymptomatic stage 1 cases
options_after: No metastatic imaging is appropriate in the source
PET/CT is mandatory before treating most stage 1 cancers
Brain MRI is mandatory before treating most stage 1 cancers
Bone scan is mandatory before treating most stage 1 cancers
CT chest abdomen pelvis is rated highly appropriate for most asymptomatic stage 1 cases
updates.explanation: The source states that no imaging is appropriate to rule out metastases in newly diagnosed asymptomatic stage 1 breast cancer. CT, MRI, PET and other metastatic staging studies are not indicated by default.

updates.question_text: Regarding surveillance for local recurrence after stage 1 breast cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI is rated 9 and replaces mammography for local recurrence surveillance
Diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis is appropriate and rated 9 in the source
PET/CT is rated 9 for asymptomatic local recurrence surveillance
Ultrasound might be appropriate and is rated 5
No imaging can be used for local recurrence surveillance
options_after: MRI is rated 9 and replaces mammography for local recurrence surveillance
Diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis is appropriate and rated 9 in the source
PET/CT is rated 9 for asymptomatic local recurrence surveillance
Ultrasound might be appropriate and is rated 5
Local-recurrence surveillance relies on clinical assessment rather than imaging
updates.explanation: The source lists diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis as appropriate and highly rated for surveillance/local recurrence assessment. Ultrasound and MRI might be appropriate with lower ratings. PET/CT is not listed as the main local surveillance test in this section.

updates.question_text: Regarding ACR-style symptomatic male breast variants, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Gynecomastia or pseudogynecomastia on history and physical examination requires no imaging
Mammography is never used in men older than 25 with an indeterminate palpable finding
A classic gynecomastia history requires breast MRI as the initial test
In a man younger than 25 with an indeterminate palpable finding, ultrasound is appropriate
Male breast symptoms are worked up with screening mammography rather than diagnostic assessment
options_after: Gynecomastia or pseudogynecomastia on history and physical examination requires no imaging
Mammography is not used in men older than 25 with an indeterminate palpable finding
A classic gynecomastia history requires breast MRI as the initial test
In a man younger than 25 with an indeterminate palpable finding, ultrasound is appropriate
Male breast symptoms are worked up with screening mammography rather than diagnostic assessment
updates.explanation: The source separates classic gynecomastia from indeterminate palpable findings. Classic gynecomastia or pseudogynecomastia does not require imaging. Under the ACR-style variant, ultrasound is appropriate for an indeterminate palpable finding in a man younger than 25; after age 25, mammography becomes the appropriate investigation rather than being excluded.

updates.question_text: Regarding a physically concerning male breast presentation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: No imaging is appropriate even when there is nipple retraction or axillary adenopathy
Mammography is appropriate when the examination is highly concerning for malignancy
MRI is the first-line examination for any ulcerative male breast mass
A negative physical examination is required before imaging can be performed
Ultrasound is appropriate to assess the breast and axilla
options_after: Clinical follow-up is preferred to immediate imaging for nipple retraction or axillary adenopathy
Mammography is appropriate when the examination is highly concerning for malignancy
MRI is the first-line examination for any ulcerative male breast mass
A negative physical examination is required before imaging can be performed
Ultrasound is appropriate to assess the breast and axilla
updates.explanation: For a male patient with a highly concerning examination such as an ulcerative mass, nipple retraction or axillary nodes, the source supports diagnostic mammography and ultrasound. Ultrasound is used to assess the breast and axilla in the same staging logic as female breast cancer. The no-imaging pathway applies only to history and examination consistent with gynecomastia or pseudogynecomastia.

updates.question_text: Regarding women older than 40 with palpable findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A suspicious mammographic finding should be followed by ultrasound
A palpable finding in this age group is initially assessed with breast MRI
A palpable finding with a negative mammogram should be followed by ultrasound
A lipoma at the palpable site requires mandatory additional imaging
No imaging is appropriate for every palpable finding over age 40
options_after: A suspicious mammographic finding should be followed by ultrasound
A palpable finding in this age group is initially assessed with breast MRI
A palpable finding with a negative mammogram should be followed by ultrasound
A lipoma at the palpable site requires mandatory additional imaging
Clinical assessment without imaging is appropriate for a palpable finding in a woman over 40
updates.explanation: The source states that a woman older than 40 with a suspicious mammogram should have ultrasound, and that a palpable finding with a negative mammogram also requires ultrasound. If mammography shows a lipoma at the site of the palpable abnormality, no additional imaging is appropriate. MRI is not the first-line test in this scenario list.

updates.question_text: Regarding initial evaluation of palpable breast findings in younger women, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In women aged 30-39, mammography is inappropriate even when a palpable finding is present
In women younger than 30, PET/CT is appropriate as the initial test
In women younger than 30, ultrasound is appropriate for initial evaluation
In women aged 30-39, ultrasound is appropriate
Women aged 30-39 with a palpable finding require no imaging
options_after: In women aged 30-39, mammography is inappropriate even when a palpable finding is present
In women younger than 30, PET/CT is appropriate as the initial test
In women younger than 30, ultrasound is appropriate for initial evaluation
In women aged 30-39, ultrasound is appropriate
Women aged 30–39 with a palpable finding are managed initially without imaging
updates.explanation: The source gives ultrasound as appropriate for women younger than 30. For women aged 30-39, ultrasound is appropriate and mammography is also appropriate. PET/CT is not part of the initial palpable-breast algorithm.

updates.question_text: Regarding a woman younger than 30 with a suspicious ultrasound, which statement is correct?
options_before: No follow-up is required because of young age
Core biopsy is appropriate
MRI replaces tissue diagnosis
Screening mammography alone is sufficient
The lesion should be ignored if it is palpable
options_after: Young age is sufficient reason to omit follow-up
Core biopsy is appropriate
MRI replaces tissue diagnosis
Screening mammography alone is sufficient
The lesion should be ignored if it is palpable
updates.explanation: For a woman younger than 30 whose ultrasound is suspicious for cancer, the source states that core biopsy is appropriate. Mammography may also be appropriate, but tissue diagnosis is the key next step. Young age does not remove the need to biopsy suspicious imaging.

updates.question_text: Regarding practical ultrasound biopsy technique, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Local anaesthetic should be placed into the lesion to make sampling easier
The deeper part of a lesion can be sampled first to preserve access if bleeding obscures the target
Most masses require no image guidance once palpated
When two lesions require biopsy, the smaller lesion can be sampled first
For a solid-cystic lesion, the solid component should be biopsied
options_after: Local anaesthetic should be placed into the lesion to make sampling easier
The deeper part of a lesion can be sampled first to preserve access if bleeding obscures the target
A palpable mass is sampled without image guidance
When two lesions require biopsy, the smaller lesion can be sampled first
For a solid-cystic lesion, the solid component should be biopsied
updates.explanation: The source advises placing anaesthetic up to but not into the lesion, especially when it is small. Sampling the deeper part first may preserve access if bleeding obscures the target, and sampling the smaller of two lesions first reduces the chance that bleeding from the larger one hides it. In a mixed solid-cystic lesion, the solid component is the biopsy target.

updates.question_text: Regarding an ultrasound biopsy complicated by air obscuring the mass, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The procedure should be rescheduled if the injected air prevents visualisation of the mass
Blind biopsy is appropriate if the mass was clearly visible before the air injection
The source advises not trying to biopsy the target blind
Stereotactic biopsy is mandatory for every obscured ultrasound mass regardless of target type
The correct response is to ignore the loss of visualisation
options_after: The procedure should be rescheduled if the injected air prevents visualisation of the mass
Blind biopsy is appropriate if the mass was clearly visible before the air injection
The source advises not trying to biopsy the target blind
Stereotactic biopsy is mandatory for most obscured ultrasound masses despite variation in target type
The correct response is to ignore the loss of visualisation
updates.explanation: The source presents injected air obscuring the mass as a next-step scenario. If the lesion can no longer be seen, the procedure should be rescheduled rather than attempted blindly. The key safety principle is that breast biopsy should not proceed without visualising the target.

updates.question_text: Regarding axillary lymph node biopsy in the breast setting, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The fatty hilum is always the preferred target rather than the cortex
FNA is always preferred over core biopsy when the diagnosis is uncertain
The node cortex should be targeted
Core biopsy is preferred over FNA when the diagnosis is uncertain
A normal lymph node should be removed surgically before imaging-guided biopsy
options_after: The fatty hilum is characteristically the preferred target rather than the cortex
FNA is characteristically preferred over core biopsy when the diagnosis is uncertain
The node cortex should be targeted
Core biopsy is preferred over FNA when the diagnosis is uncertain
A normal lymph node should be removed surgically before imaging-guided biopsy
updates.explanation: When biopsying an axillary node, the source says to target the cortex. Core biopsy is preferred over FNA when the diagnosis is uncertain. If the patient has known breast cancer and the node is almost certainly metastatic, FNA is acceptable.

updates.question_text: Regarding a suspected debris-filled cyst versus hypoechoic mass, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A disappearing lesion after non-bloody aspirate should proceed directly to mastectomy
Aspiration is the first step if it is unclear whether the lesion is a debris-filled cyst or a solid mass
MRI is required before any aspiration attempt
Aspirated non-bloody fluid must always be sent for cytology
If non-bloody fluid is aspirated and the lesion disappears, no cytology is needed
options_after: A disappearing lesion after non-bloody aspirate should proceed directly to mastectomy
Aspiration is the first step if it is unclear whether the lesion is a debris-filled cyst or a solid mass
MRI is required before any aspiration attempt
Aspirated non-bloody fluid must characteristically be sent for cytology
If non-bloody fluid is aspirated and the lesion disappears, no cytology is needed
updates.explanation: The source handles this as a classic next-step scenario. If a hypoechoic mass may be a debris-filled cyst, aspiration is the first step. If non-bloody fluid is obtained and the lesion disappears, the fluid can be discarded without cytology.

updates.question_text: Regarding stereotactic breast biopsy, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is never performed under mammographic localisation
It replaces ultrasound guidance for every visible mass
It is the preferred approach for calcifications
Specimen radiography is unnecessary when sampling calcifications
It is performed without breast compression
options_after: It is not performed under mammographic localisation
It replaces ultrasound guidance for most visible masses
It is the preferred approach for calcifications
Specimen radiography is unnecessary when sampling calcifications
It is performed without breast compression
updates.explanation: The source describes stereotactic biopsy as mammographic localisation and targeting, and states that it is preferred for calcifications. The specimen is usually radiographed to confirm calcifications are present in the sampled tissue. Ultrasound remains preferred when a mass is visible on ultrasound.

updates.question_text: Regarding marker placement and post-biopsy checks, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The marker is omitted after stereotactic biopsy because calcifications are already visible
A marker should be placed after each biopsy
Clip migration can occur after placement
Clip migration is impossible because compression prevents tissue motion
A post-placement mammogram in the orthogonal view can assess clip migration
options_after: The marker is omitted after stereotactic biopsy because calcifications are already visible
A marker should be placed after each biopsy
Clip migration can occur after placement
Adequate compression prevents clinically significant clip migration
A post-placement mammogram in the orthogonal view can assess clip migration
updates.explanation: The source states that a small metal marker should be placed after each biopsy. Clip migration can occur because of the accordion effect, so a mammogram in an orthogonal view is used to assess position. The marker is not omitted simply because calcifications were the original target.

updates.question_text: Regarding MQSA communication and patient-access requirements, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lay results can be delayed indefinitely if the radiologist is busy
Facilities need a mechanism for consumer complaints
Patients can obtain original mammograms when needed
Only referring clinicians receive written mammography results
Facilities must notify patients and doctors if substandard mammograms pose a public-health risk
options_after: Lay results can be delayed indefinitely if the radiologist is busy
Facilities need a mechanism for consumer complaints
Patients can obtain original mammograms when needed
Primarily referring clinicians receive written mammography results
Facilities must notify patients and doctors if substandard mammograms pose a public-health risk
updates.explanation: The source lists a consumer complaint mechanism, access to original mammograms when needed, and notification of patients and doctors if substandard mammograms are a public-health risk. It also states that lay reports must be sent within the required time limit. Written patient communication is therefore a core MQSA point.

updates.question_text: Regarding mammography training and interpretive qualifications listed in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Three months of mammography training during residency is listed
Documented education hours are listed as 60
No formal mammography training is listed
The source table lists 240 mammograms read during the last two years of training
The requirement is framed as a PET/CT qualification requirement
options_after: Three months of mammography training during residency is listed
Documented education hours are listed as 60
Formal mammography training is not a stated requirement
The source table lists 240 mammograms read during the last two years of training
The requirement is framed as a PET/CT qualification requirement
updates.explanation: The source's MQSA table lists three months of formal training, 60 documented education hours and 240 mammograms read during the last two years of training. These are mammography-specific qualification points. PET/CT qualification is not the topic of this table.

updates.question_text: Regarding mammography phantom and system quality checks, which statement is correct?
options_before: Localization and accuracy testing is performed daily before patient examinations
Localization and accuracy testing is performed yearly only
Quality checks are unnecessary for stereotactic systems
The source says quality control is optional
The interpreting physician has no role in quality control
options_after: Localization and accuracy testing is performed daily before patient examinations
Localization and accuracy testing is performed yearly
Quality checks are unnecessary for stereotactic systems
The source says quality control is optional
The interpreting physician has negligible role in quality control
updates.explanation: The source states that a localization and accuracy test verifying system alignment and performance is performed daily before patient examinations. This is presented as a quality-control requirement. The broader MQSA section also assigns ultimate quality-control responsibility to the interpreting physician.

updates.question_text: Regarding the scenario with different posterior nipple line measurements on MLO and CC views, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The positioning discrepancy can be dismissed without recall because it proves benignity
It is treated as a technical callback
The correct assessment is BI-RADS 5
The assessment is BI-RADS 0
No callback is needed because a posterior nipple line difference proves benignity
options_after: The positioning discrepancy can be dismissed without recall because it proves benignity
It is treated as a technical callback
The correct assessment is BI-RADS 5
The assessment is BI-RADS 0
A posterior-nipple-line difference establishes benignity and avoids callback
updates.explanation: The scenario describes a baseline screening mammogram where the posterior nipple line differs substantially between views. The source labels this as a technical callback and BI-RADS 0. This is a positioning/technical adequacy issue rather than a benign or malignant final assessment.

updates.question_text: Regarding a screening mammogram showing a mass on two views, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ultrasound is never used after diagnostic mammography confirms a mass
The correct screening assessment is BI-RADS 1
The screening assessment is BI-RADS 0
Immediate chemotherapy is the next step before diagnostic workup
The next step is return for diagnostic mammography including spot compression views
options_after: Ultrasound is not used after diagnostic mammography confirms a mass
The correct screening assessment is BI-RADS 1
The screening assessment is BI-RADS 0
Immediate chemotherapy is the next step before diagnostic workup
The next step is return for diagnostic mammography including spot compression views
updates.explanation: The source scenario calls a mass seen on two views at screening BI-RADS 0. The patient returns for diagnostic mammography with spot compression views and likely ultrasound. Screening detection of a mass is not a final benign assessment.

updates.question_text: Regarding diagnostic workup after a two-view mass is confirmed, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The source proceeds to ultrasound for further characterisation
A malignant-appearing ultrasound mass is ignored if mammography already detected it
The axilla is never scanned during breast cancer workup
If ultrasound shows a clearly malignant mass, the rest of the breast and axilla are assessed for staging
The next step after diagnostic confirmation is always screening recall in one year
options_after: The source proceeds to ultrasound for further characterisation
A malignant-appearing ultrasound mass is ignored if mammography already detected it
The axilla is not scanned during breast cancer workup
If ultrasound shows a clearly malignant mass, the rest of the breast and axilla are assessed for staging
The next step after diagnostic confirmation is characteristically screening recall in one year
updates.explanation: After the diagnostic mammogram clearly shows the mass in two views, the source proceeds to ultrasound. If ultrasound shows an obviously malignant mass, the workflow includes assessing the remainder of the breast for multifocal disease and the axilla for pathological nodes. This is local staging rather than routine annual screening.

updates.question_text: Regarding a one-view screening asymmetry, which statement is correct?
options_before: A one-view finding is automatically BI-RADS 5
The source calls it BI-RADS 0 with return for spot compression views
No comparison with prior imaging is permitted
MRI is mandatory before spot compression
The finding is ignored permanently
options_after: A one-view finding is ordinarily BI-RADS 5
The source calls it BI-RADS 0 with return for spot compression views
Prior mammograms are not used for comparison
MRI is mandatory before spot compression
The finding is ignored permanently
updates.explanation: The source defines the one-view finding as an asymmetry because it is seen on the CC view only. The next step is BI-RADS 0 callback with spot compression views. It is not treated as a final malignant assessment at screening.

updates.question_text: Regarding a young male patient with a palpable subareolar density on mammography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A flame-shaped density beneath the nipple is consistent with gynecomastia
A flame-shaped subareolar density is diagnostic of inflammatory breast cancer
The source suggests looking for a clinical cause of gynecomastia after mammographic confirmation
A benign gynecomastia mammogram can explain a suspicious-appearing outside ultrasound
The source treats every gynecomastia case as BI-RADS 5
options_after: A flame-shaped density beneath the nipple is consistent with gynecomastia
A flame-shaped subareolar density is diagnostic of inflammatory breast cancer
The source suggests looking for a clinical cause of gynecomastia after mammographic confirmation
A benign gynecomastia mammogram can explain a suspicious-appearing outside ultrasound
The source treats most gynecomastia cases as BI-RADS 5
updates.explanation: In the scenario review, the mammogram shows a flame-shaped subareolar density corresponding to the palpable marker, consistent with gynecomastia. The source then looks for a reason for gynecomastia. It also emphasises that gynecomastia can look alarming on ultrasound while being benign on mammography.

updates.question_text: Regarding suspected local recurrence after lumpectomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Increasing density at the lumpectomy bed on screening prompts BI-RADS 0 recall with spot compression views
Fine pleomorphic calcifications in the lumpectomy bed are further characterised with magnification views
Prior lumpectomy makes any new density automatically BI-RADS 1
A suspicious ultrasound mass leads to assessment of the remainder of the breast and axilla
The final scenario diagnosis is local recurrence when the scar is denser with suspicious calcifications and mass
options_after: Increasing density at the lumpectomy bed on screening prompts BI-RADS 0 recall with spot compression views
Fine pleomorphic calcifications in the lumpectomy bed are further characterised with magnification views
Prior lumpectomy makes any new density ordinarily BI-RADS 1
A suspicious ultrasound mass leads to assessment of the remainder of the breast and axilla
The final scenario diagnosis is local recurrence when the scar is denser with suspicious calcifications and mass
updates.explanation: The source scenario starts with increasing density at the lumpectomy bed and recalls the patient for spot compression. Suspicious calcifications are evaluated with magnification views, and ultrasound is used to assess the mass and stage the breast and axilla. The scenario concludes with BI-RADS 5 local recurrence.

updates.question_text: Regarding procedure selection across breast targets, which statement is correct?
options_before: Stereotactic biopsy is preferred when a mass is clearly visible on ultrasound
Cyst aspiration is never diagnostic or therapeutic
The source generally favours ultrasound biopsy for masses visible on ultrasound and stereotactic biopsy for calcifications
Calcifications should be sampled with palpation-guided FNA
A residual solid mass after aspiration should be ignored
options_after: Stereotactic biopsy is preferred when a mass is clearly visible on ultrasound
Cyst aspiration is not diagnostic or therapeutic
The source generally favours ultrasound biopsy for masses visible on ultrasound and stereotactic biopsy for calcifications
Calcifications should be sampled with palpation-guided FNA
A residual solid mass after aspiration should be ignored
updates.explanation: The source's practical rule is to use ultrasound guidance when a mass is visible and stereotactic biopsy for calcifications. Cyst aspiration can clarify a debris-filled cyst scenario, but a persistent residual solid component after aspiration requires core biopsy. Calcifications require image-guided sampling rather than palpation-guided FNA.

updates.question_text: Which cardiac MRI view is highlighted as ideal for assessing left ventricular outflow tract flow such as aortic stenosis or regurgitation?
options_before: Two-chamber long-axis view
Four-chamber horizontal long-axis view
Three-chamber/apical long-axis view
Coronal localiser only
Right ventricular inflow view
options_after: Two-chamber long-axis view
Four-chamber horizontal long-axis view
Three-chamber/apical long-axis view
Coronal localiser
Right ventricular inflow view
updates.explanation: The source states that the three-chamber/apical long-axis view is advantageous because it visualises the left ventricular outflow tract and is ideal for looking at flow through this area, such as aortic regurgitation or stenosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding coronary dominance and branch names in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The conus branch supplies the posterior left ventricular wall.
Diagonals arise from the circumflex artery.
Obtuse marginals arise from the circumflex artery and supply the margin.
Co-dominance means all three coronary arteries arise from one cusp.
Co-dominance can mean PDA from RCA and posterior left ventricular branches from LCX.
options_after: The conus branch supplies the posterior left ventricular wall.
Diagonals arise from the circumflex artery.
Obtuse marginals arise from the circumflex artery and supply the margin.
Co-dominance means most three coronary arteries arise from one cusp.
Co-dominance can mean PDA from RCA and posterior left ventricular branches from LCX.
updates.explanation: The source places obtuse marginal branches on the LCX and links them to the margin. Co-dominance is described when the PDA arises from the RCA and the posterior left ventricular branches arise from the LCX. Diagonals are LAD branches, and the conus branch supplies the ventricular outflow tract.

updates.question_text: Regarding indications and risk assessment for coronary CT in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Intermediate-risk or atypical chest pain patients are an ideal group for coronary CT.
Framingham risk score of 10-20% is treated as low-risk only and not relevant.
Coronary CT can evaluate suspected aberrant coronary anatomy.
Coronary CT cannot evaluate larger stents or CABG patency.
A high Agatston score reflects calcified plaque burden and increased MACE risk.
options_after: Intermediate-risk or atypical chest pain patients are an ideal group for coronary CT.
Framingham risk score of 10-20% is treated as low-risk primarily and not relevant.
Coronary CT can evaluate suspected aberrant coronary anatomy.
Coronary CT will not evaluate larger stents or CABG patency.
A high Agatston score reflects calcified plaque burden and increased MACE risk.
updates.explanation: The source lists intermediate-risk or atypical chest pain patients, suspected anomalous coronary anatomy, larger stent/CABG patency evaluation, and pre-TAVI assessment as coronary CT uses. It defines intermediate MI risk as Framingham 10-20%. High Agatston score, especially over 160, reflects calcified plaque burden and increased major adverse cardiac event risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding mitral regurgitation and pulmonary valve disease in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute mitral regurgitation is not caused by endocarditis or papillary muscle/chordal rupture after MI.
Isolated right upper-lobe pulmonary oedema is associated with mitral regurgitation.
Subvalvular pulmonary stenosis is the most common pulmonary stenosis form.
Peripheral pulmonary stenosis is associated with Alagille syndrome.
Pulmonary stenosis is never associated with Noonan syndrome.
options_after: Acute mitral regurgitation is not caused by endocarditis or papillary muscle/chordal rupture after MI.
Isolated right upper-lobe pulmonary oedema is associated with mitral regurgitation.
Subvalvular pulmonary stenosis is the most common pulmonary stenosis form.
Peripheral pulmonary stenosis is associated with Alagille syndrome.
Pulmonary stenosis is not associated with Noonan syndrome.
updates.explanation: The source lists acute MR causes as endocarditis and papillary muscle/chordal rupture after MI, with chronic primary or secondary causes. Isolated right upper-lobe oedema is linked to MR. Pulmonary stenosis has valvular, subvalvular, and supravalvular forms, with valvular most common; it is associated with Noonan syndrome and peripheral pulmonary stenosis with Alagille syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding pulmonary regurgitation after tetralogy of Fallot repair, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pulmonary regurgitation is the primary complication discussed after TOF repair.
TOF repair can require disruption of pulmonary valve integrity to relieve RV outflow obstruction.
Cardiac MRI is used to guide timing of pulmonary valve repair.
Repair outcomes are better before severe RV dilatation.
Pulmonary regurgitation after TOF repair is assessed only by chest radiography.
options_after: Pulmonary regurgitation is the primary complication discussed after TOF repair.
TOF repair can require disruption of pulmonary valve integrity to relieve RV outflow obstruction.
Cardiac MRI is used to guide timing of pulmonary valve repair.
Repair outcomes are better before severe RV dilatation.
Pulmonary regurgitation after TOF repair is assessed primarily by chest radiography.
updates.explanation: The source describes pulmonary regurgitation as the main late complication after repaired TOF because relieving RV outflow obstruction can disrupt pulmonary valve integrity. Cardiac MRI guides timing of repair; outcomes are better before severe RV dilatation, around the threshold discussed in the text.

updates.question_text: Regarding tricuspid regurgitation and Ebstein anomaly in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Tricuspid regurgitation is the most common form of tricuspid disease.
Tricuspid regurgitation primarily causes RV hypertrophy rather than RV dilatation in the source.
The most common adult cause of tricuspid regurgitation is pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Ebstein anomaly has apical displacement of the posterior tricuspid leaflet and atrialisation of the RV.
Ebstein anomaly classically produces a tiny left atrium with no right atrial enlargement.
options_after: Tricuspid regurgitation is the most common form of tricuspid disease.
Tricuspid regurgitation primarily causes RV hypertrophy rather than RV dilatation in the source.
The most common adult cause of tricuspid regurgitation is pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Ebstein anomaly has apical displacement of the posterior tricuspid leaflet and atrialisation of the RV.
Ebstein anomaly classically produces a tiny left atrium without right atrial enlargement.
updates.explanation: The source states that tricuspid regurgitation is the most common tricuspid disease and that in adults the most common cause is pulmonary arterial hypertension. It causes RV dilatation rather than hypertrophy. Ebstein anomaly has a hypoplastic tricuspid valve with apically displaced posterior leaflet, enlarged RA, atrialised RV, and a box-shaped heart.

updates.question_text: Which valve combination should prompt consideration of rheumatic heart disease according to the source?
options_before: Pulmonic valve only
Tricuspid valve only
Pulmonic and tricuspid valves only
Mitral and aortic valves
Pulmonic valve and pulmonary artery aneurysm
options_after: Pulmonic valve
Tricuspid valve
Pulmonic and tricuspid valves
Mitral and aortic valves
Pulmonic valve and pulmonary artery aneurysm
updates.explanation: The source states that rheumatic heart disease most commonly involves the mitral and aortic valves and advises thinking of rheumatic fever when multivalve disease is present.

updates.question_text: Regarding aortic arch branching variants in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bovine arch means the left subclavian and left common carotid share a common origin.
Bovine arch means the brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid share a common origin.
Right versus left arch is defined by the arch relationship to the oesophagus only.
Right arch with aberrant left subclavian is identified by a left subclavian origin from the front of the arch.
Right arch with mirror-image branching has the left subclavian arising from the front of the arch.
options_after: Bovine arch means the left subclavian and left common carotid share a common origin.
Bovine arch means the brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid share a common origin.
Right versus left arch is defined by the arch relationship to the oesophagus.
Right arch with aberrant left subclavian is identified by a left subclavian origin from the front of the arch.
Right arch with mirror-image branching has the left subclavian arising from the front of the arch.
updates.explanation: The source defines bovine arch as common origin of the brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery. It defines right versus left arch by the relationship to the trachea. In right arch variants, mirror branching has the left subclavian arising from the front of the arch; aberrant left subclavian arises posteriorly.

Left ventricular leads should point posteriorly on the lateral view.
Left ventricular and right ventricular leads have identical lateral-view orientation in the source.
options_after: Right atrial leads often sit in the right atrial appendage and curve upward/anteriorly on the lateral view.
Right ventricular apical leads should have the tip left of the spine and anterior on the lateral view.
Left ventricular leads reach the LV through the coronary sinus and posterior/lateral cardiac vein.
Left ventricular leads should point posteriorly on the lateral view.
Left ventricular and right ventricular leads have closely comparable lateral-view orientation in the source.
updates.explanation: The source describes RA leads in the right atrial appendage, RV apical leads left of the spine and anterior on lateral view, and LV leads reaching the posterior/lateral cardiac vein through the coronary sinus. LV leads should point posteriorly, unlike RV leads.

updates.question_text: Regarding retroperitoneal spaces around the kidney, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The perirenal space contains the kidneys, proximal ureters, and adrenals
The posterior pararenal space contains the duodenum and pancreatic head
The anterior pararenal space contains only fat pads
The anterior pararenal space contains pancreas, duodenum, and ascending and descending colon
The perirenal space excludes the adrenal glands
options_after: The perirenal space contains the kidneys, proximal ureters, and adrenals
The posterior pararenal space contains the duodenum and pancreatic head
The anterior pararenal space contains primarily fat pads
The anterior pararenal space contains pancreas, duodenum, and ascending and descending colon
The perirenal space excludes the adrenal glands
updates.explanation: The perirenal space contains the kidneys, proximal ureters, and adrenals. The anterior pararenal space contains the pancreas, duodenum, and ascending and descending colon. The posterior pararenal space contains fat pads only.

updates.question_text: Regarding pathology expected in the retroperitoneal spaces, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Renal mass, renal haematoma, renal abscess, and most proximal urine leaks are perirenal space processes
Pancreatitis-related fluid collections can involve the anterior pararenal space
A duodenal haematoma is expected in the posterior pararenal space only
Pancreatic pseudocysts are listed with anterior pararenal space pathology
The source emphasises the peri-renal versus para-renal distinction as testable anatomy
options_after: Renal mass, renal haematoma, renal abscess, and most proximal urine leaks are perirenal space processes
Pancreatitis-related fluid collections can involve the anterior pararenal space
A duodenal haematoma is expected in the posterior pararenal space
Pancreatic pseudocysts are listed with anterior pararenal space pathology
The source emphasises the peri-renal versus para-renal distinction as testable anatomy
updates.explanation: The source places renal masses, renal haematoma, renal abscess, and most proximal urine leaks in the perirenal space. Pancreatitis-related collections and pseudocysts, as well as duodenal haematoma, are listed with the anterior pararenal space. It explicitly treats the perirenal/pararenal distinction as high-yield anatomy.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal renal ultrasound anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal adult renal length is expected to be less than 6 cm
Renal echogenicity should be equal to or slightly less than liver and spleen
Echogenic perirenal fat is separate from the renal sinus and never continuous with it
The normal kidney should be between 9 cm and 15 cm in length
Renal echogenicity greater than liver suggests impaired renal function
options_after: Normal adult renal length is expected to be less than 6 cm
Renal echogenicity should be equal to or slightly less than liver and spleen
Echogenic perirenal fat is separate from, rather than continuous with, the renal sinus
The normal kidney should be between 9 cm and 15 cm in length
Renal echogenicity greater than liver suggests impaired renal function
updates.explanation: The normal adult kidney should be 9-15 cm long, and renal echogenicity should be equal to or slightly less than liver and spleen. Renal echogenicity greater than liver suggests medical renal disease. Echogenic perirenal fat is continuous with the renal sinus.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal pseudomasses and variants, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A dromedary hump is a right renal bulge caused by the liver
A dromedary hump is a focal bulge of the left kidney related to the adjacent spleen
A prominent column of Bertin is hypertrophied cortical tissue between pyramids
A column of Bertin enhances and vascularises similarly to adjacent normal cortex
A prominent column of Bertin is classically between the lower pole and pelvis only
options_after: A dromedary hump is a right renal bulge caused by the liver
A dromedary hump is a focal bulge of the left kidney related to the adjacent spleen
A prominent column of Bertin is hypertrophied cortical tissue between pyramids
A column of Bertin enhances and vascularises similarly to adjacent normal cortex
A prominent column of Bertin is classically between the lower pole and pelvis
updates.explanation: A dromedary hump is a left renal contour bulge from adaptation to the adjacent spleen. A prominent column of Bertin is hypertrophied cortical tissue between pyramids, classically in the middle third, and it enhances and shows Doppler flow like adjacent cortex. These features prevent misdiagnosis as a mass.

updates.question_text: Regarding fetal lobulation versus reflux scarring, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fetal lobulation produces indentations directly over dilated and blunted calyces
Reflux scarring causes indentations between pyramids without calyceal distortion
Fetal lobulation creates renal surface indentations over the spaces between pyramids
Fetal lobulation always indicates chronic infection
Reflux scarring tends to favour the upper and lower poles with calyceal blunting
options_after: Fetal lobulation produces indentations directly over dilated and blunted calyces
Reflux scarring causes indentations between pyramids without calyceal distortion
Fetal lobulation creates renal surface indentations over the spaces between pyramids
Fetal lobulation characteristically indicates chronic infection
Reflux scarring tends to favour the upper and lower poles with calyceal blunting
updates.explanation: Persistent fetal lobulation causes surface indentations over the spaces between pyramids. Reflux scarring produces indentations over dilated or blunted calyces and tends to favour the upper and lower poles. The spatial relationship to pyramids and calyces is the key distinction.

updates.question_text: Regarding unilateral renal agenesis and associated findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is often sporadic and asymptomatic
In women, it may be associated with genital tract anomalies including unicornuate uterus
It is always caused by prior nephrectomy
In men, it excludes ipsilateral seminal vesicle abnormalities
A pancake adrenal sign supports congenital absence rather than surgical absence
options_after: It is often sporadic and asymptomatic
In women, it may be associated with genital tract anomalies including unicornuate uterus
It is characteristically caused by prior nephrectomy
In men, it excludes ipsilateral seminal vesicle abnormalities
A pancake adrenal sign supports congenital absence rather than surgical absence
updates.explanation: Unilateral renal agenesis is often sporadic and asymptomatic. The source lists associated genital anomalies, including unicornuate uterus in women and ipsilateral epididymis, vas deferens, or seminal vesicle abnormalities in men. An elongated pancake adrenal is a sign of congenital absence because the adrenal has not been moulded by an adjacent kidney.

updates.question_text: Regarding CT renal contrast phases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The corticomedullary phase occurs at approximately 25-40 seconds
The excretory phase is the most sensitive phase for detecting renal cell carcinoma
The nephrographic phase occurs at approximately 70-180 seconds
The non-contrast phase is described as contrast within the collecting system
The corticomedullary phase begins at 8 minutes only
options_after: The corticomedullary phase occurs at approximately 25-40 seconds
The excretory phase is the most sensitive phase for detecting renal cell carcinoma
The nephrographic phase occurs at approximately 70-180 seconds
The non-contrast phase is described as contrast within the collecting system
The corticomedullary phase begins at 8 minutes
updates.explanation: The source gives corticomedullary phase timing as 25-40 seconds and nephrographic phase timing as 70-180 seconds. The nephrographic phase is the most sensitive phase for detecting renal cell carcinoma. The excretory phase follows contrast excretion into the collecting system.

updates.question_text: Regarding delays or shifts in renal contrast phases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cardiac failure can delay the corticomedullary phase
Renal artery stenosis causes earlier nephrographic onset in the source
Obstruction cannot affect renal phase timing
Renal failure can prolong the corticomedullary phase
Increasing contrast infusion rate can make the nephrographic phase onset earlier
options_after: Cardiac failure can delay the corticomedullary phase
Renal artery stenosis causes earlier nephrographic onset in the source
Obstruction will not affect renal phase timing
Renal failure can prolong the corticomedullary phase
Increasing contrast infusion rate can make the nephrographic phase onset earlier
updates.explanation: The corticomedullary phase can last longer with poor renal function, renal artery stenosis, obstruction, or cardiac failure. If corticomedullary phase lasts longer, nephrographic onset is delayed. The source notes that higher contrast infusion rate can make nephrographic phase onset earlier.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal cell carcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A fatty renal mass with calcification should be treated as simple angiomyolipoma
Enhancement greater than 15 HU supports a solid enhancing renal mass
Tobacco use, VHL, chronic dialysis, and family history are listed risk factors
RCC skeletal metastases are described as always lytic in the source
Pseudoenhancement less than 10 HU is considered technical rather than true enhancement
options_after: A fatty renal mass with calcification should be treated as simple angiomyolipoma
Enhancement greater than 15 HU supports a solid enhancing renal mass
Tobacco use, VHL, chronic dialysis, and family history are listed risk factors
RCC skeletal metastases are described as characteristically lytic in the source
Pseudoenhancement less than 10 HU is considered technical rather than true enhancement
updates.explanation: The source uses enhancement greater than 15 HU as concerning for RCC and treats less than 10 HU increase as pseudoenhancement/technical limitation. Listed risk factors include tobacco use, VHL, chronic dialysis, and family history. RCC bone metastases are described as lytic. A fat-containing renal lesion with calcification should raise concern for RCC rather than classic AML.

updates.question_text: Regarding ADPKD and renal malignancy risk in the source discussion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: ADPKD itself is not described as intrinsically increasing RCC risk
Dialysis is the risk-amplifying context that can complicate the question
Every patient with ADPKD has medullary RCC by definition
ADPKD protects completely from malignancy even after dialysis
The source recommends saying ADPKD alone does not increase risk unless dialysis is specified
options_after: ADPKD itself is not described as intrinsically increasing RCC risk
Dialysis is the risk-amplifying context that can complicate the question
Most patients with ADPKD has medullary RCC by definition
ADPKD protects completely from malignancy even after dialysis
The source recommends saying ADPKD alone does not increase risk unless dialysis is specified
updates.explanation: The source states that ADPKD as a genetic syndrome does not intrinsically increase RCC risk, while dialysis does. Because many ADPKD patients eventually require dialysis, the clinical wording matters. The recommended exam approach is to answer no for ADPKD alone unless dialysis is specified.

updates.question_text: Regarding lipid-poor AML and fat-containing renal masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lipid-poor AMLs are always T2 bright in the source
All renal masses containing fat are benign AMLs regardless of calcification
About 5% of AMLs are lipid-poor
Lipid-poor AMLs are included in the T2-dark differential
Traditional fat saturation or in/out-of-phase imaging can never suggest AML
options_after: Lipid-poor AMLs are characteristically T2 bright in the source
Most renal masses containing fat are benign AMLs despite variation in calcification
About 5% of AMLs are lipid-poor
Lipid-poor AMLs are included in the T2-dark differential
Traditional fat saturation or in/out-of-phase imaging will not suggest AML
updates.explanation: The source states that about 5% of AMLs are lipid poor and that these are T2 dark. It also notes that traditional spectral fat saturation or in/out-of-phase imaging can suggest AML. Fat with calcification should raise concern for RCC, whereas fat without calcification is more likely AML.

updates.question_text: Regarding oncocytoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the second most common benign renal tumour after AML
It can show a central scar, classically on exam-style imaging
It is reliably distinguished from RCC on imaging and never requires RCC-style management
Spoke-wheel vascular pattern and PET activity hotter than surrounding cortex are described clues
Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome is associated with bilateral oncocytomas and chromophobe RCC
options_after: It is the second most common benign renal tumour after AML
It can show a central scar, classically on exam-style imaging
It is reliably distinguished from RCC on imaging and will not require RCC-style management
Spoke-wheel vascular pattern and PET activity hotter than surrounding cortex are described clues
Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome is associated with bilateral oncocytomas and chromophobe RCC
updates.explanation: Oncocytoma is the second most common benign renal tumour after AML. The source describes central scar, spoke-wheel vascular pattern, and PET activity hotter than surrounding renal cortex as exam clues. It also notes Birt-Hogg-Dube association with bilateral oncocytomas and chromophobe RCC. Imaging cannot reliably separate oncocytoma from RCC in clinical practice.

updates.question_text: Regarding primary retroperitoneal neoplasms and fat-containing masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Most primary retroperitoneal tumours are benign in the source
A deep retroperitoneal fat-containing mass should be treated with suspicion
Calcification, solid components, or failure to fat-saturate make liposarcoma more concerning
Liposarcoma is the most common primary malignant retroperitoneal tumour in adults
A giant fat-containing retroperitoneal lesion with calcification should never suggest liposarcoma
options_after: Most primary retroperitoneal tumours are benign in the source
A deep retroperitoneal fat-containing mass should be treated with suspicion
Calcification, solid components, or failure to fat-saturate make liposarcoma more concerning
Liposarcoma is the most common primary malignant retroperitoneal tumour in adults
A giant fat-containing retroperitoneal lesion with calcification should not suggest liposarcoma
updates.explanation: The source states that about 75% of primary retroperitoneal neoplasms are malignant. Liposarcoma is the most common primary malignant retroperitoneal tumour in adults. Deep fat-containing lesions are suspicious, and complexity such as calcifications, solid components, or failure to fat-saturate increases concern. A giant apparent AML with uncertain renal origin and calcification should suggest liposarcoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding Von Hippel-Lindau disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is autosomal dominant
Renal cysts occur in fewer than 5% of patients in the source
Clear cell RCC is the associated renal malignancy
The pancreas can show cysts, serous microcystic adenomas, and neuroendocrine tumours
The kidneys are characteristically small from dialysis-associated acquired cystic disease only
options_after: It is autosomal dominant
Renal cysts occur in fewer than 5% of patients in the source
Clear cell RCC is the associated renal malignancy
The pancreas can show cysts, serous microcystic adenomas, and neuroendocrine tumours
The kidneys are characteristically small from dialysis-associated acquired cystic disease
updates.explanation: VHL is described as an autosomal dominant multisystem disorder. The source lists renal cysts in 50-75% and clear cell RCC in 25-50%. Pancreatic manifestations include cysts, serous microcystic adenomas, and neuroendocrine tumours.

updates.question_text: Regarding parapelvic and peripelvic cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Parapelvic cysts originate from renal parenchyma and bulge inward
Peripelvic cysts originate from the renal sinus and can mimic hydronephrosis
A delayed pyelogram phase can help distinguish peripelvic cysts from collecting system dilatation
Parapelvic cysts are synonymous with ureteric stones
Peripelvic cysts always communicate freely with calyces
options_after: Parapelvic cysts originate from renal parenchyma and bulge inward
Peripelvic cysts originate from the renal sinus and can mimic hydronephrosis
A delayed pyelogram phase can help distinguish peripelvic cysts from collecting system dilatation
Parapelvic cysts are synonymous with ureteric stones
Peripelvic cysts characteristically communicate freely with calyces
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes para as beside and peri as around. Parapelvic cysts arise from parenchyma and bulge inward, whereas peripelvic cysts arise in the renal sinus and can mimic hydronephrosis. A delayed pyelogram/excretory phase can show whether the collecting system is actually opacified/dilated.

updates.question_text: Regarding the differential diagnosis of a striated nephrogram, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute ureteral obstruction is included in the differential
Splenic infarction is the defining cause in the source list
Acute renal vein thrombosis is included in the differential
It is never bilateral in hypotension
Infantile polycystic kidney disease is excluded from the source differential
options_after: Acute ureteral obstruction is included in the differential
Splenic infarction is the defining cause in the source list
Acute renal vein thrombosis is included in the differential
It is not bilateral in hypotension
Infantile polycystic kidney disease is excluded from the source differential
updates.explanation: The source differential for striated nephrogram includes acute ureteral obstruction, acute pyelonephritis, acute renal vein thrombosis, radiation nephritis, acute renal contusion, hypotension when bilateral, and infantile polycystic kidney when bilateral. The unifying concept is altered blood flow or oedema.

updates.question_text: Regarding infection versus infarction in wedge-shaped renal abnormalities, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In acute pyelonephritis the reduced-enhancement wedge extends from medulla to capsule
Renal infarcts classically spare the cortex, producing the cortical rim sign
The cortical rim sign is a reliable immediate finding after infarction in all cases
Pyelonephritis is distinguished by preserved thin cortical enhancement at the capsule
The cortical rim sign is described as helpful but not always present in real-world infarcts
options_after: In acute pyelonephritis the reduced-enhancement wedge extends from medulla to capsule
Renal infarcts classically spare the cortex, producing the cortical rim sign
The cortical rim sign is a reliable immediate finding after infarction in most cases
Pyelonephritis is distinguished by preserved thin cortical enhancement at the capsule
The cortical rim sign is described as helpful but not always present in real-world infarcts
updates.explanation: The source contrasts infection and infarction by extension to the capsule. In pyelonephritis, the reduced-enhancement wedge extends to the capsule. Infarct may spare the cortex via collateral capsular supply, creating a cortical rim sign, but this is not immediate and is not always present.

updates.question_text: Regarding obstructed infection, pyonephrosis, and renal abscess, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Infection in an obstructed collecting system is an emergency
Pyonephrosis is treated by delayed outpatient ultrasound only
Percutaneous nephrostomy is often indicated for infected obstruction
Renal abscess can appear as a non-enhancing central low-attenuation collection with enhancing rim
Abscesses larger than 3 cm may require drainage
options_after: Infection in an obstructed collecting system is an emergency
Pyonephrosis is treated by delayed outpatient ultrasound
Percutaneous nephrostomy is often indicated for infected obstruction
Renal abscess can appear as a non-enhancing central low-attenuation collection with enhancing rim
Abscesses larger than 3 cm may require drainage
updates.explanation: The source treats pyelonephritis with obstruction as an emergency, often requiring urgent decompression with nephrostomy. Pyonephrosis refers to infected obstructed collecting system, and ultrasound may show a fluid-fluid level. Abscess complicating pyelonephritis can have a low-attenuation non-enhancing centre with an enhancing rim, and lesions over 3 cm may need drainage.

updates.question_text: Regarding the pyelonephritis spectrum, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lobar nephronia is always a sharply marginated cystic lesion with an enhancing wall
Acute focal nephritis/lobar nephronia is excluded from the infection spectrum in the source
Renal abscess is focal but never well-defined
Abscess is described as having a well-defined cystic core with thick irregular wall
Chronic pyelonephritis can show renal scarring, atrophy, cortical thinning, and compensatory hypertrophy of residual tissue
options_after: Lobar nephronia is characteristically a sharply marginated cystic lesion with an enhancing wall
Acute focal nephritis/lobar nephronia is excluded from the infection spectrum in the source
A renal abscess is focal but characteristically ill-defined
Abscess is described as having a well-defined cystic core with thick irregular wall
Chronic pyelonephritis can show renal scarring, atrophy, cortical thinning, and compensatory hypertrophy of residual tissue
updates.explanation: Lobar nephronia or acute focal nephritis sits in the infection spectrum and is poorly defined low density, focal but not well-defined, and not yet cystic. Abscess is a more organised collection with a defined cystic core and often thick irregular wall. Chronic pyelonephritis is characterised by scarring, atrophy, cortical thinning, wedge defects, and hypertrophy of residual normal tissue.

updates.question_text: Regarding end-stage or associated calcified findings in renal tuberculosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A putty kidney refers to extensive renal calcification/autonephrectomised end-stage TB kidney
Multiple calcified mesenteric lymph nodes exclude renal TB in the right context
Calcified adrenal glands exclude TB in the source
TB never calcifies the kidney
The urinary tract is the most common extrapulmonary site of TB infection in the source
options_after: A putty kidney refers to extensive renal calcification/autonephrectomised end-stage TB kidney
Multiple calcified mesenteric lymph nodes exclude renal TB in the right context
Calcified adrenal glands exclude TB in the source
TB will not calcify the kidney
The urinary tract is the most common extrapulmonary site of TB infection in the source
updates.explanation: Extensive renal calcification replacing the kidney is the classic putty kidney, representing autonephrectomised end-stage renal TB. The source also notes that calcified mesenteric lymph nodes and calcified adrenal glands can support the diagnosis in context, so treating them as exclusions would be wrong. It states that the urinary tract is the most common extrapulmonary site of TB infection.

updates.question_text: Regarding urinary stone composition and visibility, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Calcium oxalate is the most common stone type in the source, about 75%
Struvite stones are associated with UTI and more common in women
Uric acid stones are unseen on x-ray
Indinavir stones in HIV patients are the only stones not seen on CT in the source
Cystine stones are common age-related stones with no metabolic association
options_after: Calcium oxalate is the most common stone type in the source, about 75%
Struvite stones are associated with UTI and more common in women
Uric acid stones are unseen on x-ray
Indinavir stones in HIV patients are the only stones not seen on CT in the source
Cystine stones are common age-related stones without metabolic association
updates.explanation: The source states calcium oxalate is the most common stone type at about 75%. Struvite stones are associated with UTI and are more common in women. Uric acid stones are radiographically occult on x-ray, and indinavir stones in HIV patients are highlighted as the only stones not seen on CT. Cystine stones are rare and linked to congenital metabolic disorders.

updates.question_text: Regarding causes of medullary nephrocalcinosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Distal renal tubular acidosis is excluded from the source list
RTA and hyperparathyroidism tend to produce less dense calcification than medullary sponge kidney in the source
Medullary sponge kidney is a commonly cited cause
Loop diuretics are never mentioned in children
Hyperparathyroidism is a commonly cited cause
options_after: Distal renal tubular acidosis is excluded from the source list
RTA and hyperparathyroidism tend to produce less dense calcification than medullary sponge kidney in the source
Medullary sponge kidney is a commonly cited cause
Loop diuretics are not mentioned in children
Hyperparathyroidism is a commonly cited cause
updates.explanation: The source lists hyperparathyroidism, medullary sponge kidney, loop diuretic use in children, and distal/type 1 renal tubular acidosis as causes of medullary nephrocalcinosis. It notes that RTA and hyperparathyroidism tend to cause denser calcification than medullary sponge kidney.

updates.question_text: Regarding Page kidney and nephrogram patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Page kidney is a subcapsular haematoma causing renal compression and hypertension
The classic history includes hypertension after biopsy, lithotripsy, or trauma
Delayed nephrogram means one kidney enhances less or later than the other because of pressure or obstruction
Persistent nephrogram is a unilateral finding caused specifically by subcapsular renal compression
Persistent nephrogram is diagnosed when only one kidney is compressed by subcapsular haematoma
options_after: Page kidney is a subcapsular haematoma causing renal compression and hypertension
The classic history includes hypertension after biopsy, lithotripsy, or trauma
Delayed nephrogram means one kidney enhances less or later than the other because of pressure or obstruction
Persistent nephrogram is a unilateral finding caused specifically by subcapsular renal compression
Persistent nephrogram is diagnosed when a single kidney is compressed by subcapsular haematoma
updates.explanation: Page kidney is caused by a subcapsular haematoma compressing the kidney within a tight capsule, leading to renin-angiotensin-mediated hypertension. The classic clinical setting is post-biopsy, lithotripsy, or trauma. A delayed nephrogram is unilateral/asymmetric delayed enhancement from extrinsic or intrinsic pressure, whereas persistent nephrogram is bilateral retained nephrogram in hypotension/shock or ATN.

updates.question_text: Which Doppler pattern is described for renal vein thrombosis in the source?
options_before: High-resistance venous arterialisation with normal venous flow
Brisk arterial upstroke with increased venous pulsatility only
Absent arterial flow with normal renal vein flow
Reversed arterial diastolic flow with absent venous flow
Tardus-parvus waveform in the hepatic artery
options_after: High-resistance venous arterialisation with normal venous flow
Brisk arterial upstroke with increased venous pulsatility
Absent arterial flow with normal renal vein flow
Reversed arterial diastolic flow with absent venous flow
Tardus-parvus waveform in the hepatic artery
updates.explanation: The source states that renal vein thrombosis can show reversed arterial diastolic flow and absent venous flow on Doppler. Clinical contexts include dehydration, umbilical venous catheters in neonates, and nephrotic syndrome in adults. It can mimic stone disease with flank pain, enlarged kidney, and delayed nephrogram.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal transplant obstruction and early urologic complications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: True transplant ureteric obstruction usually occurs far from the ureteral implantation site
All mild transplant hydronephrosis with normal labs proves obstruction
Stones are more common than implantation-site scarring as the usual cause of transplant obstruction in the source
Mild hydronephrosis can be normal in a transplant because of denervation and ureteric hypotonia
Post-operative oedema, scarring, and technical kinking are common causes of true obstruction
options_after: True transplant ureteric obstruction usually occurs far from the ureteral implantation site
Most mild transplant hydronephrosis with normal labs proves obstruction
Stones are more common than implantation-site scarring as the usual cause of transplant obstruction in the source
Mild hydronephrosis can be normal in a transplant because of denervation and ureteric hypotonia
Post-operative oedema, scarring, and technical kinking are common causes of true obstruction
updates.explanation: The source warns that mild hydronephrosis is common in transplanted kidneys due to denervation and reduced ureteric tone, particularly if labs are normal. True obstruction is usually at the ureteral implantation site, caused by post-operative oedema, scarring, or technical kinking. Stones can occur but are less common than those implantation-site causes.

updates.question_text: Regarding transplant haematoma, urinoma, abscess, and lymphocele timing, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Haematoma is common immediately post-operatively and often resolves spontaneously
Urinoma is classically around day 10 and may show delayed contrast/tracer leak
Lymphocele is most common within the first two hours after transplant
Abscess is described as a weeks-to-months complex hyperaemic collection
Lymphocele always shows MAG3 tracer accumulation outside the bladder
options_after: Haematoma is common immediately post-operatively and often resolves spontaneously
Urinoma is classically around day 10 and may show delayed contrast/tracer leak
Lymphocele is most common within the first two hours after transplant
Abscess is described as a weeks-to-months complex hyperaemic collection
Lymphocele characteristically shows MAG3 tracer accumulation outside the bladder
updates.explanation: Immediate post-operative haematoma is common and often resolves. Urinoma is classically around day 10 and may demonstrate delayed contrast leak or MAG3/DTPA tracer outside the bladder. Abscess is later, over weeks to months, and is complex and hyperaemic. Lymphocele usually does not accumulate urinary tracer or delayed contrast.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal transplant rejection and ATN timing, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hyperacute rejection is a late years-after-transplant process
Acute rejection is usually seen around week 1-3 and is rare in the first 3 days
Acute tubular necrosis is unrelated to ischaemia during transplant harvesting or implantation
Chronic rejection occurs only in the first 48 hours
Delayed graft function means dialysis requirement in the first week
options_after: Hyperacute rejection is a late years-after-transplant process
Acute rejection is usually seen around week 1-3 and is rare in the first 3 days
Acute tubular necrosis is unrelated to ischaemia during transplant harvesting or implantation
Chronic rejection occurs primarily in the first 48 hours
Delayed graft function means dialysis requirement in the first week
updates.explanation: Acute rejection is usually a week 1-3 problem and is uncommon in the first 3 days. Delayed graft function is defined as transplant requiring dialysis during the first week. ATN is related to ischaemia during organ retrieval and implantation, so denying that mechanism is incorrect; chronic rejection is a gradual months-to-years process.

updates.question_text: Regarding MAG3 patterns and renal transplant dysfunction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MAG3 always replaces biopsy for differentiating rejection from ATN
Acute rejection has poor flow and delayed uptake/excretion in the source table
ATN has normal to mildly delayed flow with relatively preserved uptake but poor excretion
Cyclosporin toxicity may resemble ATN but occurs later, around a month
Chronic rejection has normal flow and normal uptake in the source table
options_after: MAG3 characteristically replaces biopsy for differentiating rejection from ATN
Acute rejection has poor flow and delayed uptake/excretion in the source table
ATN has normal to mildly delayed flow with relatively preserved uptake but poor excretion
Cyclosporin toxicity may resemble ATN but occurs later, around a month
Chronic rejection has normal flow and normal uptake in the source table
updates.explanation: MAG3 can help frame rejection versus ATN, but biopsy remains the standard in many cases. Acute rejection has poor flow, delayed uptake, and poor progressive excretion. ATN shows normal to mildly delayed flow, relatively preserved uptake, and poor excretion. Calcineurin inhibitor toxicity can look similar to ATN but usually occurs later, around a month.

updates.question_text: Regarding post-biopsy transplant vascular lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pseudoaneurysm is always managed conservatively even if large or enlarging
Arteriovenous fistula can show tissue vibration artefact with high arterial velocity
Arteriovenous fistula can produce turbulent arterialised venous flow
Pseudoaneurysm can show yin-yang colour flow
Pseudoaneurysm can show to-and-fro flow at the neck
options_after: Pseudoaneurysm is characteristically managed conservatively even if large or enlarging
Arteriovenous fistula can show tissue vibration artefact with high arterial velocity
Arteriovenous fistula can produce turbulent arterialised venous flow
Pseudoaneurysm can show yin-yang colour flow
Pseudoaneurysm can show to-and-fro flow at the neck
updates.explanation: AV fistula after biopsy may show tissue vibration artefact, high arterial velocity, and pulsatile/turbulent arterialised venous flow. Pseudoaneurysm can show yin-yang colour flow in the sac and to-and-fro flow at the neck. Large or enlarging pseudoaneurysms often need intervention.

updates.question_text: Regarding focal contrast collections on delayed trauma imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Urine leaks appear hyperdense outside the collecting system on delays
Focal collections that decrease in attenuation on delays suggest active bleeding
Focal collections that decrease in attenuation on delays suggest pseudoaneurysm or AV fistula
Delayed imaging cannot distinguish urine leak from vascular contrast collections
Active bleeding is defined by decreasing attenuation on delayed images in the source
options_after: Urine leaks appear hyperdense outside the collecting system on delays
Focal collections that decrease in attenuation on delays suggest active bleeding
Focal collections that decrease in attenuation on delays suggest pseudoaneurysm or AV fistula
Delayed imaging will not distinguish urine leak from vascular contrast collections
Active bleeding is defined by decreasing attenuation on delayed images in the source
updates.explanation: Delayed imaging can show hyperdense urine outside the collecting system. Focal contrast collections that decrease in attenuation on delays suggest pseudoaneurysm or AV fistula, while those that increase in attenuation suggest active bleeding. This delayed behaviour is the key distinction.

updates.question_text: Regarding AAST renal trauma grading and management, which of the following statements are correct?
