Grade 4 includes laceration extending into the hilum/fractured kidney, segmental infarcts, or bleeding outside the perirenal space
Grade 5 includes shattered kidney, renal hilum injury, or devascularised kidney
options_after: Grade 1 is shattered kidney by definition
Grades 4 and 5 are not surgical in the source
Grades 1-3 are typically managed conservatively in the source
Grade 4 includes laceration extending into the hilum/fractured kidney, segmental infarcts, or bleeding outside the perirenal space
Grade 5 includes shattered kidney, renal hilum injury, or devascularised kidney
updates.explanation: The source table states that grades 1-3 are typically managed conservatively, whereas grades 4-5 are typically surgical. Grade 4 includes hilar extension/fractured kidney, segmental infarcts, or bleeding outside the perirenal space. Grade 5 includes shattered kidney, renal hilum injury with urine leak or main vessel injury, and devascularised kidney.

updates.question_text: Regarding ureteral stones and chronic inflammatory ureteral disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stones tend to lodge at the UPJ, UVJ, and pelvic brim
Ureteral wall calcification excludes TB and schistosomiasis
Ureteritis cystica is caused by a single congenital distal ureter outpouching
Ureteral pseudodiverticulosis is a congenital single distal ureter diverticulum only
Ureteritis cystica is typically seen with chronic infection or stones, often in diabetics with recurrent UTI
options_after: Stones tend to lodge at the UPJ, UVJ, and pelvic brim
Ureteral wall calcification excludes TB and schistosomiasis
Ureteritis cystica is caused by a single congenital distal ureter outpouching
Ureteral pseudodiverticulosis is a congenital single distal ureter diverticulum
Ureteritis cystica is typically seen with chronic infection or stones, often in diabetics with recurrent UTI
updates.explanation: The source lists the UPJ, UVJ, and pelvic brim as common stone lodging sites. Wall calcification should suggest TB or schistosomiasis rather than exclude them. Ureteritis cystica consists of many small subepithelial fluid-filled cysts from chronic inflammation, classically with stones or recurrent infection in diabetics. Ureteral pseudodiverticulosis consists of multiple small outpouchings rather than one congenital distal diverticulum.

updates.question_text: Regarding retroperitoneal fibrosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is characterised by fibro-inflammatory tissue around the aorta, IVC, iliac vessels, and often ureters
It is idiopathic about 75% of the time and is also called Ormond disease
It is associated with IgG4 disorders such as autoimmune pancreatitis and Riedel thyroiditis
It classically causes medial deviation of ureters
It is more common in women and never obstructs ureters
options_after: It is characterised by fibro-inflammatory tissue around the aorta, IVC, iliac vessels, and often ureters
It is idiopathic about 75% of the time and is also called Ormond disease
It is associated with IgG4 disorders such as autoimmune pancreatitis and Riedel thyroiditis
It classically causes medial deviation of ureters
It is more common in women and will not obstruct ureters
updates.explanation: Retroperitoneal fibrosis is fibro-inflammatory tissue surrounding major retroperitoneal vessels and often trapping/obstructing ureters. It is idiopathic in about 75%, also called Ormond disease, associated with IgG4-related disease, and classically causes medial ureteral deviation. It is more common in men.

updates.question_text: Regarding risk factors and multiplicity for upper tract TCC, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Smoking, azo dye, cyclophosphamide, aristolochic acid, stones, and HNPCC type 2 are listed risk factors
Upper tract TCC has no relationship to future bladder TCC in the source
Balkan nephropathy is linked to aristolochic acid and high renal pelvis/upper ureter TCC risk
Bladder TCC gives about a 40% chance of renal pelvis or ureteral TCC in the source
Ureteral TCC is bilateral in 80% of cases
options_after: Smoking, azo dye, cyclophosphamide, aristolochic acid, stones, and HNPCC type 2 are listed risk factors
Upper tract TCC lacks relationship to future bladder TCC in the source
Balkan nephropathy is linked to aristolochic acid and high renal pelvis/upper ureter TCC risk
Bladder TCC gives about a 40% chance of renal pelvis or ureteral TCC in the source
Ureteral TCC is bilateral in 80% of cases
updates.explanation: The source lists multiple TCC risk factors including smoking, azo dye, cyclophosphamide, aristolochic acid/Balkan nephropathy, horseshoe kidney, stones, ureteral pseudodiverticulosis, and HNPCC type 2. Upper tract TCC carries about a 40% later bladder cancer risk, while bladder TCC has about a 4% later renal pelvis or ureteral TCC risk. Ureteral TCC is bilateral in about 5%, not 80%.

updates.question_text: Regarding ureteral mass mimics and fibroepithelial polyp clues, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Squamous cell carcinoma of the ureter/bladder is associated with schistosomiasis
Haematogenous ureteral metastases are common and usually intraluminal pedunculated lesions only
Fibroepithelial polyp is benign and can mimic TCC, clot, or radiolucent stone
Fibroepithelial polyp tends to occur in younger patients than TCC
Fibroepithelial polyp is classically fixed, irregular, and older-patient disease compared with TCC
options_after: Squamous cell carcinoma of the ureter/bladder is associated with schistosomiasis
Haematogenous ureteral metastases are common and usually intraluminal pedunculated lesions
Fibroepithelial polyp is benign and can mimic TCC, clot, or radiolucent stone
Fibroepithelial polyp tends to occur in younger patients than TCC
Fibroepithelial polyp is classically fixed, irregular, and older-patient disease compared with TCC
updates.explanation: Fibroepithelial polyp is a benign filling defect in the renal pelvis or proximal ureter that can mimic TCC, clot, or radiolucent stone. The source's comparison places polyp in younger patients with smooth/oblong and mobile features, while TCC is older, irregular, and fixed. Squamous carcinoma is associated with schistosomiasis, and metastases are rare and usually periureteral/transmural.

updates.question_text: Regarding bladder anatomy and developmental conditions, which of the following statements are correct?

Prune belly syndrome triad includes abdominal wall musculature deficiency, hydroureteronephrosis, and cryptorchidism
Urachal soft tissue with calcification should raise concern for adenocarcinoma
Bladder diverticula cannot be acquired from chronic outlet obstruction in the source
Hutch diverticulum is associated with posterior urethral valves rather than reflux in the source
options_after: The bladder is an extraperitoneal structure with peritoneal cover at the dome
Prune belly syndrome triad includes abdominal wall musculature deficiency, hydroureteronephrosis, and cryptorchidism
Urachal soft tissue with calcification should raise concern for adenocarcinoma
Bladder diverticula will not be acquired from chronic outlet obstruction in the source
Hutch diverticulum is associated with posterior urethral valves rather than reflux in the source
updates.explanation: The bladder is extraperitoneal, with a peritoneal cover at the dome and transitional urothelium. Prune belly syndrome includes deficient abdominal musculature, hydroureteronephrosis, and cryptorchidism. Urachal soft tissue with calcification raises concern for midline adenocarcinoma. Hutch diverticulum is not associated with posterior urethral valves and is associated with ipsilateral reflux.

updates.question_text: Regarding urothelial carcinoma of the bladder, which of the following statements are correct?

It favours the urachal remnant at the bladder dome in the source
Papillary tumours are always high-grade and non-frond-like
Papillary tumours are frond-like and tend to be low grade
Non-papillary tumours tend to be less aggressive than papillary tumours in the source
options_after: Smoking is the classic risk factor
It favours the urachal remnant at the bladder dome in the source
Papillary tumours are characteristically high-grade and non-frond-like
Papillary tumours are frond-like and tend to be low grade
Non-papillary tumours tend to be less aggressive than papillary tumours in the source
updates.explanation: Smoking is the classic risk factor for urothelial carcinoma. The source states bladder urothelial cancer favours the base/inferior posterior bladder, papillary tumours are frond-like and tend to be low grade, and non-papillary tumours tend to be more aggressive. The false papillary statement reverses the source description.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric bladder rhabdomyosarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the most common bladder tumour in paediatric patients in the source
It may be infiltrative, making the site of origin difficult to determine
Renal pelvis filling defect is the source buzzword for bladder rhabdomyosarcoma
The botryoid variant produces grape-like polypoid masses
It never metastasises to lung, bone, or nodes in the source
options_after: It is the most common bladder tumour in paediatric patients in the source
It may be infiltrative, making the site of origin difficult to determine
Renal pelvis filling defect is the source buzzword for bladder rhabdomyosarcoma
The botryoid variant produces grape-like polypoid masses
It will not metastasise to lung, bone, or nodes in the source
updates.explanation: Rhabdomyosarcoma is the key paediatric bladder tumour in the source and is often infiltrative. Paratesticular mass, not renal pelvis filling defect, is the associated buzzword. The botryoid variant has grape-like polypoid masses, and the tumour can metastasise to lungs, bones, and nodes.

updates.question_text: Regarding urinary diversion after radical cystectomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A piece of bowel is used as a conduit or reservoir and the ureters are attached to it
Adynamic ileus is the most common early complication and occurs in almost 25% in the source
Small bowel obstruction is excluded because bowel is never used in urinary diversion
Urinary leakage usually occurs at the ureteral-reservoir anastomosis
Fistula is commonest in patients with no prior pelvic radiation
options_after: A piece of bowel is used as a conduit or reservoir and the ureters are attached to it
Adynamic ileus is the most common early complication and occurs in almost 25% in the source
Small bowel obstruction is excluded because bowel is not used in urinary diversion
Urinary leakage usually occurs at the ureteral-reservoir anastomosis
Fistula is commonest in patients without prior pelvic radiation
updates.explanation: Urinary diversion uses bowel to form a conduit or reservoir, with ureters attached. Adynamic ileus is the commonest early complication, and urinary leakage typically occurs at the ureteral-reservoir anastomosis. Small bowel obstruction can occur near the enteroenteric anastomosis; fistula is uncommon and more likely after pelvic radiation.

updates.question_text: Regarding late complications of urinary diversion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Tumour recurrence cannot present as a soft tissue mass at ureter, bladder, or pelvic lymph node
Urinary infection can be early or late
Stones should be assessed on non-contrast imaging
Parastomal herniation occurs in about 15% of ileal conduits in the source
Left-sided urinary stricture risk is higher because of angulation through or under the mesentery
options_after: Tumour recurrence will not present as a soft tissue mass at ureter, bladder, or pelvic lymph node
Urinary infection can be early or late
Stones should be assessed on non-contrast imaging
Parastomal herniation occurs in about 15% of ileal conduits in the source
Left-sided urinary stricture risk is higher because of angulation through or under the mesentery
updates.explanation: Late diversion complications include urinary infection, stones, parastomal herniation, urinary stricture, and tumour recurrence. Non-contrast imaging helps find stones. Parastomal hernia occurs in about 15% of ileal conduits, and the left ureter is higher risk for stricture because of its course/angulation through or under the mesentery.

updates.question_text: Regarding bladder stasis conditions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Neurogenic bladder is never small/contracted or large/atonic in the source
Pine cone bladder is a classic urachal adenocarcinoma descriptor in the source
Acquired bladder diverticula exclude outlet obstruction
Acquired bladder diverticula are most common at the UVJ
Pear-shaped bladder suggests renal artery stenosis only
options_after: Neurogenic bladder is not small/contracted or large/atonic in the source
Pine cone bladder is a classic urachal adenocarcinoma descriptor in the source
Acquired bladder diverticula exclude outlet obstruction
Acquired bladder diverticula are most common at the UVJ
Pear-shaped bladder suggests renal artery stenosis only
updates.explanation: Neurogenic bladder can be contracted or atonic/large, and pine cone bladder is the source descriptor for neurogenic bladder. Acquired diverticula are mainly related to outlet obstruction and are most common at the UVJ. Pear-shaped bladder suggests pelvic lipomatosis or haematoma, not renal artery stenosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding bladder stones and pear-shaped bladder, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bladder stones cannot descend from the kidney into the bladder
Bladder stones may form in the bladder because of stasis from outlet obstruction or neurogenic bladder
Bladder stones can cause chronic irritation and are risk factors for TCC and SCC
Pear-shaped bladder is specific for urachal carcinoma
Pear-shaped bladder suggests pelvic lipomatosis or haematoma
options_after: Bladder stones will not descend from the kidney into the bladder
Bladder stones may form in the bladder because of stasis from outlet obstruction or neurogenic bladder
Bladder stones can cause chronic irritation and are risk factors for TCC and SCC
Pear-shaped bladder is specific for urachal carcinoma
Pear-shaped bladder suggests pelvic lipomatosis or haematoma
updates.explanation: Bladder stones may either drop from the kidney or form in the bladder secondary to stasis, particularly outlet obstruction or neurogenic bladder. Chronic irritation from stones is a risk factor for both urothelial and squamous carcinoma. Pear-shaped bladder suggests pelvic lipomatosis or haematoma, not urachal carcinoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding extraperitoneal bladder rupture, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is less common than intraperitoneal rupture
It is almost always associated with pelvic fracture
Molar tooth sign refers to contrast in the prevesical space of Retzius around the bladder
It always requires surgery because bowel loops are outlined
It requires surgical repair because contrast outlines bowel loops
options_after: It is less common than intraperitoneal rupture
It is almost always associated with pelvic fracture
Molar tooth sign refers to contrast in the prevesical space of Retzius around the bladder
It characteristically requires surgery because bowel loops are outlined
It requires surgical repair because contrast outlines bowel loops
updates.explanation: Extraperitoneal rupture is the more common type, around 80-90%, and is almost always associated with pelvic fracture. The molar tooth sign is contrast surrounding the bladder in the prevesical space of Retzius. It is usually managed medically, whereas intraperitoneal rupture requires surgery and outlines bowel loops.

updates.question_text: Regarding pseudoazotaemia after bladder rupture, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Creatinine in urine can be absorbed across the peritoneal lining
Serum creatinine can appear markedly elevated despite normal kidneys
The mechanism requires extraperitoneal urinary leak only in the source explanation
Pseudoazotaemia proves acute intrinsic renal cortical necrosis
The kidneys themselves are normal
options_after: Creatinine in urine can be absorbed across the peritoneal lining
Serum creatinine can appear markedly elevated despite normal kidneys
The mechanism requires extraperitoneal urinary leak primarily in the source explanation
Pseudoazotaemia proves acute intrinsic renal cortical necrosis
The kidneys themselves are normal
updates.explanation: Pseudoazotaemia occurs when urinary creatinine is absorbed across the peritoneal lining after bladder rupture, causing a falsely alarming serum creatinine that mimics renal failure. The kidneys themselves are normal. It does not prove intrinsic renal cortical necrosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding male urethral imaging technique and landmarks, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The anterior urethra fills only on antegrade voiding urethrography
The posterior urethra fills on antegrade/voiding urethrography
Dynamic urethrography is the term for CT cystography of the bladder
The proximal bulbar urethra has a cone shape tapering into the membranous urethra
A line connecting the inferior margins of the obturator foramina can help identify the bulbar-membranous junction if the urethra is not opacified
options_after: The anterior urethra fills primarily on antegrade voiding urethrography
The posterior urethra fills on antegrade/voiding urethrography
Dynamic urethrography is the term for CT cystography of the bladder
The proximal bulbar urethra has a cone shape tapering into the membranous urethra
A line connecting the inferior margins of the obturator foramina can help identify the bulbar-membranous junction if the urethra is not opacified
updates.explanation: Retrograde urethrography fills the anterior urethra, and voiding/antegrade urethrography fills the posterior urethra; combined use is dynamic urethrography. The bulbar-membranous junction can be identified by the cone-shaped proximal bulbar urethra tapering into membranous urethra or by drawing a line along the inferior obturator margins when the urethra is not opacified.

updates.question_text: Regarding the final GU cancer summary, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Clear cell RCC enhances equal to cortex on corticomedullary phase and is associated with VHL
Papillary RCC enhances equal to cortex on corticomedullary phase and is unrelated to transplant kidney malignancy
Medullary RCC is associated with sickle cell trait
Bladder urothelial carcinoma is never multicentric and has no upper tract relationship in the source
Bladder can be isolated, but ureteral cancer usually also has bladder cancer in the source summary
options_after: Clear cell RCC enhances equal to cortex on corticomedullary phase and is associated with VHL
Papillary RCC enhances equal to cortex on corticomedullary phase and is unrelated to transplant kidney malignancy
Medullary RCC is associated with sickle cell trait
Bladder urothelial carcinoma is not multicentric and lacks upper tract relationship in the source
Bladder can be isolated, but ureteral cancer usually also has bladder cancer in the source summary
updates.explanation: The summary reiterates that clear cell RCC enhances like cortex and is associated with VHL, while papillary RCC enhances less than cortex and is associated with hereditary papillary RCC and transplant kidney. Medullary RCC is associated with sickle cell trait. Bladder urothelial carcinoma may be multicentric, and the source emphasises that bladder cancer can be isolated whereas ureteral cancer usually also has bladder cancer.

updates.question_text: Regarding clinical importance of a rudimentary horn in a unicornuate uterus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A rudimentary horn should be ignored if it is non-communicating because it cannot contain endometrium
Rudimentary horn endometrium protects against miscarriage

Pregnancy within a rudimentary horn can rupture and cause life-threatening bleeding
Non-communicating cavitary horns are particularly problematic if pregnancy occurs
options_after: A rudimentary horn should be ignored if it is non-communicating because it will not contain endometrium
Rudimentary horn endometrium protects against miscarriage
Endometrium within a rudimentary horn can cause dysmenorrhoea or haematometra
Pregnancy within a rudimentary horn can rupture and cause life-threatening bleeding
Non-communicating cavitary horns are particularly problematic if pregnancy occurs
updates.explanation: The text emphasises looking for a rudimentary horn because it may contain endometrium. Endometrial tissue in a rudimentary horn can cause dysmenorrhoea, haematometra, haematosalpinx, miscarriage, and rudimentary horn pregnancy. Rupture is especially highlighted for non-communicating horn pregnancy. The source does not describe the horn as harmless or protective.

updates.question_text: Regarding HSG filling defects, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Irregular linear filling defects suggest synechiae or intrauterine adhesions
Mobile transient round filling defects are diagnostic of endometrial carcinoma
Bubbles are fixed and should not change position during HSG
Round or oval filling defects are only caused by salpingitis isthmica nodosa
Polyps or fibroids can produce round or oval filling defects
options_after: Irregular linear filling defects suggest synechiae or intrauterine adhesions
Mobile transient round filling defects are diagnostic of endometrial carcinoma
Bubbles are fixed and should not change position during HSG
Round or oval filling defects are primarily caused by salpingitis isthmica nodosa
Polyps or fibroids can produce round or oval filling defects
updates.explanation: The source links irregular, often linear filling defects arising from a uterine wall to synechiae, scarring, or intrauterine adhesions. It also states that endometrial polyps and fibroids can produce round or oval filling defects, especially during early filling. Bubbles may also appear rounded but should be mobile and transient. These findings are not the described HSG pattern of endometrial carcinoma or salpingitis isthmica nodosa.

updates.question_text: Regarding intrauterine adhesions and Asherman syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Prior dilation and curettage is the most common cause described in the source
It is primarily a congenital fusion anomaly of the Müllerian ducts
HSG should always show a smoothly enlarged endometrial canal with free filling
MRI may show multiple T2-dark bands
It is typically defined by a T-shaped uterine cavity after diethylstilbestrol exposure
options_after: Prior dilation and curettage is the most common cause described in the source
It is primarily a congenital fusion anomaly of the Müllerian ducts
HSG should characteristically show a smoothly enlarged endometrial canal with free filling
MRI may show multiple T2-dark bands
It is typically defined by a T-shaped uterine cavity after diethylstilbestrol exposure
updates.explanation: The source describes intrauterine adhesions as scarring secondary to injury, with prior dilation and curettage as the most common cause. HSG may show non-filling of the uterus, multiple irregular linear filling defects, a lacunar pattern, or failure to distend the canal, and MRI may show T2-dark bands. This is an acquired process, not a Müllerian fusion anomaly or the diethylstilbestrol-related T-shaped uterus.

updates.question_text: Regarding endometritis in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is described within the pelvic inflammatory disease spectrum
It may occur 2–5 days after delivery, especially after prolonged labour or premature rupture
Postpartum gas in the endometrial cavity is specific for endometritis
It cannot progress to pyometrium
Imaging may show fluid and a thickened endometrial cavity
options_after: It is described within the pelvic inflammatory disease spectrum
It may occur 2–5 days after delivery, especially after prolonged labour or premature rupture
Postpartum gas in the endometrial cavity is specific for endometritis
It will not progress to pyometrium
Imaging may show fluid and a thickened endometrial cavity
updates.explanation: The text places endometritis in the PID spectrum and highlights the postpartum setting, particularly 2–5 days after delivery with prolonged labour or premature rupture. Imaging may show fluid and thickening of the endometrial cavity. Gas can be present but is not specific in a postpartum patient. The source states that progression to pyometrium can occur.

updates.question_text: Regarding pelvic floor anatomy and MRI assessment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The anterior compartment contains the bladder and urethra
The middle compartment contains the vagina, cervix, uterus, and adnexa
The posterior compartment contains the anus and rectum
The endopelvic fascia is the main support for the posterior compartment only
The levator ani includes puborectalis, pubococcygeus, and iliococcygeus components
options_after: The anterior compartment contains the bladder and urethra
The middle compartment contains the vagina, cervix, uterus, and adnexa
The posterior compartment contains the anus and rectum
The endopelvic fascia is the main support for the posterior compartment
The levator ani includes puborectalis, pubococcygeus, and iliococcygeus components
updates.explanation: The source divides pelvic floor support into anterior, middle, and posterior compartments containing bladder and urethra; vagina, cervix, uterus, and adnexa; and anus and rectum respectively. The levator ani is listed as puborectalis, pubococcygeus, and iliococcygeus. Endopelvic fascia is described as the main support for the anterior and middle compartments, not posterior support alone.

updates.question_text: Regarding typical imaging appearances of fibroids, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: On ultrasound, they are usually hypoechoic and may show peripheral flow and shadowing
On CT, they always contain macroscopic fat
On MRI, typical fibroids are T1 dark to intermediate and T2 dark with variable enhancement
Higher T2 signal fibroids are described as responding worse to interventional treatment
Peripheral or popcorn calcification excludes leiomyoma
options_after: On ultrasound, they are usually hypoechoic and may show peripheral flow and shadowing
On CT, they characteristically contain macroscopic fat
On MRI, typical fibroids are T1 dark to intermediate and T2 dark with variable enhancement
Higher T2 signal fibroids are described as responding worse to interventional treatment
Peripheral or popcorn calcification excludes leiomyoma
updates.explanation: The source states that fibroids are usually hypoechoic on ultrasound, often with peripheral blood flow and shadowing, and classically T1 dark to intermediate, T2 dark, with variable enhancement on MRI. CT may show peripheral or popcorn calcification. A fat-containing uterine fibroid variant is lipoleiomyoma, but ordinary fibroids do not all contain macroscopic fat. Higher T2 signal is described as responding better to interventional treatment.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal endometrial thickness and postmenopausal bleeding, which statement is correct?
options_before: Premenopausal endometrial thickness greater than 8 mm is always abnormal
Fluid in the endometrial canal should be included when measuring the endometrial stripe
A postmenopausal endometrium less than 5 mm usually proceeds directly to PET CT
The secretory endometrium is trilaminar and thinner than the proliferative endometrium
Focal or generalised postmenopausal endometrial thickening greater than about 4–5 mm should be sampled
options_after: Premenopausal endometrial thickness greater than 8 mm is characteristically abnormal
Fluid in the endometrial canal should be included when measuring the endometrial stripe
A postmenopausal endometrium less than 5 mm usually proceeds directly to PET CT
The secretory endometrium is trilaminar and thinner than the proliferative endometrium
Focal or generalised postmenopausal endometrial thickening greater than about 4–5 mm should be sampled
updates.explanation: The source states that focal or generalised postmenopausal thickening greater than about 4–5 mm should undergo sampling. Premenopausal endometrium can be much thicker, up to around 20 mm in the source, and the stripe is measured without including canal fluid. Proliferative endometrium is trilaminar and roughly 4–12 mm, while the secretory endometrium is homogeneous hyperechoic and can reach around 16 mm. A thin postmenopausal endometrium is more likely atrophy.

updates.question_text: Regarding biopsy decisions in tamoxifen-related endometrial change, which statement is correct?
options_before: All asymptomatic postmenopausal patients taking tamoxifen require routine ultrasound screening
Tamoxifen blocks oestrogen effects in the pelvis and therefore thins the endometrium
A postmenopausal patient on tamoxifen should be biopsied if she has bleeding
Endometrial thickness over 4 mm in an asymptomatic tamoxifen patient always mandates biopsy
Tamoxifen has no association with endometrial polyps
options_after: Most asymptomatic postmenopausal patients taking tamoxifen require routine ultrasound screening
Tamoxifen blocks oestrogen effects in the pelvis and therefore thins the endometrium
A postmenopausal patient on tamoxifen should be biopsied if she has bleeding
Endometrial thickness over 4 mm in an asymptomatic tamoxifen patient characteristically mandates biopsy
Tamoxifen lacks association with endometrial polyps
updates.explanation: The source states that postmenopausal bleeding in a tamoxifen patient is the indication for biopsy. It also says there is no routine screening and no role for ultrasound if the patient is asymptomatic. Tamoxifen acts like oestrogen in the pelvis, can thicken the endometrium, and is associated with subendometrial cysts and endometrial polyps. A thick endometrium alone in an asymptomatic tamoxifen patient is not treated like ordinary postmenopausal thickening in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding tamoxifen and endometrial polyps, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Tamoxifen is used in breast cancer and acts like oestrogen in the pelvis
Tamoxifen reduces the risk of endometrial cancer to zero
Tamoxifen-related endometrial tissue should remain thinner than 4 mm in nearly all patients after 5 years
Tamoxifen can produce subendometrial cysts and endometrial polyps
Sonohysterography can outline a bright intracavitary polyp with fluid
options_after: Tamoxifen is used in breast cancer and acts like oestrogen in the pelvis
Tamoxifen reduces the risk of endometrial cancer to zero
Tamoxifen-related endometrial tissue should remain thinner than 4 mm in the large majority of patients after 5 years
Tamoxifen can produce subendometrial cysts and endometrial polyps
Sonohysterography can outline a bright intracavitary polyp with fluid
updates.explanation: Tamoxifen is described as a selective oestrogen receptor modulator used in breast cancer, with pelvic oestrogenic effects. The source links it to a marginally increased endometrial cancer risk, subendometrial cysts, and endometrial polyps. It also notes that the endometrium can be thick on tamoxifen and cites thick measurements after prolonged use. Endometrial polyps are typically bright focal lesions and can be shown as intracavitary masses outlined during sonohysterography.

updates.question_text: Regarding endometrial fluid and vaginal solid masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Endometrial fluid in postmenopausal women is always physiologic ovulatory fluid
A solid vaginal mass is usually assumed benign if it enhances
Endometrial fluid in postmenopausal women suggests cervical stenosis or an obstructing mass
Solid vaginal masses can be secondary to cervical or uterine carcinoma protruding into the vagina
Primary vaginal solid tumours include clear cell adenocarcinoma and rhabdomyosarcoma
options_after: Endometrial fluid in postmenopausal women is characteristically physiologic ovulatory fluid
A solid vaginal mass is usually assumed benign if it enhances
Endometrial fluid in postmenopausal women suggests cervical stenosis or an obstructing mass
Solid vaginal masses can be secondary to cervical or uterine carcinoma protruding into the vagina
Primary vaginal solid tumours include clear cell adenocarcinoma and rhabdomyosarcoma
updates.explanation: The source states that endometrial fluid is common in premenopausal women but in postmenopausal women suggests cervical stenosis or an obstructing mass, usually stenosis. It also warns that a solid vaginal mass is usually concerning and may be secondary to cervical or uterine carcinoma protruding into the vagina. Primary examples listed include clear cell adenocarcinoma and rhabdomyosarcoma. Enhancement alone is not used as a benign discriminator in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding vaginal metastasis patterns described in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A metastasis to the anterior wall upper third of the vagina is usually from the upper genital tract
A metastasis to the anterior wall upper third of the vagina is usually from colorectal cancer
A metastasis to the posterior wall lower third of the vagina is usually from the gastrointestinal tract
Vaginal metastasis location is described as having no relationship to likely primary site
Posterior lower-third vaginal metastases are usually from the thyroid
options_after: A metastasis to the anterior wall upper third of the vagina is usually from the upper genital tract
A metastasis to the anterior wall upper third of the vagina is usually from colorectal cancer
A metastasis to the posterior wall lower third of the vagina is usually from the gastrointestinal tract
The location of a vaginal metastasis is independent of the likely primary site
Posterior lower-third vaginal metastases are usually from the thyroid
updates.explanation: The source gives two high-yield location rules for vaginal metastases. An anterior wall upper-third vaginal metastasis is usually from the upper genital tract. A posterior wall lower-third vaginal metastasis is usually from the gastrointestinal tract. The text does not support random primary-site assignment or thyroid as the usual source.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian size and normal follicular development, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ovarian volume can be considered normal up to about 15 ml in the source
Postmenopausal ovaries should normally be larger than 20 cc
Early-cycle follicles are typically small, less than 5 mm
The dominant follicle is usually no larger than 5 mm by mid-cycle
The dominant follicle reaches around 20 mm by mid-cycle
options_after: Ovarian volume can be considered normal up to about 15 ml in the source
Postmenopausal ovaries should normally be larger than 20 cc
Early-cycle follicles are typically small, less than 5 mm
The dominant follicle usually remains below 5 mm by mid-cycle
The dominant follicle reaches around 20 mm by mid-cycle
updates.explanation: The source states that ovarian volume can be considered normal up to about 15 ml, with some using 20 ml. It describes early-cycle follicles as small, less than 5 mm, and a dominant follicle that reaches around 20 mm by mid-cycle. Postmenopausal ovarian volume should not exceed about 6 cc. A 5 mm dominant follicle at mid-cycle is therefore too small for the described normal physiology.

updates.question_text: Regarding paraovarian or paratubal cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are adnexal cysts adjacent to the ovary or tube rather than within the ovary
A simple paraovarian cyst requires follow-up regardless of size
Simple paraovarian cysts have a high malignancy rate in the source
They are defined by enhancing mural nodules and thick septa
A clearly non-ovarian simple paraovarian cyst does not require follow-up
options_after: They are adnexal cysts adjacent to the ovary or tube rather than within the ovary
A simple paraovarian cyst requires follow-up despite variation in size
Simple paraovarian cysts have a high malignancy rate in the source
They are defined by enhancing mural nodules and thick septa
A clearly non-ovarian simple paraovarian cyst does not require follow-up
updates.explanation: The source defines paraovarian or paratubal cysts as adnexal cysts located adjacent to the ovary or tube rather than within the ovary. If the cyst is simple and clearly not ovarian, it does not require follow-up, regardless of size, because the malignancy rate is described as extremely low. Thick septations, nodularity, and solid elements would move the lesion away from the simple cyst category.

updates.question_text: Regarding incidental simple-appearing ovarian cyst follow-up thresholds in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: On CT, a simple-appearing cyst under 3 cm in a premenopausal patient can be called a normal follicle
On CT, every simple cyst in a premenopausal patient requires immediate surgery
On CT, a simple-appearing cyst over 1 cm in a postmenopausal patient should get ultrasound
On ultrasound, a simple cyst under 7 cm in a premenopausal patient needs no follow-up
On ultrasound, a simple cyst under 5 cm in a postmenopausal patient needs no follow-up
options_after: On CT, a simple-appearing cyst under 3 cm in a premenopausal patient can be called a normal follicle
On CT, a simple cyst in a premenopausal patient requires immediate surgery
On CT, a simple-appearing cyst over 1 cm in a postmenopausal patient should get ultrasound
On ultrasound, a simple cyst under 7 cm in a premenopausal patient needs no follow-up
On ultrasound, a simple cyst under 5 cm in a postmenopausal patient needs no follow-up
updates.explanation: The source gives modality- and menopausal-status thresholds. For CT, a premenopausal simple-appearing cyst under 3 cm is called a normal follicle, while a postmenopausal cyst over 1 cm gets ultrasound. For ultrasound, a premenopausal simple cyst under 7 cm and a postmenopausal simple cyst under 5 cm require no follow-up. These rules apply to simple-appearing cysts, not complex masses requiring surgical consultation.

updates.question_text: Regarding complex ovarian cyst features that should trigger gynaecology consultation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A completely simple cyst always needs gynaecology consultation regardless of size or age
Irregular septations make a cyst non-simple
Papillary projections make a cyst non-simple
Solid elements make a cyst non-simple
A small simple cyst in a postmenopausal patient is always managed as ovarian carcinoma
options_after: A completely simple cyst characteristically needs gynaecology consultation despite variation in size or age
Irregular septations make a cyst non-simple
Papillary projections make a cyst non-simple
Solid elements make a cyst non-simple
A small simple cyst in a postmenopausal patient is characteristically managed as ovarian carcinoma
updates.explanation: The source states that a cyst that is not simple because of irregular septations, papillary projections, or solid elements should prompt gynaecology consultation. It separately states that simple cysts are almost certainly benign regardless of age and gives follow-up thresholds. The key distinction is simple versus complex morphology, not automatic malignancy based on a small simple cyst alone.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound and follow-up features of endometrioma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Endometriomas always resolve within one menstrual cycle
Endometriomas are usually pure anechoic cysts with no internal echoes
Small echogenic foci adherent to the wall exclude endometrioma
A rounded mass with homogeneous low-level internal echoes and increased through transmission is classic
Lack of change on follow-up helps distinguish endometrioma from haemorrhagic cyst
options_after: Endometriomas characteristically resolve within one menstrual cycle
Endometriomas are usually pure anechoic cysts without internal echoes
Small echogenic foci adherent to the wall exclude endometrioma
A rounded mass with homogeneous low-level internal echoes and increased through transmission is classic
Lack of change on follow-up helps distinguish endometrioma from haemorrhagic cyst
updates.explanation: The source describes the classic endometrioma appearance as a rounded mass with homogeneous low-level internal echoes and increased through transmission. It also states that endometriomas do not change on follow-up, unlike haemorrhagic cysts. Small echogenic wall foci can support the diagnosis in about 30% of cases, provided they are not true mural nodules. A simple anechoic cyst or rapid resolution would not match the source description.

updates.question_text: Regarding haemorrhagic ovarian cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They can show homogeneous internal content with enhanced through transmission
They should always demonstrate internal Doppler flow
A lacy fishnet appearance is considered classic
They are expected to persist unchanged for years
They are T1 dark on MRI because they contain clear serous fluid
options_after: They can show homogeneous internal content with enhanced through transmission
They should characteristically demonstrate internal Doppler flow
A lacy fishnet appearance is considered classic
They are expected to persist unchanged for years
They are T1 dark on MRI because they contain clear serous fluid
updates.explanation: The source describes haemorrhagic cysts as re-expanded follicles that bleed internally and can show homogeneous material with enhanced through transmission. A lacy fishnet appearance is considered classic. Doppler flow should be absent within the haemorrhagic contents, and follow-up resolution in 1–2 menstrual cycles helps distinguish them from endometrioma. They are T1 bright on MRI because of blood.

updates.question_text: Regarding haemorrhagic cysts in postmenopausal patients, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All postmenopausal haemorrhagic-appearing cysts are ignored without follow-up
Early postmenopausal women may occasionally ovulate, so short-interval follow-up can be appropriate
Late postmenopausal haemorrhagic-appearing cysts are treated as physiologic follicles
A haemorrhagic-cyst appearance in a 70-year-old is cancer until proven otherwise in the source
Follow-up over 6–12 weeks is used to confirm resolution when appropriate
options_after: Most postmenopausal haemorrhagic-appearing cysts are ignored without follow-up
Early postmenopausal women may occasionally ovulate, so short-interval follow-up can be appropriate
Late postmenopausal haemorrhagic-appearing cysts are treated as physiologic follicles
A haemorrhagic-cyst appearance in a 70-year-old is cancer until proven otherwise in the source
Follow-up over 6–12 weeks is used to confirm resolution when appropriate
updates.explanation: The source notes that postmenopausal women may occasionally ovulate, so a haemorrhagic cyst appearance can be followed in 6–12 weeks in that setting. It sharply distinguishes late postmenopausal women: a haemorrhagic-cyst appearance in a 70-year-old is considered malignant until proven otherwise. Therefore neither blanket dismissal nor automatic physiologic interpretation is supported. Resolution on follow-up is the key benign behaviour when short-interval follow-up is appropriate.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian dermoids, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Dermoids typically occur in elderly postmenopausal women only
The tip-of-the-iceberg sign means complete acoustic transmission through simple fluid
A Rokitansky nodule is a hyperechoic solid mural nodule within a cystic mass
Dermoids are T1 bright because of blood and therefore never suppress on fat-saturated MRI
A gross fat-containing ovarian mass on CT is a dermoid clue
options_after: Dermoids typically occur in elderly postmenopausal women
The tip-of-the-iceberg sign means complete acoustic transmission through simple fluid
A Rokitansky nodule is a hyperechoic solid mural nodule within a cystic mass
Dermoids are T1 bright because of blood and therefore will not suppress on fat-saturated MRI
A gross fat-containing ovarian mass on CT is a dermoid clue
updates.explanation: The source describes dermoids as occurring typically in young women and as the most common ovarian neoplasm in patients under 20. The classic ultrasound pattern is a cystic mass with a hyperechoic solid mural Rokitansky nodule, and gross fat on CT is a major clue. Dermoids are T1 bright because of fat and suppress on fat-saturated MRI. The tip-of-the-iceberg sign refers to absorption of most of the ultrasound beam at the top of the mass, not simple fluid transmission.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian cancer imaging red flags described at the start of the ovarian cancer section, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Most extra-ovarian adnexal masses are malignant in the source
Complex cystic adnexal masses with thick septations and papillary projections should raise concern for cancer
A nodule with blood flow in an ovarian mass should be ignored if the patient is premenopausal
Ancillary findings such as ascites, invasive spread, or lymphadenopathy increase concern for malignancy
Solid nodules without flow are automatically benign and do not require MRI
options_after: Most extra-ovarian adnexal masses are malignant in the source
Complex cystic adnexal masses with thick septations and papillary projections should raise concern for cancer
A nodule with blood flow in an ovarian mass should be ignored if the patient is premenopausal
Ancillary findings such as ascites, invasive spread, or lymphadenopathy increase concern for malignancy
Solid nodules without flow are ordinarily benign and do not require MRI
updates.explanation: The source says ovarian cancers often present as complex cystic and solid intra-ovarian masses, while most extra-ovarian masses are benign. Red flags include thick septations, papillary projections with flow, solid adnexal masses with necrosis, ascites, invasive spread, and lymphadenopathy. A nodule with flow should prompt surgical concern. A solid nodule without flow should be evaluated with MRI to exclude dermoid plug; if not dermoid, surgical consultation follows.

updates.question_text: Regarding mucinous ovarian cystadenocarcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is often a large mass
It is usually unilocular with papillary projections more common than in serous tumours
It cannot produce pseudomyxoma peritonei
It typically presents as a T2-dark solid fibrous ovarian tumour with ascites and pleural effusion
Smoking is described as a risk factor, especially for mucinous types
options_after: It is often a large mass
It is usually unilocular with papillary projections more common than in serous tumours
It will not produce pseudomyxoma peritonei
It typically presents as a T2-dark solid fibrous ovarian tumour with ascites and pleural effusion
Smoking is described as a risk factor, especially for mucinous types
updates.explanation: The source describes mucinous ovarian cystadenocarcinoma as often large and typically multiloculated, with thin septa. Papillary projections are less common than in serous tumours. It can be associated with pseudomyxoma peritonei and solid organ scalloping. Smoking is given as a risk factor, especially for mucinous tumours, while a T2-dark fibrous tumour with Meigs syndrome points more towards fibroma.

updates.question_text: Regarding serous versus mucinous ovarian epithelial tumours, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Serous tumours are typically multilocular with many septations
Serous tumours are commonly unilocular with fewer septations
Papillary projections are commoner in serous tumours than mucinous tumours
Mucinous tumours are typically unilocular with no septations
Mucinous tumours are more often multilocular with more septations
options_after: Serous tumours are typically multilocular with many septations
Serous tumours are commonly unilocular with fewer septations
Papillary projections are commoner in serous tumours than mucinous tumours
Mucinous tumours are typically unilocular without septations
Mucinous tumours are more often multilocular with more septations
updates.explanation: The source contrasts serous and mucinous tumours directly. Serous tumours are described as unilocular with fewer septations and papillary projections common. Mucinous tumours are described as multilocular with more septations and papillary projections less common. Reversing these patterns would misclassify the tumour type.

updates.question_text: Regarding hydrosalpinx, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It appears as an elongated tubular pelvic structure, thin- or thick-walled depending on chronicity
The cogwheel appearance refers to thickened longitudinal folds of the fallopian tube
The waist sign describes a tubular mass with indentations of opposing walls
The most common cause listed is an ovarian dermoid
Hydrosalpinx never occurs after hysterectomy or tubal ligation
options_after: It appears as an elongated tubular pelvic structure, thin- or thick-walled depending on chronicity
The cogwheel appearance refers to thickened longitudinal folds of the fallopian tube
The waist sign describes a tubular mass with indentations of opposing walls
The most common cause listed is an ovarian dermoid
Hydrosalpinx will not occur after hysterectomy or tubal ligation
updates.explanation: The source describes hydrosalpinx as an elongated tubular pelvic structure, with wall thickness depending on chronicity. The cogwheel appearance reflects thickened longitudinal folds, and the waist sign reflects indentations of opposing walls in a tubular mass. Causes listed include PID, endometriosis, tubal cancer, post-hysterectomy without salpingectomy or oophorectomy, and tubal ligation. Dermoid is not the cause highlighted here.

updates.question_text: Regarding pelvic inflammatory disease in this source, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is limited to the lower vagina and never involves adnexa
Ultrasound should show a normal fallopian tube with no hydrosalpinx
It cannot progress to tubo-ovarian abscess
It is infection or inflammation of the upper female genital tract, often associated with gonorrhoea or chlamydia
Bowel and urinary tract inflammatory changes exclude PID
options_after: It is limited to the lower vagina and will not involve adnexa
Ultrasound should show a normal fallopian tube without hydrosalpinx
It will not progress to tubo-ovarian abscess
It is infection or inflammation of the upper female genital tract, often associated with gonorrhoea or chlamydia
Bowel and urinary tract inflammatory changes exclude PID
updates.explanation: The source defines PID as infection or inflammation of the upper female genital tract and links it to gonorrhoea and chlamydia. Ultrasound may show hydrosalpinx, and the uterine margin can become ill-defined. It can progress to tubo-ovarian abscess or pelvic abscess. Bowel or urinary tract inflammatory changes may occur rather than excluding the diagnosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian vein thrombophlebitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is most commonly seen postpartum, often with acute pelvic pain and fever around 10 days after delivery
It is bilateral in nearly all cases according to the source
It is usually diagnosed as a thin-walled simple ovarian cyst
Pulmonary embolus is not considered a complication
CT may show a tubular structure with enhancing wall and low-attenuation thrombus in the expected ovarian vein location
options_after: It is most commonly seen postpartum, often with acute pelvic pain and fever around 10 days after delivery
It is bilateral in the large majority of cases according to the source
It is usually diagnosed as a thin-walled simple ovarian cyst
Pulmonary embolus is not considered a complication
CT may show a tubular structure with enhancing wall and low-attenuation thrombus in the expected ovarian vein location
updates.explanation: The source describes ovarian vein thrombophlebitis as most common in postpartum women, often about 10 days after delivery with pelvic pain and fever. It is right-sided about 80% of the time. CT can show a tubular structure with an enhancing wall and low-attenuation thrombus in the expected ovarian vein location. Pulmonary embolus is described as a dreaded sequela, and treatment includes anticoagulation with antibiotics if fever is present.

updates.question_text: Regarding gestational trophoblastic disease and hydatidiform mole, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Marked beta-hCG elevation is a key clue and beta-hCG is followed for tumour activity
Low beta-hCG is the key biochemical clue
Moles are more common under age 20 and a prior mole lowers future risk
Hydatidiform mole is the most common and benign form in the source
Theca lutein cysts are never associated with molar pregnancy
options_after: Marked beta-hCG elevation is a key clue and beta-hCG is followed for tumour activity
Low beta-hCG is the key biochemical clue
Moles are more common under age 20 and a prior mole lowers future risk
Hydatidiform mole is the most common and benign form in the source
Theca lutein cysts are not associated with molar pregnancy
updates.explanation: The source links gestational trophoblastic disease to marked beta-hCG elevation and states that beta-hCG is trended for tumour activity. Hydatidiform mole is described as the most common and benign form. The text also notes hyperemesis, older maternal age over 40, and prior mole increasing future risk, so statements reversing those concepts are incorrect. Theca lutein cysts are specifically mentioned in molar pregnancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding complete and partial hydatidiform moles, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A complete mole involves only a portion of the placenta and has a fetus
A complete mole involves the entire placenta and has no fetus
First-trimester complete mole can show an echogenic solid highly vascular uterine mass with a snowstorm appearance
Partial mole involves only part of the placenta and can show fetal parts
Partial mole is classically diploid from an empty ovum fertilised by one sperm
options_after: A complete mole involves primarily a portion of the placenta and has a fetus
A complete mole involves the entire placenta and has no fetus
First-trimester complete mole can show an echogenic solid highly vascular uterine mass with a snowstorm appearance
Partial mole involves only part of the placenta and can show fetal parts
Partial mole is classically diploid from an empty ovum fertilised by one sperm
updates.explanation: The source describes complete mole as involving the entire placenta, with no fetus, and classically showing an echogenic highly vascular uterine mass in the first trimester. Partial mole involves only part of the placenta, may show fetal parts, and has an enlarged placenta with multiple anechoic lesions. The complete mole is the diploid classic mole in the source, while partial mole is triploid after fertilisation by two sperm. Reversing those features is a common trap.

updates.question_text: Regarding invasive mole and choriocarcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Invasive mole refers to molar tissue invading the myometrium
MRI is inferior to ultrasound for demonstrating myometrial invasion in invasive mole
Choriocarcinoma forms only trophoblasts without villous structure
Rising beta-hCG 8–10 weeks after molar evacuation is the classic choriocarcinoma scenario
Choriocarcinoma spreads only through lymphatics and never haematogenously
options_after: Invasive mole refers to molar tissue invading the myometrium
MRI is inferior to ultrasound for demonstrating myometrial invasion in invasive mole
Choriocarcinoma forms only trophoblasts without villous structure
Rising beta-hCG 8–10 weeks after molar evacuation is the classic choriocarcinoma scenario
Choriocarcinoma spreads primarily through lymphatics and will not haematogenously
updates.explanation: The source defines invasive mole as molar tissue invading the myometrium, often after treatment of hydatidiform mole, and states that MRI is better than ultrasound for demonstrating muscle invasion. Choriocarcinoma forms trophoblasts without villous structure and is aggressive. A classic scenario is beta-hCG rising in the 8–10 weeks after evacuation of a molar pregnancy. The source describes local spread followed by haematogenous dissemination to any site.

updates.question_text: Regarding penile fracture anatomy and imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Penile fracture is defined by fracture of the corpus cavernosum and its surrounding tunica albuginea
CT is the preferred modality in the source and ultrasound has no role
The tunica albuginea is irrelevant because only the corpus spongiosum matters
Imaging may show interruption of the low-signal tunica albuginea and T1-bright haemorrhage in the corpus cavernosum
Peyronie disease cannot occur after this injury because scar formation is not relevant
options_after: Penile fracture is defined by fracture of the corpus cavernosum and its surrounding tunica albuginea
CT is the preferred modality in the source and ultrasound has negligible role
The tunica albuginea is irrelevant because primarily the corpus spongiosum matters
Imaging may show interruption of the low-signal tunica albuginea and T1-bright haemorrhage in the corpus cavernosum
Peyronie disease will not occur after this injury because scar formation is not relevant
updates.explanation: The source defines penile fracture as fracture of the corpus cavernosum and its surrounding tunica albuginea. It can be shown by ultrasound or MRI, with interruption of the low-signal tunica line and T1-bright haemorrhage in the corpus cavernosum as key features. The tunica is central to the diagnosis rather than irrelevant. Fibrous scar formation can lead to Peyronie disease, so denying scar-related angulation is incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI findings of prostate cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Prostate cancer is bright on T2 against the high-signal peripheral-zone background
Prostate cancer is dark on T2
Prostate cancer restricts diffusion and is low on ADC
Prostate cancer enhances early and washes out early
Prostate cancer should not enhance because enhancement is a benign BPH feature only
options_after: Prostate cancer is bright on T2 against the high-signal peripheral-zone background
Prostate cancer is dark on T2
Prostate cancer restricts diffusion and is low on ADC
Prostate cancer enhances early and washes out early
Prostate cancer should not enhance because enhancement is a benign BPH feature
updates.explanation: The source describes prostate cancer as dark on T2, low on ADC because of restricted diffusion, and showing early enhancement with early washout. This is especially conspicuous in the T2-bright peripheral zone background. Enhancement is not benign-specific; both cancer and BPH may enhance, but cancer has the early enhancement and washout pattern in the source. Bright T2 signal would not match the described cancer appearance.

updates.question_text: Regarding BPH nodules, post-biopsy haemorrhage, and the prostate pathology summary, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: BPH nodules are usually in the transitional zone and can be T2 heterogeneous
Post-biopsy change is classically T1-bright blood in the gland
Peripheral-zone haemorrhage typically shows early enhancement and early washout
Peripheral-zone tumour is T2 dark, ADC dark, and shows early enhancement with early washout
Central-gland transitional-zone tumour is always T2 bright and never restricts diffusion
options_after: BPH nodules are usually in the transitional zone and can be T2 heterogeneous
Post-biopsy change is classically T1-bright blood in the gland
Peripheral-zone haemorrhage typically shows early enhancement and early washout
Peripheral-zone tumour is T2 dark, ADC dark, and shows early enhancement with early washout
Central-gland transitional-zone tumour is characteristically T2 bright and will not restrict diffusion
updates.explanation: The source places BPH nodules in the transitional zone or central gland and notes they may be T2 heterogeneous, restrict diffusion, and enhance. Post-biopsy change is classically T1-bright subacute blood. Peripheral-zone tumour is T2 dark, ADC dark, and shows early enhancement with early washout. Peripheral-zone haemorrhage does not enhance in the summary chart, and central-gland tumour is described as dark charcoal with diffusion restriction and early enhancement/washout.

updates.question_text: Regarding calcified vas deferens and seminal vesicle cysts, which statement is correct?
options_before: Calcified vas deferens is only visible on MRI
Seminal vesicle cysts are always midline prostatic urethral outpouchings
Congenital seminal vesicle cysts are unrelated to renal agenesis or vas deferens agenesis
Acquired seminal vesicle cysts are never related to obstruction or prior prostate surgery
A congenital seminal vesicle cyst may be associated with renal agenesis, vas deferens agenesis, ectopic ureter insertion, or polycystic kidney disease
options_after: Calcified vas deferens is primarily visible on MRI
Seminal vesicle cysts are characteristically midline prostatic urethral outpouchings
Congenital seminal vesicle cysts are unrelated to renal agenesis or vas deferens agenesis
Acquired seminal vesicle cysts are not related to obstruction or prior prostate surgery
A congenital seminal vesicle cyst may be associated with renal agenesis, vas deferens agenesis, ectopic ureter insertion, or polycystic kidney disease
updates.explanation: The source describes calcified vas deferens as visible on plain film or CT and associated with severe diabetes. Seminal vesicle cysts are lateral cysts, although large ones can appear midline. Congenital associations listed include renal agenesis, vas deferens agenesis, ectopic ureter insertion, and polycystic kidney disease. Acquired causes include obstruction from prostatic hypertrophy, chronic infection or scarring, and prior prostate surgery.

updates.question_text: Regarding midline male pelvic cysts and prostate abscess, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A prostatic utricle cyst does not communicate with the urethra and should not opacify on retrograde urethrogram
A prostatic utricle cyst communicates with the urethra and can opacify on retrograde urethrogram
Müllerian duct cysts have the same urethral communication and associations as utricle cysts
Müllerian duct cysts do not communicate with the urethra and may extend above the prostate base
Prostate abscess is always a thin-walled unilocular cyst that should not be drained
options_after: A prostatic utricle cyst does not communicate with the urethra and should not opacify on retrograde urethrogram
A prostatic utricle cyst communicates with the urethra and can opacify on retrograde urethrogram
Müllerian duct cysts have the same urethral communication and associations as utricle cysts
Müllerian duct cysts do not communicate with the urethra and may extend above the prostate base
Prostate abscess is characteristically a thin-walled unilocular cyst that should not be drained
updates.explanation: The source describes prostatic utricle cyst as a focal dilation in the prostatic urethra, meaning it communicates with the urethra and can opacify on retrograde urethrogram. Müllerian duct cyst is a failed regression of caudal Müllerian ducts, does not communicate with the urethra, and can extend above the prostate base. A prostate abscess can be thick-walled, septated, heterogeneous, and cystic, often assessed by transrectal ultrasound because image-guided drainage may be performed. The urethral communication and associated conditions are important discriminators between utricle and Müllerian duct cysts.

updates.question_text: Regarding testicular torsion ultrasound, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Doppler ultrasound is the current first-line imaging test described in the source
The affected testis is always smaller in the acute setting
Preserved arterial flow excludes torsion
A normal cremasteric artery waveform should have continuous diastolic flow
Grey-scale findings can include an asymmetrically enlarged hypoechoic testis
options_after: Doppler ultrasound is the current first-line imaging test described in the source
The affected testis is characteristically smaller in the acute setting
Preserved arterial flow excludes torsion
A normal cremasteric artery waveform should have continuous diastolic flow
Grey-scale findings can include an asymmetrically enlarged hypoechoic testis
updates.explanation: The source states that modern evaluation of suspected torsion is Doppler ultrasound. Grey-scale findings can include an asymmetrically enlarged hypoechoic testis, especially in established torsion. Preserved arterial flow does not exclude torsion, because waveform resistance and diastolic flow matter. The cremasteric artery is a muscle artery and normally high resistance, so it should not be interpreted like the testicular artery.

updates.question_text: Regarding abnormal testicular arterial waveforms in torsion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The only possible torsion pattern is absent arterial flow
High-resistance arterial flow with decreased or reversed diastolic flow can occur
A monophasic arterial waveform with loss of the normal dicrotic notch can occur
Increased diastolic flow is the classic torsion waveform pattern
The testis is compared conceptually to the brain because both require continuous diastolic flow
options_after: The principal possible torsion pattern is absent arterial flow
High-resistance arterial flow with decreased or reversed diastolic flow can occur
A monophasic arterial waveform with loss of the normal dicrotic notch can occur
Increased diastolic flow is the classic torsion waveform pattern
The testis is compared conceptually to the brain because both require continuous diastolic flow
updates.explanation: The source gives three torsion Doppler patterns: absent arterial flow, high-resistance arterial flow with decreased or reversed diastolic flow, and monophasic arterial waveform with loss of the dicrotic notch. It emphasises that continuous diastolic flow is important, comparing the testis conceptually to the brain. Increased diastolic flow suggests a hyperaemic process rather than the torsion pattern described here. Therefore absent flow is classic but not the only diagnostic pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding the predisposing anatomy and viability timing in testicular torsion, which statement is correct?
options_before: The bell-clapper deformity is a low attachment of the tunica vaginalis that fixes the testis
The bell-clapper deformity is usually unilateral and contralateral orchiopexy is avoided
The bell-clapper deformity is an abnormal high attachment of the tunica vaginalis that increases testicular mobility
Viability depends only on patient age and not on duration or degree of torsion
Surgery is generally delayed beyond 24 hours to allow detorsion
options_after: The bell-clapper deformity is a low attachment of the tunica vaginalis that fixes the testis
The bell-clapper deformity is usually unilateral and contralateral orchiopexy is avoided
The bell-clapper deformity is an abnormal high attachment of the tunica vaginalis that increases testicular mobility
Viability depends primarily on patient age and not on duration or degree of torsion
Surgery is generally delayed beyond 24 hours to allow detorsion
updates.explanation: The source defines the bell-clapper deformity as abnormal high attachment of the tunica vaginalis, increasing mobility and predisposing to torsion. It is usually bilateral, so the contralateral side also undergoes orchiopexy. Viability depends on the degree of torsion and duration, with the general surgical aim of operating before 6 hours. Delayed management is not the message of the section.

updates.question_text: Regarding testicular cancer risk factors and classic presentation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Orchiopexy eliminates the cancer risk from cryptorchidism according to the source
Cryptorchidism increases cancer risk only in the undescended testis
Cryptorchidism is a key risk factor and increases risk in both testes
A classic presentation is a man aged 18–35 with prior undescended testis and seminoma
Unexplained retroperitoneal adenopathy in a young man should prompt scrotal ultrasound
options_after: Orchiopexy eliminates the cancer risk from cryptorchidism according to the source
Cryptorchidism increases cancer risk primarily in the undescended testis
Cryptorchidism is a key risk factor and increases risk in both testes
A classic presentation is a man aged 18–35 with prior undescended testis and seminoma
Unexplained retroperitoneal adenopathy in a young man should prompt scrotal ultrasound
updates.explanation: The source lists cryptorchidism as a key testicular cancer risk factor and states that risk is increased in both testes and is not reduced by orchiopexy. The classic scenario is a man aged 18–35 with a history of undescended testis and seminoma. It also highlights mystery retroperitoneal adenopathy in a young man as a reason to image the testes. Restricting risk to only the undescended side is therefore incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding seminoma and non-seminomatous germ cell tumours, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Seminoma is typically a homogeneous hypoechoic round mass
Seminoma is usually heterogeneous with cystic spaces and macrocalcification
Non-seminomatous germ cell tumours are more heterogeneous and can have cystic spaces and larger calcifications
Seminoma has the worst prognosis because it is radioresistant
Non-seminomatous tumours classically occur only after age 60
options_after: Seminoma is typically a homogeneous hypoechoic round mass
Seminoma is usually heterogeneous with cystic spaces and macrocalcification
Non-seminomatous germ cell tumours are more heterogeneous and can have cystic spaces and larger calcifications
Seminoma has the worst prognosis because it is radioresistant
Non-seminomatous tumours classically occur primarily after age 60
updates.explanation: The source describes seminoma as the most common testicular tumour, typically homogeneous, hypoechoic, round, and often replacing the testis. Non-seminomatous germ cell tumours are described as more heterogeneous, with cystic spaces and larger calcifications. Seminomas are radiosensitive and have the best prognosis in this section. Non-seminomatous tumours tend to occur younger than seminomas, not after 60.

updates.question_text: Regarding testicular lymphoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Testicular lymphoma is most common in men aged 18–35
Age over 60 is the primary discriminator in the source
Testicular lymphoma is always bilateral
Bilateral lymphoma is the most common bilateral testicular tumour
It may appear as a diffusely enlarged ill-defined hypoechoic testis or multiple hypoechoic masses
options_after: Testicular lymphoma is most common in men aged 18–35
Age over 60 is the primary discriminator in the source
Testicular lymphoma is characteristically bilateral
Bilateral lymphoma is the most common bilateral testicular tumour
It may appear as a diffusely enlarged ill-defined hypoechoic testis or multiple hypoechoic masses
updates.explanation: The source states that testicular lymphoma is most common over age 60, making age the main discriminator. Most testicular lymphoma is unilateral, but lymphoma is still the most common bilateral testicular tumour. Imaging can show diffuse ill-defined hypoechoic enlargement or multiple hypoechoic masses. Young adult presentation is more typical of germ cell tumours.

updates.question_text: Regarding cryptorchidism, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Undescended testes are usually found in the inguinal canal
Orchiopexy removes the increased cancer risk entirely
It increases malignancy risk in both the undescended and contralateral testis
Associated complications include infertility, torsion, and bowel incarceration from indirect inguinal hernia
It is most commonly seen in premature children
options_after: Undescended testes are usually found in the inguinal canal
Orchiopexy removes the increased cancer risk predominantly
It increases malignancy risk in both the undescended and contralateral testis
Associated complications include infertility, torsion, and bowel incarceration from indirect inguinal hernia
It is most commonly seen in premature children
updates.explanation: The source states that an undescended testis is usually in the inguinal canal and is most common in premature children. Cryptorchidism increases malignancy risk in both the undescended and contralateral testis, and this risk is not reduced by orchiopexy in the source. Other associated complications include infertility, torsion, and bowel incarceration related to indirect inguinal hernia. Orchitis is specifically mentioned as a distractor rather than a reported increased association.

updates.question_text: Regarding vaginoplasty procedures described in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Penoscrotal inversion is described as the most common vaginoplasty procedure with the lowest complication rate
Penoscrotal inversion uses rectosigmoid colon as the first-line tunnel tissue
Intestinal interposition is always first-line because penile and scrotal tissue is never usable
Intestinal interposition is a second-line strategy using bowel, usually rectosigmoid colon, to create a neovagina
Vaginoplasty is unrelated to creating a functional neovagina
options_after: Penoscrotal inversion is described as the most common vaginoplasty procedure with the lowest complication rate
Penoscrotal inversion uses rectosigmoid colon as the first-line tunnel tissue
Intestinal interposition is characteristically first-line because penile and scrotal tissue is not usable
Intestinal interposition is a second-line strategy using bowel, usually rectosigmoid colon, to create a neovagina
Vaginoplasty is unrelated to creating a functional neovagina
updates.explanation: The source describes vaginoplasty as creation of a functional and cosmetically acceptable neovagina. Penoscrotal inversion is stated to be the most common procedure and has the lowest complication rate. Intestinal interposition is a second-line strategy using a bowel segment, usually rectosigmoid colon, by coloperineal anastomosis. It is used when there is insufficient tissue for the primary inversion approach.

updates.question_text: Regarding phalloplasty, metoidioplasty, and prostheses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Phalloplasty aims to create a functional and cosmetically acceptable neopenis, with standing urination a typical success metric
Metoidioplasty has a lower complication rate than phalloplasty in the source
Metoidioplasty always creates sufficient length for penetrative intercourse in the source
Testicular prostheses are generally silicone and can be high density on CT
Hydraulic pump apparatus can include tubing and water-density components
options_after: Phalloplasty aims to create a functional and cosmetically acceptable neopenis, with standing urination a typical success metric
Metoidioplasty has a lower complication rate than phalloplasty in the source
Metoidioplasty characteristically creates sufficient length for penetrative intercourse in the source
Testicular prostheses are generally silicone and can be high density on CT
Hydraulic pump apparatus can include tubing and water-density components
updates.explanation: The source describes phalloplasty as creation of a functional neopenis, with standing urination a typical success metric. Metoidioplasty is described as an alternative with lower complication rate but usually insufficient length for intercourse, though standing urination may still be possible. Testicular prostheses are generally silicone and high density on CT, while hydraulic pump apparatus can include tubing and water-density components. These imaging clues help recognise post-operative anatomy.

updates.question_text: Regarding early pregnancy vocabulary, which statement is correct?
options_before: Menstrual age equals embryologic age minus 14 days
Threatened abortion is bleeding with a closed cervix
Inevitable abortion means all products of conception are already out
Missed abortion means residual products remain after partial expulsion
Embryo refers to menstrual age greater than 10 weeks
options_after: Menstrual age equals embryologic age minus 14 days
Threatened abortion is bleeding with a closed cervix
Inevitable abortion means most products of conception are already out
Missed abortion means residual products remain after partial expulsion
Embryo refers to menstrual age greater than 10 weeks
updates.explanation: The source defines threatened abortion as bleeding with a closed cervix. Menstrual age equals embryologic age plus 14 days. Inevitable abortion involves cervical dilatation and/or placental or fetal tissue at the cervix, incomplete abortion means residual products in the uterus, complete abortion means all products are out, and missed abortion means the fetus is dead but remains in the uterus. Embryo is used for 0–10 weeks menstrual age, fetus after 10 weeks.

updates.question_text: Regarding the intradecidual and double decidual sac signs, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The intradecidual sign is a late third-trimester sign
The uterine cavity line should stop at the sac to confirm a true gestational sac
The double decidual sac sign is produced by visualising only the yolk sac and amnion
The intradecidual sign can be seen around 4.5 weeks
The double decidual sac sign is another positive sign of early pregnancy caused by decidual layers
options_after: The intradecidual sign is a late third-trimester sign
The uterine cavity line should stop at the sac to confirm a true gestational sac
The double decidual sac sign is produced by visualising primarily the yolk sac and amnion
The intradecidual sign can be seen around 4.5 weeks
The double decidual sac sign is another positive sign of early pregnancy caused by decidual layers
updates.explanation: The source describes the intradecidual sign as an early gestational sac sign that can be seen around 4.5 weeks.
