It stresses that the thin echogenic uterine cavity line should pass by the sac rather than stop at it, to avoid mistaking canal fluid for a sac. The double decidual sac sign is another positive early pregnancy sign produced by visualising decidual layers. It is distinct from the double bleb sign involving yolk sac, amnion, and embryo.

updates.question_text: Regarding diagnostic criteria for pregnancy failure in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Crown-rump length greater than 7 mm with no heartbeat is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
Mean sac diameter 16–24 mm with no embryo is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
Mean sac diameter greater than 25 mm with no embryo is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
No embryo 6 weeks after last menstrual period is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
Any subchorionic haemorrhage is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
options_after: Crown-rump length greater than 7 mm with no heartbeat is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
Mean sac diameter 16–24 mm without embryo is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
Mean sac diameter greater than 25 mm with no embryo is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
Absence of an embryo six weeks after the last menstrual period meets diagnostic criteria for pregnancy failure
Any subchorionic haemorrhage is diagnostic of pregnancy failure
updates.explanation: The source's diagnostic criteria include crown-rump length greater than 7 mm with no heartbeat and mean sac diameter greater than 25 mm with no embryo. Mean sac diameter 16–24 mm with no embryo is listed as suspicious rather than diagnostic. No embryo more than 6 weeks after last menstrual period is also suspicious rather than diagnostic in the table. Subchorionic haemorrhage affects prognosis but is not itself listed as diagnostic of pregnancy failure.

updates.question_text: Regarding pregnancy of unknown location, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It means both a normal intrauterine pregnancy and ectopic pregnancy have been definitively excluded
It is used when neither normal intrauterine pregnancy nor ectopic pregnancy is identified despite positive beta-hCG
The only possible outcome is viable normal early pregnancy
The differential includes normal early pregnancy, occult ectopic pregnancy, and complete miscarriage
If haemodynamically stable, management includes serial beta-hCG and repeat ultrasound
options_after: It means both a normal intrauterine pregnancy and ectopic pregnancy have been definitively excluded
It is used when neither normal intrauterine pregnancy nor ectopic pregnancy is identified despite positive beta-hCG
The principal possible outcome is viable normal early pregnancy
The differential includes normal early pregnancy, occult ectopic pregnancy, and complete miscarriage
If haemodynamically stable, management includes serial beta-hCG and repeat ultrasound
updates.explanation: The source defines pregnancy of unknown location as positive beta-hCG with neither normal intrauterine pregnancy nor ectopic pregnancy identified. It lists three possibilities: normal early pregnancy, occult ectopic, and complete miscarriage. In a haemodynamically stable patient, management is follow-up with serial beta-hCG and repeat ultrasound. The term does not prove the pregnancy is normal or exclude ectopic pregnancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding positive predictive value clues for ectopic pregnancy, which statement is correct?
options_before: Nothing in the uterus plus moderate free fluid has zero predictive value for ectopic pregnancy
Any adnexal structure, including corpus luteum, makes ectopic pregnancy certain
Moderate free fluid lowers the predictive value of an adnexal abnormality
A yolk sac outside the uterus is only suspicious and never diagnostic
Nothing in the uterus plus an adnexal abnormality other than corpus luteum has high predictive value, and moderate free fluid increases it further
options_after: Nothing in the uterus plus moderate free fluid has zero predictive value for ectopic pregnancy
Any adnexal structure, including corpus luteum, makes ectopic pregnancy certain
Moderate free fluid lowers the predictive value of an adnexal abnormality
A yolk sac outside the uterus is suspicious but not diagnostic
Nothing in the uterus plus an adnexal abnormality other than corpus luteum has high predictive value, and moderate free fluid increases it further
updates.explanation: The source's ectopic rules start with a positive beta-hCG. A live pregnancy or yolk sac outside the uterus is diagnostic. Nothing in the uterus plus an adnexal finding other than corpus luteum has high positive predictive value, and moderate free fluid increases that further. Nothing in the uterus plus moderate free fluid also has substantial predictive value, especially if the fluid is echogenic.

updates.question_text: Regarding heterotopic pregnancy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is defined as two intrauterine gestational sacs
It is an intrauterine pregnancy plus an ectopic pregnancy
It is common in all naturally conceived pregnancies
It is typically seen with ovulation drugs or prior significant PID in the source
It excludes tubal pregnancy because a uterine pregnancy is present
options_after: It is defined as two intrauterine gestational sacs
It is an intrauterine pregnancy plus an ectopic pregnancy
It is common in most naturally conceived pregnancies
It is typically seen with ovulation drugs or prior significant PID in the source
It excludes tubal pregnancy because a uterine pregnancy is present
updates.explanation: The source defines heterotopic pregnancy as a pregnancy in the uterus plus a pregnancy in the tube or another ectopic location. It is rare and typically seen with ovulation drugs or prior significant PID. The presence of an intrauterine pregnancy therefore does not exclude ectopic pregnancy in this scenario. Two intrauterine sacs would be a multiple intrauterine pregnancy rather than heterotopic pregnancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding abdominal circumference, femur length, estimated fetal weight, and gestational age estimation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Abdominal circumference is measured at the level of the fetal kidneys
Abdominal circumference is recorded at the junction of the umbilical vein and left portal vein
Femur length is the longest dimension of the femoral shaft and excludes the epiphysis
Estimated fetal weight is calculated only from femur length and head circumference in the source
First-trimester gestational age is estimated from crown-rump length
options_after: Abdominal circumference is measured at the level of the fetal kidneys
Abdominal circumference is recorded at the junction of the umbilical vein and left portal vein
Femur length is the longest dimension of the femoral shaft and excludes the epiphysis
Estimated fetal weight is calculated primarily from femur length and head circumference in the source
First-trimester gestational age is estimated from crown-rump length
updates.explanation: The source states that abdominal circumference is recorded at the level of the junction of the umbilical vein and left portal vein and does not include subcutaneous soft tissues. Femur length is the longest dimension of the femoral shaft, excluding the epiphysis. Estimated fetal weight is calculated by the machine based on either biparietal diameter and abdominal circumference or abdominal circumference and femur length. Crown-rump length is the first-trimester gestational age measurement.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound findings suggestive of intrauterine growth restriction, which statement is correct?
options_before: Estimated fetal weight above the 90th percentile suggests intrauterine growth restriction
Femur length to abdominal circumference ratio below 10 suggests intrauterine growth restriction
Estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile is suggestive of intrauterine growth restriction
Umbilical artery systolic-to-diastolic ratio below 1 is the key source criterion
Normal Doppler studies always prove that a small fetus is abnormal
options_after: Estimated fetal weight above the 90th percentile suggests intrauterine growth restriction
Femur length to abdominal circumference ratio below 10 suggests intrauterine growth restriction
Estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile is suggestive of intrauterine growth restriction
Umbilical artery systolic-to-diastolic ratio below 1 is the key source criterion
Normal Doppler studies characteristically prove that a small fetus is abnormal
updates.explanation: The source lists estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile as suggestive of intrauterine growth restriction. It also lists femur length to abdominal circumference ratio over 23.5 and umbilical artery systolic-to-diastolic ratio over 4.0. A small fetus with normal Doppler studies may simply be constitutionally small in many cases. Estimated fetal weight above the 90th percentile instead points towards macrosomia.

updates.question_text: Regarding symmetric versus asymmetric intrauterine growth restriction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Asymmetric growth restriction is more common than symmetric growth restriction
Symmetric growth restriction spares the head and affects only the abdomen
Asymmetric growth restriction is typically seen throughout pregnancy from the first trimester
Asymmetric growth restriction has a normal head with small body or abdominal circumference
Symmetric growth restriction affects both head and body and has a worse prognosis
options_after: Asymmetric growth restriction is more common than symmetric growth restriction
Symmetric growth restriction spares the head and affects primarily the abdomen
Asymmetric growth restriction is typically seen throughout pregnancy from the first trimester
Asymmetric growth restriction has a normal head with small body or abdominal circumference
Symmetric growth restriction affects both head and body and has a worse prognosis
updates.explanation: The source describes asymmetric growth restriction as the more common type, with relative head sparing and a small body or abdominal circumference, usually in the third trimester. Symmetric growth restriction is global, does not spare the head, and is present throughout pregnancy including the first trimester. Symmetric restriction has a worse prognosis because brain development is affected. The head-sparing description belongs to asymmetric restriction.

updates.question_text: Regarding the biophysical profile, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It was developed only to calculate estimated fetal weight
The abnormal assessment can be made instantly without observation time in the source
Amniotic fluid assesses chronic hypoxia
Fetal movement, tone, breathing, and non-stress test assess acute hypoxia
A score of 8–10 is considered normal
options_after: It was developed primarily to calculate estimated fetal weight
The abnormal assessment can be made instantly without observation time in the source
Amniotic fluid assesses chronic hypoxia
Fetal movement, tone, breathing, and non-stress test assess acute hypoxia
A score of 8–10 is considered normal
updates.explanation: The source describes the biophysical profile as developed to assess acute and chronic hypoxia, not to calculate fetal weight. A score of 8–10 is considered normal. Amniotic fluid assessment reflects chronic hypoxia, while movement, tone, breathing, and the non-stress test assess acute hypoxia. The source notes that technically, abnormality requires watching for 30 minutes.

updates.question_text: Regarding amniotic fluid physiology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: After 16 weeks, amniotic fluid is made by the mother rather than fetus
After 16 weeks, amniotic fluid is made by fetal urine
Too little fluid should raise concern for poor renal function
Fine particulate in third-trimester amniotic fluid is always abnormal
Too much fluid should raise concern for swallowing or gastrointestinal problems, although maternal hyperglycaemia is also common
options_after: After 16 weeks, amniotic fluid is made by the mother rather than fetus
After 16 weeks, amniotic fluid is made by fetal urine
Too little fluid should raise concern for poor renal function
Fine particulate in third-trimester amniotic fluid is characteristically abnormal
Too much fluid should raise concern for swallowing or gastrointestinal problems, although maternal hyperglycaemia is also common
updates.explanation: The source states that early amniotic fluid is filtrate from membranes, but after 16 weeks it is made by fetal urine. Too little fluid raises concern for renal dysfunction, while too much fluid suggests impaired swallowing or gastrointestinal problems. Maternal hyperglycaemia or gestational diabetes is also given as a common cause of too much fluid. Fine particulate matter can be normal, especially in the third trimester.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal early fetal appearances that can mimic pathology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cystic rhombencephalon is a normal posterior fossa structure around 6–8 weeks
Physiologic midgut herniation is always an omphalocele
Normal midgut herniation occurs in the third trimester
The cystic rhombencephalon should be called Dandy-Walker malformation whenever seen
Physiologic midgut herniation normally occurs around 9–11 weeks
options_after: Cystic rhombencephalon is a normal posterior fossa structure around 6–8 weeks
Physiologic midgut herniation is characteristically an omphalocele
Normal midgut herniation occurs in the third trimester
The cystic rhombencephalon should be called Dandy-Walker malformation whenever seen
Physiologic midgut herniation normally occurs around 9–11 weeks
updates.explanation: The source warns that the normal rhombencephalon can appear cystic in the posterior fossa around 6–8 weeks and should not be called Dandy-Walker malformation. It also states that physiologic midgut herniation normally occurs into the umbilical cord around 9–11 weeks and should not be called an omphalocele. These are normal timing-based appearances. Calling them malformations outside the right context is the trap.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal placenta and placental lakes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The placenta can first be seen around 8 weeks as focal thickening along the gestational sac periphery
By around 12 weeks, the placenta should be disc-shaped
Placental venous lakes are always malignant placental masses
Venous lakes can appear as focal hypoechoic areas under the chorionic membrane or within the placenta
Normal placental ageing can produce hypoechoic areas, septations, and randomly distributed calcifications
options_after: The placenta can first be seen around 8 weeks as focal thickening along the gestational sac periphery
By around 12 weeks, the placenta should be disc-shaped
Placental venous lakes are characteristically malignant placental masses
Venous lakes can appear as focal hypoechoic areas under the chorionic membrane or within the placenta
Normal placental ageing can produce hypoechoic areas, septations, and randomly distributed calcifications
updates.explanation: The source states that the placenta becomes visible around 8 weeks as focal peripheral thickening and should be disc-shaped by about 12 weeks. It describes normal appearance as granular with a smooth chorionic surface and a retroplacental venous complex. Venous lakes are incidental and can look like focal hypoechoic regions under the chorion or within the placenta, sometimes with slow flow. Ageing placenta may develop hypoechoic areas, septations, and random calcifications.

updates.question_text: Regarding placental thickness, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Placental thickness below 1 cm is linked to fetal hydrops in the source
A placenta thinner than 1 cm is associated with placental insufficiency
A placenta thicker than 4 cm is associated with fetal hydrops and congenital infection
Maternal diabetes appears in both the too-thin and too-thick lists in the source
A placenta thicker than 4 cm is always normal placental ageing
options_after: Placental thickness below 1 cm is linked to fetal hydrops in the source
A placenta thinner than 1 cm is associated with placental insufficiency
A placenta thicker than 4 cm is associated with fetal hydrops and congenital infection
Maternal diabetes appears in both the too-thin and too-thick lists in the source
A placenta thicker than 4 cm is characteristically normal placental ageing
updates.explanation: The source lists too-thin placenta below 1 cm with placental insufficiency, maternal hypertension, maternal diabetes, trisomy 13, trisomy 18, and toxemia of pregnancy. Too-thick placenta over 4 cm is linked to fetal hydrops, maternal diabetes, severe maternal anaemia, congenital fetal cancer, congenital infection, and abruption. Maternal diabetes therefore appears in both lists. Thickness over 4 cm is not described as a normal ageing feature.

updates.question_text: Regarding placenta accreta spectrum, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: There are no risk factors for placenta accreta spectrum listed in the source
Sonographic signs include placental vascular channels extending into the myometrium with turbulent flow
Myometrial thinning below 1 mm is another sign
Placenta accreta is the rarest and most severe form, with villi penetrating beyond serosa
Placenta percreta means villi are limited to the endometrium and never reach serosa
options_after: Placenta accreta spectrum is described as occurring independently of recognised risk factors
Sonographic signs include placental vascular channels extending into the myometrium with turbulent flow
Myometrial thinning below 1 mm is another sign
Placenta accreta is the rarest and most severe form, with villi penetrating beyond serosa
Placenta percreta means villi are limited to the endometrium and will not reach serosa
updates.explanation: The source lists prior caesarean section, placenta previa, and advanced maternal age as risk factors, so the absence of risk factors is incorrect. Sonographic findings include a moth-eaten or Swiss-cheese placenta, vascular channels extending into myometrium with turbulent Doppler flow, and myometrium thinner than 1 mm. Placenta accreta is the most common and mildest form, with villi attaching to myometrium without invasion. Percreta is the severe form that penetrates through the myometrium or beyond the serosa.

updates.question_text: Regarding placental chorioangioma, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is the most common malignant tumour of the placenta
It is a hamartoma and the most common benign placental tumour
It is usually a diffuse calcified placental process without a mass
It is diagnosed when a placental mass has no Doppler flow
It is always clinically significant regardless of size
options_after: It is the most common malignant tumour of the placenta
It is a hamartoma and the most common benign placental tumour
It is usually a diffuse calcified placental process without a mass
It is diagnosed when a placental mass lacks Doppler flow
It is characteristically clinically significant despite variation in size
updates.explanation: The source describes chorioangioma as essentially a placental hamartoma and the most common benign placental tumour. It is usually a well-circumscribed hypoechoic mass near the cord insertion. Doppler flow within the mass pulsating at the fetal heart rate is diagnostic and helps distinguish it from haematoma. Most are insignificant, but large lesions over 4 cm or multiple lesions can cause platelet sequestration and high-output failure with hydrops.

updates.question_text: Regarding vasa previa, nuchal cord, and umbilical cord cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Vasa previa is fetal vessels crossing or nearly crossing the internal cervical os
Type 1 vasa previa relates to fetal vessels connecting to a velamentous cord insertion in the main placental body
Type 2 vasa previa relates to bilobed placenta or succenturiate lobe
Nuchal cord means the cord is wrapped around the fetal neck
Umbilical cord cysts persisting into the second or third trimester have no association with trisomy 18 or 13 in the source
options_after: Vasa previa is fetal vessels crossing or nearly crossing the internal cervical os
Type 1 vasa previa relates to fetal vessels connecting to a velamentous cord insertion in the main placental body
Type 2 vasa previa relates to bilobed placenta or succenturiate lobe
Nuchal cord means the cord is wrapped around the fetal neck
Umbilical cord cysts persisting into the second or third trimester lack association with trisomy 18 or 13 in the source
updates.explanation: The source defines vasa previa as fetal vessels crossing or nearly crossing the internal cervical os and notes it is more common with twins and variant placental morphology. Type 1 involves vessels connecting to a velamentous cord insertion in the main placental body. Type 2 involves bilobed placenta or succenturiate lobe. Nuchal cord is cord around the fetal neck, while persistent cord cysts into later pregnancy may be associated with trisomy 18 and 13.

updates.question_text: Regarding true umbilical cord cyst terminology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: An omphalomesenteric duct cyst is usually peripheral
An allantoic cyst is usually peripheral
An allantoic cyst is usually central
Cord cysts are never multiple
Cord cysts occur in 30% of pregnancies in the source
options_after: An omphalomesenteric duct cyst is usually peripheral
An allantoic cyst is usually peripheral
An allantoic cyst is usually central
Cord cysts are not multiple
Cord cysts occur in 30% of pregnancies in the source
updates.explanation: The source states that umbilical cord cysts are common, seen about 3% of the time, and are usually single but can be multiple. It divides true cysts into named types: omphalomesenteric duct cyst is usually peripheral and allantoic cyst is usually central. Persistence into the second or third trimester should prompt a careful search for other abnormalities. The source does not give a 30% incidence.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound findings concerning for Down syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: More than half of affected fetuses have congenital heart disease, most commonly AV canal and VSD in the source
Duodenal atresia is the most common intra-abdominal pathology associated with Down syndrome
Nuchal translucency greater than 3 mm in the first trimester is concerning
Nuchal fold thickness greater than 6 mm in the second trimester is concerning
Choroid plexus cyst is highly specific for Down syndrome and requires no other survey
options_after: More than half of affected fetuses have congenital heart disease, most commonly AV canal and VSD in the source
Duodenal atresia is the most common intra-abdominal pathology associated with Down syndrome
Nuchal translucency greater than 3 mm in the first trimester is concerning
Nuchal fold thickness greater than 6 mm in the second trimester is concerning
Choroid plexus cyst is highly specific for Down syndrome and does not require other survey
updates.explanation: The source lists congenital heart disease, most commonly AV canal and VSD, in more than half of Down syndrome fetuses. It also lists duodenal atresia as the most common intra-abdominal pathology associated with Down syndrome. First-trimester nuchal translucency over 3 mm and second-trimester nuchal fold thickness over 6 mm are concerning markers. Choroid plexus cyst is nonspecific, seen more with trisomy 18, and should prompt a careful search rather than being specific for Down syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding nuchal translucency measurement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is measured between 9 and 12 weeks in the source
The anechoic space between the neck or occiput and the skin should be less than 3 mm
Neck position is irrelevant and flexion or extension cannot create false positives
Ideal positioning includes neutral neck, mid-sagittal head position, visualised nasal bone, and clear skin edge
Maternal serum free beta-hCG and PAPP-A are also analysed
options_after: It is measured between 9 and 12 weeks in the source
The anechoic space between the neck or occiput and the skin should be less than 3 mm
Neck position is irrelevant and flexion or extension will not create false positives
Ideal positioning includes neutral neck, mid-sagittal head position, visualised nasal bone, and clear skin edge
Maternal serum free beta-hCG and PAPP-A are also analysed
updates.explanation: The source states that nuchal translucency is measured between 9 and 12 weeks and should be less than 3 mm. Positioning is important to avoid false positives; the ideal is a neutral neck, nasal bone visualised, mid-sagittal head position, and a well-defined skin edge. The maternal blood sample is also analysed for free beta-hCG and pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A. Measurements over 3 mm are associated with Down syndrome or other chromosomal abnormalities.

updates.question_text: Regarding nonspecific Down syndrome markers in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Short femur length is nonspecific
Echogenic bowel is nonspecific and can be seen with obstruction, infection, cystic fibrosis, and ischaemia
Echogenic intracardiac focus is nonspecific but increases Down syndrome risk
Choroid plexus cyst should prompt close survey for other findings and is normal if isolated in the source
Nuchal fold thickness over 6 mm is specific for Down syndrome and cannot occur with Turner syndrome
options_after: Short femur length is nonspecific
Echogenic bowel is nonspecific and can be seen with obstruction, infection, cystic fibrosis, and ischaemia
Echogenic intracardiac focus is nonspecific but increases Down syndrome risk
Choroid plexus cyst should prompt close survey for other findings and is normal if isolated in the source
Nuchal fold thickness over 6 mm is specific for Down syndrome and will not occur with Turner syndrome
updates.explanation: The source labels short femur length and echogenic bowel as nonspecific. Echogenic bowel may be seen with obstruction, infection, cystic fibrosis, ischaemia, and other conditions. Echogenic intracardiac focus is also nonspecific but increases Down syndrome risk. Choroid plexus cyst is nonspecific, seen more with trisomy 18, and normal if isolated after close survey; nuchal fold thickening can also be seen with Turner syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding severe placenta accreta spectrum and chorioangioma complications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Placenta percreta is the mildest form and does not extend beyond endometrium
Placenta percreta can penetrate through myometrium or beyond serosa and may invade bladder or bowel
Chorioangioma has no internal flow and is therefore identical to haematoma
Large or multiple chorioangiomas can sequester platelets and cause high-output failure with hydrops
Placenta accreta spectrum can cause life-threatening bleeding and may require hysterectomy
options_after: Placenta percreta is the mildest form and does not extend beyond endometrium
Placenta percreta can penetrate through myometrium or beyond serosa and may invade bladder or bowel
Chorioangioma lacks internal flow and is therefore closely comparable to haematoma
Large or multiple chorioangiomas can sequester platelets and cause high-output failure with hydrops
Placenta accreta spectrum can cause life-threatening bleeding and may require hysterectomy
updates.explanation: The source describes percreta as the severe form in which villi penetrate through the myometrium or beyond serosa, sometimes invading bladder or bowel. Accreta spectrum can cause life-threatening bleeding and may require hysterectomy. Chorioangioma is distinguished from haematoma by pulsating Doppler flow, and large or multiple lesions can sequester platelets and cause high-output failure with hydrops. The statement making percreta the mildest form reverses the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding amniotic band syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It can result from amnion disruption with fetal parts becoming entangled in fibrous bands
It requires a normal intact amniotic sac and normal fetal movement
It is primarily diagnosed by increased MCA peak systolic velocity
It is best recognised only after delivery and never on fetal ultrasound
It can be shown as amputated digits or limbs on radiography, or bands entangling fetal limbs on ultrasound
options_after: It can result from amnion disruption with fetal parts becoming entangled in fibrous bands
It requires a normal intact amniotic sac and normal fetal movement
It is primarily diagnosed by increased MCA peak systolic velocity
It is best recognised primarily after delivery and not on fetal ultrasound
It can be shown as amputated digits or limbs on radiography, or bands entangling fetal limbs on ultrasound
updates.explanation: The source explains amniotic band syndrome as a consequence of disrupted amnion, allowing the fetus or fetal parts to become caught in fibrous bands in the chorionic cavity. It can produce severe deformity, including limb or digit amputation. It may be shown after birth on radiography or antenatally by ultrasound showing bands entangling fetal arms or legs. MCA Doppler is discussed for anaemia and hydrops risk, not as the defining test for amniotic bands.

updates.question_text: Regarding ventriculomegaly, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ventriculomegaly has no causes other than aqueduct stenosis
Aqueductal stenosis is the most common cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus in a neonate
Ventricular atrium diameter over 5 mm is too big in the source
Dangling choroid is normal when the choroid hangs more than 10 mm from the wall
Ventricular atrium diameter over 10 mm is too big
options_after: Ventriculomegaly lacks causes other than aqueduct stenosis
Aqueductal stenosis is the most common cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus in a neonate
Ventricular atrium diameter over 5 mm is too big in the source
Dangling choroid is normal when the choroid hangs more than 10 mm from the wall
Ventricular atrium diameter over 10 mm is too big
updates.explanation: The source states that ventriculomegaly has multiple causes, including communicating and non-communicating hydrocephalus and cerebral atrophy. Aqueductal stenosis is the most common cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus in a neonate. A ventricular atrium diameter greater than 10 mm is too large. Dangling choroid more than 3 mm off the wall is also too large in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding selected congenital fetal findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Anencephaly is compatible with life in the source
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is nearly always right-sided
Anencephaly is absence of the cranial vault and brain above the orbits
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is associated with pulmonary hypoplasia and malrotation
Echogenic intracardiac focus is usually papillary muscle calcification, often in the left ventricle
options_after: Anencephaly is compatible with life in the source
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is nearly characteristically right-sided
Anencephaly is absence of the cranial vault and brain above the orbits
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is associated with pulmonary hypoplasia and malrotation
Echogenic intracardiac focus is usually papillary muscle calcification, often in the left ventricle
updates.explanation: The source describes anencephaly as absence of cranial vault and brain above the orbits and states that it is incompatible with life. Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is nearly all left-sided, about 85%, and has high mortality because of pulmonary hypoplasia. The source also states that all affected children are malrotated. Echogenic intracardiac focus is papillary muscle calcification, usually in the left ventricle.

updates.question_text: Regarding sacrococcygeal teratoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the most common tumour of the fetus or infant
It is always entirely internal to the pelvis
It can cause high-output cardiac failure
It never causes delivery complications
It is always malignant at birth
options_after: It is the most common tumour of the fetus or infant
It is characteristically predominantly internal to the pelvis
It can cause high-output cardiac failure
It will not cause delivery complications
It is characteristically malignant at birth
updates.explanation: The source describes sacrococcygeal teratoma as the most common tumour of the fetus or infant. It may be solid or cystic, often large, and can cause mass effect, nerve compression, high-output cardiac failure, premature delivery, dystocia, and tumour haemorrhage. It is usually benign at birth, about 80%, with higher malignant potential in older infants. Its location can be external, internal, or both internal and external.

updates.question_text: Regarding HELLP syndrome, which statement is correct?
options_before: HELLP stands for hyperglycaemia, elevated lipase, and low protein
It is the mildest form of pre-eclampsia
It is typically shown as hydronephrosis in the pregnant patient
It may be shown as a subcapsular hepatic haematoma in a pregnant or recently pregnant patient
It has no association with disseminated intravascular coagulation in the source
options_after: HELLP stands for hyperglycaemia, elevated lipase, and low protein
It is the mildest form of pre-eclampsia
It is typically shown as hydronephrosis in the pregnant patient
It may be shown as a subcapsular hepatic haematoma in a pregnant or recently pregnant patient
It lacks association with disseminated intravascular coagulation in the source
updates.explanation: HELLP stands for haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets. The source calls it the most severe form of pre-eclampsia and notes that 20–40% can develop disseminated intravascular coagulation. If shown radiologically, the source expects a subcapsular hepatic haematoma in a pregnant or recently pregnant patient. Hydronephrosis is discussed separately as common in pregnancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding peripartum cardiomyopathy, Sheehan syndrome, and postpartum ovarian vein thrombophlebitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Peripartum cardiomyopathy occurs only in the first trimester
Peripartum cardiomyopathy MRI can show global depressed function and non-vascular subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement
Sheehan syndrome is postpartum pituitary apoplexy after large-volume haemorrhage and hypotension
Ovarian vein thrombophlebitis can cause postpartum fever and is more often right-sided
Sheehan syndrome is defined by a large enhancing ovarian mass
options_after: Peripartum cardiomyopathy occurs primarily in the first trimester
Peripartum cardiomyopathy MRI can show global depressed function and non-vascular subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement
Sheehan syndrome is postpartum pituitary apoplexy after large-volume haemorrhage and hypotension
Ovarian vein thrombophlebitis can cause postpartum fever and is more often right-sided
Sheehan syndrome is defined by a large enhancing ovarian mass
updates.explanation: The source describes peripartum cardiomyopathy as a dilated cardiomyopathy occurring from the last month of pregnancy to 5 months postpartum, not only in the first trimester. MRI findings include globally depressed function and non-vascular-territory subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement. Sheehan syndrome is postpartum pituitary apoplexy after large-volume haemorrhage and acute hypotension, with variable MRI appearance. Ovarian vein thrombophlebitis can cause postpartum fever and is right-sided much more often than left-sided.

updates.question_text: Regarding retained products of conception and postpartum endometritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Retained products of conception classically present with continued bleeding after delivery or induced abortion
Absence of Doppler flow excludes retained products of conception
Endometritis requires a completely thin homogeneous endometrium with no fluid or air
Retained products are unrelated to placenta accreta in the source
Postpartum endometritis history may include fever, uterine tenderness, recent caesarean section, or prolonged labour
options_after: Retained products of conception classically present with continued bleeding after delivery or induced abortion
Absence of Doppler flow excludes retained products of conception
Endometritis requires a completely thin homogeneous endometrium without fluid or air
Retained products are unrelated to placenta accreta in the source
Postpartum endometritis history may include fever, uterine tenderness, recent caesarean section, or prolonged labour
updates.explanation: The source gives continued bleeding after delivery or induced abortion as the typical retained-products history. The common appearance is an echogenic mass in the uterine cavity, with variable flow that may be abundant or absent. It can also appear as irregular thickening over 10 mm with reflective fetal parts, and associations include medical termination, second-trimester miscarriage, and placenta accreta. Endometritis may present with fever, uterine tenderness, recent caesarean section, or prolonged labour and a thickened heterogeneous endometrium with or without fluid or air.

updates.question_text: Regarding twin growth assessment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal growth charts can be used in the first and second trimesters, but not the third
More than 15% difference in fetal weight or abdominal circumference is significant
Femur length is never useful for twin age estimation later in pregnancy
Monochorionic twins share a placenta
Abnormal placental vascular connections can transfer blood from one fetus to the other
options_after: Normal growth charts can be used in the first and second trimesters, but not the third
More than 15% difference in fetal weight or abdominal circumference is significant
Femur length is not useful for twin age estimation later in pregnancy
Monochorionic twins share a placenta
Abnormal placental vascular connections can transfer blood from one fetus to the other
updates.explanation: The source states that normal growth charts can be used in the first and second trimesters, but not the third, and femur length tends to work best for twin age later in pregnancy. It defines over 15% difference in fetal weight or abdominal circumference as significant. Monochorionic twins share a placenta, and abnormal vascular connections can allow blood transfer between fetuses. The omitted facts are true in the source, but this question focuses on the selected statements after the distractors are considered.

updates.question_text: Regarding twin reversed arterial perfusion syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: TRAP is unrelated to monochorionic placentation
The acardiac twin is structurally normal and supports the pump twin
The pump twin is always absent
Umbilical artery flow can be directed toward the acardiac twin
Umbilical vein flow can be away from the acardiac twin
options_after: TRAP is unrelated to monochorionic placentation
The acardiac twin is structurally normal and supports the pump twin
The pump twin is characteristically absent
Umbilical artery flow can be directed toward the acardiac twin
Umbilical vein flow can be away from the acardiac twin
updates.explanation: The source describes TRAP as a severe variant of TTTS physiology in monochorionic twins, with a pump twin supporting an acardiac twin. The acardiac twin is severely malformed and lacks a functional heart. Doppler can show umbilical artery flow toward the acardiac twin and umbilical vein flow away from it. The pump twin may do well unless cardiac strain becomes excessive.

updates.question_text: Regarding fetal hydrops causes and Doppler clues, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Causes listed include TORCH infections, Turner syndrome, twin-related conditions, and alpha thalassaemia
Hydrops requires all four of pleural effusion, ascites, pericardial effusion, and subcutaneous oedema
MCA peak systolic flow can increase before hydrops in fetal anaemia
Thickened placenta excludes hydrops
Hydrops is diagnosed by normal amniotic fluid and normal body wall
options_after: Causes listed include TORCH infections, Turner syndrome, twin-related conditions, and alpha thalassaemia
Hydrops requires most four of pleural effusion, ascites, pericardial effusion, and subcutaneous oedema
MCA peak systolic flow can increase before hydrops in fetal anaemia
Thickened placenta excludes hydrops
Hydrops is diagnosed by normal amniotic fluid and normal body wall
updates.explanation: The source lists causes including Rh sensitisation, TORCH infections, Turner syndrome, twin-related problems, and alpha thalassaemia. Diagnosis requires two of the listed fluid or oedema findings, not all four. MCA Doppler can show increased peak systolic flow before hydrops, particularly in fetal anaemia. A thickened placenta can be a clue rather than an exclusion.

updates.question_text: Regarding Chiari II and open neural tube defect signs, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The banana sign is loss of normal bilobed cerebellar shape
The lemon sign is flat or concave frontal bones
The lemon sign is specific enough that it cannot be seen in Dandy-Walker, absent corpus callosum, or encephalocele
Hydrocephalus is seen later in gestation and only when severe in the source
The banana sign is more sensitive and specific than the lemon sign
options_after: The banana sign is loss of normal bilobed cerebellar shape
The lemon sign is flat or concave frontal bones
The lemon sign is specific enough that it will not be seen in Dandy-Walker, absent corpus callosum, or encephalocele
Hydrocephalus is seen later in gestation and only when severe in the source
The banana sign is more sensitive and specific than the lemon sign
updates.explanation: The source defines the banana sign as loss of the normal bilobed cerebellar shape and the lemon sign as flat or concave frontal bones. It states that the banana sign is more sensitive and specific. The lemon sign is less sensitive and specific and can be seen with Dandy-Walker, absent corpus callosum, encephalocele, and other entities. Hydrocephalus can occur later in gestation when Chiari II with open neural tube defect is severe.

updates.question_text: Regarding fetal soft markers and congenital anomaly associations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Echogenic intracardiac focus is seen only in Down syndrome and never in the normal population
Echogenic bowel should be called abnormal only if less bright than liver
Echogenic bowel differential includes cystic fibrosis, trisomies, viral infection, and bowel atresia
Short femur below percentile should never raise skeletal dysplasia
Posterior urethral valves can be shown by bilateral hydronephrosis on fetal ultrasound or third-trimester MRI
options_after: Echogenic intracardiac focus is seen primarily in Down syndrome and not in the normal population
Echogenic bowel should be called abnormal primarily if less bright than liver
Echogenic bowel differential includes cystic fibrosis, trisomies, viral infection, and bowel atresia
Short femur below percentile should not raise skeletal dysplasia
Posterior urethral valves can be shown by bilateral hydronephrosis on fetal ultrasound or third-trimester MRI
updates.explanation: The source states that echogenic intracardiac focus is common in the normal population but occurs more often in Down syndrome and trisomy 13. Echogenic bowel is concerning when it is as echogenic as bone, and the differential includes cystic fibrosis, Down syndrome and other trisomies, viral infections, and bowel atresia. A short femur below percentile can raise skeletal dysplasia. Posterior urethral valves can appear as bilateral hydronephrosis on fetal ultrasound or third-trimester MRI.

updates.question_text: Regarding congenital diaphragmatic hernia and fetal cardiac findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is associated with pulmonary hypoplasia
Nearly all congenital diaphragmatic hernias are left-sided in the source
All affected children are normally rotated, so malrotation excludes the diagnosis
Echogenic intracardiac focus is usually papillary muscle calcification
Fetal tachycardia is defined as heart rate over 180 bpm and bradycardia as under 100 bpm
options_after: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is associated with pulmonary hypoplasia
Nearly all congenital diaphragmatic hernias are left-sided in the source
Most affected children are normally rotated, so malrotation excludes the diagnosis
Echogenic intracardiac focus is usually papillary muscle calcification
Fetal tachycardia is defined as heart rate over 180 bpm and bradycardia as under 100 bpm
updates.explanation: The source states that congenital diaphragmatic hernia is nearly always left-sided and is high mortality because of pulmonary hypoplasia. It also states that affected children are malrotated. Echogenic intracardiac focus is usually papillary muscle calcification, usually left ventricular, and is often incidental but associated with trisomies. The fetal heart-rate thresholds in the source are tachycardia over 180 bpm and bradycardia under 100 bpm.

updates.question_text: Regarding postpartum retained products of conception, which statement is correct?
options_before: Doppler flow is always absent, so any vascularity excludes the diagnosis
The source states that the usual appearance is a completely empty uterine cavity
It occurs only after spontaneous first-trimester miscarriage
It has no association with placenta accreta
The most common appearance is an echogenic mass within the uterine cavity, with variable flow
options_after: Doppler flow is characteristically absent, so any vascularity excludes the diagnosis
The source states that the usual appearance is a completely empty uterine cavity
It occurs primarily after spontaneous first-trimester miscarriage
It lacks association with placenta accreta
The most common appearance is an echogenic mass within the uterine cavity, with variable flow
updates.explanation: The source gives continued bleeding after delivery or induced abortion as the classic story. The most common appearance is an echogenic mass within the uterine cavity. Doppler flow is variable, and the lesion may have a lot of flow or none. Associations include medical termination, second-trimester miscarriage, and placenta accreta.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging follow-up of a suspected neonatal adrenal haemorrhage, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Serial ultrasound is preferred for follow-up
A stable or enlarging complex mass proves haemorrhage
Biopsy is the standard first-line test in every suspected case
Persistent arterial enhancement is expected as the lesion involutes
Reduction in size over time helps distinguish haemorrhage from cystic neuroblastoma
options_after: Serial ultrasound is preferred for follow-up
A stable or enlarging complex mass proves haemorrhage
Biopsy is the standard first-line test in most suspected cases
Persistent arterial enhancement is expected as the lesion involutes
Reduction in size over time helps distinguish haemorrhage from cystic neuroblastoma
updates.explanation: The source favours serial ultrasound to follow suspected neonatal adrenal haemorrhage. A lesion that shrinks over time supports haemorrhage and helps separate it from cystic neuroblastoma. Stability, growth, or persistent vascularity would weaken the diagnosis rather than prove it.

updates.question_text: Regarding congenital adrenal hyperplasia on ultrasound, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The adrenal gland may be enlarged
A large macroscopic fat component is the key diagnostic feature
The adrenal contour may look wrinkled or cerebriform
A central bright layer may be lost
The gland should always be smaller than normal
options_after: The adrenal gland may be enlarged
A large macroscopic fat component is the key diagnostic feature
The adrenal contour may look wrinkled or cerebriform
A central bright layer may be lost
The gland should characteristically be smaller than normal
updates.explanation: The source describes adrenal hyperplasia as a large adrenal gland with a wrinkled or cerebriform contour. Size criteria include gland length greater than 20 mm and limb thickness greater than 4 mm, and the central bright layer may be lost. A fat-containing mass would point away from hyperplasia and towards a different adrenal lesion such as myelolipoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding Cushing disease and Cushing syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cushing disease is caused by a primary adrenal adenoma in all cases
Cushing disease refers to pituitary ACTH adenoma
Adrenal adenoma always causes bilateral adrenal hyperplasia
Cushing syndrome can result from chronic steroid administration
Cushing syndrome excludes ACTH-producing tumours outside the pituitary
options_after: Cushing disease is caused by a primary adrenal adenoma in most cases
Cushing disease refers to pituitary ACTH adenoma
Adrenal adenoma characteristically causes bilateral adrenal hyperplasia
Cushing syndrome can result from chronic steroid administration
Cushing syndrome excludes ACTH-producing tumours outside the pituitary
updates.explanation: The source separates Cushing disease from the broader Cushing syndrome: Cushing disease is due to a pituitary ACTH adenoma, while Cushing syndrome has multiple causes including ACTH tumours, adrenal adenoma, primary adrenal hyperplasia, and chronic steroid use. A primary adrenal adenoma does not require bilateral adrenal hyperplasia to be present.

updates.question_text: Regarding infradiaphragmatic extralobar sequestration as an adrenal mimic, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is always located inside the adrenal cortex
It may appear as a heterogeneous suprarenal mass
A systemic arterial supply from the aorta supports the diagnosis
Neonatal respiratory distress or cyanosis can be a clinical clue
It is distinguished from adrenal lesions by macroscopic adrenal fat
options_after: It is characteristically located inside the adrenal cortex
It may appear as a heterogeneous suprarenal mass
A systemic arterial supply from the aorta supports the diagnosis
Neonatal respiratory distress or cyanosis can be a clinical clue
It is distinguished from adrenal lesions by macroscopic adrenal fat
updates.explanation: The source highlights infradiaphragmatic extralobar sequestration as an adrenal mass mimic. It may present as a heterogeneous suprarenal mass, with a systemic arterial supply from the aorta, and neonatal respiratory distress or cyanosis can be a clue. It is not an adrenal cortical lesion and macroscopic adrenal fat is not the diagnostic discriminator.

updates.question_text: Regarding adrenal washout CT, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Relative washout greater than 10% is the source threshold for adenoma
Absolute washout greater than 60% supports adenoma
Metastases from renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma cannot mimic adenoma washout
Washout is calculated only on unenhanced images
Relative washout greater than 40% supports adenoma
options_after: Relative washout greater than 10% is the source threshold for adenoma
Absolute washout greater than 60% supports adenoma
Metastases from renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma will not mimic adenoma washout
Washout is calculated primarily on unenhanced images
Relative washout greater than 40% supports adenoma
updates.explanation: The source uses absolute washout greater than 60% and relative washout greater than 40% as adenoma-supporting thresholds. It also warns that hypervascular metastases, including from renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma, and phaeochromocytoma can mimic adenoma washout. Washout assessment depends on contrast-enhanced delayed imaging, not just the unenhanced acquisition.

updates.question_text: Regarding very high enhancement in an adrenal mass, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Portal venous attenuation above 120 HU is diagnostic of lipid-rich adenoma
Arterial enhancement above 120 HU excludes phaeochromocytoma
High arterial or portal venous attenuation above 120 HU is typical of benign myelolipoma
An adrenal lesion above about 120 HU on arterial or portal venous phase should not be treated as an adenoma by washout alone
High enhancement means the lesion cannot be metastatic
options_after: Portal venous attenuation above 120 HU is diagnostic of lipid-rich adenoma
Arterial enhancement above 120 HU excludes phaeochromocytoma
High arterial or portal venous attenuation above 120 HU is typical of benign myelolipoma
An adrenal lesion above about 120 HU on arterial or portal venous phase should not be treated as an adenoma by washout alone
High enhancement means the lesion will not be metastatic
updates.explanation: The source warns that an adrenal lesion measuring more than about 120 HU on arterial or portal venous phase should not simply be labelled an adenoma. Phaeochromocytoma and hypervascular metastases can show adenoma-like washout behaviour. The point is to prevent overconfidence in washout criteria when enhancement is extremely high.

updates.question_text: Regarding adrenal lesion size and morphology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Small homogeneous lesions below 3 cm are more typical of adenoma
Every adrenal lesion above 4 cm is benign
Lesions above 4 cm have a substantial malignancy risk in the source
Lesions above 6 cm are usually ignored if they are homogeneous
Myelolipoma and phaeochromocytoma are important exceptions to simple size-based rules
options_after: Small homogeneous lesions below 3 cm are more typical of adenoma
Most adrenal lesions above 4 cm is benign
Lesions above 4 cm have a substantial malignancy risk in the source
Lesions above 6 cm are usually ignored if they are homogeneous
Myelolipoma and phaeochromocytoma are important exceptions to simple size-based rules
updates.explanation: The source describes adenomas as commonly small and homogeneous, often below 3 cm. It also gives high malignancy risk estimates for larger adrenal masses, especially above 4 cm and 6 cm, while noting exceptions such as myelolipoma and phaeochromocytoma. Size therefore contributes to risk assessment but is not interpreted in isolation.

updates.question_text: Regarding functional adrenal adenomas, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Conn syndrome is caused by excessive cortisol secretion
Functional adenomas may cause Cushing syndrome
Conn syndrome is related to excessive aldosterone production
Conn syndrome is always caused by bilateral cortical carcinoma
Functional adrenal adenomas are excluded if they are small
options_after: Conn syndrome is caused by excessive cortisol secretion
Functional adenomas may cause Cushing syndrome
Conn syndrome is related to excessive aldosterone production
Conn syndrome is characteristically caused by bilateral cortical carcinoma
Functional adrenal adenomas are excluded if they are small
updates.explanation: The source links functional adrenal adenomas to Cushing syndrome and Conn syndrome. Conn syndrome reflects excessive aldosterone production and is commonly related to a benign adenoma. Lesion size alone does not exclude hormonal activity.

updates.question_text: Regarding phaeochromocytoma imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The classic lesion is a heterogeneous avidly enhancing adrenal mass
Phaeochromocytoma is always below 10 HU on unenhanced CT
Marked T2 hyperintensity may be seen
Macroscopic fat is the defining imaging feature
Large size above 3 cm is common in the source description
options_after: The classic lesion is a heterogeneous avidly enhancing adrenal mass
Phaeochromocytoma is characteristically below 10 HU on unenhanced CT
Marked T2 hyperintensity may be seen
Macroscopic fat is the defining imaging feature
Large size above 3 cm is common in the source description
updates.explanation: The source describes phaeochromocytoma as often larger than 3 cm, variable in appearance, classically heterogeneous and avidly enhancing, and potentially bright on T2-weighted MRI. It is not defined by lipid-rich attenuation or bulk fat. Very high enhancement is part of why it can be confused with adenoma if washout criteria are used uncritically.

updates.question_text: Regarding extra-adrenal phaeochromocytoma and nuclear imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The organ of Zuckerkandl lies at the carotid bifurcation in this source
Octreotide is always superior to MIBG for phaeochromocytoma in this source
Extra-adrenal lesions may arise at the organ of Zuckerkandl near the inferior mesenteric artery
MIBG is described as better than octreotide for phaeochromocytoma imaging
Extra-adrenal disease is excluded by normal adrenal morphology
options_after: The organ of Zuckerkandl lies at the carotid bifurcation in this source
Octreotide is characteristically superior to MIBG for phaeochromocytoma in this source
Extra-adrenal lesions may arise at the organ of Zuckerkandl near the inferior mesenteric artery
MIBG is described as better than octreotide for phaeochromocytoma imaging
Extra-adrenal disease is excluded by normal adrenal morphology
updates.explanation: The source places the organ of Zuckerkandl near the inferior mesenteric artery and identifies it as a site for extra-adrenal phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma. It also states that MIBG performs better than octreotide for phaeochromocytoma imaging. Normal adrenal morphology therefore does not exclude extra-adrenal disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding adrenal cysts, metastases and adrenal calcification, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adrenal cysts should have a thin wall and no enhancement
Adrenal metastases commonly arise from lung, breast and melanoma primaries
Adrenal calcification can follow trauma or infection
Lipid-poor adenomas are always confidently separated from metastases on routine CT alone
Calcification proves that an adrenal lesion is benign
options_after: Adrenal cysts should have a thin wall and no enhancement
Adrenal metastases commonly arise from lung, breast and melanoma primaries
Adrenal calcification can follow trauma or infection
Lipid-poor adenomas are characteristically confidently separated from metastases on routine CT alone
Calcification proves that an adrenal lesion is benign
updates.explanation: The source describes adrenal cysts as thin-walled non-enhancing lesions and lists lung, breast and melanoma among common metastatic sources. It also notes that calcification may follow trauma or infection such as tuberculosis as well as tumours. Routine CT is not always definitive for lipid-poor adenoma versus metastasis, and calcification is not proof of benignity.

updates.question_text: Regarding adrenal collision tumours and problem-solving imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A lesion can contain more than one pathological component
All adrenal lesions should be assumed to be adenomas if any part loses signal on opposed-phase MRI
FDG PET or MRI can help when imaging features are mixed or discordant
Collision tumour is a synonym for a congenital adrenal cyst
Problem-solving is unnecessary if the patient has a known malignancy
options_after: A lesion can contain more than one pathological component
Most adrenal lesions should be assumed to be adenomas if any part loses signal on opposed-phase MRI
FDG PET or MRI can help when imaging features are mixed or discordant
Collision tumour is a synonym for a congenital adrenal cyst
Problem-solving is unnecessary if the patient has a known malignancy
updates.explanation: The source mentions adrenal collision tumours and notes that FDG PET and MRI can help when appearances are mixed. A collision lesion may include an adenoma component and another lesion, so partial signal drop-out does not automatically solve the diagnosis. Known malignancy increases the need for careful characterisation rather than removing it.

updates.question_text: Regarding differentiating adrenal haemorrhage from cystic neuroblastoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cystic neuroblastoma should always disappear within days
Macroscopic fat is the expected discriminator
A vascular solid component supports haemorrhage
Interval decrease in size supports haemorrhage
MRI or serial ultrasound can help when the diagnosis is uncertain
options_after: Cystic neuroblastoma should characteristically disappear within days
Macroscopic fat is the expected discriminator
A vascular solid component supports haemorrhage
Interval decrease in size supports haemorrhage
MRI or serial ultrasound can help when the diagnosis is uncertain
updates.explanation: The source recommends serial ultrasound, and sometimes MRI, to separate adrenal haemorrhage from cystic neuroblastoma. Haemorrhage should involute over time. A persistent vascular solid component or failure to shrink would raise concern for tumour rather than simple haemorrhage.

updates.question_text: Regarding a rapid review approach to adrenal lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lipid-rich adenoma is supported by non-contrast attenuation below 10 HU
Bulk fat strongly supports myelolipoma
Every bilateral adrenal mass in an adult is congenital hyperplasia
A neonatal adrenal mass that enlarges on serial ultrasound favours uncomplicated haemorrhage
Phaeochromocytoma can be avidly enhancing and T2 bright
options_after: Lipid-rich adenoma is supported by non-contrast attenuation below 10 HU
Bulk fat strongly supports myelolipoma
Most bilateral adrenal masses in an adult is congenital hyperplasia
A neonatal adrenal mass that enlarges on serial ultrasound favours uncomplicated haemorrhage
Phaeochromocytoma can be avidly enhancing and T2 bright
updates.explanation: The source provides a practical imaging pattern list: low attenuation supports lipid-rich adenoma, bulk fat supports myelolipoma, and phaeochromocytoma can enhance avidly and be T2 bright. A neonatal adrenal mass that shrinks on serial ultrasound supports haemorrhage; enlargement would raise concern for another process. Bilateral adult adrenal masses are not automatically congenital hyperplasia.

updates.question_text: Regarding MEN1, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Primary hyperparathyroidism is a major feature
Medullary thyroid carcinoma is the defining thyroid tumour
Pituitary adenoma is part of the syndrome
Phaeochromocytoma is the dominant endocrine tumour in nearly every patient
Gastrinoma is a recognised pancreatic/duodenal tumour association
options_after: Primary hyperparathyroidism is a major feature
Medullary thyroid carcinoma is the defining thyroid tumour
Pituitary adenoma is part of the syndrome
Phaeochromocytoma is the dominant endocrine tumour in most patients
Gastrinoma is a recognised pancreatic/duodenal tumour association
updates.explanation: The source summarises MEN1 with the classic parathyroid, pituitary and pancreatic/duodenal tumour pattern. It specifically highlights parathyroid hyperplasia/primary hyperparathyroidism, pituitary adenoma, and gastrinoma. Medullary thyroid carcinoma and phaeochromocytoma point toward MEN2 rather than MEN1.

updates.question_text: Regarding colloid nodules, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: They are defined by diffuse thyroid uptake on radioiodine imaging
They are the same entity as Riedel thyroiditis
They are diagnostic of medullary thyroid carcinoma
Comet-tail artefact is a recognised feature
They are always malignant if cystic
options_after: They are defined by diffuse thyroid uptake on radioiodine imaging
They are the same entity as Riedel thyroiditis
They are diagnostic of medullary thyroid carcinoma
Comet-tail artefact is a recognised feature
They are characteristically malignant if cystic
updates.explanation: The source associates colloid nodules with comet-tail artefact. This is a benign-leaning ultrasound pattern rather than a diagnostic sign of medullary thyroid carcinoma or Riedel thyroiditis. Cystic change in this context is not automatically malignant.

updates.question_text: Regarding thyroid adenoma and multinodular goitre, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A hyperfunctioning toxic adenoma can appear hot with colder background thyroid
Multinodular goitre is excluded if there are compressive symptoms
Multinodular goitre can produce asymmetry and compressive symptoms
In North America, multinodular goitre and Graves disease are common causes of goitre
Thyroid adenoma is always a cystic non-functioning lesion
options_after: A hyperfunctioning toxic adenoma can appear hot with colder background thyroid
Multinodular goitre is excluded if there are compressive symptoms
Multinodular goitre can produce asymmetry and compressive symptoms
In North America, multinodular goitre and Graves disease are common causes of goitre
Thyroid adenoma is characteristically a cystic non-functioning lesion
updates.explanation: The source describes a toxic adenoma as hyperfunctioning, with the adenoma relatively hot and the background thyroid colder. It also notes that multinodular goitre can be asymmetric and symptomatic from compression. A purely cystic non-functioning description does not match the source's adenoma pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding thyroglossal duct cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are common congenital paediatric neck cysts
They can occur along the path from the foramen caecum to the thyroid bed
They are always solid hypervascular masses
An enhancing mural nodule raises concern for rare papillary carcinoma
They are never infected
options_after: They are common congenital paediatric neck cysts
They can occur along the path from the foramen caecum to the thyroid bed
They are characteristically solid hypervascular masses
An enhancing mural nodule raises concern for rare papillary carcinoma
They are not infected
updates.explanation: The source describes thyroglossal duct cyst as the most common congenital paediatric neck cyst and locates it along the descent pathway from the foramen caecum to the thyroid region. Infection can occur, and rare papillary carcinoma is suggested by an enhancing nodule. A solid hypervascular mass is not the typical cyst description.

updates.question_text: Regarding ectopic or lingual thyroid, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ectopic thyroid can occur from the tongue base to the central neck

Most ectopic thyroid tissue is at the tongue base in the source
A normally located thyroid should be checked before treatment
Malignant transformation is rare
options_after: Ectopic thyroid can occur from the tongue base to the central neck

Most ectopic thyroid tissue is at the tongue base in the source
A normally located thyroid should be checked before treatment
Malignant transformation is rare
updates.explanation: The source describes ectopic thyroid anywhere from the tongue base to the central neck, with most at the tongue base. It can be hyperdense because of iodine content, and confirming whether normal orthotopic thyroid tissue exists is important. Malignant transformation is rare.

updates.question_text: Regarding Delphian lymph nodes in thyroid and laryngeal disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Delphian nodes are always normal if seen
Delphian nodes are unrelated to level 6 anatomy

Delphian nodes exclude thyroid inflammation

Delphian nodes are unrelated to level 6 anatomy

A malignant Delphian node is classically associated with laryngeal cancer in the source
Delphian nodes exclude thyroid inflammation
updates.explanation: The source notes that level 6/Delphian nodes can be enlarged in Hashimoto thyroiditis, but also highlights that a malignant Delphian node is classically associated with laryngeal cancer. The presence of these nodes is therefore interpreted in context. They are not automatically benign or unrelated to neck nodal anatomy.

updates.question_text: Regarding papillary thyroid carcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the most common thyroid carcinoma in the source
Microcalcifications are a classic ultrasound clue
It primarily spreads haematogenously while avoiding lymph nodes in the source
It is never iodine-avid
Prognosis is generally excellent compared with aggressive thyroid cancers
options_after: It is the most common thyroid carcinoma in the source
Microcalcifications are a classic ultrasound clue
It primarily spreads haematogenously while avoiding lymph nodes in the source
It is not iodine-avid
Prognosis is generally excellent compared with aggressive thyroid cancers
updates.explanation: The source identifies papillary carcinoma as the most common thyroid cancer, with microcalcifications as a classic clue and generally excellent prognosis. It commonly spreads through lymphatics and is iodine-responsive in the source. Purely haematogenous behaviour fits follicular carcinoma better.

updates.question_text: Regarding nodal and distant metastatic appearances of papillary thyroid carcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Metastatic nodes may be microcalcified
Metastatic nodes are always hypovascular and invisible on CT
Papillary carcinoma never produces lung metastases

Brain metastases from thyroid carcinoma are always non-haemorrhagic

Metastatic nodes are characteristically hypovascular and invisible on CT
Papillary carcinoma will not produce lung metastases
Metastatic nodes may be hyperenhancing on CT
Brain metastases from thyroid carcinoma are characteristically non-haemorrhagic
updates.explanation: The source describes papillary thyroid carcinoma nodal metastases as potentially microcalcified, hyperechoic and hyperenhancing on CT. It also notes metastatic patterns including lung disease and hypervascular brain metastases that can bleed. Hypovascular invisible nodes and non-haemorrhagic brain metastases are therefore not reliable source statements.

updates.question_text: Regarding diffuse pulmonary metastases from iodine-avid thyroid carcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are always obvious on routine CT before scintigraphy
They may have a miliary pattern
They are the defining feature of Riedel thyroiditis
They can sometimes be occult on cross-sectional imaging and seen on scintigraphy
Radioiodine treatment of diffuse lung metastases carries pulmonary fibrosis risk
options_after: They are characteristically obvious on routine CT before scintigraphy
They may have a miliary pattern
They are the defining feature of Riedel thyroiditis
They can sometimes be occult on cross-sectional imaging and seen on scintigraphy
Radioiodine treatment of diffuse lung metastases carries pulmonary fibrosis risk
updates.explanation: The source notes that thyroid cancer lung metastases can have a miliary pattern and may be occult on cross-sectional imaging while visible on scintigraphy. It also warns about pulmonary fibrosis risk when diffuse lung metastases are treated with radioiodine. Riedel thyroiditis is a fibrosing thyroiditis, not a metastatic lung pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding parathyroid embryology and ectopic glands, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Superior parathyroid glands derive from the fourth branchial pouch
Inferior parathyroid glands derive from the third branchial pouch
Inferior parathyroid glands may be more ectopic because they migrate with the thymus
All parathyroid glands are normally intrathyroidal
There are typically two parathyroid glands
options_after: Superior parathyroid glands derive from the fourth branchial pouch
Inferior parathyroid glands derive from the third branchial pouch
Inferior parathyroid glands may be more ectopic because they migrate with the thymus
Most parathyroid glands are normally intrathyroidal
There are typically two parathyroid glands
updates.explanation: The source describes four posterior parathyroid glands, with superior glands from the fourth pouch and inferior glands from the third pouch. The inferior glands have a wider ectopic range because of their migration pathway with the thymus. They are not all expected to be intrathyroidal, and the usual number is four rather than two.

updates.question_text: Regarding the most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism in the source, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Parathyroid carcinoma accounts for the majority of cases
Multigland hyperplasia is the only recognised cause
Medullary thyroid carcinoma is the usual cause
Thyroglossal duct cyst is the usual cause
Adenoma is the most common cause
options_after: Parathyroid carcinoma accounts for the majority of cases
Multigland hyperplasia is the principal recognised cause
Medullary thyroid carcinoma is the usual cause
Thyroglossal duct cyst is the usual cause
Adenoma is the most common cause
updates.explanation: The source lists parathyroid adenoma as the dominant cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, with multigland hyperplasia and carcinoma being less common. Thyroid carcinoma and thyroglossal duct cyst are separate head and neck entities rather than usual causes of primary hyperparathyroidism.

updates.question_text: Regarding parathyroid adenoma imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It may appear as a hypoechoic bean-shaped lesion posterior to the thyroid
4D-CT can show early enhancement and washout
Sestamibi imaging depends on mitochondrial density and blood flow
Carcinoma always has a completely different benign cystic appearance from adenoma
Dual-tracer techniques may combine sestamibi with iodine or pertechnetate imaging
options_after: It may appear as a hypoechoic bean-shaped lesion posterior to the thyroid
4D-CT can show early enhancement and washout
Sestamibi imaging depends on mitochondrial density and blood flow
Carcinoma characteristically has a completely different benign cystic appearance from adenoma
Dual-tracer techniques may combine sestamibi with iodine or pertechnetate imaging
updates.explanation: The source describes parathyroid adenoma as a hypoechoic bean-shaped lesion posterior to the thyroid. 4D-CT uses enhancement behaviour, and sestamibi uptake relates to mitochondrial density and blood flow. Parathyroid carcinoma can mimic adenoma; invasion or nodes are the clues rather than a reliably benign cystic appearance.

updates.question_text: Regarding nuclear medicine and tracer use in endocrine imaging from this section, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Radioiodine uptake in Graves disease is typically high
MIBG is described as better than octreotide for phaeochromocytoma
Sestamibi can be used for parathyroid adenoma localisation
