options_after: Radioiodine uptake in Graves disease is typically high
MIBG is described as better than octreotide for phaeochromocytoma
Sestamibi can be used for parathyroid adenoma localisation
In-111 octreotide is the source's named study for acute suppurative thyroiditis
Sestamibi localises parathyroid adenoma by showing renal excretion
updates.explanation: The endocrine section uses tracer knowledge clinically: high radioiodine uptake supports Graves disease, MIBG is favoured over octreotide for phaeochromocytoma in the source, and sestamibi is used for parathyroid adenoma localisation. In-111 octreotide is mentioned for carcinoid rather than acute suppurative thyroiditis. Sestamibi performance is related to mitochondrial density and blood flow rather than renal excretion alone.

updates.question_text: Regarding thyroid nodule biopsy logic in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Suspicious ultrasound features are more important than size alone
Every hyperechoic nodule requires biopsy regardless of all other features
Microcalcifications and irregular margins increase concern
Pure cystic nodules are the highest-risk pattern in the source
A cold thyroid nodule on iodine imaging is always malignant
options_after: Suspicious ultrasound features are more important than size alone
Most hyperechoic nodules requires biopsy despite variation in most other features
Microcalcifications and irregular margins increase concern
Pure cystic nodules are the highest-risk pattern in the source
A cold thyroid nodule on iodine imaging is characteristically malignant
updates.explanation: The source states that suspicious features guide biopsy rather than size alone. Microcalcifications and irregular margins are among the high-risk ultrasound features. Hyperechoic, pure cystic or spongiform patterns are generally more reassuring, and most cold nodules are benign even though malignancy remains possible.

updates.question_text: Regarding LeFort fracture buzzwords, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: LeFort I may be described as floating palate
LeFort I is the pattern that separates the entire face from the cranium
LeFort II may be described as pyramidal
LeFort III may be described as floating face
LeFort III is defined by isolated palate separation only
options_after: LeFort I may be described as floating palate
LeFort I is the pattern that separates the entire face from the cranium
LeFort II may be described as pyramidal
LeFort III may be described as floating face
LeFort III is defined by isolated palate separation
updates.explanation: The source gives the classic shorthand: LeFort I is floating palate, LeFort II is pyramidal or maxillary separation from the face, and LeFort III is floating face or craniofacial dissociation. The pterygoid process is common to all, but the higher patterns add orbital and zygomatic components. Isolated palate separation belongs to LeFort I rather than LeFort III.

updates.question_text: Regarding frontal sinus mucocele and CSF leak after facial trauma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A mucocele is usually a solidly enhancing aggressive tumour of the frontal sinus
Disruption of the frontal sinus outflow tract can lead to adhesions, obstruction and mucocele formation
Recurrent bacterial meningitis excludes a CSF leak
Facial bone fractures cannot cause CSF leakage
The most common fracture site causing CSF leak is the anterior skull base
options_after: A mucocele is usually a solidly enhancing aggressive tumour of the frontal sinus
Disruption of the frontal sinus outflow tract can lead to adhesions, obstruction and mucocele formation
Recurrent bacterial meningitis excludes a CSF leak
Facial bone fractures will not cause CSF leakage
The most common fracture site causing CSF leak is the anterior skull base
updates.explanation: The source links frontal sinus outflow tract disruption after trauma to later mucocele formation. A mucocele is described as an airless expanded sinus, often T1 bright with a thin enhancing rim rather than solid tumour-like enhancement. Facial, sinus wall and anterior skull base fractures can cause CSF leak, with recurrent bacterial meningitis as an associated clue.

updates.question_text: Regarding high-yield facial fracture facts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The nasal bone is the most common facial fracture

The zygomaticomaxillary complex or tripod pattern involves the zygoma, inferior orbit and lateral orbit
Tripod fracture is another name for isolated nasal bone fracture
Otic capsule violation is more predictive than the traditional temporal bone fracture orientation classification
options_after: The nasal bone is the most common facial fracture
LeFort fractures are diagnosed primarily when the zygomatic arch is intact
The zygomaticomaxillary complex or tripod pattern involves the zygoma, inferior orbit and lateral orbit
Tripod fracture is another name for isolated nasal bone fracture
Otic capsule violation is more predictive than the traditional temporal bone fracture orientation classification
updates.explanation: The source lists nasal bone fracture as the most common fracture and zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture as the common fracture pattern involving the zygoma, inferior orbit and lateral orbit. It also explicitly states that otic capsule violation is more useful than simple longitudinal versus transverse classification. Tripod fracture is not an isolated nasal bone injury.

updates.question_text: Regarding cholesteatoma in the temporal bone, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It represents exfoliated epithelial debris growing in an abnormal location
It is primarily a vascular tumour of the jugular fossa
It can erode temporal bone and ossicles
It restricts diffusion
It never causes bony erosion
options_after: It represents exfoliated epithelial debris growing in an abnormal location
It is primarily a vascular tumour of the jugular fossa
It can erode temporal bone and ossicles
It restricts diffusion
It will not cause bony erosion
updates.explanation: The source frames cholesteatoma as epithelial debris in the wrong place, producing inflammatory mass effect and erosion. Diffusion restriction is a key imaging clue. The jugular fossa vascular tumour description fits paraganglioma rather than cholesteatoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding complications of otitis media, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Coalescent mastoiditis involves erosion of mastoid septae with or without intramastoid abscess
Facial nerve palsy can occur from inflammation of the tympanic segment
Otitis media cannot spread intracranially
Dural sinus thrombosis can lead to venous infarct
Lateral sinus thrombosis can alter CSF resorption and produce otitic hydrocephalus
options_after: Coalescent mastoiditis involves erosion of mastoid septae with or without intramastoid abscess
Facial nerve palsy can occur from inflammation of the tympanic segment
Otitis media will not spread intracranially
Dural sinus thrombosis can lead to venous infarct
Lateral sinus thrombosis can alter CSF resorption and produce otitic hydrocephalus
updates.explanation: The source lists coalescent mastoiditis, facial nerve palsy, dural sinus thrombosis, meningitis, labyrinthitis, venous infarct and otitic hydrocephalus as complications of otitis media. Dural sinus thrombosis can trigger downstream venous infarction. Lateral sinus thrombosis can impair CSF resorption and cause hydrocephalus.

updates.question_text: Regarding labyrinthitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is always bilateral and never related to otomastoiditis

It is inflammation of the membranous labyrinth
It is primarily diagnosed by scutum erosion
The cochlea and semicircular canals may enhance on post-contrast T1-weighted MRI
options_after: It is characteristically bilateral and independent of otomastoiditis
Bacterial meningitis will not cause labyrinthitis
It is inflammation of the membranous labyrinth
It is primarily diagnosed by scutum erosion
The cochlea and semicircular canals may enhance on post-contrast T1-weighted MRI
updates.explanation: Labyrinthitis is inflammation of the membranous labyrinth. The source describes enhancement of the cochlea and semicircular canals on post-contrast T1 imaging. Viral respiratory infection is common, acute otomastoiditis can spread directly and bacterial meningitis can produce bilateral labyrinthitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal and abnormal facial nerve enhancement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Nodular enhancement should be ignored as a normal pattern

The labyrinthine segment can sometimes enhance normally
The facial nerve never enhances normally
Normal enhancement is not expected in the cisternal, canalicular or extratemporal segments
options_after: Nodular enhancement should be ignored as a normal pattern
The tympanic and mastoid segments, including the geniculate ganglion, can enhance normally
The labyrinthine segment can sometimes enhance normally
The facial nerve will not enhance normally
Normal enhancement is not expected in the cisternal, canalicular or extratemporal segments
updates.explanation: The source highlights that the facial nerve is unusual because some portions may normally enhance. The tympanic and mastoid segments including the geniculate ganglion can enhance, and the labyrinthine segment may do so sometimes. Cisternal, canalicular and extratemporal enhancement is not normal, and nodular enhancement raises concern for tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding facial nerve pathology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bell palsy is usually a clinical diagnosis and is probably viral

Ramsay Hunt syndrome never involves another cranial nerve
Ramsay Hunt syndrome is caused by varicella zoster reactivation and has a classic rash around the ear
Transverse temporal bone fracture is less likely than longitudinal fracture to damage the facial nerve
options_after: Bell palsy is usually a clinical diagnosis and is probably viral
Canalicular segment enhancement within the internal auditory canal is a classic imaging finding in Bell palsy
Ramsay Hunt syndrome will not involve another cranial nerve
Ramsay Hunt syndrome is caused by varicella zoster reactivation and has a classic rash around the ear
Transverse temporal bone fracture is less likely than longitudinal fracture to damage the facial nerve
updates.explanation: Bell palsy is described as probably viral and usually diagnosed clinically, with canalicular enhancement as the classic imaging finding. Ramsay Hunt syndrome results from varicella zoster reactivation and has a rash around the ear, with trigeminal involvement often noted in the source. Transverse temporal bone fractures are more associated with facial nerve damage than longitudinal fractures.

updates.question_text: Regarding otosclerosis or otospongiosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Conductive hearing loss in an adult female is a classic clinical clue
Retrofenestral disease is almost always unilateral and asymmetric
Fenestral disease is centred on the posterior semicircular canal
Fenestral disease involves bony resorption anterior to the oval window at the fissula ante fenestram
Retrofenestral disease has demineralisation around the cochlea and often adds a sensorineural component
options_after: Conductive hearing loss in an adult female is a classic clinical clue
Retrofenestral disease is typically unilateral and asymmetric
Fenestral disease is centred on the posterior semicircular canal
Fenestral disease involves bony resorption anterior to the oval window at the fissula ante fenestram
Retrofenestral disease has demineralisation around the cochlea and often adds a sensorineural component
updates.explanation: The source gives adult female conductive hearing loss as a classic clue. Fenestral otosclerosis is centred anterior to the oval window at the fissula ante fenestram, while retrofenestral disease extends around the cochlea and introduces a sensorineural component. Retrofenestral involvement is described as bilateral and symmetric nearly all the time.

updates.question_text: Regarding asymmetric petrous apex marrow, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Asymmetric petrous apex marrow always represents malignant infiltration
Normal petrous apex marrow should be lower signal than orbital fat on both T1 and T2
Fat-saturated imaging such as STIR helps avoid mistaking asymmetric marrow fat for disease or missing a T1-bright lesion
A T1-bright petrous apex lesion can never mimic marrow fat
Petrous apex marrow variation is unrelated to pneumatization or marrow fat
options_after: Asymmetric petrous apex marrow characteristically represents malignant infiltration
Normal petrous apex marrow should be lower signal than orbital fat on both T1 and T2
Fat-saturated imaging such as STIR helps avoid mistaking asymmetric marrow fat for disease or missing a T1-bright lesion
A T1-bright petrous apex lesion will not mimic marrow fat
Petrous apex marrow variation is unrelated to pneumatization or marrow fat
updates.explanation: The source warns that asymmetric petrous apex marrow can create two pitfalls: falsely diagnosing infiltration or overlooking a T1-bright lesion by assuming it is fat. STIR or another fat-saturating sequence is the recommended way to resolve the issue. The petrous apex normally contains marrow fat that follows scalp and orbital fat signal.

updates.question_text: Regarding aberrant internal carotid artery in the temporal bone, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It should be biopsied to distinguish it from paraganglioma
It can present with pulsatile tinnitus and mimic a vascular retrotympanic mass
It is caused by complete absence of the membranous labyrinth
It always appears as a non-enhancing cystic Meckel cave herniation
The key imaging clue is connection to the horizontal carotid canal
options_after: It should be biopsied to distinguish it from paraganglioma
It can present with pulsatile tinnitus and mimic a vascular retrotympanic mass
It is caused by complete absence of the membranous labyrinth
It characteristically appears as a non-enhancing cystic Meckel cave herniation
The key imaging clue is connection to the horizontal carotid canal
updates.explanation: The source describes aberrant internal carotid artery as a pitfall that may look like a paraganglioma clinically or otoscopically. The classic imaging clue is its connection to the horizontal carotid canal. Biopsy is specifically unsafe because the lesion is vascular.

updates.question_text: Regarding otic capsule violation in temporal bone trauma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is less useful than classifying every fracture as purely longitudinal or purely transverse
It is only relevant for LeFort fracture classification
It is the most predictive temporal bone fracture feature described in the source
It proves the fracture is a nasal bone fracture
It is used to diagnose large vestibular aqueduct syndrome
options_after: It is less useful than classifying fractures as purely longitudinal or purely transverse
It is primarily relevant for LeFort fracture classification
It is the most predictive temporal bone fracture feature described in the source
It proves the fracture is a nasal bone fracture
It is used to diagnose large vestibular aqueduct syndrome
updates.explanation: The source explicitly states that longitudinal versus transverse classification is old and limited because many fractures are mixed. Violation of the otic capsule is presented as the more predictive modern finding. This concept applies to temporal bone trauma rather than LeFort or nasal fracture classification.

updates.question_text: Regarding Gradenigo syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a complication of apical petrositis involving Dorello canal
It is caused by isolated scutum erosion from pars flaccida cholesteatoma
The classic triad includes otomastoiditis, facial pain and lateral rectus palsy
Lateral rectus palsy reflects sixth cranial nerve involvement
It presents with conductive hearing loss from stapes fixation only
options_after: It is a complication of apical petrositis involving Dorello canal
It is caused by isolated scutum erosion from pars flaccida cholesteatoma
The classic triad includes otomastoiditis, facial pain and lateral rectus palsy
Lateral rectus palsy reflects sixth cranial nerve involvement
It presents with conductive hearing loss from stapes fixation
updates.explanation: Gradenigo syndrome occurs when apical petrositis involves Dorello canal and affects the sixth cranial nerve. The classic triad in the source is otomastoiditis, facial pain from trigeminal neuropathy and lateral rectus palsy. Scutum erosion and stapes fixation belong to separate middle ear diagnoses.

updates.question_text: Regarding cholesterol granuloma versus petrous apex cholesteatoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Both can produce smooth expansile bony change
Cholesterol granuloma is T1 bright and T2 bright
Petrous apex cholesteatoma is T1 dark and T2 bright
Petrous apex cholesteatoma restricts diffusion whereas cholesterol granuloma does not
Both are expected to show identical restricted diffusion
options_after: Both can produce smooth expansile bony change
Cholesterol granuloma is T1 bright and T2 bright
Petrous apex cholesteatoma is T1 dark and T2 bright
Petrous apex cholesteatoma restricts diffusion whereas cholesterol granuloma does not
Both are expected to show closely comparable restricted diffusion
updates.explanation: The source comparison table emphasises that both lesions can remodel the petrous apex smoothly. The practical distinction is MRI signal and diffusion: cholesterol granuloma is T1 and T2 bright without restriction, whereas cholesteatoma is T1 dark, T2 bright and restricts. This makes diffusion imaging decisive in many cases.

updates.question_text: Regarding external auditory canal exostosis and osteoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Exostosis is almost exclusively seen in diabetic patients with bony destruction
Osteoma is a congenital absent external auditory canal
External auditory canal exostoses are usually bilateral and associated with repeated irritation or infections in swimmers or surfers
External auditory canal osteoma is usually incidental and unilateral near the cartilage-bone junction
Both lesions are defined by a vascular retrotympanic mass
options_after: Exostosis is predominantly seen in diabetic patients with bony destruction
Osteoma is a congenital absent external auditory canal
External auditory canal exostoses are usually bilateral and associated with repeated irritation or infections in swimmers or surfers
External auditory canal osteoma is usually incidental and unilateral near the cartilage-bone junction
Both lesions are defined by a vascular retrotympanic mass
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes exostoses as usually bilateral bony overgrowths related to repeated external canal irritation from osteoma, which is usually unilateral and incidental near the cartilage-bone junction. Necrotising otitis externa, not exostosis, is the diabetic destructive infection. A vascular retrotympanic mass suggests vascular pathology rather than these benign bony lesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding CT and MRI strategy in sinus disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CT is typically used for orbital and sinus infections and helps assess anterior orbital spread
A hyperdense opacified sinus is nearly always malignant tumour in the source strategy
CT is not useful for anatomical variation before endoscopic sinus surgery
MRI is superior for cavernous sinus involvement, orbital apex disease, perineural spread and marrow involvement
MRI cannot assess tumour extension
options_after: CT is typically used for orbital and sinus infections and helps assess anterior orbital spread
A hyperdense opacified sinus is nearly characteristically malignant tumour in the source strategy
CT is not useful for anatomical variation before endoscopic sinus surgery
MRI is superior for cavernous sinus involvement, orbital apex disease, perineural spread and marrow involvement
MRI will not assess tumour extension
updates.explanation: The source describes CT as useful for sinus and orbital infection, especially anterior orbital involvement, and for benign dense sinus contents and surgical anatomy. MRI is more valuable for posterior orbital apex, cavernous sinus, perineural and marrow involvement. Hyperdense sinus contents are usually benign causes such as blood, inspissated secretion or fungus rather than tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding inverted papilloma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It classically arises from the lateral wall of the nasal cavity, often near the middle turbinate
It is always centred at the cribriform plate with intracranial cysts
A focal hyperostosis may indicate the tumour origin
MRI may show a cerebriform pattern
It has no association with squamous cell carcinoma in the source
options_after: It classically arises from the lateral wall of the nasal cavity, often near the middle turbinate
It is characteristically centred at the cribriform plate with intracranial cysts
A focal hyperostosis may indicate the tumour origin
MRI may show a cerebriform pattern
It lacks association with squamous cell carcinoma in the source
updates.explanation: Inverted papilloma has testable imaging features in the source: lateral nasal wall origin, often near the middle turbinate, focal hyperostosis at the site of origin and a cerebriform MRI pattern. A minority harbour squamous cell carcinoma. Cribriform plate dumbbell shape with intracranial cysts belongs to esthesioneuroblastoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding epistaxis and embolisation targets, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The first-line embolisation target is usually the ophthalmic artery
Anterior septal bleeding from the Kiesselbach plexus is common and often manually compressible
The posterior nose is mainly supplied by the anterior cerebral artery
Nasal packing is never attempted before angiographic treatment
Posterior epistaxis is less common but more likely to require angiographic management
options_after: The first-line embolisation target is usually the ophthalmic artery
Anterior septal bleeding from the Kiesselbach plexus is common and often manually compressible
The posterior nose is mainly supplied by the anterior cerebral artery
Nasal packing is not attempted before angiographic treatment
Posterior epistaxis is less common but more likely to require angiographic management
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes common anterior septal bleeding from less common but more severe posterior epistaxis. Posterior bleeding may require angiography when packing fails, with the sphenopalatine artery as the main first-line target. Anastomoses to the ophthalmic artery are important hazards, not intended targets.

updates.question_text: Regarding nasal septal perforation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It always involves the posterior osseous septum regardless of cause
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis cannot affect the nasal septum
Syphilis is highlighted as a cause that affects the bony septum
Prior septoplasty techniques are unrelated to septal perforation
It is diagnosed by an enlarged vestibular aqueduct
options_after: It characteristically involves the posterior osseous septum despite variation in cause
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis will not affect the nasal septum
Syphilis is highlighted as a cause that affects the bony septum
Prior septoplasty techniques are unrelated to septal perforation
It is diagnosed by an enlarged vestibular aqueduct
updates.explanation: The source lists several causes of nasal septal perforation and specifically notes that syphilis affects the bony septum, while most other causes affect cartilaginous regions. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis and prior septal surgery are among the listed considerations. Vestibular aqueduct enlargement is an inner ear diagnosis, not a nasal septal finding.

updates.question_text: Regarding odontogenic infection spread, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The mylohyoid attachment has no role in the spread pattern
Spread above the mylohyoid line from anterior mandibular teeth goes to the sublingual space
Spread below the mylohyoid line from second and third molars goes to the submandibular space
Infection from an extracted tooth is less common than infection from an intact tooth in the source
An odontogenic abscess is described as the most common masticator space mass in an adult
options_after: The mylohyoid attachment has negligible role in the spread pattern
Spread above the mylohyoid line from anterior mandibular teeth goes to the sublingual space
Spread below the mylohyoid line from second and third molars goes to the submandibular space
Infection from an extracted tooth is less common than infection from an intact tooth in the source
An odontogenic abscess is described as the most common masticator space mass in an adult
updates.explanation: The source emphasises the mylohyoid line as the key anatomical determinant of mandibular odontogenic infection spread. Infection above the line reaches the sublingual space, while infection below the line reaches the submandibular space. It also notes that odontogenic abscess is the most common masticator space mass in adults and that extracted teeth are a common source.

updates.question_text: Regarding cystic floor-of-mouth lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A ranula is a mucous retention cyst arising from the sublingual gland, sublingual space or minor salivary glands
A thyroglossal duct cyst is always lateral and arises from Wharton duct
A plunging ranula extends below the mylohyoid muscle into the submandibular space
A floor-of-mouth dermoid or epidermoid may show a sack-of-marbles appearance from fat globules
A ranula is a vascular tumour centred on the sphenopalatine foramen
options_after: A ranula is a mucous retention cyst arising from the sublingual gland, sublingual space or minor salivary glands
A thyroglossal duct cyst is characteristically lateral and arises from Wharton duct
A plunging ranula extends below the mylohyoid muscle into the submandibular space
A floor-of-mouth dermoid or epidermoid may show a sack-of-marbles appearance from fat globules
A ranula is a vascular tumour centred on the sphenopalatine foramen
updates.explanation: The source describes ranula as a mucous retention cyst from sublingual or minor salivary tissue. When it extends below the mylohyoid into the submandibular space it is called plunging, diving or cervical. Floor-of-mouth dermoid or epidermoid is associated with a sack-of-marbles appearance from fat globules.

updates.question_text: Regarding mouth cancer and HPV-related squamous cell carcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A young adult with a new level II neck mass should automatically be called a branchial cleft cyst
Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common mouth and head-and-neck cancer in the source
In older patients the source highlights smoking and alcohol exposure as classic associations
HPV-related disease is excluded by necrotic nodal disease
In younger patients, HPV-related squamous cell carcinoma may present with large necrotic level IIa nodes
options_after: A young adult with a new level II neck mass should ordinarily be called a branchial cleft cyst
Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common mouth and head-and-neck cancer in the source
In older patients the source highlights smoking and alcohol exposure as classic associations
HPV-related disease is excluded by necrotic nodal disease
In younger patients, HPV-related squamous cell carcinoma may present with large necrotic level IIa nodes
updates.explanation: The source frames squamous cell carcinoma as the common mouth and head-and-neck cancer. In older patients smoking and alcohol exposure are classic associations; in younger patients HPV-related disease is important. A necrotic level II node in a young adult should not be dismissed as a branchial cleft cyst.

updates.question_text: Regarding pleomorphic adenoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It occurs only in the parotid gland and is usually bilateral in smokers
It is the most common malignant minor salivary gland tumour
It is the most common major and minor salivary gland tumour described in the source
It is defined by perineural spread as the primary imaging clue
It is a thrombophlebitis syndrome with septic pulmonary emboli
options_after: It occurs primarily in the parotid gland and is usually bilateral in smokers
It is the most common malignant minor salivary gland tumour
It is the most common major and minor salivary gland tumour described in the source
It is defined by perineural spread as the primary imaging clue
It is a thrombophlebitis syndrome with septic pulmonary emboli
updates.explanation: Pleomorphic adenoma, or benign mixed tumour, is described as the most common major and minor salivary gland tumour. It is most common in the parotid and often arises in the superficial lobe, with T2 hyperintensity and a low-signal rim. Warthin tumour is the parotid-only smoker-associated lesion, while mucoepidermoid carcinoma and adenoid cystic carcinoma are malignant salivary tumours.

updates.question_text: Regarding parapharyngeal fat displacement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A parotid space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat medially
A masticator space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat laterally
A superficial mucosal space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat medially
A carotid space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat anteriorly
All neighbouring spaces displace parapharyngeal fat identically
options_after: A parotid space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat medially
A masticator space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat laterally
A superficial mucosal space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat medially
A carotid space mass pushes parapharyngeal fat anteriorly
Most neighbouring spaces displace parapharyngeal fat identically
updates.explanation: Parapharyngeal fat displacement is useful because each neighbouring space pushes it in a different direction. Parotid lesions push it medially and carotid space lesions push it anteriorly. Masticator lesions push posteriorly and medially, while superficial mucosal space lesions push laterally.

updates.question_text: Regarding the masticator space, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The masticator space contains muscles of mastication and the mandibular ramus or angle
Masticator space lesions displace parapharyngeal fat laterally
Odontogenic infection is described as the most common adult masticator space mass
The masticator space is defined by parotid gland and retromandibular vein contents
The masticator space is limited inferiorly and cannot track superiorly along temporalis
options_after: The masticator space contains muscles of mastication and the mandibular ramus or angle
Masticator space lesions displace parapharyngeal fat laterally
Odontogenic infection is described as the most common adult masticator space mass
The masticator space is defined by parotid gland and retromandibular vein contents
The masticator space is limited inferiorly and will not track superiorly along temporalis
updates.explanation: The masticator space contains the muscles of mastication, mandibular ramus/angle and V3-related structures. Odontogenic infection is the common adult masticator space mass in the source. Its lesions displace parapharyngeal fat posteriorly and medially, and aggressive disease can track superiorly along the temporalis muscle.

updates.question_text: Regarding the retropharyngeal and danger spaces, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The true retropharyngeal space extends caudally to about C6-C7
The danger space is limited to the hard palate
Prevertebral space infection is usually ordinary tonsillar spread rather than spinal/disc infection
The posterior danger space can extend into the mediastinum
Retropharyngeal infection cannot spread inferiorly
options_after: The true retropharyngeal space extends caudally to about C6-C7
The danger space is limited to the hard palate
Prevertebral space infection is usually ordinary tonsillar spread rather than spinal/disc infection
The posterior danger space can extend into the mediastinum
Retropharyngeal infection will not spread inferiorly
updates.explanation: The source separates the anterior true retropharyngeal space, which extends to about C6-C7, from the posterior danger space, which can extend into the mediastinum. Prevertebral space infection is considered separately and is more related to spinal/disc osteomyelitis. Inferior spread is exactly why the danger space matters.

updates.question_text: Regarding retropharyngeal infection and nodes of Rouviere, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adult necrotic retropharyngeal nodes are always benign infection
Retropharyngeal infection most often spreads from tonsillar tissue
Lymphoma in nodes of Rouviere is typically necrotic before treatment
Nodes of Rouviere are midline laryngeal structures
Delayed imaging can help distinguish phlegmon from drainable abscess
options_after: Adult necrotic retropharyngeal nodes are characteristically benign infection
Retropharyngeal infection most often spreads from tonsillar tissue
Lymphoma in nodes of Rouviere is typically necrotic before treatment
Nodes of Rouviere are midline laryngeal structures
Delayed imaging can help distinguish phlegmon from drainable abscess
updates.explanation: Retropharyngeal infection most often spreads from tonsillar tissue, and delayed imaging helps distinguish phlegmon from a drainable abscess. Necrotic retropharyngeal nodes in adults raise concern for metastases rather than being assumed benign. Nodes of Rouviere are lateral retropharyngeal nodes, and lymphoma is not usually necrotic until treated.

updates.question_text: Regarding laryngeal anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The supraglottic region includes the epiglottis, valleculae, aryepiglottic folds and pre-epiglottic fat
The pre-epiglottic fat has no lymphatic relevance for tumour staging
The glottic region includes the true cords and anterior commissure
The subglottic region is at the level below the true cords toward the cricoid ring
The paraglottic spaces do not communicate with the pre-epiglottic space
options_after: The supraglottic region includes the epiglottis, valleculae, aryepiglottic folds and pre-epiglottic fat
The pre-epiglottic fat lacks lymphatic relevance for tumour staging
The glottic region includes the true cords and anterior commissure
The subglottic region is at the level below the true cords toward the cricoid ring
The paraglottic spaces do not communicate with the pre-epiglottic space
updates.explanation: The source anatomy review divides the larynx into supraglottic, glottic and subglottic regions. It specifically notes that the para-epiglottic or paraglottic spaces communicate superiorly with the pre-epiglottic fat. The pre-epiglottic fat is rich in lymphatics, making invasion important for staging.

updates.question_text: Regarding paraglottic space and transglottic disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Paraglottic space involvement makes the tumour T3 and transglottic in the source discussion
Paraglottic involvement proves benign laryngocele rather than carcinoma
The paraglottic space has no communication with supraglottic structures
Coronal imaging is particularly useful for paraglottic/transglottic assessment
Transglottic disease means tumour isolated to the nasopharynx
options_after: Paraglottic space involvement makes the tumour T3 and transglottic in the source discussion
Paraglottic involvement proves benign laryngocele rather than carcinoma
The paraglottic space lacks communication with supraglottic structures
Coronal imaging is particularly useful for paraglottic/transglottic assessment
Transglottic disease means tumour isolated to the nasopharynx
updates.explanation: The source specifically states that paraglottic space involvement makes a tumour T3 and transglottic, and notes that this is best seen on coronal images. The paraglottic space communicates superiorly with the pre-epiglottic space, which is part of why spread matters. This is a laryngeal staging issue, not nasopharyngeal disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding cricoarytenoid joint and cricoid cartilage involvement in laryngeal cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Irregular sclerotic cricoid cartilage alone is always diagnostic of invasion
Cord fixation indicates at least T3 disease and can be suspected when tumour involves the cricoarytenoid joint
Cricoid invasion is irrelevant to conservation surgery decisions
Cord fixation is best assessed by ASPECTS
Tumour on both sides of cricoid cartilage is the reliable sign of cricoid invasion in the source
options_after: Irregular sclerotic cricoid cartilage alone is characteristically diagnostic of invasion
Cord fixation indicates at least T3 disease and can be suspected when tumour involves the cricoarytenoid joint
Cricoid invasion is irrelevant to conservation surgery decisions
Cord fixation is best assessed by ASPECTS
Tumour on both sides of cricoid cartilage is the reliable sign of cricoid invasion in the source
updates.explanation: The source notes that cord fixation means at least T3 disease and is best assessed clinically, though cricoarytenoid joint involvement can suggest it radiologically. Cricoid invasion is reliably indicated by tumour on both sides of the cartilage, whereas irregular sclerosis can be normal. Cricoid invasion contraindicates laryngeal conservation surgery because the cricoid is required for postoperative stability.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute parotitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Obstruction of salivary flow is the most common cause in the source
Sialography is the recommended acute investigation
Stensen duct stones may be seen with duct dilatation
It is always painless and associated with HIV
It is caused by carotid space paraganglioma
options_after: Obstruction of salivary flow is the most common cause in the source
Sialography is the recommended acute investigation
Stensen duct stones may be seen with duct dilatation
It is characteristically painless and associated with HIV
It is caused by carotid space paraganglioma
updates.explanation: The source describes obstruction of salivary secretions as the common cause of acute parotitis, often with stones in Stensen duct and ductal dilatation. Post-infectious parotitis is usually bacterial, and mumps is noted as a common viral cause. Sialography is contraindicated in the acute setting.

updates.question_text: Regarding the general benign-versus-malignant salivary gland rule in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The parotid gland is the salivary gland with no lymph nodes
Minor salivary gland tumours are nearly always benign pleomorphic adenomas
The smaller the salivary gland, the more common malignant tumours are relative to benign tumours
Warthin tumour is the most common malignant tumour of minor salivary glands
Adenoid cystic carcinoma is excluded when perineural spread is present
options_after: The parotid gland is the salivary gland without lymph nodes
Minor salivary gland tumours are nearly characteristically benign pleomorphic adenomas
The smaller the salivary gland, the more common malignant tumours are relative to benign tumours
Warthin tumour is the most common malignant tumour of minor salivary glands
Adenoid cystic carcinoma is excluded when perineural spread is present
updates.explanation: The source's general rule is that smaller salivary glands have a higher relative frequency of malignant tumours, while larger glands have more benign tumours. The parotid is unique among salivary glands because it contains lymph nodes. Perineural spread is a hallmark consideration for adenoid cystic carcinoma rather than an exclusion.

updates.question_text: Regarding orbital metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Breast metastasis classically produces anterior displacement of the globe from a primary orbital tumour
Metastatic neuroblastoma can produce periorbital tumour infiltration with proptosis
Neuroblastoma orbital metastasis is always unilateral in the source comparison
Metastases are more common to the orbit than to the eye in the source
Scirrhous breast carcinoma metastasis can cause an infiltrative retrobulbar mass with enophthalmos
options_after: Breast metastasis classically produces anterior displacement of the globe from a primary orbital tumour
Metastatic neuroblastoma can produce periorbital tumour infiltration with proptosis
Neuroblastoma orbital metastasis is characteristically unilateral in the source comparison
Metastases are more common to the orbit than to the eye in the source
Scirrhous breast carcinoma metastasis can cause an infiltrative retrobulbar mass with enophthalmos
updates.explanation: The source describes neuroblastoma metastasis as periorbital infiltration with proptosis, often bilateral. Scirrhous breast carcinoma can cause an infiltrative retrobulbar mass with desmoplastic enophthalmos rather than the proptosis typical of many primary orbital masses. It also notes that metastases are more common to the eye than to the orbit.

updates.question_text: Regarding dacryocystitis and orbital subperiosteal abscess, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Dacryocystitis is centred in the optic nerve sheath and surrounds the optic nerve
Dacryocystitis is inflammation and dilation of the lacrimal sac
Subperiosteal abscess is primarily a benign intraocular calcified tumour
Dacryocystitis is treated as postseptal infection in all cases
Orbital subperiosteal abscess is usually associated with ethmoid sinusitis
options_after: Dacryocystitis is centred in the optic nerve sheath and surrounds the optic nerve
Dacryocystitis is inflammation and dilation of the lacrimal sac
Subperiosteal abscess is primarily a benign intraocular calcified tumour
Dacryocystitis is treated as postseptal infection in most cases
Orbital subperiosteal abscess is usually associated with ethmoid sinusitis
updates.explanation: Dacryocystitis is lacrimal sac inflammation and dilation, usually due to obstruction with secondary bacterial infection. Orbital subperiosteal abscess forms under periosteum and is usually associated with ethmoid sinusitis. Optic nerve sheath involvement, retinoblastoma-like calcification and automatic postseptal surgical treatment are not the defining features of simple dacryocystitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding miscellaneous orbital and globe conditions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Optic neuritis enhances without enlargement of the nerve/sheath complex and is often painful and unilateral
Ectopia lentis is caused only by cataract surgery in the source
Papilloedema may show dilation or swelling of the optic nerve sheath
Drusen are mineralisation at the optic disc
A unilateral coloboma should primarily suggest CHARGE syndrome rather than sporadic disease
options_after: Optic neuritis enhances without enlargement of the nerve/sheath complex and is often painful and unilateral
Ectopia lentis is caused primarily by cataract surgery in the source
Papilloedema may show dilation or swelling of the optic nerve sheath
Drusen are mineralisation at the optic disc
A unilateral coloboma should primarily suggest CHARGE syndrome rather than sporadic disease
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes optic neuritis from optic nerve glioma by enhancement without nerve enlargement. Papilloedema can dilate or swell the optic nerve sheath, and drusen are optic disc mineralisation. Lens dislocation can be caused by trauma, Marfan syndrome or homocystinuria, while bilateral rather than unilateral colobomas suggest CHARGE syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding common aortic arch variants in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A bovine arch has a common origin of the brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery
The normal arch pattern is described as present in only 5% of people
A left vertebral artery may originate separately from the arch
A bovine arch means the left vertebral artery always arises from the brachiocephalic artery
The posterior sinus of Valsalva gives rise to the right coronary artery
options_after: A bovine arch has a common origin of the brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery
The normal arch pattern is described as present in approximately 5% of people
A left vertebral artery may originate separately from the arch
A bovine arch means the left vertebral artery characteristically arises from the brachiocephalic artery
The posterior sinus of Valsalva gives rise to the right coronary artery
updates.explanation: The source lists normal branching, bovine arch, left common carotid from the brachiocephalic artery and separate left vertebral origin as common variants. Normal branching is the common pattern, not the rare one. The right and left coronary arteries arise from the right and left sinuses; the posterior cusp is the non-coronary cusp.

updates.question_text: Regarding common hepatic artery variants, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A replaced right hepatic artery most commonly arises from the SMA
A replaced right hepatic artery is anterior to the right portal vein, just like the proper right hepatic artery
An accessory left hepatic artery most commonly arises from the left gastric artery
Traditional hepatic arterial anatomy is present in nearly all patients
A replaced left hepatic artery most commonly arises from the left gastric artery
options_after: A replaced right hepatic artery most commonly arises from the SMA
A replaced right hepatic artery is anterior to the right portal vein, just like the proper right hepatic artery
An accessory left hepatic artery most commonly arises from the left gastric artery
Traditional hepatic arterial anatomy is present in the large majority of patients
A replaced left hepatic artery most commonly arises from the left gastric artery
updates.explanation: The source lists replaced right hepatic artery from SMA, accessory left hepatic artery from left gastric and replaced left hepatic artery from left gastric as common variants. The proper right hepatic artery is anterior to the right portal vein, whereas the replaced right hepatic artery is posterior to the main portal vein. Traditional celiac hepatic anatomy is only present in about 60%.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian artery and persistent sciatic artery anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The ovarian arteries usually arise from the anterior-medial aorta
The ovarian artery has no anastomosis with the uterine artery
Persistent sciatic artery is a continuation of the internal iliac artery passing posterior to the femur
Persistent sciatic artery protects against aneurysm and early atherosclerosis
Persistent sciatic artery is a duplicated left SVC variant
options_after: The ovarian arteries usually arise from the anterior-medial aorta
The ovarian artery lacks anastomosis with the uterine artery
Persistent sciatic artery is a continuation of the internal iliac artery passing posterior to the femur
Persistent sciatic artery protects against aneurysm and early atherosclerosis
Persistent sciatic artery is a duplicated left SVC variant
updates.explanation: The source states that ovarian arteries usually arise from the anterior-medial aorta and anastomose with the uterine artery. Persistent sciatic artery is an internal iliac continuation that passes posterior to the femur and connects to distal vasculature. It can develop aneurysm or early atherosclerosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding left-sided SVC, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is described as the most common congenital venous anomaly in the chest
It usually drains into the coronary sinus
It always causes a right-to-left shunt
It is commonly duplicated with a right-sided SVC also present
Atrial septal defect is listed as the most common associated congenital heart disease
options_after: It is described as the most common congenital venous anomaly in the chest
It usually drains into the coronary sinus
It characteristically causes a right-to-left shunt
It is commonly duplicated with a right-sided SVC also present
Atrial septal defect is listed as the most common associated congenital heart disease
updates.explanation: Left-sided SVC is the most common congenital venous anomaly in the chest and most often drains to the coronary sinus. The source notes that isolated left SVC is uncommon; most cases are duplicated with a right SVC. ASD and unroofed coronary sinus are important associations, while right-to-left shunt occurs only rarely.

updates.question_text: Regarding the classic persistent sciatic artery scenario, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute external iliac occlusion always abolishes pedal pulses regardless of variants
Acute external iliac occlusion with a strong foot pulse suggests persistent sciatic artery
Persistent sciatic artery is a replaced right hepatic artery
Persistent sciatic artery drains into the coronary sinus
Persistent sciatic artery is a duplicated left SVC
options_after: Acute external iliac occlusion characteristically abolishes pedal pulses despite variation in variants
Acute external iliac occlusion with a strong foot pulse suggests persistent sciatic artery
Persistent sciatic artery is a replaced right hepatic artery
Persistent sciatic artery drains into the coronary sinus
Persistent sciatic artery is a duplicated left SVC
updates.explanation: The source gives the board-style scenario: external iliac occlusion with preserved strong foot pulse suggests a persistent sciatic artery. The variant continues from the internal iliac, runs posterior to the femur and anastomoses with distal vasculature. It is not a thoracic venous or hepatic arterial variant.

updates.question_text: Regarding a left paramediastinal vascular structure on chest imaging in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The only possible diagnosis is pulmonary sling
The only possible diagnosis is gastric varix
The finding proves duplicated IVC
The finding proves coronary artery aneurysm
The source frames the differential as lymph node versus duplicated or left-sided SVC
options_after: The principal possible diagnosis is pulmonary sling
The principal possible diagnosis is gastric varix
The finding proves duplicated IVC
The finding proves coronary artery aneurysm
The source frames the differential as lymph node versus duplicated or left-sided SVC
updates.explanation: The source states that the classic left-sided SVC appearance can only realistically be a lymph node or a duplicated/left-sided SVC in that location. This is a chest venous anomaly recognition clue. Pulmonary sling, gastric varix, duplicated IVC and coronary aneurysm are different entities.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute aortic syndromes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stanford type B disease is entirely proximal to the left subclavian artery
The three acute aortic syndromes discussed are dissection, intramural haematoma and penetrating ulcer
Stanford type A disease begins distal to the left subclavian artery in the source
Penetrating ulcer is primarily a disease of the aortic root in the source
Stanford type A disease involves the ascending aorta or arch proximal to the left subclavian artery
options_after: Stanford type B disease is predominantly proximal to the left subclavian artery
The three acute aortic syndromes discussed are dissection, intramural haematoma and penetrating ulcer
Stanford type A disease begins distal to the left subclavian artery in the source
Penetrating ulcer is primarily a disease of the aortic root in the source
Stanford type A disease involves the ascending aorta or arch proximal to the left subclavian artery
updates.explanation: The source groups dissection, intramural haematoma and penetrating ulcer as acute aortic syndromes and applies the Stanford location framework to them. Stanford type A involves the ascending aorta/proximal arch, while type B begins distal to the left subclavian artery. Penetrating ulcers nearly never occur in the aortic root in the source because high flow protects that region from atherosclerosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding penetrating ulcer treatment and morphology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Uncomplicated type B penetrating ulcer may be managed medically like type B dissection
Penetrating ulcers treated with grafting always do better than dissections
Fusiform infrarenal aneurysm is the source pattern rule for penetrating ulcer
Intervention is considered for instability, pain, rupture, distal emboli or rapid enlargement
Saccular aneurysm below the diaphragm is always benign atherosclerosis in the source
options_after: Uncomplicated type B penetrating ulcer may be managed medically like type B dissection
Penetrating ulcers treated with grafting characteristically do better than dissections
Fusiform infrarenal aneurysm is the source pattern rule for penetrating ulcer
Intervention is considered for instability, pain, rupture, distal emboli or rapid enlargement
Saccular aneurysm below the diaphragm is characteristically benign atherosclerosis in the source
updates.explanation: The source treats uncomplicated type B penetrating ulcer similarly to type B dissection, but lists instability, pain, rupture, emboli and rapid enlargement as reasons to treat. A saccular aneurysm above the diaphragm suggests penetrating ulcer; below the diaphragm, infection/mycotic aneurysm should lead the differential rather than benign atherosclerosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding aortic dissection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Atherosclerosis is the main tested cause of classic dissection in the source
Dissection is the commonest acute aortic syndrome in the source
Pregnancy and sympathomimetic stimulant use are unrelated to dissection risk in the source
Dissection nearly never occurs in the aortic root
Hypertension is the main factor producing intimal tear and two lumens
options_after: Atherosclerosis is the main tested cause of classic dissection in the source
Dissection is the commonest acute aortic syndrome in the source
Pregnancy and sympathomimetic stimulant use are unrelated to dissection risk in the source
Dissection nearly will not occur in the aortic root
Hypertension is the main factor producing intimal tear and two lumens
updates.explanation: The source describes dissection as the commonest acute aortic syndrome and emphasises hypertension causing an intimal tear and two lumens. Connective tissue disease, pregnancy and sympathomimetic stimulant use are classic risk settings. Atherosclerosis is instead the key driver for penetrating ulcer in the source framing.

updates.question_text: Regarding Stanford classification of dissection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stanford A dissections involve the ascending aorta and are treated surgically in the source
Stanford B always requires immediate open surgery, even if uncomplicated
Stanford B accounts for most dissections in the source
Stanford B dissections occur distal to the left subclavian artery and are treated medically unless complicated
Stanford A is defined by isolated abdominal aortic involvement below the renal arteries
options_after: Stanford A dissections involve the ascending aorta and are treated surgically in the source
Stanford B characteristically requires immediate open surgery, even if uncomplicated
Stanford B accounts for most dissections in the source
Stanford B dissections occur distal to the left subclavian artery and are treated medically unless complicated
Stanford A is defined by isolated abdominal aortic involvement below the renal arteries
updates.explanation: Stanford A involves the ascending aorta/proximal arch and is surgical. Stanford B is distal to the left subclavian and usually treated medically unless complicated by malperfusion or other high-risk features. The source states that Stanford A, not Stanford B, accounts for most dissections.

updates.question_text: Regarding branch vessel origins in aortic dissection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The true lumen usually contains the origins of the celiac trunk, SMA and right renal artery in the source
The false lumen always supplies the right renal artery in the source
The floating viscera sign describes branch vessels opacifying during aortography while little true-lumen aortic opacification is seen
The true lumen usually contains the origin of the left renal artery in the source
The floating viscera sign is a finding of gastric varices
options_after: The true lumen usually contains the origins of the celiac trunk, SMA and right renal artery in the source
The false lumen characteristically supplies the right renal artery in the source
The floating viscera sign describes branch vessels opacifying during aortography while little true-lumen aortic opacification is seen
The true lumen usually contains the origin of the left renal artery in the source
The floating viscera sign is a finding of gastric varices
updates.explanation: The source gives a memory rule for abdominal branch origins: true lumen tends to supply the celiac trunk, SMA and right renal artery, while the false lumen tends to supply the left renal artery. The floating viscera sign is an angiographic dissection sign where branch vessels opacify while normal antegrade true-lumen aortic opacification is poor. Gastric varices are unrelated portal-systemic collaterals.

updates.question_text: Regarding differentiating aneurysm with mural thrombus from thrombosed dissection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mural thrombus always produces a cobweb sign
Thrombosed dissection cannot displace calcifications
Dissection tends to spiral, whereas mural thrombus tends to drop straight down
Mural thrombus usually displaces intimal calcification into the lumen in the source
This distinction is made by measuring the ovarian artery
options_after: Mural thrombus characteristically produces a cobweb sign
Thrombosed dissection will not displace calcifications
Dissection tends to spiral, whereas mural thrombus tends to drop straight down
Mural thrombus usually displaces intimal calcification into the lumen in the source
This distinction is made by measuring the ovarian artery
updates.explanation: The source gives a practical shape rule: dissection tends to spiral, while mural thrombus tends to descend more directly. Dissection can displace intimal calcifications; ordinary mural thrombus does not have that same calcification-displacement pattern. Cobweb sign belongs to the false lumen in dissection rather than ordinary mural thrombus.

updates.question_text: Regarding intramural haematoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Intramural haematoma can appear as a T1-bright crescent
It is defined by a visible intimal flap with two contrast-filled lumens
It is always caused by a replaced hepatic artery
It is primarily a portal-systemic collateral
It is diagnostic of coarctation
options_after: Intramural haematoma can appear as a T1-bright crescent
It is defined by a visible intimal flap with two contrast-filled lumens
It is characteristically caused by a replaced hepatic artery
It is primarily a portal-systemic collateral
It is diagnostic of coarctation
updates.explanation: The source lists T1-bright crescent as one way intramural haematoma can be shown. Non-contrast CT hyperdensity is another presentation, and contrast CT may make it hard to distinguish from plaque. A visible flap with two lumens is more typical of dissection.

updates.question_text: Regarding predictors of poor outcome in intramural haematoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All intramural haematomas inevitably rupture immediately
Haematoma thickness greater than 2 cm is a poor prognostic feature
Intramural haematoma with penetrating ulcer has a better outcome than all other combinations
Aneurysmal aortic dilatation of 5 cm or more is a poor prognostic feature
Thin intramural haematoma with no progression is listed as the highest-risk pattern
options_after: Most intramural haematomas inevitably rupture immediately
Haematoma thickness greater than 2 cm is a poor prognostic feature
Intramural haematoma with penetrating ulcer has a better outcome than most other combinations
Aneurysmal aortic dilatation of 5 cm or more is a poor prognostic feature
Thin intramural haematoma without progression is listed as the highest-risk pattern
updates.explanation: The source lists thickness greater than 2 cm and aortic aneurysmal dilatation of 5 cm or more as adverse features. Progression to dissection or penetrating ulcer is also adverse, and IMH with penetrating ulcer is worse than IMH with dissection. Many intramural haematomas regress rather than rupturing immediately.

updates.question_text: Regarding true aneurysm and pseudoaneurysm, which of the following statements are correct?

Yin-yang flow alone is completely specific for pseudoaneurysm
A true aneurysm is enlargement to 1.5 times expected diameter with all three wall layers intact
Pseudoaneurysm has lower rupture risk than true aneurysm in the source framing
To-and-fro flow in the neck plus clinical history helps distinguish pseudoaneurysm
options_after: A pseudoaneurysm is a contained rupture with primarily the adventitia characteristically intact
Yin-yang flow alone is completely specific for pseudoaneurysm
A true aneurysm is enlargement to 1.5 times expected diameter with all three wall layers intact
Pseudoaneurysm has lower rupture risk than true aneurysm in the source framing
To-and-fro flow in the neck plus clinical history helps distinguish pseudoaneurysm
updates.explanation: The source defines true aneurysm by intact vessel wall layers and pseudoaneurysm by contained rupture with wall layers not intact. To-and-fro flow in the neck plus the clinical history is the most useful ultrasound distinction. Yin-yang flow can also be seen in saccular true aneurysms, and pseudoaneurysms carry higher rupture risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding SVC syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: SVC syndrome occurs from complete or near-complete obstruction of SVC flow

Fibrosing mediastinitis is impossible as a cause in the source
Central venous catheter or pacemaker wire thrombus cannot cause it
Partial SVC narrowing without flow obstruction is sufficient for the classic syndrome in the source

The classic presentation is isolated calf swelling
Fibrosing mediastinitis is excluded from the differential in the source
Central venous catheter or pacemaker wire thrombus will not cause it
Partial SVC narrowing without flow obstruction is sufficient for the classic syndrome in the source
updates.explanation: SVC syndrome is caused by complete or near-complete SVC obstruction. The source lists external compression by lymphoma or lung cancer and intravascular obstruction from central venous catheter or pacemaker wire thrombus. The expected presentation is face, neck and bilateral arm swelling; fibrosing mediastinitis is a less common testable cause.

updates.question_text: Regarding traumatic thoracic aortic pseudoaneurysm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The ascending aorta is never injured in trauma
The aortic isthmus is the most common site in surviving patients
Chest radiograph clues include widened mediastinum and depressed left main bronchus, but rightward NG tube deviation is not listed in the source
The mechanism is related to tethering at the ligamentum arteriosum in the source
The most common visible living-patient site is the inferior mesenteric artery
options_after: The ascending aorta is not injured in trauma
The aortic isthmus is the most common site in surviving patients
Chest radiograph clues include widened mediastinum and depressed left main bronchus, but rightward NG tube deviation is not listed in the source
The mechanism is related to tethering at the ligamentum arteriosum in the source
The most common visible living-patient site is the inferior mesenteric artery
updates.explanation: The source states that the isthmus is the most common traumatic pseudoaneurysm site in living patients, likely due to tethering by the ligamentum arteriosum. It lists several classic radiographic clues of acute injury, including widened mediastinum, rightward NG tube deviation, depressed left main bronchus and left apical cap. Ascending aortic injury may be common but is often fatal before imaging.

updates.question_text: Regarding ascending aortic calcification and aneurysm aetiology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Atherosclerosis typically spares the ascending aorta in the source
Connective tissue disease tends to spare the aortic root
Atherosclerosis is never a cause of aneurysm anywhere in the source
Takayasu arteritis and syphilis should be considered with ascending aortic calcification
Medial degeneration is the most common cause of ascending aortic aneurysm
options_after: Atherosclerosis typically spares the ascending aorta in the source
Connective tissue disease tends to spare the aortic root
Atherosclerosis is not a cause of aneurysm anywhere in the source
Takayasu arteritis and syphilis should be considered with ascending aortic calcification
Medial degeneration is the most common cause of ascending aortic aneurysm
updates.explanation: The source notes that ordinary atherosclerosis tends to spare the ascending aorta, making Takayasu and syphilis important considerations with ascending calcification. Ascending aneurysm is most commonly related to medial degeneration. Connective tissue disease often involves the aortic root, and atherosclerosis remains the most common overall aneurysm cause.

updates.question_text: Regarding vascular manifestations of NF1, which of the following statements are correct?

Aneurysms and stenoses can occur in the aorta and larger arteries

The mechanism is usually arterial wall dysplasia rather than simple atherosclerosis

Aneurysms and stenoses can occur in the aorta and larger arteries
Renal artery stenosis can cause renovascular hypertension in children
The classic vascular look is orificial renal artery stenosis in a hypertensive child or teenager
The mechanism is usually arterial wall dysplasia rather than simple atherosclerosis
updates.explanation: The source notes that vascular findings can occur in NF1, including aneurysms and stenoses of larger vessels and dysplastic smaller vessels. Renal artery stenosis can produce renovascular hypertension in children, classically orificial. The mechanism is arterial wall dysplasia more often than perivascular neurofibroma.

updates.question_text: Regarding Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?

Conventional angiography and other percutaneous procedures should be avoided when possible because of arterial dissection risk
It is defined by atherosclerotic calcification of the ascending aorta only
Aortic aneurysm imaging may resemble Marfan syndrome and involve the aortic root
Abdominal visceral artery aneurysms are common in the source

Conventional angiography and other percutaneous procedures should be avoided when possible because of arterial dissection risk
It is defined by atherosclerotic calcification of the ascending aorta
Aortic aneurysm imaging may resemble Marfan syndrome and involve the aortic root
Abdominal visceral artery aneurysms are common in the source
updates.explanation: The source emphasises vascular fragility in Ehlers-Danlos, with bleeding and dissection risk. It warns against invasive angiography and percutaneous procedures when possible. Aortic aneurysms may resemble Marfan syndrome and visceral arterial aneurysms are common.

updates.question_text: Regarding inflammatory aortic aneurysm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Inflammatory aneurysm is more common in young men and most patients are symptomatic in the source
Elevated ESR is more typical than in ordinary atherosclerotic AAA
It has no rupture risk unless larger than ordinary atherosclerotic thresholds
Ureteral involvement can cause hydronephrosis or renal failure
It is characterised by complete distal aortic occlusion at the bifurcation

Elevated ESR is more typical than in ordinary atherosclerotic AAA
It lacks rupture risk unless larger than ordinary atherosclerotic thresholds
Ureteral involvement can cause hydronephrosis or renal failure
It is characterised by complete distal aortic occlusion at the bifurcation
updates.explanation: The source describes inflammatory aneurysm as symptomatic, more common in young men and associated with elevated ESR. Periaortic inflammation can involve the ureters, causing hydronephrosis or renal failure. It carries increased rupture risk regardless of size, and complete distal occlusion is Leriche syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding aortic coarctation and pseudocoarctation, which of the following statements are correct?

Adult/postductal coarctation can show leg claudication, arm-leg blood pressure differences, rib notching and figure 3 sign
Rib notching most often involves ribs 4-8 and spares ribs 1-2

Pseudocoarctation has no pressure gradient, collateral formation or rib notching

Rib notching most often involves ribs 4-8 and spares ribs 1-2
Pseudocoarctation requires immediate repair because it characteristically has a high pressure gradient
Pseudocoarctation has no pressure gradient, collateral formation or rib notching
updates.explanation: The source links coarctation with Turner syndrome, bicuspid aortic valve, figure 3 sign and rib notching. Adult/postductal disease causes collateral formation and arm-leg pressure differences; rib notching spares the first two ribs. Pseudocoarctation mimics narrowing but lacks pressure gradient, collaterals and rib notching, although aneurysmal dilatation can require follow-up.

updates.question_text: Regarding thoracic outlet syndrome and Paget-Schroetter syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stenting is usually first-line before decompressive surgery in Paget-Schroetter syndrome
Thoracic outlet syndrome is compression of subclavian vessels and/or brachial plexus at the thoracic inlet
Thoracic outlet syndrome is caused only by pulmonary sling

Paget-Schroetter syndrome is effort thrombosis of the subclavian vein related to thoracic outlet physiology
options_after: Stenting is usually first-line before decompressive surgery in Paget-Schroetter syndrome
Thoracic outlet syndrome is compression of subclavian vessels and/or brachial plexus at the thoracic inlet
Thoracic outlet syndrome is caused primarily by pulmonary sling
Most cases are neurogenic in the source, with nerve involvement much more common than venous or arterial involvement
Paget-Schroetter syndrome is effort thrombosis of the subclavian vein related to thoracic outlet physiology
updates.explanation: Thoracic outlet syndrome is a spectrum of brachial plexus and subclavian vessel compression, with neurogenic disease much more common than venous or arterial disease. Paget-Schroetter syndrome is effort thrombosis of the subclavian vein, usually in athletes or repetitive arm elevation. Stenting is generally avoided until after decompression to prevent crush injury.

updates.question_text: Regarding treatment priorities for visceral artery aneurysms in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All splenic artery aneurysms under 2 cm are always ignored in patients planning pregnancy
Splenic artery pseudoaneurysm should be treated
Hepatic artery aneurysm is treated only if it is caused by thoracic outlet syndrome
SMA aneurysm is usually less clinically important than an incidental venous malformation
SMA aneurysm is treated because of rupture and mesenteric ischaemia risk
options_after: Most splenic artery aneurysms under 2 cm are characteristically ignored in patients planning pregnancy
Splenic artery pseudoaneurysm should be treated
Hepatic artery aneurysm is treated primarily if it is caused by thoracic outlet syndrome
SMA aneurysm is usually less clinically important than an incidental venous malformation
SMA aneurysm is treated because of rupture and mesenteric ischaemia risk
updates.explanation: The source advises treatment of visceral pseudoaneurysms and treats SMA aneurysms aggressively because rupture and mesenteric ischaemia are important risks. Splenic aneurysm treatment is favoured for larger lesions, pseudoaneurysms and women planning pregnancy. Hepatic artery aneurysm treatment is based on symptoms, size and specific conditions such as FMD or PAN, not thoracic outlet syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding median arcuate ligament syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is diagnostic only when the patient has no symptoms
It is caused by compression of the left common iliac vein by the right common iliac artery
It is compression of the celiac artery by the median arcuate ligament
It is primarily a renal parenchymal tumour angiographic pattern
It is the most common cause of pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm
options_after: It is diagnostic primarily when the patient lacks symptoms
It is caused by compression of the left common iliac vein by the right common iliac artery
It is compression of the celiac artery by the median arcuate ligament
It is primarily a renal parenchymal tumour angiographic pattern
It is the most common cause of pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm
updates.explanation: Median arcuate ligament syndrome is celiac artery compression by the median arcuate ligament. The source notes that some compression can be present without a syndrome; symptoms such as abdominal pain and weight loss make it clinically relevant. Left common iliac vein compression describes May-Thurner syndrome. RCC vascularity and pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm are unrelated topics.

updates.question_text: Regarding chronic mesenteric ischaemia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The splenic flexure is irrelevant because it has no watershed physiology
Good collaterals do not affect symptoms in chronic mesenteric ischaemia in the source
Classically, significant stenosis of two of the three main mesenteric vessels plus symptoms is expected
The source states that chronic disease is usually caused by popliteal entrapment
Postprandial pain and food fear are typical clinical clues
options_after: The splenic flexure is irrelevant because it lacks watershed physiology
Good collaterals do not affect symptoms in chronic mesenteric ischaemia in the source
Classically, significant stenosis of two of the three main mesenteric vessels plus symptoms is expected
The source states that chronic disease is usually caused by popliteal entrapment
Postprandial pain and food fear are typical clinical clues
updates.explanation: The source frames chronic mesenteric ischaemia as symptomatic stenosis of two out of three major mesenteric vessels, with postprandial pain and food fear as classic clues. Collateral adequacy modifies symptoms, so severe disease can be silent if collaterals are good. The splenic flexure is a key watershed location. Popliteal entrapment is an extremity arterial condition.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute mesenteric ischaemia categories, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Arterial occlusion is one of the major acute categories
Venous occlusion is one of the major acute categories
All acute mesenteric ischaemia requires an intimal flap extending into the SMA
Non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia is associated with systemic hypoperfusion or vasospasm
Strangulation is usually secondary to closed-loop obstruction
options_after: Arterial occlusion is one of the major acute categories
Venous occlusion is one of the major acute categories
Most acute mesenteric ischaemia requires an intimal flap extending into the SMA
Non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia is associated with systemic hypoperfusion or vasospasm
Strangulation is usually secondary to closed-loop obstruction
updates.explanation: The source divides acute mesenteric ischaemia into arterial, venous, non-occlusive and strangulation mechanisms. Non-occlusive disease is linked to shock, pressors, hypoperfusion or vasospasm, while strangulation is usually related to closed-loop obstruction. An intimal flap extending into a branch vessel describes static obstruction in aortic dissection, not the required mechanism for all mesenteric ischaemia.

updates.question_text: Regarding non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is diagnosed only when a venous thrombus is seen in the SMV
It is caused by compression of the left renal vein under the SMA
It is suggested by shock, pressor use, recent major surgery, recent myocardial infarction or major blood loss
It is usually a painless incidental angiographic finding
It is primarily a peripheral arterial aneurysm syndrome
options_after: It is diagnosed primarily when a venous thrombus is seen in the SMV
It is caused by compression of the left renal vein under the SMA
It is suggested by shock, pressor use, recent major surgery, recent myocardial infarction or major blood loss
It is usually a painless incidental angiographic finding
It is primarily a peripheral arterial aneurysm syndrome
updates.explanation: Non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia is a hypoperfusion or vasospasm problem, so the clinical setting is central: shock, pressors, blood loss, recent myocardial infarction or major surgery. It does not require an arterial or venous clot. Left renal vein compression is nutcracker syndrome, and peripheral arterial aneurysm syndromes are separate topics.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging clues to non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Delayed portal venous filling can be a clue
Watershed segments such as the splenic flexure and rectosigmoid junction may be involved
The bowel wall is always paper-thin and never thickened
Narrow SMA and intramural branches can be seen
It is classically centred on the pampiniform plexus
options_after: Delayed portal venous filling can be a clue
Watershed segments such as the splenic flexure and rectosigmoid junction may be involved
The bowel wall is characteristically paper-thin rather than thickened
Narrow SMA and intramural branches can be seen
It is classically centred on the pampiniform plexus
