options_before: Conversion can be immediate if access was uncomplicated and the patient is not bleeding or uroseptic
Conversion is mandatory even if the bladder has outlet obstruction
Neurogenic bladder is an ideal indication for internal drainage into the bladder
If the patient is bleeding significantly or uroseptic, conversion should be delayed until stabilisation
Antegrade conversion is impossible once a PCN has been placed
options_after: Conversion can be immediate if access was uncomplicated and the patient is not bleeding or uroseptic
Conversion is mandatory even if the bladder has outlet obstruction
Neurogenic bladder is an ideal indication for internal drainage into the bladder
If the patient is bleeding significantly or uroseptic, conversion should be delayed until stabilisation
Antegrade conversion is not feasible after placement of a percutaneous nephrostomy
updates.explanation: The source allows direct conversion from PCN to NUS if access was not complicated by substantial bleeding or sepsis. If the patient is bleeding or uroseptic, the patient should be allowed to stabilise before conversion. Outlet obstruction, neurogenic bladder and bladder tumours are reasons not to drain into the bladder.

updates.question_text: Regarding contraindications to suprapubic cystostomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A clearly distended bladder with no overlying bowel is a contraindication
Normal coagulation is a contraindication
Inability to distend the bladder is a contraindication
Absence of prior pelvic surgery is a contraindication
A thin anterior abdominal wall is a contraindication by itself
options_after: A clearly distended bladder without overlying bowel is a contraindication
Normal coagulation is a contraindication
Inability to distend the bladder is a contraindication
Absence of prior pelvic surgery is a contraindication
A thin anterior abdominal wall is a contraindication by itself
updates.explanation: The source lists inability to distend the bladder, inability to displace overlying small bowel, extensive pelvic surgery/scar, body habitus and coagulopathy as contraindications or limitations. A distended bladder without overlying bowel and normal coagulation are not contraindications.

updates.question_text: Regarding bleeding risk in renal biopsy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Aspirin is continued because platelet function recovers fully within 24 hours
SIR practice guidance treats renal biopsy as a significant bleeding-risk procedure
Renal biopsy bleeding is easy to detect and control in all patients
Transjugular renal biopsy is never considered in high bleeding-risk patients
Aspirin is held for 5 days before renal biopsy in the source
options_after: Aspirin is continued because platelet function recovers fully within 24 hours
SIR practice guidance treats renal biopsy as a significant bleeding-risk procedure
Renal biopsy bleeding is easy to detect and control in most patients
Transjugular renal biopsy is not considered in high bleeding-risk patients
Aspirin is held for 5 days before renal biopsy in the source
updates.explanation: Renal biopsy is treated as a significant bleeding-risk procedure that can be difficult to detect or control. The source states that aspirin is held for 5 days, reflecting irreversible platelet inhibition and partial platelet replenishment over several days. A transjugular route can be considered in high bleeding-risk situations.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal radiofrequency ablation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: RFA is an alternative to partial nephrectomy or laparoscopic nephrectomy in selected renal tumours
Lesions close to the collecting system are always safer to burn than to freeze
Angiomyolipomas are treated around 4 cm because of bleeding risk
Superficial lesions are generally more suitable for RFA
RFA is described as lowering GFR substantially in routine cases
options_after: RFA is an alternative to partial nephrectomy or laparoscopic nephrectomy in selected renal tumours
Lesions close to the collecting system are characteristically safer to burn than to freeze
Angiomyolipomas are treated around 4 cm because of bleeding risk
Superficial lesions are generally more suitable for RFA
RFA is described as lowering GFR substantially in routine cases
updates.explanation: The source lists renal RFA as an alternative treatment for selected benign and malignant renal lesions. AML treatment around 4 cm is linked to bleeding risk. Superficial lesions are more suitable for RFA, whereas lesions near the collecting system may be better treated with cryoablation or protected with pyeloperfusion if RFA is used.

updates.question_text: Regarding residual or recurrent disease after renal ablation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Any initial size increase in the first 1-2 months proves treatment failure in lesions under 3 cm
Nodular or crescentic enhancement should raise concern
Further size increase after the expected early period is always benign post-treatment oedema
Absence of enhancement always proves complete cure regardless of size behaviour
A new or enlarging bright T2 signal can suggest residual or recurrent disease
options_after: Any initial size increase in the first 1-2 months proves treatment failure in lesions under 3 cm
Nodular or crescentic enhancement should raise concern
Further size increase after the expected early period is characteristically benign post-treatment oedema
Absence of enhancement characteristically proves complete cure despite variation in size behaviour
A new or enlarging bright T2 signal can suggest residual or recurrent disease
updates.explanation: The source lists nodular or crescentic enhancement and new or enlarging bright T2 signal as concerning findings. It also notes that small lesions may appear larger in the first 1-2 months after successful treatment, so early size increase alone is not definitive failure. Later size increase should not be dismissed as benign oedema.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal artery stenosis treatment in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Atherosclerotic ostial stenosis is generally managed with high-quality medical therapy for multiple-choice purposes
All atherosclerotic renal artery stenoses require immediate stenting regardless of clinical context
Fibromuscular dysplasia is treated with angioplasty alone when there is a significant pressure gradient
FMD is treated primarily with covered stent placement before angioplasty
Surgery is first-line for all renal FMD lesions
options_after: Atherosclerotic ostial stenosis is generally managed with high-quality medical therapy for multiple-choice purposes
Most atherosclerotic renal artery stenoses require immediate stenting despite variation in clinical context
Fibromuscular dysplasia is treated with angioplasty alone when there is a significant pressure gradient
FMD is treated primarily with covered stent placement before angioplasty
Surgery is first-line for most renal FMD lesions
updates.explanation: The source states that atherosclerotic ostial stenosis is generally answered as high-quality medical therapy on multiple-choice questions, with angioplasty and stenting as a fallback if medical therapy is not an option. FMD is treated with angioplasty alone when pressure gradient criteria are met. Stents are reserved for complications such as flow-limiting dissection or rupture.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal angioplasty for fibromuscular dysplasia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The initial balloon is deliberately much larger than the normal distal renal artery
The balloon is not increased if a pressure gradient persists
Simultaneous pressure measurement in the distal renal artery and aorta is used
A distal renal/aortic pressure ratio below 0.90 supports angioplasty in the source
Pain during ballooning is ignored and never influences the procedure
options_after: The initial balloon is deliberately much larger than the normal distal renal artery
The balloon is not increased if a pressure gradient persists
Simultaneous pressure measurement in the distal renal artery and aorta is used
A distal renal/aortic pressure ratio below 0.90 supports angioplasty in the source
Pain during ballooning is ignored and will not influence the procedure
updates.explanation: The source describes simultaneous pressure measurements to identify a significant gradient, using a distal renal-to-aortic pressure ratio below 0.90. Balloon size is based on the normal distal renal artery and can be increased incrementally. Stenting is not first-line for uncomplicated FMD angioplasty.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal angioplasty risks and medications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Heparin is avoided because it increases restenosis
Thrombosis and vessel spasm are recognised risks
Aspirin is never used after renal angioplasty
Dissection and rupture are treated by coil embolising both kidneys
Calcium channel blockers may be used to decrease spasm risk
options_after: Heparin is avoided because it increases restenosis
Thrombosis and vessel spasm are recognised risks
Aspirin is not used after renal angioplasty
Dissection and rupture are treated by coil embolising both kidneys
Calcium channel blockers may be used to decrease spasm risk
updates.explanation: The source lists thrombosis and vessel spasm as risks of renal angioplasty. Calcium channel blockers can reduce spasm risk, while heparin is used to reduce thrombosis risk. Dissection or rupture may be treated with stenting if possible, and aspirin is commonly used around the procedure to reduce restenosis risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal haemorrhage after iatrogenic renal trauma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Renal arterial trauma can often be embolised
Renal arteries behave as end arteries, so infarction is a real risk
Renal collaterals reliably protect all renal parenchyma from infarction
Superselective embolisation is preferred when the patient is stable and kidney salvage is desired
If the patient is crashing, haemorrhage control takes priority over maximal nephron preservation
options_after: Renal arterial trauma can often be embolised
Renal arteries behave as end arteries, so infarction is a real risk
Renal collaterals reliably protect most renal parenchyma from infarction
Superselective embolisation is preferred when the patient is stable and kidney salvage is desired
If the patient is crashing, haemorrhage control takes priority over maximal nephron preservation
updates.explanation: The source notes that renal arterial trauma, often iatrogenic, can usually be embolised. Because renal arteries are end arteries, infarction is an important risk and superselective embolisation is preferred if feasible. In an unstable patient, bleeding control takes priority over prolonged attempts at superselection.

updates.question_text: Regarding occult arterial bleeding after nephrostomy placement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: If angiography is initially negative, all access should be abandoned without preserving the tract
The nephrostomy catheter can never tamponade bleeding
If angiography is initially negative, the PCN should be removed over a wire and angiography repeated
The next step is routine discharge because negative angiography excludes haemorrhage
The PCN should be removed without a wire to prevent re-access
options_after: If angiography is initially negative, most access should be abandoned without preserving the tract
The nephrostomy catheter will not tamponade bleeding
If angiography is initially negative, the PCN should be removed over a wire and angiography repeated
The next step is routine discharge because negative angiography excludes haemorrhage
The PCN should be removed without a wire to prevent re-access
updates.explanation: The source emphasises removing the nephrostomy tube over a wire and repeating angiography when the bleeding source is occult, because the catheter itself may tamponade the bleeding site. Preserving wire access matters. A negative initial angiogram does not exclude catheter-tamponaded bleeding in an unstable patient.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal artery aneurysm treatment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Small segmental renal artery aneurysms can be treated with coils
Main renal artery aneurysms are always treated by sacrificing the entire kidney
Covered stents are contraindicated for main renal artery aneurysms
Bare metal stents cannot be used as a scaffold for detachable coils
Segmental aneurysms are best managed by suprapubic cystostomy
options_after: Small segmental renal artery aneurysms can be treated with coils
Main renal artery aneurysms are characteristically treated by sacrificing the entire kidney
Covered stents are contraindicated for main renal artery aneurysms
Bare metal stents will not be used as a scaffold for detachable coils
Segmental aneurysms are best managed by suprapubic cystostomy
updates.explanation: The source gives coils for small segmental renal artery aneurysms. For main renal artery aneurysms, a covered stent can exclude the aneurysm, or a bare metal stent can be used as a scaffold with detachable coils placed into the sac. The management depends on location, not bladder drainage.

updates.question_text: Regarding pleural drainage and chest tubes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A trapped-lung vacu-thorax always requires urgent chest tube escalation
Pleurodesis is effective treatment for trapped lung
Needle or tube placement is performed above the rib to avoid the neurovascular bundle
Continuous air bubbles in the drainage chamber suggest an air leak such as bronchopleural fistula
INR is irrelevant before chest tube placement
options_after: A trapped-lung vacu-thorax characteristically requires urgent chest tube escalation
Pleurodesis is effective treatment for trapped lung
Needle or tube placement is performed above the rib to avoid the neurovascular bundle
Continuous air bubbles in the drainage chamber suggest an air leak such as bronchopleural fistula
INR is irrelevant before chest tube placement
updates.explanation: The source highlights the above-rib approach to avoid the intercostal neurovascular bundle. Continuous bubbling in the drainage system suggests an air leak, including bronchopleural fistula in a test setting. A trapped-lung vacu-thorax does not itself require urgent treatment, pleurodesis does not solve trapped lung, and INR should generally be below 1.5 before chest tube placement.

updates.question_text: Regarding management of pneumothorax after lung biopsy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Oxygen can be given to speed pneumothorax resorption
Every post-biopsy pneumothorax requires immediate surgical chest tube placement
Manual aspiration through the introducer needle may be attempted
An enlarging pneumothorax is managed with routine discharge only
Tube placement is more likely if a large volume of air is aspirated or the patient is symptomatic
options_after: Oxygen can be given to speed pneumothorax resorption
Routine post-biopsy pneumothorax requires immediate surgical chest tube placement
Manual aspiration through the introducer needle may be attempted
An enlarging pneumothorax is managed with routine discharge
Tube placement is more likely if a large volume of air is aspirated or the patient is symptomatic
updates.explanation: The source algorithm starts with oxygen and attempted manual aspiration through the introducer needle. Tube placement is suggested when a large volume is aspirated, the pneumothorax is larger or enlarging, or the patient is short of breath. Small stable pneumothoraces may be followed with chest radiographs.

updates.question_text: Regarding chest tube troubleshooting, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Loss of water-seal chamber fluctuation can indicate full lung expansion or tube obstruction
Persistent bubbling indicates an air leak
CXR can help distinguish a clogged tube from an expanded lung
Side holes outside the pleural space can contribute to subcutaneous emphysema
Subcutaneous emphysema always requires tube removal even when the tube is correctly positioned
options_after: Loss of water-seal chamber fluctuation can indicate full lung expansion or tube obstruction
Persistent bubbling indicates an air leak
CXR can help distinguish a clogged tube from an expanded lung
Side holes outside the pleural space can contribute to subcutaneous emphysema
Subcutaneous emphysema characteristically requires tube removal even when the tube is correctly positioned
updates.explanation: The source links absent fluctuation to either full lung expansion or tube obstruction, with CXR helping distinguish them. Persistent bubbling reflects an air leak. Subcutaneous emphysema requires checking that all side holes lie within the pleural space; if the tube is correctly positioned, it is often self-limited.

updates.question_text: Regarding relative contraindications to pulmonary angiography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: If pulmonary angiography proceeds despite severe pulmonary hypertension, contrast is injected into the main pulmonary artery at high volume
If proceeding in known LBBB, prophylactic pacing is never considered
Severe pulmonary hypertension with elevated right heart pressures is a relative contraindication
Known left bundle branch block is a concern because right heart catheterisation can provoke right bundle branch block
Pulmonary hypertension never changes the contrast plan
options_after: If pulmonary angiography proceeds despite severe pulmonary hypertension, contrast is injected into the main pulmonary artery at high volume
If proceeding in known LBBB, prophylactic pacing is not considered
Severe pulmonary hypertension with elevated right heart pressures is a relative contraindication
Known left bundle branch block is a concern because right heart catheterisation can provoke right bundle branch block
Pulmonary hypertension will not change the contrast plan
updates.explanation: The source flags severe pulmonary hypertension and LBBB as relative contraindication scenarios. Pulmonary hypertension can require lower-burden injection into a right or left pulmonary artery rather than the main pulmonary artery. LBBB matters because catheter-induced RBBB can create complete block, so prophylactic pacing may be used if the procedure must proceed.

updates.question_text: Regarding pulmonary embolism intervention, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Massive PE is defined by a tiny incidental clot without haemodynamic effect
Most PE patients are treated medically with anticoagulation
Patients who cannot receive anticoagulation may need an IVC filter
All PE patients should receive pulmonary artery stents as first-line therapy
Transcatheter therapies are generally reserved for unstable massive PE
options_after: Massive PE is defined by a tiny incidental clot without haemodynamic effect
Most PE patients are treated medically with anticoagulation
Patients who cannot receive anticoagulation may need an IVC filter
Most PE patients should receive pulmonary artery stents as first-line therapy
Transcatheter therapies are generally reserved for unstable massive PE
updates.explanation: The source states that PE is usually treated medically with anticoagulation. If anticoagulation cannot be given, IVC filter placement is considered. Catheter-directed lysis, aspiration, fragmentation or stenting is reserved for unstable massive PE, where hypotension is the defining clinical concern.

updates.question_text: Regarding Rasmussen aneurysm in haemoptysis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is treated by lymphangiography through the toes
It is managed by uterine artery embolisation
It should be suspected when bronchial artery angiography is negative but bleeding persists in a patient with chronic pulmonary infection such as TB
It excludes the need for pulmonary artery angiography
It is a contraindication to coil embolisation in all cases
options_after: It is treated by lymphangiography through the toes
It is managed by uterine artery embolisation
It should be suspected when bronchial artery angiography is negative but bleeding persists in a patient with chronic pulmonary infection such as TB
It excludes the need for pulmonary artery angiography
It is a contraindication to coil embolisation in most cases
updates.explanation: The source frames Rasmussen aneurysm as the trap in haemoptysis: if bronchial angiography is negative and the context suggests chronic pulmonary infection such as TB, pulmonary artery angiography is needed. Once a Rasmussen aneurysm is identified, coil embolisation is the exception to the usual avoidance of coils for haemoptysis.

updates.question_text: Regarding superior vena cava occlusion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The goal is to restore flow only through collateral veins while leaving the SVC occluded
Acute SVC occlusion has no collaterals and is treated as an emergency
Chronic SVC occlusion is always more urgent than acute SVC occlusion
The pericardial reflection is irrelevant to SVC intervention complications
Chronic SVC occlusion has collaterals and is not treated as the same emergency
options_after: The goal is to restore flow primarily through collateral veins while leaving the SVC occluded
Acute SVC occlusion has no collaterals and is treated as an emergency
Chronic SVC occlusion is characteristically more urgent than acute SVC occlusion
The pericardial reflection is irrelevant to SVC intervention complications
Chronic SVC occlusion has collaterals and is not treated as the same emergency
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes acute SVC occlusion, with no collaterals and emergency status, from chronic SVC occlusion, which has collateral pathways. The treatment goal is to restore inline flow from at least one jugular vein down the SVC, not to preserve collateral-only drainage. The lower SVC has pericardial adjacency, so injury can cause haemopericardium and tamponade.

updates.question_text: Regarding patient selection for uterine artery embolisation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pre-procedure MRI/MRA is used to characterise fibroids and vascular anatomy
Smaller fibroids tend to do better than larger lesions
Degenerated leiomyomas are more likely to respond poorly
High T2 cellular fibroids tend to respond well
Cervical fibroids respond especially well because their blood supply is identical to typical fibroids
options_after: Pre-procedure MRI/MRA is used to characterise fibroids and vascular anatomy
Smaller fibroids tend to do better than larger lesions
Degenerated leiomyomas are more likely to respond poorly
High T2 cellular fibroids tend to respond well
Cervical fibroids respond especially well because their blood supply is closely comparable to typical fibroids
updates.explanation: The source stresses pre-treatment MRI/MRA for fibroid characterisation and vascular mapping. Degenerated non-enhancing fibroids respond poorly, while high T2 cellular fibroids tend to respond well. Smaller fibroids do better, and cervical fibroids respond poorly because of different blood supply.

updates.question_text: Regarding post-embolisation syndrome after UAE, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Blood cultures are mandatory for every low-grade fever within 24 hours after UAE
Low-grade fever lasting 3 days or less can be observed if no other infection features are present
Fever persisting beyond 3 days should be investigated
Fever after UAE is always proof of retained infected intracavitary fibroid
Post-embolisation syndrome classically includes fever and systemic symptoms after fibroid embolisation
options_after: Blood cultures are mandatory for routine low-grade fever within 24 hours after UAE
Low-grade fever lasting 3 days or less can be observed if no other infection features are present
Fever persisting beyond 3 days should be investigated
Fever after UAE is characteristically proof of retained infected intracavitary fibroid
Post-embolisation syndrome classically includes fever and systemic symptoms after fibroid embolisation
updates.explanation: The source describes post-embolisation syndrome as classically associated with fibroid embolisation. Low-grade fever for up to 3 days can be observed if no other signs suggest infection. Fever beyond that window should be worked up with cultures and antibiotics as appropriate.

updates.question_text: Regarding hysterosalpingography and fallopian tube recanalisation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: HSG is contraindicated in pregnancy and active pelvic infection
The ideal timing is the late secretory phase because the endometrium is thickest
Air bubbles cannot create filling defects on HSG
FTR is aimed at proximal or interstitial tubal obstruction rather than distal obstruction
FTR is performed during active infection because the tube is easier to cross
options_after: HSG is contraindicated in pregnancy and active pelvic infection
The ideal timing is the late secretory phase because the endometrium is thickest
Air bubbles will not create filling defects on HSG
FTR is aimed at proximal or interstitial tubal obstruction rather than distal obstruction
FTR is performed during active infection because the tube is easier to cross
updates.explanation: Pregnancy and active pelvic infection are contraindications to HSG and FTR. FTR targets proximal or interstitial tubal obstruction, while distal disease is treated surgically in the source. HSG is ideally performed in the proliferative phase, and air bubbles can cause false filling defects; the false options invert those points.

updates.question_text: Regarding lymphangiography for thoracic duct intervention, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lymphangiography is performed by catheterising the hepatic artery
Excess lipiodol has no pulmonary risk
Thoracic duct embolisation can be considered for leaking chylous pleural effusions
The cisterna chyli is irrelevant to thoracic duct embolisation
The thoracic duct is embolised with uterine particles
options_after: Lymphangiography is performed by catheterising the hepatic artery
Excess lipiodol lacks pulmonary risk
Thoracic duct embolisation can be considered for leaking chylous pleural effusions
The cisterna chyli is irrelevant to thoracic duct embolisation
The thoracic duct is embolised with uterine particles
updates.explanation: The source describes lymphangiography as a route to thoracic duct embolisation for chylous pleural effusion. The technical pathway involves lymphatic visualisation and cannulation, followed by lipiodol injection until the cisterna chyli is opacified. Excess lipiodol can cause oil pneumonitis, and the cisterna chyli is the access target for thoracic duct embolisation.

updates.question_text: Regarding fluoroscopic geometry for deciding whether a needle is superficial or deep, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Tilting the image intensifier toward the head makes a superficial needle look shorter
Tilting toward the head makes a deep needle look shorter
Tilting toward the feet makes a superficial needle look shorter
Tilting the image intensifier toward the feet makes a deep needle look shorter
Needle depth cannot be assessed by changing image intensifier tilt
options_after: Tilting the image intensifier toward the head makes a superficial needle look shorter
Tilting toward the head makes a deep needle look shorter
Tilting toward the feet makes a superficial needle look shorter
Tilting the image intensifier toward the feet makes a deep needle look shorter
Needle depth will not be assessed by changing image intensifier tilt
updates.explanation: The source gives a simple geometry rule: with the image intensifier tilted toward the head, a superficial needle appears shorter and a deep needle appears longer. With tilt toward the feet, a superficial needle appears longer and a deep needle appears shorter. This can help decide whether the needle is superficial or deep to the target.

updates.question_text: Regarding air embolus during central venous catheter insertion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The first manoeuvre is to sit the patient upright with the right side down
Oxygen is contraindicated because it expands intravascular air
Durant's manoeuvre uses left-lateral decubitus and head-down positioning
The source treats air embolus as a contraindication to all future venous access
Air embolus is managed by immediate uterine artery embolisation
options_after: The first manoeuvre is to sit the patient upright with the right side down
Oxygen is contraindicated because it expands intravascular air
Durant's manoeuvre uses left-lateral decubitus and head-down positioning
The source treats air embolus as a contraindication to most future venous access
Air embolus is managed by immediate uterine artery embolisation
updates.explanation: The source describes classic air embolus symptoms during central venous catheter insertion and gives Durant's manoeuvre as left-lateral decubitus with head-down positioning, also phrased as right side up or left side down with Trendelenburg. The next step after positioning is 100% oxygen.

updates.question_text: Regarding anticoagulation, sedation and local anaesthesia in IR, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Aspirin must always be held for moderate bleeding-risk procedures in the source
For moderate bleeding-risk procedures, INR should be corrected below 1.5
Naloxone reverses midazolam and flumazenil reverses opioids
Tinnitus and dizziness exclude lidocaine toxicity
Clopidogrel should be held for 5 days before moderate bleeding-risk procedures
options_after: Aspirin must characteristically be held for moderate bleeding-risk procedures in the source
For moderate bleeding-risk procedures, INR should be corrected below 1.5
Naloxone reverses midazolam and flumazenil reverses opioids
Tinnitus and dizziness exclude lidocaine toxicity
Clopidogrel should be held for 5 days before moderate bleeding-risk procedures
updates.explanation: The source gives INR below 1.5 and holding clopidogrel for 5 days for moderate bleeding-risk procedures, while aspirin need not be held in that category. Flumazenil reverses midazolam and naloxone reverses opioids; the false option reverses those antidotes. Tinnitus or dizziness are early lidocaine toxicity signs rather than excluding toxicity.

updates.question_text: Regarding procedure indications and contraindications from the IR summary tables, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: TIPS is indicated for variceal bleeding refractory to endoscopy and refractory ascites
Percutaneous biliary drainage is absolutely contraindicated in every patient with biliary obstruction
Heart failure is an indication rather than a contraindication to TIPS
Total thrombosis of the IVC is a contraindication to IVC filter placement
Sepsis is listed as an absolute contraindication to IVC filter placement
options_after: TIPS is indicated for variceal bleeding refractory to endoscopy and refractory ascites
Percutaneous biliary drainage is absolutely contraindicated in most patients with biliary obstruction
Heart failure is an indication rather than a contraindication to TIPS
Total thrombosis of the IVC is a contraindication to IVC filter placement
Sepsis is listed as an absolute contraindication to IVC filter placement
updates.explanation: The source table lists TIPS for refractory variceal bleeding and refractory ascites, with heart failure as an absolute contraindication. Total IVC thrombosis is a contraindication to IVC filter placement, while sepsis is specifically not a contraindication. Percutaneous biliary drainage is listed without absolute contraindications; the false option reverses that table entry.

updates.question_text: Regarding fingertip tuft fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Disruption of the nail plate makes a tuft fracture an open fracture
All tuft fractures require operative washout
An intact nail bed usually makes antibiotics mandatory
Tuft fractures are described as closed regardless of nail plate status
Antibiotics are used when the nail plate is disrupted
options_after: Disruption of the nail plate makes a tuft fracture an open fracture
Most tuft fractures require operative washout
An intact nail bed usually makes antibiotics mandatory
Tuft fractures are described as closed despite variation in nail plate status
Antibiotics are used when the nail plate is disrupted
updates.explanation: The source states that fingertip tuft fractures with nail plate disruption are considered open fractures and receive antibiotics. It contrasts this with intact nail bed injuries, which often do not need antibiotics. The source does not say these typically need operative washout.

updates.question_text: Regarding early fracture healing on radiographs, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A healing fracture becomes most sclerotic at 7-14 days
Granulation tissue forms only after 6-8 weeks
Granulation tissue at 7-14 days causes increased lucency at the fracture site
Repeat radiographs after 7-10 days may show a fracture line more clearly
Healing fractures should become radiographically invisible within 48 hours
options_after: A healing fracture becomes most sclerotic at 7-14 days
Granulation tissue forms primarily after 6-8 weeks
Granulation tissue at 7-14 days causes increased lucency at the fracture site
Repeat radiographs after 7-10 days may show a fracture line more clearly
Healing fractures should become radiographically invisible within 48 hours
updates.explanation: From a radiology perspective, the source emphasises that granulation tissue and bone resorption at around 7-14 days can make a healing fracture more lucent. This is the rationale behind repeat radiographs in 7-10 days when an occult fracture is suspected. The source does not describe early healing as immediate sclerosis or disappearance.

updates.question_text: Regarding abnormal fracture healing terminology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Delayed union means the fracture has healed in poor anatomic position
Delayed union means the fracture has not healed within the expected time period but may still heal
Non-union is defined as a fracture that always heals without intervention
Malunion means union in poor anatomic position
Classic non-union sites include the scaphoid, anterior tibia and lateral femoral neck
options_after: Delayed union means the fracture has healed in poor anatomic position
Delayed union means the fracture has not healed within the expected time period but may still heal
Non-union is defined as a fracture that characteristically heals without intervention
Malunion means union in poor anatomic position
Classic non-union sites include the scaphoid, anterior tibia and lateral femoral neck
updates.explanation: The source defines delayed union as failure to heal within the expected time while still potentially healing. Non-union implies healing will not occur without intervention, with classic sites including scaphoid, anterior tibia and lateral femoral neck. Malunion is union in poor anatomic position.

updates.question_text: Regarding compressive-side and tensile-side stress fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Compressive-side fractures are constantly pushed together and tend to do better
Tensile-side fractures are constantly pulled apart and are more problematic for healing
Tensile-side femoral neck fractures are always lower risk than compressive-side fractures
The femoral neck and tibia are highlighted as key locations for this distinction
Anterior midshaft tibial stress fractures are tensile-side injuries with poor healing
options_after: Compressive-side fractures are constantly pushed together and tend to do better
Tensile-side fractures are constantly pulled apart and are more problematic for healing
Tensile-side femoral neck fractures are characteristically lower risk than compressive-side fractures
The femoral neck and tibia are highlighted as key locations for this distinction
Anterior midshaft tibial stress fractures are tensile-side injuries with poor healing
updates.explanation: The source emphasises this distinction for the femoral neck and tibia. Compressive-side fractures are pushed together and generally heal better, whereas tensile-side fractures are pulled apart and heal poorly. It specifically describes anterior midshaft tibial stress fractures as bad-news tensile injuries, often called dreaded black lines.

updates.question_text: Regarding selected foot stress fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Calcaneal stress fractures run parallel to the trabecular lines
Calcaneal stress fractures are perpendicular to the trabecular lines
Navicular stress fractures are low risk because the navicular has no AVN concern
March fractures are metatarsal stress fractures
Navicular stress fractures are described in runners on hard surfaces
options_after: Calcaneal stress fractures run parallel to the trabecular lines
Calcaneal stress fractures are perpendicular to the trabecular lines
Navicular stress fractures are low risk because the navicular lacks AVN concern
March fractures are metatarsal stress fractures
Navicular stress fractures are described in runners on hard surfaces
updates.explanation: The source states that calcaneal stress fracture lines are perpendicular to the trabecular lines. It describes navicular stress fractures in runners on hard surfaces and highlights AVN risk by analogy with the scaphoid. March fracture is the metatarsal stress fracture classically seen in military recruits.

updates.question_text: Regarding scaphoid AVN and non-union patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The first radiographic sign of scaphoid AVN is sclerosis
The distal pole is at greatest risk because of antegrade blood supply
Avascular scaphoid always becomes T1 bright on MRI
A humpback deformity can follow angulation of fragments in a scaphoid waist fracture
Prieser disease refers to atraumatic AVN of the scaphoid
options_after: The first radiographic sign of scaphoid AVN is sclerosis
The distal pole is at greatest risk because of antegrade blood supply
Avascular scaphoid characteristically becomes T1 bright on MRI
A humpback deformity can follow angulation of fragments in a scaphoid waist fracture
Prieser disease refers to atraumatic AVN of the scaphoid
updates.explanation: The source explains that the dead proximal pole cannot remodel, so sclerosis is the first sign of AVN; later fragmentation may occur. MRI shows low T1 signal. A waist fracture can lead to humpback deformity from fragment angulation, and Prieser disease is atraumatic scaphoid AVN.

updates.question_text: Regarding carpal dislocations around the lunate, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Scapholunate dissociation is the least severe pattern in the spectrum described
Perilunate dislocation means the lunate stays aligned while surrounding carpal bones move
Midcarpal dislocation preserves normal radial alignment of both the lunate and capitate
Lunate dislocation is presented as less severe than scapholunate dissociation
Perilunate dislocation is never associated with scaphoid fracture
options_after: Scapholunate dissociation is the least severe pattern in the spectrum described
Perilunate dislocation means the lunate stays aligned while surrounding carpal bones move
Midcarpal dislocation preserves normal radial alignment of both the lunate and capitate
Lunate dislocation is presented as less severe than scapholunate dissociation
Perilunate dislocation is not associated with scaphoid fracture
updates.explanation: The source presents a severity spectrum from scapholunate dissociation through perilunate and midcarpal dislocation to lunate dislocation. In perilunate dislocation, the lunate remains in place while surrounding carpal bones move. Midcarpal dislocation loses radial alignment of both lunate and capitate, and lunate dislocation is presented as the most severe pattern. Perilunate dislocation has a high association with scaphoid fracture.

updates.question_text: Regarding normally communicating joint or synovial spaces, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The pisiform recess and radiocarpal joint should normally communicate
The glenohumeral joint and subacromial bursa should normally communicate
Excessive fluid in the pisiform recess should always be considered abnormal even when there is a radiocarpal effusion
The ankle joint and common peroneal tendon sheath should normally communicate
Communication between the glenohumeral joint and subacromial bursa excludes a full-thickness rotator cuff tear
options_after: The pisiform recess and radiocarpal joint should normally communicate
The glenohumeral joint and subacromial bursa should normally communicate
Excessive fluid in the pisiform recess should characteristically be considered abnormal even when there is a radiocarpal effusion
The ankle joint and common peroneal tendon sheath should normally communicate
Communication between the glenohumeral joint and subacromial bursa excludes a full-thickness rotator cuff tear
updates.explanation: The source states that the pisiform recess and radiocarpal joint normally communicate, so pisiform recess fluid can be explained by radiocarpal effusion. It contrasts this with the glenohumeral joint and subacromial bursa, which should not communicate; communication implies a full-thickness cuff tear. The ankle joint and common peroneal tendon sheath should not communicate.

updates.question_text: Regarding the triangular fibrocartilage complex, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the primary stabiliser and shock absorber of the distal radioulnar joint
Its components include the articular disc and volar/dorsal radioulnar ligaments
The hand surgeon only cares about the ECU sheath and UCL according to the source emphasis
Its listed components include the meniscus homologue, UCL and ECU tendon sheath
It is relevant to wrist loading activities
options_after: It is the primary stabiliser and shock absorber of the distal radioulnar joint
Its components include the articular disc and volar/dorsal radioulnar ligaments
The hand surgeon primarily cares about the ECU sheath and UCL according to the source emphasis
Its listed components include the meniscus homologue, UCL and ECU tendon sheath
It is relevant to wrist loading activities
updates.explanation: The source defines the TFCC as the primary stabiliser and shock absorber of the distal radioulnar joint. It lists five key components: articular disc, volar and dorsal radioulnar ligaments, meniscus homologue, UCL and ECU tendon sheath. The author highlights the articular disc and radioulnar ligaments as especially important to the hand surgeon.

updates.question_text: Regarding TFCC MRI signal and injury patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The TFC proper should be bright on all MRI sequences
The TFC proper should be dark on every sequence
Intermediate signal at the ulnar attachment always indicates a TFCC tear
Class 2 injuries are acute traumatic injuries unrelated to ulnar variance
Central perforations are presented as unexpected in older patients
options_after: The TFC proper should be bright on routine MRI sequences
The TFC proper should be dark on every sequence
Intermediate signal at the ulnar attachment characteristically indicates a TFCC tear
Class 2 injuries are acute traumatic injuries unrelated to ulnar variance
Central perforations are presented as unexpected in older patients
updates.explanation: The source states that the articular disc or TFC proper is dark on every MRI sequence. Intermediate signal at the ulnar attachment may be normal loose connective tissue rather than a tear. Class 2 injuries are chronic degenerative injuries associated with positive ulnar variance and ulnar impaction, and central perforations are common in older patients.

updates.question_text: Regarding named distal radius fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Colles fracture is an extra-articular distal metaphyseal fracture with dorsal angulation
Smith fracture is the reverse Colles pattern with volar angulation
Ulnar styloid fracture is commonly associated with both Colles and Smith patterns
Barton fracture is always extra-articular
Residual volar displacement after Smith fracture can result in carpal tunnel syndrome
options_after: Colles fracture is an extra-articular distal metaphyseal fracture with dorsal angulation
Smith fracture is the reverse Colles pattern with volar angulation
Ulnar styloid fracture is commonly associated with both Colles and Smith patterns
Barton fracture is characteristically extra-articular
Residual volar displacement after Smith fracture can result in carpal tunnel syndrome
updates.explanation: The source describes Colles as an extra-articular distal metaphyseal fracture with dorsal angulation, and Smith as the reverse pattern with volar angulation. Ulnar styloid fracture is commonly associated. Smith fracture can be complicated by carpal tunnel syndrome if residual volar displacement persists. Barton fracture is intra-articular and involves the dorsal or volar rim.

updates.question_text: Which single statement best captures the source distinction between fatigue and insufficiency fractures?
options_before: Fatigue fracture is normal stress on abnormal bone
Fatigue fracture is abnormal stress on normal bone
Insufficiency fracture is abnormal stress on normal bone
Pathologic fracture is synonymous with every stress fracture
Open fracture is defined by ligament disruption rather than a wound
options_after: Fatigue fracture is normal stress on abnormal bone
Fatigue fracture is abnormal stress on normal bone
Insufficiency fracture is abnormal stress on normal bone
Pathologic fracture is synonymous with routine stress fracture
Open fracture is defined by ligament disruption rather than a wound
updates.explanation: The clearest distinction is that fatigue fracture means abnormal stress on normal bone. Insufficiency fracture means normal stress on abnormal bone. The source uses pathologic fracture more specifically for fracture through a lytic lesion in the multiple-choice setting, and open fracture requires an associated open wound.

updates.question_text: Regarding delayed EPL rupture after distal radius fracture, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is linked to irregular morphology of Lister tubercle after distal radius fracture
It usually involves the first extensor compartment
It occurs only in displaced open fractures
The delayed interval is described as approximately 3 weeks to 3 months
It is most commonly caused by flexor retinaculum bowing
options_after: It is linked to irregular morphology of Lister tubercle after distal radius fracture
It usually involves the first extensor compartment
It occurs primarily in displaced open fractures
The delayed interval is described as approximately 3 weeks to 3 months
It is most commonly caused by flexor retinaculum bowing
updates.explanation: The source links distal radius fracture to irregularity of the dorsal radial tubercle, or Lister tubercle, producing delayed rupture of EPL in the third extensor compartment. The time window is described as roughly 3 weeks to 3 months. It is noted as more common after non-displaced fracture, not only displaced open injury.

updates.question_text: Regarding penetrating infectious tenosynovitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Flexor tendon infectious tenosynovitis is treated as a surgical emergency
Infectious tenosynovitis cannot spread to the common flexors of the wrist
Delayed treatment is described as having excellent outcomes
Increased pressure in the tendon sheath protects the tendon from necrosis
Mycobacterium marinum is linked to direct infection in a fisherman or sushi-chef type exposure
options_after: Flexor tendon infectious tenosynovitis is treated as a surgical emergency
Infectious tenosynovitis will not spread to the common flexors of the wrist
Delayed treatment is described as having excellent outcomes
Increased pressure in the tendon sheath protects the tendon from necrosis
Mycobacterium marinum is linked to direct infection in a fisherman or sushi-chef type exposure
updates.explanation: The source describes flexor tendon infectious tenosynovitis as a surgical emergency because it can spread rapidly to the common flexors of the wrist. Increased pressure can cause tendon necrosis and delayed treatment has poor outcomes. Mycobacterium marinum is linked to direct inoculation exposure in fishermen or sushi chefs.

updates.question_text: Regarding gamekeeper thumb and Stener lesion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Gamekeeper thumb is an injury of the radial collateral ligament of the index finger
Stress radiographs are recommended as the next test because they cannot worsen displacement
It involves UCL disruption with avulsion at the base of the proximal first phalanx
MRI is preferred when assessing for a Stener lesion
Stener lesion always heals normally with conservative treatment
options_after: Gamekeeper thumb is an injury of the radial collateral ligament of the index finger
Stress radiographs are recommended as the next test because they will not worsen displacement
It involves UCL disruption with avulsion at the base of the proximal first phalanx
MRI is preferred when assessing for a Stener lesion
Stener lesion characteristically heals normally with conservative treatment
updates.explanation: The source describes gamekeeper or skier thumb as UCL disruption with avulsion fracture at the base of the proximal first phalanx. A Stener lesion occurs when the adductor aponeurosis is interposed around the torn UCL, preventing normal healing and requiring surgery. It advises against stress views and favours MRI.

updates.question_text: Regarding elbow trauma trivia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Radial head fracture is the common adult elbow fracture highlighted in the source
Supracondylar fracture is listed as the common adult elbow fracture rather than paediatric
Posterior fat pad elevation is more specific for occult fracture
A non-true lateral elbow radiograph cannot affect posterior fat pad appearance
Capitellum fracture is associated with posterior dislocation
options_after: Radial head fracture is the common adult elbow fracture highlighted in the source
Supracondylar fracture is listed as the common adult elbow fracture rather than paediatric
Posterior fat pad elevation is more specific for occult fracture
A non-true lateral elbow radiograph will not affect posterior fat pad appearance
Capitellum fracture is associated with posterior dislocation
updates.explanation: The source states that radial head fracture is common in adults, while supracondylar fracture is common in children. It describes the posterior fat pad as the more specific sign but warns it can be falsely elevated if the lateral view is not a true 90-degree flexed lateral. Capitellum fractures are associated with posterior dislocation.

updates.question_text: Regarding posterior shoulder dislocation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Rim sign describes absent overlap between glenoid and humeral head
Light bulb sign reflects a locked externally rotated arm on all views
Trough sign is an anterior humeral head impaction fracture
Reverse Bankart affects the anterior glenoid rim
Posterior dislocation is more common than anterior-inferior dislocation
options_after: Rim sign describes absent overlap between glenoid and humeral head
Light bulb sign reflects a locked externally rotated arm on most views
Trough sign is an anterior humeral head impaction fracture
Reverse Bankart affects the anterior glenoid rim
Posterior dislocation is more common than anterior-inferior dislocation
updates.explanation: The source lists posterior dislocation signs including rim sign, trough sign and light bulb sign. The light bulb sign reflects a humeral head locked in internal rotation, not external rotation. Trough sign is an anterior humeral head impaction injury. Reverse Bankart affects the posterior glenoid rim, and posterior dislocation is uncommon relative to anterior-inferior dislocation.

updates.question_text: Regarding external impingement of the rotator cuff, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: External impingement affects the bursal/superficial surface adjacent to the coracoacromial arch
The coracoacromial arch includes the coracoid process, acromion and coracoacromial ligament
External impingement always involves the deep undersurface against the glenoid labrum
A type III hooked acromion is less associated with impingement than a flat acromion
Subacromial osteophytes or thickening of the coracoacromial ligament can impinge on supraspinatus
options_after: External impingement affects the bursal/superficial surface adjacent to the coracoacromial arch
The coracoacromial arch includes the coracoid process, acromion and coracoacromial ligament
External impingement characteristically involves the deep undersurface against the glenoid labrum
A type III hooked acromion is less associated with impingement than a flat acromion
Subacromial osteophytes or thickening of the coracoacromial ligament can impinge on supraspinatus
updates.explanation: The source defines external impingement as bursal-surface cuff impingement adjacent to the coracoacromial arch, which includes coracoid, acromion and coracoacromial ligament. A hooked type III acromion, subacromial osteophytes and thickened coracoacromial ligament are primary external causes. Deep undersurface impingement against labrum and humeral head is internal impingement.

updates.question_text: Regarding posterior-superior internal impingement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It occurs when the subscapularis is pinched between the coracoid and lesser tuberosity
It is best evaluated in neutral adduction rather than ABER position
It involves the posterior-superior cuff contacting the posterior-superior glenoid
It is most associated with sedentary older patients and no overhead activity
It damages infraspinatus and posterior supraspinatus fibres and may tear the posterior-superior labrum
options_after: It occurs when the subscapularis is pinched between the coracoid and lesser tuberosity
It is best evaluated in neutral adduction rather than ABER position
It involves the posterior-superior cuff contacting the posterior-superior glenoid
It is most associated with sedentary older patients without overhead activity
It damages infraspinatus and posterior supraspinatus fibres and may tear the posterior-superior labrum
updates.explanation: Posterior-superior internal impingement occurs when the posterior-superior rotator cuff, at the supraspinatus/infraspinatus junction, contacts the posterior-superior glenoid. It is best seen in the ABER position and is associated with overhead athletes such as throwers, tennis players and swimmers. It damages infraspinatus and posterior supraspinatus fibres and is linked to posterior-superior labral tearing.

updates.question_text: Regarding the rotator cuff critical zone, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is 1-2 cm from the tendon footprint
It is the usual location for subscapularis insertional avulsion only
It is the most common location for calcium hydroxyapatite deposition
It is a hypervascular zone that protects against degeneration
It is located within the teres minor muscle belly
options_after: It is 1-2 cm from the tendon footprint
It is the usual location for subscapularis insertional avulsion
It is the most common location for calcium hydroxyapatite deposition
It is a hypervascular zone that protects against degeneration
It is located within the teres minor muscle belly
updates.explanation: The source describes the supraspinatus critical zone as a relatively avascular region 1-2 cm from the tendon footprint. It is both a common location for supraspinatus tearing and for calcium hydroxyapatite deposition or calcific tendinitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding full-thickness and massive rotator cuff tears, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A massive cuff tear involves at least two of the four cuff muscles
High T2 signal in the expected location of the tendon supports full-thickness tear
Gadolinium crossing the cuff into the bursa on T1 arthrography supports full-thickness tear
A partial tear greater than 50% is never treated surgically
Rotator cuff interval tear is excluded from the rotator cuff tear category
options_after: A massive cuff tear involves at least two of the four cuff muscles
High T2 signal in the expected location of the tendon supports full-thickness tear
Gadolinium crossing the cuff into the bursa on T1 arthrography supports full-thickness tear
A partial tear greater than 50% is not treated surgically
Rotator cuff interval tear is excluded from the rotator cuff tear category
updates.explanation: The source defines massive rotator cuff tear as involving at least two cuff muscles. Full-thickness tear is supported by high T2 signal in the expected tendon location and by gadolinium passing into the bursa on arthrography. It notes that a partial tear greater than 50% often leads to surgical intervention, and rotator cuff interval tear is still considered a cuff tear.

updates.question_text: Regarding ALPSA and true Bankart lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: ALPSA has a medially displaced labroligamentous complex with intact periosteum
ALPSA scars down medially to the glenoid
True Bankart has disrupted periosteum
True Bankart cannot be osseous
Hill-Sachs fracture is never associated with true Bankart
options_after: ALPSA has a medially displaced labroligamentous complex with intact periosteum
ALPSA scars down medially to the glenoid
True Bankart has disrupted periosteum
True Bankart will not be osseous
Hill-Sachs fracture is not associated with true Bankart
updates.explanation: The source defines ALPSA as anterior labral periosteal sleeve avulsion with a medially displaced labroligamentous complex, absent labrum on the rim and intact periosteum. True Bankart may be cartilaginous or osseous and has disrupted periosteum. The source notes frequent associated Hill-Sachs fracture with true Bankart.

updates.question_text: Regarding posterior glenohumeral instability lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Reverse osseous Bankart is a fracture of the anteroinferior glenoid rim
Bennett lesion is an extra-articular curvilinear calcification associated with posterior labral tears
POLPSA is the posterior counterpart of ALPSA with stripped but intact posterior periosteum
Kim lesion is defined by complete absence of the posterior labrum and glenoid cartilage relationship
Posterior instability lesions cannot mirror anterior Bankart-type injuries
options_after: Reverse osseous Bankart is a fracture of the anteroinferior glenoid rim
Bennett lesion is an extra-articular curvilinear calcification associated with posterior labral tears
POLPSA is the posterior counterpart of ALPSA with stripped but intact posterior periosteum
Kim lesion is defined by complete absence of the posterior labrum and glenoid cartilage relationship
Posterior instability lesions will not mirror anterior Bankart-type injuries
updates.explanation: The source explains that posterior dislocation can produce reverse versions of anterior instability lesions. Reverse osseous Bankart is a fracture of the posteroinferior glenoid rim. Bennett lesion is extra-articular curvilinear calcification associated with posterior labral tears. POLPSA strips the posterior labrum and posterior periosteum from the glenoid while the periosteum remains intact.

updates.question_text: Regarding quadrilateral space syndrome and Parsonage-Turner syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Quadrilateral space syndrome compresses the axillary nerve
Teres minor atrophy is a likely imaging clue for quadrilateral space syndrome
Parsonage-Turner syndrome is isolated compression of the axillary nerve in the quadrilateral space
Parsonage-Turner should be considered only when a single muscle in one nerve distribution is affected
Quadrilateral space borders include teres major inferiorly and triceps medially
options_after: Quadrilateral space syndrome compresses the axillary nerve
Teres minor atrophy is a likely imaging clue for quadrilateral space syndrome
Parsonage-Turner syndrome is isolated compression of the axillary nerve in the quadrilateral space
Parsonage-Turner should be considered primarily when a single muscle in one nerve distribution is affected
Quadrilateral space borders include teres major inferiorly and triceps medially
updates.explanation: The source describes quadrilateral space syndrome as axillary nerve compression, often shown by teres minor atrophy. The borders listed are teres minor above, teres major below, humeral neck laterally and triceps medially. Parsonage-Turner syndrome is idiopathic brachial plexus involvement and should be considered when abnormal muscles span multiple nerve distributions.

updates.question_text: Regarding femoral head AVN risk after hip fracture, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Displaced intracapsular fracture can disrupt circumflex femoral blood supply
The degree of fracture displacement corresponds with AVN risk
Extracapsular fracture always carries higher AVN risk than displaced intracapsular fracture in the source
Femoral head vascularity is presented as unrelated to fracture location
AVN risk is mainly determined by whether the patient has an acetabular both-column fracture
options_after: Displaced intracapsular fracture can disrupt circumflex femoral blood supply
The degree of fracture displacement corresponds with AVN risk
Extracapsular fracture characteristically carries higher AVN risk than displaced intracapsular fracture in the source
Femoral head vascularity is presented as unrelated to fracture location
AVN risk is mainly determined by whether the patient has an acetabular both-column fracture
updates.explanation: The source states that the femoral head receives blood from the circumflex femoral vessels. A displaced intracapsular fracture can disrupt this blood supply, leading to AVN. The testable point given is that the degree of fracture displacement corresponds with AVN risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding an isolated lesser-trochanter avulsion in an adult, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It should be assumed to be a normal paediatric variant
It is classically caused by hamstring avulsion
It is never clinically significant if trauma is mild
It proves anterior column acetabular fracture
It should raise concern for a pathologic fracture
options_after: It should be assumed to be a normal paediatric variant
It is classically caused by hamstring avulsion
It is not clinically significant if trauma is mild
It proves anterior column acetabular fracture
It should raise concern for a pathologic fracture
updates.explanation: The source specifically warns that an isolated lesser-trochanter avulsion after seemingly mild trauma in an adult should raise concern for pathologic fracture. The lesser trochanter is the iliopsoas attachment site, not the hamstring attachment.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging work-up of snapping hip syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Plain radiography helps evaluate degenerative change or loose bodies
If there is no degenerative change, dynamic ultrasound is used to evaluate internal snapping
Ultrasound must be static because the finding cannot be dynamic
If ultrasound is negative, MR arthrography can evaluate intra-articular causes such as labral tear
MR arthrography is the first test before clinical evaluation
options_after: Plain radiography helps evaluate degenerative change or loose bodies
If there is no degenerative change, dynamic ultrasound is used to evaluate internal snapping
Ultrasound must be static because the finding will not be dynamic
If ultrasound is negative, MR arthrography can evaluate intra-articular causes such as labral tear
MR arthrography is the first test before clinical evaluation
updates.explanation: The source's work-up starts clinically, then uses radiography to look for intra-articular degenerative disease or loose bodies. If no degenerative change is found, ultrasound assesses internal snapping dynamically, specifically cine visualisation of iliopsoas movement. If ultrasound is negative, MR arthrography evaluates intra-articular causes such as labral tear.

updates.question_text: Regarding iliopsoas bursa and tendon, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The iliopsoas bursa is the smallest bursa around the hip
It lies posterior to the sacroiliac joint rather than anterior to the hip
It is the largest bursa in the body
It communicates with the hip joint in about 15% of people
The iliopsoas tendon cannot mimic a labral tear on axial imaging
options_after: The iliopsoas bursa is the smallest bursa around the hip
It lies posterior to the sacroiliac joint rather than anterior to the hip
It is the largest bursa in the body
It communicates with the hip joint in about 15% of people
The iliopsoas tendon will not mimic a labral tear on axial imaging
updates.explanation: The source states that the iliopsoas bursa is the largest bursa in the body and communicates with the joint in about 15% of people. It is seen anterior to the hip, and a fluid-signal mass anterior to the femur near the psoas tendon can represent iliopsoas bursitis. The iliopsoas tendon runs anterior to the labrum on axial images and can mimic a labral tear.

updates.question_text: Regarding stress shielding after total hip arthroplasty, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stress shielding is primarily an infection-related process with high inflammatory markers
It is caused by acetabular labral ossification
It is always symptomatic and mandates revision
It is more common with uncemented arthroplasty
Stress is transferred through the metallic stem, unloading adjacent bone
options_after: Stress shielding is primarily an infection-related process with high inflammatory markers
It is caused by acetabular labral ossification
It is characteristically symptomatic and mandates revision
It is more common with uncemented arthroplasty
Stress is transferred through the metallic stem, unloading adjacent bone
updates.explanation: Stress shielding occurs when the metallic stem carries load and adjacent bone is relatively unloaded, leading to resorption under Wolff-law mechanics. The source states it is more common with uncemented arthroplasty and can be normal to a degree, although advanced cases can predispose to fracture.

updates.question_text: Regarding femoral stem subsidence after hip arthroplasty, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It describes downward sliding of the arthroplasty
It is diagnosed only by superior migration of the acetabular cup
It most often occurs with collared implants
It is unrelated to early THA failure
Progression after two years supports loosening
options_after: It describes downward sliding of the arthroplasty
It is diagnosed primarily by superior migration of the acetabular cup
It most often occurs with collared implants
It is unrelated to early THA failure
Progression after two years supports loosening
updates.explanation: Subsidence is downward sliding of the femoral arthroplasty component and is a reason for early THA failure. The source notes that more than 1 cm along the femoral component or progression after two years supports loosening, and it is seen most often in implants without a collar.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal creep and pathologic wear after hip arthroplasty, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A small amount of thinning in the weight-bearing region is called creep
Wear and creep are identical terms in the source
Creep is normal
Superior-lateral wear is pathologic
Particle disease is unrelated to implant wear
options_after: A small amount of thinning in the weight-bearing region is called creep
Wear and creep are closely comparable terms in the source
Creep is normal
Superior-lateral wear is pathologic
Particle disease is unrelated to implant wear
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes normal creep from pathologic wear. A little thinning in the weight-bearing area is called creep and is normal. Wear, especially superior-lateral wear, is pathologic and contributes to particle disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding magic angle phenomenon in knee MRI, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Magic angle is most conspicuous only on long TE T2-weighted imaging
It is caused by tendons being perpendicular at 90 degrees to the magnetic field
It appears on short TE sequences such as T1, PD or GRE
It is unrelated to the PCL or patellar tendon
It disappears on long TE T2 sequences
options_after: Magic angle is most conspicuous primarily on long TE T2-weighted imaging
It is caused by tendons being perpendicular at 90 degrees to the magnetic field
It appears on short TE sequences such as T1, PD or GRE
It is unrelated to the PCL or patellar tendon
It disappears on long TE T2 sequences
updates.explanation: The source describes magic angle phenomenon as intermediate signal on short TE sequences such as T1, PD and GRE, when structures such as PCL or patellar tendon form about a 55-degree angle with the magnetic field. It goes away on long TE T2 sequences.

updates.question_text: Regarding ACL graft tear, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Grossly high T2 signal is always normal in an ACL graft
The graft is most susceptible during remodelling at 4-8 months postoperatively
Uncovering of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus is the named secondary sign in the source
Anterior tibial translation excludes graft tear
A flat graft angle suggests tear
options_after: Grossly high T2 signal is characteristically normal in an ACL graft
The graft is most susceptible during remodelling at 4-8 months postoperatively
Uncovering of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus is the named secondary sign in the source
Anterior tibial translation excludes graft tear
A flat graft angle suggests tear
updates.explanation: The source states that a flat ACL graft angle suggests tear and that the graft is most susceptible during remodelling at 4-8 months. Other signs include grossly high T2 signal, fibre discontinuity, uncovering of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus and anterior tibial translation.

updates.question_text: Regarding posterolateral corner and PCL injuries, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: PCL tear is more common than ACL tear and never affects vascular risk
Missed posterolateral corner injury is irrelevant after ACL reconstruction
PCL tear should raise concern for posterior knee dislocation mechanism
Fibular head oedema excludes posterolateral corner injury
PCL injury may require assessment of the popliteal flow void or CTA run-off depending on context
options_after: PCL tear is more common than ACL tear and will not affect vascular risk
Missed posterolateral corner injury is irrelevant after ACL reconstruction
PCL tear should raise concern for posterior knee dislocation mechanism
Fibular head oedema excludes posterolateral corner injury
PCL injury may require assessment of the popliteal flow void or CTA run-off depending on context
updates.explanation: The source notes that missed posterolateral corner injury is a common cause of ACL reconstruction failure and that fibular head oedema can be a clue. PCL tear should raise concern for posterior knee dislocation, which can compromise the popliteal artery; depending on wording, CTA run-off may be needed.

updates.question_text: Regarding meniscal tear morphology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Horizontal cleavage tears are never associated with meniscal cysts
Radial tears are problematic because they disrupt hoop strength
Longitudinal tears are defined by no axial extension
Flap or parrot-beak tears are radial tears that change direction longitudinally
Horizontal cleavage tears are associated with meniscal cysts
options_after: Horizontal cleavage tears are not associated with meniscal cysts
Radial tears are problematic because they disrupt hoop strength
Longitudinal tears remain confined to the coronal plane without axial extension
Flap or parrot-beak tears are radial tears that change direction longitudinally
Horizontal cleavage tears are associated with meniscal cysts
updates.explanation: The source states that radial tears cut hoop fibres, causing loss of hoop strength and possible extrusion or early osteoarthritis. A flap or parrot-beak tear is a radial tear that changes into the longitudinal direction. Horizontal cleavage tears are associated with meniscal cysts.

updates.question_text: Regarding patellar dislocation and bipartite patella, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Patellar dislocation is usually lateral
It is associated with medial patellofemoral ligament tear
Trochlear dysplasia is an association
Bipartite patella classically involves the upper lateral corner
Bipartite patella should be diagnosed in every 8-year-old with an unfused patella
options_after: Patellar dislocation is usually lateral
It is associated with medial patellofemoral ligament tear
Trochlear dysplasia is an association
Bipartite patella classically involves the upper lateral corner
Bipartite patella should be diagnosed in routine 8-year-old with an unfused patella
updates.explanation: The source states that patellar dislocation is usually lateral and has a classic contusion pattern, associated MPFL tear and association with trochlear dysplasia. Bipartite patella is an anatomic variant in the upper lateral corner, but the source cautions not to call it in an 8-year-old because fusion normally occurs by about age 12.

updates.question_text: Regarding painful os peroneus syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The os peroneum lies within the peroneus longus tendon
The ossicle is seen in about 10% of the general population in the source
Stress reaction of the os peroneum cannot affect the peroneus longus tendon
MRI may show oedema in the os peroneus before the tendon enters the cuboid tunnel
The os peroneum lies within the posterior tibial tendon
options_after: The os peroneum lies within the peroneus longus tendon
The ossicle is seen in about 10% of the general population in the source
Stress reaction of the os peroneum will not affect the peroneus longus tendon
MRI may show oedema in the os peroneus before the tendon enters the cuboid tunnel
The os peroneum lies within the posterior tibial tendon
updates.explanation: The source states that os peroneum is an accessory ossicle within the peroneus longus tendon, seen in about 10% of the population. Stress reaction and pain can progress to tendon disruption. The key MRI finding is oedema in the os peroneus just before the tendon enters the cuboid tunnel.

updates.question_text: Regarding Lisfranc injury, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lisfranc injury can be excluded on a non-weight-bearing film
The Lisfranc ligament connects the lateral cuneiform to the fifth metatarsal base
The fleck sign is always a distal fibular avulsion fragment
The fleck sign is a small bony fragment in the Lisfranc space
Missed Lisfranc injury can lead to non-union and post-traumatic arthritis
options_after: Lisfranc injury can be excluded on a non-weight-bearing film
The Lisfranc ligament connects the lateral cuneiform to the fifth metatarsal base
The fleck sign is characteristically a distal fibular avulsion fragment
The fleck sign is a small bony fragment in the Lisfranc space
Missed Lisfranc injury can lead to non-union and post-traumatic arthritis
updates.explanation: The source says Lisfranc injury cannot be excluded on a non-weight-bearing film. The fleck sign is a small bony fragment in the Lisfranc space, associated with avulsion of the Lisfranc ligament. Missed injury risks non-union and post-traumatic arthritis.

updates.question_text: Regarding split peroneus brevis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It usually follows valgus knee trauma rather than inversion ankle injury
The tendon becomes Z-shaped with complete separation from peroneus longus
The tear occurs at the lateral malleolus
It has no association with lateral ligament injury
It may present as chronic ankle pain
options_after: It usually follows valgus knee trauma rather than inversion ankle injury
The tendon becomes Z-shaped with complete separation from peroneus longus
The tear occurs at the lateral malleolus
It lacks association with lateral ligament injury
It may present as chronic ankle pain
updates.explanation: The source describes split peroneus brevis as a longitudinal split after inversion injury, often presenting with chronic ankle pain. The tear occurs at the lateral malleolus and may show C-shaped or boomerang morphology around peroneus longus, with strong association with lateral ligament injury.

updates.question_text: Regarding tarsal tunnel syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It involves posterior tibial nerve compression behind the medial malleolus
It is typically bilateral, like carpal tunnel syndrome
Pain may involve the first three toes
It causes isolated abductor digiti minimi atrophy only
Pes planus or hindfoot valgus may predispose by tightening the retinaculum
options_after: It involves posterior tibial nerve compression behind the medial malleolus
It is typically bilateral, like carpal tunnel syndrome
Pain may involve the first three toes
It causes isolated abductor digiti minimi atrophy
Pes planus or hindfoot valgus may predispose by tightening the retinaculum
updates.explanation: The source defines tarsal tunnel syndrome as posterior tibial nerve compression behind the medial malleolus, with pain in the posterior tibial nerve distribution including the first three toes. It is usually unilateral and may be predisposed by pes planus or hindfoot valgus; muscle atrophy can involve multiple foot muscles.

updates.question_text: Regarding calcaneal tuberosity avulsion and related avulsion patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Calcaneal tuberosity avulsion is caused by Achilles traction
Plantar fascia rupture has no calcaneal avulsion association
Plantar fascia rupture may avulse the medial plantar process
