Calcaneocuboid ligament avulsion appears as a fragment medial to the talonavicular joint
Extensor digitorum brevis avulsion arises at the dorsolateral anterior calcaneus
options_after: Calcaneal tuberosity avulsion is caused by Achilles traction
Plantar fascia rupture lacks calcaneal avulsion association
Plantar fascia rupture may avulse the medial plantar process
Calcaneocuboid ligament avulsion appears as a fragment medial to the talonavicular joint
Extensor digitorum brevis avulsion arises at the dorsolateral anterior calcaneus
updates.explanation: The source describes calcaneal tuberosity avulsion as Achilles traction, with diabetes as a classic association. Plantar fascia rupture may avulse the medial plantar process. Extensor digitorum brevis avulsion arises at the dorsolateral anterior calcaneus, while calcaneocuboid ligament avulsion is lateral to the calcaneocuboid joint.

updates.question_text: Regarding stability of osteochondral lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Granulation tissue that enhances with gadolinium proves stability
High T2 signal undercutting the fragment suggests instability
Loose body formation cannot occur with unstable lesions
Absence of high T2 signal at the interface is a good sign of osseous bridging and stability
Oedema may cause a false positive for instability
options_after: Granulation tissue that enhances with gadolinium proves stability
High T2 signal undercutting the fragment suggests instability
Loose body formation will not occur with unstable lesions
Absence of high T2 signal at the interface is a good sign of osseous bridging and stability
Oedema may cause a false positive for instability
updates.explanation: The source emphasises high T2 signal undercutting the fragment as the sign to call instability, although oedema can cause false positives. Absence of high T2 signal at the interface supports osseous bridging and stability. Enhancing granulation tissue at the interface does not prove stability.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteochondroses as a group, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are usually childhood conditions involving an epiphysis or apophysis
They are primarily acute bacterial infections of metaphyses
Collapse, sclerosis and fragmentation are typical imaging themes
They always require surgical treatment
They suggest osteonecrosis-like change in the source framing
options_after: They are usually childhood conditions involving an epiphysis or apophysis
They are primarily acute bacterial infections of metaphyses
Collapse, sclerosis and fragmentation are typical imaging themes
They characteristically require surgical treatment
They suggest osteonecrosis-like change in the source framing
updates.explanation: The source defines osteochondroses as usually childhood conditions involving an epiphysis or apophysis, with collapse, sclerosis and fragmentation suggesting osteonecrosis. They are not primarily infections, and some listed entities, such as Kohler disease, are explicitly non-surgical in treatment.

updates.question_text: Regarding diabetic foot osteomyelitis work-up, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI is never used for preoperative surgical planning
Radiographic erosions or periosteal reaction exclude treatment
Bone scan is always the first test in the source pathway
Initial radiography is used when osteomyelitis is suspected near an ulcer
If radiographs are negative but suspicion persists, MRI is the next test
options_after: MRI is not used for preoperative surgical planning
Radiographic erosions or periosteal reaction exclude treatment
Bone scan is characteristically the first test in the source pathway
Initial radiography is used when osteomyelitis is suspected near an ulcer
If radiographs are negative but suspicion persists, MRI is the next test
updates.explanation: The source pathway begins with radiography when osteomyelitis is suspected near a diabetic foot ulcer. If radiographs show erosions or periosteal reaction, treatment follows; if negative and suspicion persists, MRI is used and may also be requested for preoperative planning.

updates.question_text: Regarding chronic osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is defined as osteomyelitis lasting longer than 6 weeks
Healed osteomyelitis on MRI is suggested by permanent diffuse T1 marrow loss
Draining sinus tracts are a risk factor for squamous cell carcinoma
Sequestrum is best shown with ultrasound
Sequestrum is the most specific sign of active chronic osteomyelitis in the source
options_after: It is defined as osteomyelitis lasting longer than 6 weeks
Healed osteomyelitis on MRI is suggested by long-term diffuse T1 marrow loss
Draining sinus tracts are a risk factor for squamous cell carcinoma
Sequestrum is best shown with ultrasound
Sequestrum is the most specific sign of active chronic osteomyelitis in the source
updates.explanation: The source defines chronic osteomyelitis as lasting longer than 6 weeks. It notes that draining sinus tracts are a risk factor for squamous cell carcinoma and that sequestrum is the most specific sign of active chronic osteomyelitis, best shown with CT. Healed disease on MRI is based on return of normal fatty marrow.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI diagnosis of osteomyelitis near an ulcer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Low T1 marrow signal adjacent to an ulcer or cellulitis is diagnostic in the source
Corresponding low T1 signal is more specific
STIR high signal is more sensitive
High STIR signal without T1 abnormality is always diagnostic
Bone marrow signal is irrelevant if an ulcer is present
options_after: Low T1 marrow signal adjacent to an ulcer or cellulitis is diagnostic in the source
Corresponding low T1 signal is more specific
STIR high signal is more sensitive
High STIR signal without T1 abnormality is characteristically diagnostic
Bone marrow signal is irrelevant if an ulcer is present
updates.explanation: The source states that low T1 marrow signal adjacent to an ulcer or cellulitis is diagnostic for osteomyelitis. STIR high signal is more sensitive but less specific, while corresponding T1 low signal is more specific.

updates.question_text: Regarding adult discitis and osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adult disc and vertebral body infection nearly always occur together
Seeding usually starts at the vascular vertebral endplate
Early MRI may show paraspinal or epidural inflammation, T2-bright disc signal and disc enhancement
Isolated discitis is common in adults and almost never seen in children
Later imaging may show endplate destruction and disc-space narrowing
options_after: Adult disc and vertebral body infection nearly always occur together
Seeding usually starts at the vascular vertebral endplate
Early MRI may show paraspinal or epidural inflammation, T2-bright disc signal and disc enhancement
Isolated discitis is common in adults and distinctly uncommon in children
Later imaging may show endplate destruction and disc-space narrowing
updates.explanation: The source explains that in adults disc and vertebral body infection nearly always go together because infection seeds the vascular endplate, crosses into the disc, and then involves the adjacent vertebral body. Early MRI can show paraspinal/epidural inflammation, bright disc signal and disc enhancement. Later imaging shows endplate destruction, disc-space narrowing and marrow signal abnormality. Isolated discitis is essentially paediatric, not adult.

updates.question_text: Regarding Pott disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The vertebral body is involved with relative disc-space sparing until late
Multilevel thoracic skip involvement is described
Large paraspinal abscess and calcified psoas abscess are buzzwords
Gibbus deformity is destructive focal kyphosis
It is identical to typical bacterial discitis, with early disc-centred destruction
options_after: The vertebral body is involved with relative disc-space sparing until late
Multilevel thoracic skip involvement is described
Large paraspinal abscess and calcified psoas abscess are buzzwords
Gibbus deformity is destructive focal kyphosis
It is closely comparable to typical bacterial discitis, with early disc-centred destruction
updates.explanation: The source contrasts Pott disease with typical bacterial discitis by emphasising vertebral body involvement with disc-space sparing until late. It lists multilevel thoracic skip disease, large paraspinal abscess, calcified psoas abscess and gibbus deformity. Gibbus deformity is destructive focal kyphosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding aggressive bone lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Wide zone of transition is described as the best sign of aggressiveness
Codman triangle forms when rapidly growing tumour lifts periosteum and only the edge ossifies
Sharp sclerotic margins imply slower growth and more benign behaviour
A narrow zone of transition is the strongest sign of malignancy in the source
Blurry margins or a gradient at the edge suggest a more aggressive process
options_after: Wide zone of transition is described as the best sign of aggressiveness
Codman triangle forms when rapidly growing tumour lifts periosteum and primarily the edge ossifies
Sharp sclerotic margins imply slower growth and more benign behaviour
A narrow zone of transition is the strongest sign of malignancy in the source
Blurry margins or a gradient at the edge suggest a more aggressive process
updates.explanation: The source highlights wide zone of transition as the best sign of an aggressive lesion. Sharp sclerotic margins imply bone had time to form a mature border, while blurry margins suggest faster growth and greater concern for malignancy or infection. Codman triangle is an aggressive periosteal reaction caused by incomplete ossification at the edge of lifted periosteum.

updates.question_text: Regarding lytic bone destruction patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Myeloma, lymphoma and Ewing sarcoma can show aggressive destruction patterns
Geographic destruction with sharp borders is more suggestive of a slow-growing benign lesion
Osteomyelitis and hyperparathyroidism can also show aggressive patterns
Moth-eaten or permeative destruction suggests rapid infiltrative growth
Permeative destruction is diagnostic only of benign fibrous cortical defect
options_after: Myeloma, lymphoma and Ewing sarcoma can show aggressive destruction patterns
Geographic destruction with sharp borders is more suggestive of a slow-growing benign lesion
Osteomyelitis and hyperparathyroidism can also show aggressive patterns
Moth-eaten or permeative destruction suggests rapid infiltrative growth
Permeative destruction is diagnostic primarily of benign fibrous cortical defect
updates.explanation: The source contrasts geographic destruction with sharp borders, which suggests slow benign growth, with moth-eaten or permeative patterns, which suggest rapid infiltrative growth. It gives examples including myeloma, lymphoma and Ewing sarcoma, and notes that osteomyelitis and hyperparathyroidism can also show aggressive patterns, so pre-test context matters.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteosarcoma subtypes and risk settings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Conventional intramedullary osteosarcoma is the dominant subtype in the source
Surface subtypes are higher grade than conventional intramedullary osteosarcoma
All osteosarcoma subtypes produce bone or osteoid from neoplastic cells
Osteosarcoma never occurs in young patients
Secondary osteosarcoma can be associated with radiation, Paget disease or bone infarct
options_after: Conventional intramedullary osteosarcoma is the dominant subtype in the source
Surface subtypes are higher grade than conventional intramedullary osteosarcoma
All osteosarcoma subtypes produce bone or osteoid from neoplastic cells
Osteosarcoma will not occur in young patients
Secondary osteosarcoma can be associated with radiation, Paget disease or bone infarct
updates.explanation: The source lists conventional intramedullary osteosarcoma as the common dominant subtype and states that all subtypes produce bone or osteoid from neoplastic cells. Most are idiopathic, but secondary causes include radiation, Paget disease and infarcts, usually in older patients. Conventional intramedullary is higher grade than the surface subtypes discussed.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteosarcoma imaging and staging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Skip lesions are synchronous tumour foci in the same bone or immediate opposing side of a joint, separated by normal marrow
MRI should image the entire bone during staging to assess skip lesions and biopsy planning
Sunburst and Codman triangle are aggressive periosteal reaction buzzwords
Skip lesions occur in nearly all osteosarcomas
Reverse zoning means denser mature matrix centrally and less peripherally
options_after: Skip lesions are synchronous tumour foci in the same bone or immediate opposing side of a joint, separated by normal marrow
MRI should image the entire bone during staging to assess skip lesions and biopsy planning
Sunburst and Codman triangle are aggressive periosteal reaction buzzwords
Skip lesions occur in the large majority of osteosarcomas
Reverse zoning means denser mature matrix centrally and less peripherally
updates.explanation: The source lists sunburst, lamellated reaction and Codman triangle as aggressive periosteal reaction buzzwords, and defines reverse zoning as denser mature matrix centrally and less peripherally. Skip lesions are synchronous tumour foci separated by normal marrow, typically proximal to the main tumour, but occur in only about 5%; this is why the entire bone is imaged for staging and biopsy planning.

updates.question_text: Which single post-chemotherapy biopsy result is described as favourable in osteosarcoma outcome prediction?
options_before: Ninety percent tumour death
Less than 10% tumour necrosis
Persistent unchanged tumour cellularity
No tumour death after chemotherapy
New skip lesion formation after chemotherapy
options_after: Ninety percent tumour death
Less than 10% tumour necrosis
Persistent unchanged tumour cellularity
Persistent viable tumour without chemotherapy-related tumour death
New skip lesion formation after chemotherapy
updates.explanation: The source's osteosarcoma pathway notes that biopsy after chemotherapy predicts outcome, and about 90% tumour death is favourable. It also notes that relapse usually occurs within two years and most relapse is to the lung.

updates.question_text: Regarding parosteal versus periosteal osteosarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Parosteal osteosarcoma usually has no marrow extension
Parosteal osteosarcoma is typically metaphyseal
Periosteal osteosarcoma is lower grade than parosteal osteosarcoma
Periosteal osteosarcoma tends to occur in the diaphysis
Periosteal osteosarcoma is described as intermediate grade
options_after: Parosteal osteosarcoma usually lacks marrow extension
Parosteal osteosarcoma is typically metaphyseal
Periosteal osteosarcoma is lower grade than parosteal osteosarcoma
Periosteal osteosarcoma tends to occur in the diaphysis
Periosteal osteosarcoma is described as intermediate grade
updates.explanation: The source contrasts parosteal osteosarcoma as metaphyseal and low grade with periosteal osteosarcoma as diaphyseal and intermediate grade. Periosteal disease has a worse prognosis than parosteal but better than conventional osteosarcoma. Marrow extension is listed for parosteal osteosarcoma in about half of cases, whereas periosteal disease usually lacks marrow extension.

updates.question_text: Regarding epiphyseal lucent lesions and epiphyseal equivalents, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Metastases and infection have no predilection for the metaphysis
ABC, infection, giant cell tumour and chondroblastoma are highlighted epiphyseal considerations
Epiphyseal equivalents behave like diaphyseal lesions
Clear cell chondrosarcoma should be considered for a malignant epiphyseal lesion
Carpals, patella, greater trochanter and calcaneus are listed epiphyseal equivalents
options_after: Metastases and infection lack predilection for the metaphysis
ABC, infection, giant cell tumour and chondroblastoma are highlighted epiphyseal considerations
Epiphyseal equivalents behave like diaphyseal lesions
Clear cell chondrosarcoma should be considered for a malignant epiphyseal lesion
Carpals, patella, greater trochanter and calcaneus are listed epiphyseal equivalents
updates.explanation: The source highlights ABC, infection, giant cell tumour and chondroblastoma as classic epiphyseal considerations, with clear cell chondrosarcoma as the malignant epiphyseal tumour to remember. It also lists carpals, patella, greater trochanter and calcaneus as epiphyseal equivalents. The metaphysis is specifically described as having rich blood supply and increased predilection for metastases and infection.

updates.question_text: Regarding non-ossifying fibroma and fibrous cortical defect, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They most commonly present as aggressive epiphyseal soft-tissue masses
They are common in children and often spontaneously regress
They are usually larger than 10 cm at diagnosis
They are typically eccentric with a thin sclerotic border
They should have no association with NF1
options_after: They most commonly present as aggressive epiphyseal soft-tissue masses
They are common in children and often spontaneously regress
They are usually larger than 10 cm at diagnosis
They are typically eccentric with a thin sclerotic border
They should lack association with NF1
updates.explanation: Non-ossifying fibromas and fibrous cortical defects are described as common lesions in children that regress spontaneously, often becoming more sclerotic before disappearing. Morphologically they are eccentric with a thin sclerotic border and tend to occur near the physis around the knee. The source notes an association with NF1 and distinguishes larger non-ossifying fibromas from smaller fibrous cortical defects.

updates.question_text: Regarding enchondroma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In the humerus or femur it classically shows arcs-and-rings chondroid matrix
It is expected to have marked periostitis
In fingers and toes it may appear lytic rather than calcified
It is always painful when benign
It is described as the most common cystic lesion in the hands and feet
options_after: In the humerus or femur it classically shows arcs-and-rings chondroid matrix
It is expected to have marked periostitis
In fingers and toes it may appear lytic rather than calcified
It is characteristically painful when benign
It is described as the most common cystic lesion in the hands and feet
updates.explanation: The source stresses that enchondromas look different depending on body part: arcs-and-rings matrix in humerus or femur, but a lytic appearance in fingers and toes. It also states that enchondroma is the most common cystic lesion in the hands and feet. Absence of periostitis is a point shared with fibrous dysplasia, and pain raises concern for low-grade chondrosarcoma in long bones.

updates.question_text: Regarding Ollier disease and Maffucci syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ollier disease involves multiple enchondromas
Maffucci syndrome involves multiple enchondromas with haemangiomas
Ollier disease is defined by soft-tissue myxomas
Maffucci syndrome has no increased cancer risk
Both are common incidental adult findings
options_after: Ollier disease involves multiple enchondromas
Maffucci syndrome involves multiple enchondromas with haemangiomas
Ollier disease is defined by soft-tissue myxomas
Maffucci syndrome lacks increased cancer risk
Both are common incidental adult findings
updates.explanation: The source compares Ollier disease with Maffucci syndrome as rare boards-fodder entities. Ollier disease is multiple enchondromas, while Maffucci syndrome adds haemangiomas and a greater cancer risk. Soft-tissue myxomas belong with Mazabraud syndrome in the fibrous dysplasia section.

updates.question_text: Regarding brown tumour of hyperparathyroidism, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is defined by chondroid arcs-and-rings matrix
It is a primary small round blue cell tumour of the diaphysis
It cannot become sclerotic after treatment
It represents localised accumulations of giant cells and fibrous tissue
Other signs of hyperparathyroidism should be sought
options_after: It is defined by chondroid arcs-and-rings matrix
It is a primary small round blue cell tumour of the diaphysis
It will not become sclerotic after treatment
It represents localised accumulations of giant cells and fibrous tissue
Other signs of hyperparathyroidism should be sought
updates.explanation: Brown tumour is described as a localised accumulation of giant cells and fibrous tissue in the setting of hyperparathyroidism. The source stresses that associated findings of hyperparathyroidism, such as subperiosteal bone resorption, are needed. Lesions may show different stages of healing and can become sclerotic after treatment of hyperparathyroidism.

updates.question_text: Regarding hip lesion locations and differentials, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The greater trochanter is an epiphyseal equivalent
Greater trochanteric lesions may include chondroblastoma, ABC, infection and GCT
Lesser trochanter avulsion without significant clinical history should suggest pathological fracture
Greater trochanteric lesions are always metastatic until proven otherwise
Intertrochanteric lucent lesions include lipoma, solitary bone cyst, monostotic fibrous dysplasia and liposclerosing myxofibroma
options_after: The greater trochanter is an epiphyseal equivalent
Greater trochanteric lesions may include chondroblastoma, ABC, infection and GCT
Lesser trochanter avulsion without significant clinical history should suggest pathological fracture
Greater trochanteric lesions are characteristically metastatic until proven otherwise
Intertrochanteric lucent lesions include lipoma, solitary bone cyst, monostotic fibrous dysplasia and liposclerosing myxofibroma
updates.explanation: The source treats the greater trochanter as an epiphyseal equivalent and notes that chondroblastoma, ABC, infection and GCT can occur there. Lesser trochanter avulsion without a convincing trauma history should raise concern for pathological fracture. The intertrochanteric region has a specific benign differential including lipoma, solitary bone cyst, monostotic fibrous dysplasia and liposclerosing myxofibroma.

updates.question_text: Regarding the calcaneus as a site of bone lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Every calcaneal lucency in an adult should be called chondroblastoma
The calcaneus has no epiphyseal-equivalent behaviour
It can be conceptualised as a hybrid long bone with epiphyseal, metaphyseal and diaphyseal regions
The posterior meta-epiphyseal region is favoured by haematogenous infection and metastasis
The anterior lateral diaphyseal region is a typical site for solitary bone cyst and intraosseous lipoma
options_after: Routine calcaneal lucency in an adult should be called chondroblastoma
The calcaneus lacks epiphyseal-equivalent behaviour
It can be conceptualised as a hybrid long bone with epiphyseal, metaphyseal and diaphyseal regions
The posterior meta-epiphyseal region is favoured by haematogenous infection and metastasis
The anterior lateral diaphyseal region is a typical site for solitary bone cyst and intraosseous lipoma
updates.explanation: The source recommends using location within the calcaneus first, treating it as a hybrid long bone with specific epiphyseal, metaphyseal and diaphyseal areas. Infection and metastasis favour the posterior meta-epiphyseal region. Solitary bone cyst, intraosseous lipoma and pseudocyst occur in the anterior third laterally, creating a location-based differential.

updates.question_text: Regarding anterior calcaneal lucencies, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pseudocyst is defined by aggressive cortical destruction
Intraosseous lipoma is always T2 dark and never contains calcification
Solitary bone cyst is usually centred in the posterior epiphysis
Solitary bone cyst may show a fallen fragment sign
Intraosseous lipoma may show fat signal or fat density
options_after: Pseudocyst is defined by aggressive cortical destruction
Intraosseous lipoma is characteristically T2 dark and will not contain calcification
Solitary bone cyst is usually centred in the posterior epiphysis
Solitary bone cyst may show a fallen fragment sign
Intraosseous lipoma may show fat signal or fat density
updates.explanation: The source groups solitary bone cyst, intraosseous lipoma and pseudocyst around the anterior third of the calcaneus laterally. Solitary bone cyst may show a fallen fragment, while intraosseous lipoma is recognised by fat density or fat signal and may have a central fragment from fat necrosis. Pseudocyst is a normal trabecular variant rather than aggressive destruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding liposclerosing myxofibroma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It has a characteristic intertrochanteric femoral location
It is usually an aggressive permeative diaphyseal lesion in children
It may appear as a geographic lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin
It is defined by multiple epiphyseal osteochondromas
It requires no follow-up because malignant degeneration is not described
options_after: It has a characteristic intertrochanteric femoral location
It is usually an aggressive permeative diaphyseal lesion in children
It may appear as a geographic lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin
It is defined by multiple epiphyseal osteochondromas
It does not require follow-up because malignant degeneration is not described
updates.explanation: Liposclerosing myxofibroma is presented as having a very characteristic location in the intertrochanteric region of the femur. It looks like a geographic lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin. Despite a non-aggressive appearance, the source states that a minority may undergo malignant degeneration, so follow-up is needed.

updates.question_text: Regarding multiple hereditary exostoses, Trevor disease and supracondylar spur, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Multiple hereditary exostoses is an autosomal dominant condition with multiple osteochondromas
Trevor disease produces epiphyseal osteochondroma-like lesions that point into the joint
Trevor disease is centred in the diaphysis and never affects the joint
A supracondylar spur can compress the median nerve through the ligament of Struthers mechanism
Supracondylar spur is diagnosed by marrow continuity with a metaphyseal exostosis pointing away from the joint
options_after: Multiple hereditary exostoses is an autosomal dominant condition with multiple osteochondromas
Trevor disease produces epiphyseal osteochondroma-like lesions that point into the joint
Trevor disease is centred in the diaphysis and will not affect the joint
A supracondylar spur can compress the median nerve through the ligament of Struthers mechanism
Supracondylar spur is diagnosed by marrow continuity with a metaphyseal exostosis pointing away from the joint
updates.explanation: Multiple hereditary exostoses is described as autosomal dominant with multiple osteochondromas and an increased malignant transformation risk. Trevor disease, or dysplasia epiphysealis hemimelica, forms epiphyseal osteochondroma-like lesions that point into the joint and cause deformity. A supracondylar spur is a normal variant that points toward the joint and may compress the median nerve via the ligament of Struthers.

updates.question_text: Regarding periosteal chondroma and osteofibrous dysplasia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Osteofibrous dysplasia is best recognised as a sacral midline tumour
Periosteal chondroma is a common cause of diffuse sclerotic metaphyseal lines
A cartilaginous lesion in a child's finger suggests periosteal chondroma
Osteofibrous dysplasia and adamantinoma are always separable by imaging
Osteofibrous dysplasia is centred in the anterior tibia and associated with anterior tibial bowing
options_after: Osteofibrous dysplasia is best recognised as a sacral midline tumour
Periosteal chondroma is a common cause of diffuse sclerotic metaphyseal lines
A cartilaginous lesion in a child's finger suggests periosteal chondroma
Osteofibrous dysplasia and adamantinoma are characteristically separable by imaging
Osteofibrous dysplasia is centred in the anterior tibia and associated with anterior tibial bowing
updates.explanation: The source states that a lesion in the finger of a child should suggest periosteal chondroma, a rare cartilaginous juxtacortical lesion that can saucerise adjacent cortex. Osteofibrous dysplasia is a benign lesion of the tibia or fibula in young children, centred in the anterior tibia with bowing. It may occur with adamantinoma, and imaging cannot reliably differentiate the two.

updates.question_text: Regarding thalassaemia and sickle cell skeletal appearances, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Thalassaemia can produce hair-on-end skull changes
Sickle cell disease is described as obliterating the paranasal sinuses more than thalassaemia
Thalassaemia can be associated with extramedullary haematopoiesis
Thalassaemia is primarily recognised by a solitary epiphyseal lucency
Sickle cell disease is never associated with avascular necrosis
options_after: Thalassaemia can produce hair-on-end skull changes
Sickle cell disease is described as obliterating the paranasal sinuses more than thalassaemia
Thalassaemia can be associated with extramedullary haematopoiesis
Thalassaemia is primarily recognised by a solitary epiphyseal lucency
Sickle cell disease is not associated with avascular necrosis
updates.explanation: The source highlights thalassaemia skeletal changes from marrow expansion, including hair-on-end skull, facial bone expansion, rib expansion and extramedullary haematopoiesis. It contrasts thalassaemia as obliterating the sinuses, whereas sickle cell disease does not. Sickle cell disease is also listed as a cause of avascular necrosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding plain film stages of femoral head osteonecrosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stage one requires secondary osteoarthritis on radiography
Stage two is defined by complete joint-space loss only
Stage zero has normal imaging
Stage four has a normal radiograph but marrow oedema on MRI
Stage three includes crescent sign with articular collapse but preserved joint space
options_after: Stage one requires secondary osteoarthritis on radiography
Stage two is defined by complete joint-space loss
Stage zero has normal imaging
Stage four has a normal radiograph but marrow oedema on MRI
Stage three includes crescent sign with articular collapse but preserved joint space
updates.explanation: The source lists plain film stages: zero is normal, one has normal radiograph with marrow oedema on MRI, two is mixed lytic/sclerotic change, three has crescent sign or articular collapse with preserved joint space, and four has secondary osteoarthritis. The statements reversing stages one and four are therefore incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding classic signs and complications of Paget disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Blade of grass sign refers to a lucent leading edge in a long bone
Picture-frame vertebra involves cortical thickening on all four margins
Cotton-wool bone reflects thick disorganised trabeculae
Rugger jersey spine and Paget picture-frame vertebra both involve only superior and inferior endplates
Saber shin refers to tibial bowing
options_after: Blade of grass sign refers to a lucent leading edge in a long bone
Picture-frame vertebra involves cortical thickening on all four margins
Cotton-wool bone reflects thick disorganised trabeculae
Rugger jersey spine and Paget picture-frame vertebra both involve primarily superior and inferior endplates
Saber shin refers to tibial bowing
updates.explanation: The source lists blade of grass sign as the lucent leading edge in a long bone, picture-frame vertebra as thickening on all four vertebral margins, cotton-wool bone as thick disorganised trabeculae and saber shin as tibial bowing. Rugger jersey spine is the process limited to superior and inferior endplates; Paget picture-frame vertebra involves all margins.

updates.question_text: Regarding spine pattern recognition in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Paget disease may produce an enlarged ivory vertebra or picture-frame vertebra
Renal osteodystrophy produces rugger jersey bands at the top and bottom of vertebral bodies
Osteopetrosis can produce dense vertebral bands with sharply defined sclerosis
H-shaped vertebra is the classic descriptor for Paget picture-frame vertebra
Picture-frame vertebra in Paget disease is limited to the superior and inferior endplates only
options_after: Paget disease may produce an enlarged ivory vertebra or picture-frame vertebra
Renal osteodystrophy produces rugger jersey bands at the top and bottom of vertebral bodies
Osteopetrosis can produce dense vertebral bands with sharply defined sclerosis
H-shaped vertebra is the classic descriptor for Paget picture-frame vertebra
Picture-frame vertebra in Paget disease is limited to the superior and inferior endplates
updates.explanation: The source contrasts several spinal patterns. Paget disease can show an enlarged ivory vertebra or picture-frame vertebra. Renal osteodystrophy produces rugger jersey bands at the superior and inferior endplates, while osteopetrosis can produce dense sharply defined bands and dark marrow on MRI. H-shaped vertebra is a sickle cell clue rather than a Paget picture-frame descriptor.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI and nuclear medicine in Paget disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bone scan is useless for treatment-response assessment
The characteristic bone scan appearance is isolated joint-space uptake only
Active Paget disease is always photopenic on all phases
Malignant transformation loses normal T1 marrow signal
Bone scan helps define the extent of disease
options_after: Bone scan is useless for treatment-response assessment
The characteristic bone scan appearance is isolated joint-space uptake
Active Paget disease is characteristically photopenic on most phases
Malignant transformation loses normal T1 marrow signal
Bone scan helps define the extent of disease
updates.explanation: The source compares malignant transformation with active Paget disease, noting that both may be T2 bright and enhance, but malignant transformation loses normal T1 signal. It states that bone scan is useful to define disease extent and help assess response to treatment. The characteristic nuclear medicine pattern is whole-bone involvement rather than isolated joint uptake.

updates.question_text: Regarding tibial bowing patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Physiologic bowing is smooth, lateral, bilateral and symmetric in toddlers
Rickets is expected to have normal metaphyses and normal growth-plate width
NF1 can produce anterolateral bowing with fibular pseudoarthrosis
Blount disease is primarily a distal fibular physeal growth disturbance
Osteogenesis imperfecta affects only the tibia
options_after: Physiologic bowing is smooth, lateral, bilateral and symmetric in toddlers
Rickets is expected to have normal metaphyses and normal growth-plate width
NF1 can produce anterolateral bowing with fibular pseudoarthrosis
Blount disease is primarily a distal fibular physeal growth disturbance
Osteogenesis imperfecta affects primarily the tibia
updates.explanation: The source lists physiologic bowing as smooth, lateral, bilateral and symmetric between roughly 18 months and 2 years. NF1 is described with anterolateral bowing and possible fibular pseudoarthrosis. Rickets should show metaphyseal fraying and widened growth plates, while Blount disease involves a proximal tibial posteromedial physeal disturbance rather than a distal fibular process.

updates.question_text: What broad principle does the source emphasise about MRI diagnosis of soft-tissue masses?
options_before: All soft-tissue masses have pathognomonic MRI appearances
T2 hyperintensity excludes malignancy
Enhancement reliably separates benign from malignant lesions
Only a minority can be accurately diagnosed on MRI, so focus on recognisable exceptions
Soft-tissue tumour questions should ignore age and location
options_after: Most soft-tissue masses have pathognomonic MRI appearances
T2 hyperintensity excludes malignancy
Enhancement reliably separates benign from malignant lesions
Only a minority can be accurately diagnosed on MRI, so focus on recognisable exceptions
Soft-tissue tumour questions should ignore age and location
updates.explanation: The source states that only about 20-30% of soft-tissue masses can be accurately diagnosed on MRI because many are T2 bright and enhance. For multiple-choice purposes, the strategy is to learn the exceptions and the epidemiological or location clues. Age, location and atypical signal behaviour remain important discriminators.

updates.question_text: Regarding additional clues for pleomorphic undifferentiated sarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It may be associated with spontaneous haemorrhage from outgrowing its blood supply
Radiation is listed as a risk factor
It is always a benign cyst between gastrocnemius and semimembranosus
It is limited to the epiphysis of children
It is diagnosed by a fallen fragment sign
options_after: It may be associated with spontaneous haemorrhage from outgrowing its blood supply
Radiation is listed as a risk factor
It is characteristically a benign cyst between gastrocnemius and semimembranosus
It is limited to the epiphysis of children
It is diagnosed by a fallen fragment sign
updates.explanation: The source describes a classic clinical trap in which an older patient has a large proximal muscular haematoma with an underlying pleomorphic undifferentiated sarcoma. It also lists radiation as a risk factor and notes sarcomatous transformation of bone infarct. Baker cyst anatomy and fallen fragment sign refer to different entities.

updates.question_text: For a suspected Baker cyst mimic in the popliteal fossa, which next step is emphasised when the lesion is complex or vascular?
options_before: No further work-up because all popliteal cystic lesions are Baker cysts
Immediate steroid injection without imaging
MRI to evaluate for synovial sarcoma or another mass
Bone scan to exclude Paget disease
Call it physiologic bowing
options_after: Further work-up is unnecessary because a popliteal cystic lesion is presumed to be a Baker cyst
Immediate steroid injection without imaging
MRI to evaluate for synovial sarcoma or another mass
Bone scan to exclude Paget disease
Call it physiologic bowing
updates.explanation: The source warns that not every popliteal fossa lesion is a Baker cyst. A Baker cyst must be located between the medial head of gastrocnemius and semimembranosus, and if a mass is complex or has flow, synovial sarcoma should be considered with MRI as the next step. The other options ignore the soft-tissue tumour concern.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging clues and trivia for synovial sarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The T2 triple sign can be seen
A bowl-of-grapes appearance with fluid-fluid levels can be seen
Soft-tissue calcifications with bone erosions exclude synovial sarcoma
It never causes pain
It is always a rapidly enlarging huge mass at presentation
options_after: The T2 triple sign can be seen
A bowl-of-grapes appearance with fluid-fluid levels can be seen
Soft-tissue calcifications with bone erosions exclude synovial sarcoma
It will not cause pain
It is characteristically a rapidly enlarging huge mass at presentation
updates.explanation: The source lists several ways synovial sarcoma may be shown: a T2 triple sign, a bowl-of-grapes appearance from multiple fluid-fluid levels, and soft-tissue calcification with bone erosion on radiography. Therefore calcification with bone erosion does not exclude synovial sarcoma. It also notes that synovial sarcomas may hurt and may be slow-growing and small, which can lead to benign misclassification.

updates.question_text: Regarding practical lipomatous tumour clues, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A superficial homogeneous fat-signal lesion is automatically high-grade liposarcoma
Liposarcomas tend to be deep
A retroperitoneal lipomatous mass should be assumed to be a simple subcutaneous lipoma
Liposarcomas tend to be large
Lipomas tend to be superficial
options_after: A superficial homogeneous fat-signal lesion is ordinarily high-grade liposarcoma
Liposarcomas tend to be deep
A retroperitoneal lipomatous mass should be assumed to be a simple subcutaneous lipoma
Liposarcomas tend to be large
Lipomas tend to be superficial
updates.explanation: The source gives the practical exam heuristic that liposarcomas tend to be deep and big, while lipomas tend to be superficial. This is used alongside internal complexity and fat-suppression behaviour. A superficial homogeneous fat-signal lesion is not automatically a high-grade tumour, and retroperitoneal deep location should increase suspicion rather than reassure.

updates.question_text: Regarding myxoid liposarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is listed as the most common liposarcoma in patients younger than 20
It is always fully fat-suppressing like a simple lipoma
It can be T2 bright and T1 dark, so gadolinium is needed rather than calling it a cyst
It is defined by phleboliths on plain radiography
It is a synovial proliferation with hemosiderin deposition
options_after: It is listed as the most common liposarcoma in patients younger than 20
It is characteristically fully fat-suppressing like a simple lipoma
It can be T2 bright and T1 dark, so gadolinium is needed rather than calling it a cyst
It is defined by phleboliths on plain radiography
It is a synovial proliferation with hemosiderin deposition
updates.explanation: The source states that myxoid liposarcoma is the most common liposarcoma in patients younger than 20. It may be T2 bright yet T1 dark, creating a cyst mimic, so contrast is needed for characterisation. Phleboliths point toward haemangioma and hemosiderin-rich synovial proliferation points toward PVNS.

updates.question_text: Regarding intra-articular pigmented villonodular synovitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It characteristically preserves no joint space and causes diffuse osteoporosis
It involves synovial proliferation and hemosiderin deposition
It is primarily treated with systemic chemotherapy
The knee is by far the most common joint
MRI blooming on gradient echo is a key imaging clue
options_after: It characteristically obliterates the joint space and causes diffuse osteoporosis
It involves synovial proliferation and hemosiderin deposition
It is primarily treated with systemic chemotherapy
The knee is by far the most common joint
MRI blooming on gradient echo is a key imaging clue
updates.explanation: PVNS is described as synovial proliferation with hemosiderin deposition, usually affecting the knee. Radiographs may show effusion and erosions with preserved joint space and normal mineralisation, but MRI is more specific because of blooming on gradient echo. Treatment is complete synovectomy, with a substantial recurrence rate.

updates.question_text: Regarding giant cell tumour of the tendon sheath, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is described as PVNS of the tendon sheath
It is T1 bright and T2 bright like a simple cyst
It is typically found in the hand, especially palmar tendons
It never causes erosion of underlying bone
It is diagnosed by a fallen fragment sign
options_after: It is described as PVNS of the tendon sheath
It is T1 bright and T2 bright like a simple cyst
It is typically found in the hand, especially palmar tendons
It will not cause erosion of underlying bone
It is diagnosed by a fallen fragment sign
updates.explanation: The source describes giant cell tumour of the tendon sheath as PVNS of the tendon sheath and notes typical palmar tendon involvement in the hand. It can cause erosions of underlying bone and is soft-tissue density with T1 and T2 dark signal. The cystic T2 bright uniformly enhancing lesion in the comparison is a glomus tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding diabetic myonecrosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It most commonly affects the hand flexor tendons
MRI should show no oedema or enhancement
It is muscle infarction in poorly controlled type 1 diabetes
It is primarily a synovial loose-body disease
Biopsy should be avoided because it delays recovery and has a high complication rate
options_after: It most commonly affects the hand flexor tendons
MRI should fail to show oedema or enhancement
It is muscle infarction in poorly controlled type 1 diabetes
It is primarily a synovial loose-body disease
Biopsy should be avoided because it delays recovery and has a high complication rate
updates.explanation: Diabetic myonecrosis is described as infarction of muscle in poorly controlled type 1 diabetics, usually in the thigh or calf. MRI shows marked oedema, enhancement and irregular muscle necrosis. The source specifically warns against biopsy because it delays recovery and has a high complication rate.

updates.question_text: Regarding synovial chondromatosis and metastatic calcification, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Metastatic calcification is expected only when serum calcium is normal and phosphate is abnormal
Primary synovial chondromatosis most commonly involves the shoulder rather than the knee
Metastatic calcification is distinguished from tumoral calcinosis by normal calcium and abnormal phosphate
Primary synovial chondromatosis produces multiple small uniformly sized mineralised nodules near a joint
Metastatic calcification may show fine diffuse soft-tissue calcifications with renal and lung calcifications
options_after: Metastatic calcification is expected primarily when serum calcium is normal and phosphate is abnormal
Primary synovial chondromatosis most commonly involves the shoulder rather than the knee
Metastatic calcification is distinguished from tumoral calcinosis by normal calcium and abnormal phosphate
Primary synovial chondromatosis produces multiple small uniformly sized mineralised nodules near a joint
Metastatic calcification may show fine diffuse soft-tissue calcifications with renal and lung calcifications
updates.explanation: Primary synovial chondromatosis produces multiple small uniform ossified or peripherally mineralised nodules in an intra-articular location, with the knee as the common joint. Metastatic calcification produces fine diffuse soft-tissue calcifications and can also involve renal and lung tissues. The source links metastatic calcification to hypercalcaemia, renal failure or hyperparathyroidism, whereas tumoral calcinosis usually has normal calcium with phosphate abnormality.

updates.question_text: Regarding 'do not biopsy' musculoskeletal lesions in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Myositis ossificans can show circumferential calcification with a lucent centre
Avulsion injury near the pelvis can have aggressive periosteal reaction
Cortical desmoid has a characteristic posterior distal femoral location
Synovial herniation pit is located in the anterosuperior femoral neck
All of these entities are primary malignant bone tumours requiring immediate biopsy
options_after: Myositis ossificans can show circumferential calcification with a lucent centre
Avulsion injury near the pelvis can have aggressive periosteal reaction
Cortical desmoid has a characteristic posterior distal femoral location
Synovial herniation pit is located in the anterosuperior femoral neck
Most of these entities are primary malignant bone tumours requiring immediate biopsy
updates.explanation: The source lists myositis ossificans, avulsion injury, cortical desmoid and synovial herniation pit as benign lesions that may look aggressive but should not be biopsied. Myositis ossificans has peripheral/circumferential maturation, pelvic avulsion can create aggressive periosteal reaction, cortical desmoid sits at the posterior distal femur, and Pitt pit is in the anterosuperior femoral neck. Their importance is recognition to avoid inappropriate biopsy.

updates.question_text: What is the main biopsy-planning principle emphasised for suspected musculoskeletal tumours?
options_before: Use the shortest route regardless of future resection planes
Cross any joint space if it makes the procedure easier
Biopsy all benign-appearing incidental cortical desmoids
Avoid all image-guided biopsies in the pelvis
Discuss the biopsy route with the orthopaedic surgeon to avoid contaminating uninvolved compartments
options_after: Use the shortest route despite variation in future resection planes
Cross any joint space if it makes the procedure easier
Biopsy most benign-appearing incidental cortical desmoids
Avoid most image-guided biopsies in the pelvis
Discuss the biopsy route with the orthopaedic surgeon to avoid contaminating uninvolved compartments
updates.explanation: The source stresses that biopsy route should be discussed with the orthopaedic surgeon so compartments not involved by the tumour, or not included in the planned resection, are not contaminated. It gives special routes to avoid around pelvis, knee and shoulder. The principle is planned oncological access, not simply the shortest needle path.

updates.question_text: Regarding neuropathic joint and Charcot foot, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Diabetic Charcot foot typically spares the midfoot and never collapses the arch
Neuropathic joint can resemble very severe osteoarthritis with destruction, debris and dislocation
Charcot foot classically begins as isolated DIP erosive arthritis
Surgical-like margins are a buzzword clue
Neuropathic joint is defined by preserved alignment and no debris
options_after: Diabetic Charcot foot typically spares the midfoot and will not collapse the arch
Neuropathic joint can resemble very severe osteoarthritis with destruction, debris and dislocation
Charcot foot classically begins as isolated DIP erosive arthritis
Surgical-like margins are a buzzword clue
Neuropathic joint is defined by preserved alignment without debris
updates.explanation: The source describes neuropathic joint as an exaggerated destructive arthropathy with deformity, debris, dislocation, dense subchondral bone and articular cortex destruction. Surgical-like margins are a buzzword clue. In diabetic Charcot foot, the midfoot is favoured and collapse of the arch can cause rocker-bottom deformity, so a midfoot-sparing statement is incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding psoriatic arthritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Skin findings usually precede arthritis
Nail involvement correlates with DIP involvement
Symmetric sacroiliac involvement is required in every case
It combines erosive change with bone proliferation
It classically causes osteoporosis without bone proliferation
options_after: Skin findings usually precede arthritis
Nail involvement correlates with DIP involvement
Symmetric sacroiliac involvement is required in most cases
It combines erosive change with bone proliferation
It classically causes osteoporosis without bone proliferation
updates.explanation: The source states that in most cases skin findings precede psoriatic arthritis and that nail involvement correlates strongly with DIP joint involvement. Imaging combines erosive change and bone proliferation, with hands most common and feet second. Sacroiliac involvement may occur and is often asymmetric, so mandatory symmetry would be wrong.

updates.question_text: Regarding reactive arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and enteropathic arthritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Reactive arthritis resembles psoriatic arthritis with bone proliferation and asymmetric SI involvement
Reactive arthritis tends to affect the feet more than the hands
Ankylosing spondylitis begins with sacroiliac involvement and produces bamboo spine from syndesmophytes
Enteropathic arthritis has no axial or peripheral imaging patterns
Normal sacroiliac joints with isolated spinal disease strongly support ankylosing spondylitis
options_after: Reactive arthritis resembles psoriatic arthritis with bone proliferation and asymmetric SI involvement
Reactive arthritis tends to affect the feet more than the hands
Ankylosing spondylitis begins with sacroiliac involvement and produces bamboo spine from syndesmophytes
Enteropathic arthritis lacks axial or peripheral imaging patterns
Normal sacroiliac joints with isolated spinal disease strongly support ankylosing spondylitis
updates.explanation: The source describes reactive arthritis as similar to psoriatic arthritis, with bone proliferation, erosions and asymmetric sacroiliac involvement, but more commonly affecting the feet than the hands. Ankylosing spondylitis favours the spine and sacroiliac joints, with SI involvement usually first and bamboo spine from syndesmophytes. Enteropathic arthritis is described in axial and peripheral forms, so denying these patterns is incorrect. Normal SI joints argue against ankylosing spondylitis in the test framing.

updates.question_text: Regarding hyperparathyroidism skeletal findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Brown tumours exclude hyperparathyroidism
Subperiosteal bone resorption along the radial aspects of the second and third fingers is classic
The source states that phosphate retention cannot be the cause
Terminal tuft erosions can be seen
Rugger jersey spine is listed as a classic presentation
options_after: Brown tumours exclude hyperparathyroidism
Subperiosteal bone resorption along the radial aspects of the second and third fingers is classic
The source states that phosphate retention will not be the cause
Terminal tuft erosions can be seen
Rugger jersey spine is listed as a classic presentation
updates.explanation: Hyperparathyroidism is summarised with classic buzzwords including subperiosteal bone resorption along the radial aspects of the second and third fingers, terminal tuft erosions, rugger jersey spine and brown tumours. The source also lists rib notching and pelvic changes with narrowed femoral necks and wide SI joints. It specifically warns that phosphate retention may be the requested mechanism in these classic images.

updates.question_text: Within the inflammatory arthritis branch of the source algorithm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bony proliferation with distal distribution is the hallmark of simple osteoarthritis in typical joints
No bony proliferation with proximal distribution favours rheumatoid arthritis
Proximal distribution with osteoporosis is the classic psoriatic pattern
Bony proliferation with distal distribution favours psoriatic/reactive/IBD-related disease
Atypical joint degeneration always means gout
options_after: Bony proliferation with distal distribution is the hallmark of simple osteoarthritis in typical joints
No bony proliferation with proximal distribution favours rheumatoid arthritis
Proximal distribution with osteoporosis is the classic psoriatic pattern
Bony proliferation with distal distribution favours psoriatic/reactive/IBD-related disease
Atypical joint degeneration characteristically means gout
updates.explanation: The algorithm separates inflammatory polyarthritis into a no-bony-proliferation/proximal branch, favouring RA, and a bony-proliferation/distal branch, favouring psoriatic, reactive and inflammatory-bowel-related disease. Typical osteoarthritis follows a degenerative branch, not this inflammatory branch. Atypical degenerative distribution broadens the differential to post-traumatic disease, gout, CPPD or haemophilia.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal marrow components and conversion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adults normally retain only red marrow in hands and feet
Bone marrow consists of trabecular bone, red marrow and yellow marrow
Yellow marrow increases with age
Normal red-to-yellow conversion proceeds from extremities toward the axial skeleton
Conversion is usually completed by the mid-20s
options_after: Adults normally retain primarily red marrow in hands and feet
Bone marrow consists of trabecular bone, red marrow and yellow marrow
Yellow marrow increases with age
Normal red-to-yellow conversion proceeds from extremities toward the axial skeleton
Conversion is usually completed by the mid-20s
updates.explanation: The source defines marrow as trabecular bone plus red and yellow marrow. Yellow marrow increases with age, with red-to-yellow conversion progressing from distal extremities toward the axial skeleton and usually completing by the mid-20s. Adults normally retain red marrow mainly in the axial skeleton and proximal metaphyses, not only in hands and feet.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal marrow variants or spared areas, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Epiphyses are always the first region to reconvert in normal demand states
Any proximal femoral red marrow in a teenager is malignant by definition
Red marrow is never present in adult humeral or femoral heads as a variant
Patchy red marrow may be seen in the proximal femoral metaphysis of teenagers
Distal femoral sparing can be seen in teenagers and menstruating women
options_after: Epiphyses are characteristically the first region to reconvert in normal demand states
Any proximal femoral red marrow in a teenager is malignant by definition
Red marrow is not present in adult humeral or femoral heads as a variant
Patchy red marrow may be seen in the proximal femoral metaphysis of teenagers
Distal femoral sparing can be seen in teenagers and menstruating women
updates.explanation: The source lists patchy red marrow in the proximal femoral metaphysis of teenagers and distal femoral sparing in teenagers or menstruating women as normal variants/spared areas. Reconversion begins centrally and moves peripherally, with epiphyses usually spared unless haematopoietic demand is very high. Red marrow can also be seen in humeral and femoral heads as a normal adult variant.

updates.question_text: Regarding leukaemic marrow infiltration, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Leukaemic cell proliferation can replace red marrow
Marrow may be darker than muscle and normal discs on T1
STIR signal may be brighter than muscle because of increased water content
Normal red marrow should be darker than muscle on T1
Leukaemia is best recognised by marrow that exactly parallels fat on all sequences
options_after: Leukaemic cell proliferation can replace red marrow
Marrow may be darker than muscle and normal discs on T1
STIR signal may be brighter than muscle because of increased water content
Normal red marrow should be darker than muscle on T1
Leukaemia is best recognised by marrow that exactly parallels fat on most sequences
updates.explanation: The source describes leukaemia as proliferation of leukaemic cells replacing red marrow, making marrow darker than muscle and normal discs on T1. STIR signal may be brighter than muscle because of increased water content, while T2 is variable. Normal red marrow still contains fat and should be brighter than muscle on T1.

updates.question_text: Regarding marrow infiltrative disorders in this source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chloroma is described as a benign fat-signal lesion unrelated to leukaemia
All infiltrative marrow conditions are strictly epiphyseal and never diffuse
Lucent metaphyseal bands in a child can be a leukaemia presentation
Multiple myeloma is an exception that can show focal speckled deposits
Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia is linked to infarcts
options_after: Chloroma is described as a benign fat-signal lesion unrelated to leukaemia
Most infiltrative marrow conditions are strictly epiphyseal and will not diffuse
Lucent metaphyseal bands in a child can be a leukaemia presentation
Multiple myeloma is an exception that can show focal speckled deposits
Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia is linked to infarcts
updates.explanation: The source gives lucent metaphyseal bands in a child and T1-dark marrow as ways leukaemia may be shown. Most infiltrative conditions affect marrow diffusely, but multiple myeloma can show focal speckled deposits and Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia can cause infarcts. Chloroma is described as a destructive bone mass in a leukaemia patient, not as a benign fat-signal lesion.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound anisotropy of tendons, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A tendon may appear hypoechoic if it is not perpendicular to the ultrasound beam
The supraspinatus tendon is a common site for this problem as it curves over the humeral head
Anisotropy proves a full-thickness tendon tear
The long head of biceps in the bicipital groove is another problematic site
Normal tendons are expected to be hypoechoic regardless of beam angle
options_after: A tendon may appear hypoechoic if it is not perpendicular to the ultrasound beam
The supraspinatus tendon is a common site for this problem as it curves over the humeral head
Anisotropy proves a full-thickness tendon tear
The long head of biceps in the bicipital groove is another problematic site
Normal tendons are expected to be hypoechoic despite variation in beam angle
updates.explanation: The source emphasises anisotropy as a common ultrasound pitfall: a normally hyperechoic tendon may look hypoechoic when scanned non-perpendicularly. The supraspinatus and long head of biceps are highlighted because of their curved course. Hypoechogenicity from anisotropy does not prove a tear.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound assessment of tendon tears, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ultrasound always reliably distinguishes partial from complete tears
MRI is never used for tendon-tear clarification
Tendon is usually hyperechoic
Anisotropy is not relevant to tendon imaging
Focal hypoechoic areas can represent tears
options_after: Ultrasound characteristically reliably distinguishes partial from complete tears
MRI is not used for tendon-tear clarification
Tendon is usually hyperechoic
Anisotropy is not relevant to tendon imaging
Focal hypoechoic areas can represent tears
updates.explanation: The source states that tendons are usually hyperechoic and focal hypoechoic areas can indicate tears. It also warns that distinguishing partial from complete tears can be difficult on ultrasound, and that MRI is used for that problem. Anisotropy is a key pitfall in tendon sonography.

updates.question_text: Regarding general principles for joint injections and arthrography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The target is always the central cartilage surface
The safest technique is to ignore adjacent vessels and compartments
The target is the capsule rather than the centre of the joint space
The needle only needs to contact bone within the capsule
Avoid air in joints intended for MR arthrography because it creates susceptibility artefact
options_after: The target is characteristically the central cartilage surface
The safest technique is to ignore adjacent vessels and compartments
The target is the capsule rather than the centre of the joint space
The needle only needs to contact bone within the capsule
Avoid air in joints intended for MR arthrography because it creates susceptibility artefact
updates.explanation: The procedures section emphasises that the practical target is the capsule: the needle should contact bone within the capsule rather than chase the centre of the joint. It also warns against injecting air when MR imaging is planned because susceptibility artefact can result. Avoiding contamination or adjacent structure injury is a key procedural goal.

updates.question_text: Regarding contrast confirmation during joint injection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Contrast remaining as a focal blob at the tip confirms ideal intra-articular position
Contrast is never used in hip or shoulder arthrograms
Needle position cannot be checked before full injection
A small amount of contrast is injected to confirm position
Contrast should flow away from the needle tip if the needle is in the capsule/space
options_after: Contrast remaining as a focal blob at the tip confirms ideal intra-articular position
Contrast is not used in hip or shoulder arthrograms
Needle position will not be checked before full injection
A small amount of contrast is injected to confirm position
Contrast should flow away from the needle tip if the needle is in the capsule/space
updates.explanation: For both hip and shoulder arthrogram technique, the source recommends a small test injection of contrast to confirm position. Contrast should flow away from the tip if the needle is in the capsule or joint space. If the contrast simply stays at the tip, the needle is not in the desired space.

updates.question_text: If a patient cannot receive gadolinium but needs an arthrogram to evaluate the labrum, which options are supported by the source?
options_before: Consider CT arthrogram
Inject air into the joint and proceed to MR arthrogram
Use iodinated contrast and lidocaine without gadolinium
Cancel all arthrographic evaluation because no alternative exists
Use phosphate retention as the contrast mechanism
options_after: Consider CT arthrogram
Inject air into the joint and proceed to MR arthrogram
Use iodinated contrast and lidocaine without gadolinium
Arthrographic evaluation is abandoned when an alternative access route is unavailable
Use phosphate retention as the contrast mechanism
updates.explanation: For gadolinium allergy or phobia in a patient needing labral arthrography, the source suggests CT arthrogram using iodinated contrast and lidocaine without gadolinium. Air is not appropriate before MR arthrography because it causes susceptibility artefact. The scenario is contrast-procedure planning, not metabolic bone disease.

updates.question_text: If a patient cannot receive iodinated contrast but needs a steroid joint injection rather than an arthrogram, what confirmation method is supported?
options_before: Use gadolinium MR arthrogram contrast as mandatory first-line
Inject air to confirm placement, then inject steroid
Avoid placing the needle because confirmation is impossible
Perform whole-spine CT
Use bone scan tracer in the joint
options_after: Use gadolinium MR arthrogram contrast as mandatory first-line
Inject air to confirm placement, then inject steroid
Needle placement should be avoided when confirmation is unobtainable
Perform whole-spine CT
Use bone scan tracer in the joint
updates.explanation: For iodinated contrast allergy or phobia when the procedure is a steroid joint injection rather than arthrography, the source allows air injection to confirm placement before steroid injection. This is different from MR arthrography, where air would create susceptibility artefact. The goal is only correct needle placement, not imaging the labrum.

updates.question_text: Which joint procedure indication is the one expected to proceed to imaging after needle placement?
options_before: Arthrogram to evaluate the labrum
Steroid/lidocaine injection for pain management
Possible joint infection requiring aspiration
Aspiration only for crystal analysis
Therapeutic local anaesthetic injection alone
options_after: Arthrogram to evaluate the labrum
Steroid/lidocaine injection for pain management
Possible joint infection requiring aspiration
Aspiration primarily for crystal analysis
Therapeutic local anaesthetic injection alone
updates.explanation: The procedures section lists three reasons to place a needle in a joint: arthrogram for labral evaluation, steroid/lidocaine injection, and aspiration for possible infection. Only the arthrogram proceeds to imaging; the other two require correct needle placement but not diagnostic post-injection imaging. This affects the contrast/air strategy.

updates.question_text: Regarding the motor homunculus and vascular territories, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The inverted omega/posteriorly directed knob corresponds to hand motor cortex
MCA territory supplies only the leg region
ACA territory supplies the leg region
The hippocampus controls primary hand motor function
The motor hand area is in the cavernous sinus
options_after: The inverted omega/posteriorly directed knob corresponds to hand motor cortex
MCA territory supplies primarily the leg region
ACA territory supplies the leg region
The hippocampus controls primary hand motor function
The motor hand area is in the cavernous sinus
updates.explanation: The source links the inverted omega or posteriorly directed knob on the central sulcus/gyrus to the motor cortex controlling hand function. It also summarises the vascular-territory rule as ACA for legs and MCA for the rest. The hippocampus and cavernous sinus are unrelated to primary hand motor localisation.

updates.question_text: Regarding dilated perivascular spaces, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are always enhancing solid masses
They accompany perforating vessels
They are a common normal variant
They contain interstitial fluid rather than CSF
Common locations include basal ganglia, centrum semiovale and midbrain
options_after: They are characteristically enhancing solid masses
They accompany perforating vessels
They are a common normal variant
They contain interstitial fluid rather than CSF
Common locations include basal ganglia, centrum semiovale and midbrain
updates.explanation: The source defines Virchow-Robin spaces as fluid-filled spaces accompanying perforating vessels and describes them as common normal variants. It explicitly notes that they contain interstitial fluid, not CSF. Common locations listed include around lenticulostriate arteries in the lower basal ganglia, centrum semiovale and midbrain.

updates.question_text: Regarding cavum septum pellucidum, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is seen in essentially all preterm infants in the source table
It lies anterior to the foramen of Monro between the frontal horns
It is posterior to the foramen of Monro between the bodies of the lateral ventricles
It is an extension of the quadrigeminal plate cistern
It always causes obstructive hydrocephalus
options_after: It is seen in essentially all preterm infants in the source table
It lies anterior to the foramen of Monro between the frontal horns
It is posterior to the foramen of Monro between the bodies of the lateral ventricles
It is an extension of the quadrigeminal plate cistern
It characteristically causes obstructive hydrocephalus
updates.explanation: The source table describes cavum septum pellucidum as normal in preterm infants and present in a minority of adults. It lies anterior to the foramen of Monro between the frontal horns. A posterior continuation behind the foramen of Monro describes cavum vergae, while extension of the quadrigeminal cistern describes cavum velum interpositum.

updates.question_text: Regarding arachnoid granulations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They project into the venous system and participate in CSF reabsorption
They are normally hyperdense calcified thrombi
They are hypodense on CT and usually round or oval
They cannot scallop the inner table
Their round or oval shape helps distinguish them from linear venous sinus clot
options_after: They project into the venous system and participate in CSF reabsorption
They are normally hyperdense calcified thrombi
They are hypodense on CT and usually round or oval
They will not scallop the inner table
Their round or oval shape helps distinguish them from linear venous sinus clot
updates.explanation: Arachnoid granulations are described as arachnoid projections into the venous system that allow CSF reabsorption. They are hypodense on CT, similar to CSF, and are usually round or oval, helping distinguish them from linear venous sinus clot. The source also notes that they can scallop the inner table.

updates.question_text: Regarding cervical ICA segment pathology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A retropharyngeal cervical ICA cannot be injured during pharyngeal procedures
Pharyngeal infection cannot cause pseudoaneurysm at this level
Atherosclerosis commonly involves the origin
Dissection can be spontaneous or associated with connective-tissue disorders
Dissection may produce partial Horner syndrome followed by MCA-territory stroke
options_after: A retropharyngeal cervical ICA will not be injured during pharyngeal procedures
Pharyngeal infection will not cause pseudoaneurysm at this level
Atherosclerosis commonly involves the origin
Dissection can be spontaneous or associated with connective-tissue disorders
Dissection may produce partial Horner syndrome followed by MCA-territory stroke
updates.explanation: The source lists atherosclerosis at the cervical ICA origin and dissection as important C1/cervical segment pathology. Dissection may be spontaneous, associated with Marfan or Ehlers-Danlos syndromes, and can present with partial Horner syndrome then MCA stroke. A retropharyngeal course can create procedural risk, and pharyngeal infection may cause pseudoaneurysm at this level.

updates.question_text: Regarding the cavernous ICA segment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It can be affected by carotid-cavernous fistula
It routinely contains the internal auditory canal nerves
Aneurysms here are associated with hypertension in the source
It is identical to the cervical carotid bifurcation
It is the segment where the ophthalmic artery originates at the dural ring
options_after: It can be affected by carotid-cavernous fistula
It routinely contains the internal auditory canal nerves
Aneurysms here are associated with hypertension in the source
It is closely comparable to the cervical carotid bifurcation
It is the segment where the ophthalmic artery originates at the dural ring
updates.explanation: The C4 cavernous ICA segment is described as affected by multiple pathologies including carotid-cavernous fistula, and aneurysms here are strongly associated with hypertension. The ophthalmic/supraclinoid segment begins at the dural ring in the source discussion. Internal auditory canal nerves are a separate skull-base anatomy topic.

updates.question_text: On carotid ultrasound, which feature most directly supports external rather than internal carotid artery?
options_before: Continuous low-resistance diastolic flow
Posterior orientation without branches
Branching in the neck
No waveform response to temporal tap
Origin at the dural ring
options_after: Continuous low-resistance diastolic flow
Posterior orientation without branches
Branching in the neck
A temporal tap leaves the Doppler waveform unchanged
Origin at the dural ring
updates.explanation: The source contrasts ECA and ICA by the presence of branches: the ECA has branches, while the cervical ICA normally does not. ECA also tends to be anterior, high resistance, and responsive to temporal tap. Dural ring origin refers to the ophthalmic/supraclinoid ICA segment, not the cervical ultrasound distinction.

updates.question_text: Regarding persistent trigeminal artery, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It has no aneurysm association despite the additional branch point
It is the same entity as fetal PCA
It is a persistent fetal connection between the cavernous ICA and the basilar artery
It is a thrombosed superficial anastomotic vein
A sagittal MRI tau sign has been described
options_after: It lacks aneurysm association despite the additional branch point
It is the same entity as fetal PCA
It is a persistent fetal connection between the cavernous ICA and the basilar artery
It is a thrombosed superficial anastomotic vein
A sagittal MRI tau sign has been described
updates.explanation: Persistent trigeminal artery is described as a persistent fetal connection between the cavernous internal carotid artery and basilar artery. The source notes a tau sign on sagittal MRI and increased aneurysm risk at branch points, so denying that association is incorrect. This is distinct from fetal PCA, which refers to PCA supply from the anterior circulation through the posterior communicating artery.

updates.question_text: Regarding collateral dural sinus drainage pathways, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They have no role in temperature regulation or pressure equalisation
They connect dural sinuses to extracranial veins
They are always pathological and have no physiologic role
They can allow spread of sinus infection/inflammation leading to venous sinus thrombosis
They are identical to the ICA bifurcation
options_after: They have negligible role in temperature regulation or pressure equalisation
They connect dural sinuses to extracranial veins
They are characteristically pathological and lack physiologic role
They can allow spread of sinus infection/inflammation leading to venous sinus thrombosis
They are closely comparable to the ICA bifurcation
updates.explanation: The source describes accessory dural sinus drainage pathways connecting to extracranial veins. They can be useful for temperature regulation and pressure equalisation, so denying any physiologic role is wrong. They also provide a route for sinus infection or inflammation to spread, potentially causing venous sinus thrombosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding venous gas embolus on head imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Small venous gas emboli are common and often unnoticed
It usually represents a permanent arterial occlusion requiring aneurysm clipping
The cavernous sinus is the classic location
It should be treated as an arterial PCA aneurysm until proven otherwise
Peripheral or central IV tubing air can be the cause
options_after: Small venous gas emboli are common and often unnoticed
It usually represents a long-term arterial occlusion requiring aneurysm clipping
The cavernous sinus is the classic location
It should be treated as an arterial PCA aneurysm until proven otherwise
Peripheral or central IV tubing air can be the cause
