updates.explanation: The source describes venous gas embolus as common, often unnoticed and classically seen in the cavernous sinus. It can arise from air in peripheral or central IV tubing and usually resolves within 48 hours without clinical consequence. The teaching point is not to confuse this benign venous finding with arterial aneurysm pathology.

updates.question_text: Regarding concha bullosa, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It can never contribute to obstructive symptoms regardless of size
It is pneumatization of the middle concha
It is a persistent carotid-basilar fetal artery
It is usually a common variant with little clinical consequence
It is a deep cerebral vein
options_after: It will not contribute to obstructive symptoms despite variation in size
It is pneumatization of the middle concha
It is a persistent carotid-basilar fetal artery
It is usually a common variant with little clinical consequence
It is a deep cerebral vein
updates.explanation: The source defines concha bullosa as pneumatization of the middle concha. It is common and usually clinically insignificant, although a very large concha bullosa can rarely cause obstructive symptoms. It is a sinonasal anatomic variant, not a vascular or venous structure.

updates.question_text: Regarding neuroanatomy test-taking pearls in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Image-identification questions may use CTA, MRA or angiography
CN III palsy should first prompt concern for isolated concha bullosa
Skull-base foramina contents are a likely test area
CN VI palsy is never related to increased intracranial pressure
CN II and CN V3 are specifically not cavernous sinus contents
options_after: Image-identification questions may use CTA, MRA or angiography
CN III palsy should first prompt concern for isolated concha bullosa
Skull-base foramina contents are a likely test area
CN VI palsy is not related to increased intracranial pressure
CN II and CN V3 are specifically not cavernous sinus contents
updates.explanation: The source lists first-order neuroanatomy trivia as image identification and what passes through foramina. It specifically notes that CN II and CN V3 do not run through the cavernous sinus. Second-order pearls include CN III palsy suggesting posterior communicating artery aneurysm and CN VI palsy with increased intracranial pressure from stretch during inferior brainstem displacement.

updates.question_text: Regarding timing of T1 and T2 myelination patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: T1 changes precede T2 changes
An adult T1 pattern is seen around age 1 year
An adult T2 pattern is seen around age 2 years
T2 is most useful for assessing myelination in the first 0-6 months
T2 changes always precede T1 changes
options_after: T1 changes precede T2 changes
An adult T1 pattern is seen around age 1 year
An adult T2 pattern is seen around age 2 years
T2 is most useful for assessing myelination in the first 0-6 months
T2 changes characteristically precede T1 changes
updates.explanation: The source gives a simple memory rule: T1 changes precede T2 changes, with adult T1 pattern around age 1 and adult T2 pattern around age 2. It also states that T1 is most useful in the first year and T2 in the second year, especially from about 6 to 18 months. Reversing the sequence or assigning T2 to the earliest months is incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding late myelination areas, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Subcortical white matter is the last part of the brain to myelinate
Occipital white matter myelinates around 12 months in the source
Terminal zones of myelination are complete at birth
Frontal regions finish around 18 months in the source
Brainstem and posterior limb of internal capsule are never myelinated at birth
options_after: Subcortical white matter is the last part of the brain to myelinate
Occipital white matter myelinates around 12 months in the source
Terminal zones of myelination are complete at birth
Frontal regions finish around 18 months in the source
Brainstem and posterior limb of internal capsule are not myelinated at birth
updates.explanation: The source states that subcortical white matter is the last region to myelinate, with occipital white matter around 12 months and frontal regions around 18 months. It also lists terminal zones in the frontotemporoparietal subcortical regions finishing around 40 months, not at birth. Brainstem and posterior limb of the internal capsule are specifically described as normally myelinated at birth.

updates.question_text: Regarding corpus callosum development, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hypoplasia usually means absence of the genu with splenium intact
The splenium is always the first part to form and the genu last
The corpus callosum forms front to back
Callosal agenesis is primarily a venous sinus disease
The rostrum forms last
options_after: Hypoplasia usually means absence of the genu with splenium intact
The splenium is characteristically the first part to form and the genu last
The corpus callosum forms front to back
Callosal agenesis is primarily a venous sinus disease
The rostrum forms last
updates.explanation: The source states that the corpus callosum forms front to back and that the rostrum forms last. Therefore callosal hypoplasia commonly manifests as absence of the splenium with the genu intact, not the reverse. This is a developmental malformation rather than a venous sinus disorder.

updates.question_text: Regarding intracranial lipoma associated with corpus callosum dysgenesis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the most classic association with corpus callosum agenesis in the source
About half are found in the interhemispheric fissure in the source
It is normally treated urgently because it almost always causes symptoms
The quadrigeminal cistern is listed as the second most common location
It is a congenital malformation rather than a true neoplasm
options_after: It is the most classic association with corpus callosum agenesis in the source
About half are found in the interhemispheric fissure in the source
It is normally treated urgently because it typically causes symptoms
The quadrigeminal cistern is listed as the second most common location
It is a congenital malformation rather than a true neoplasm
updates.explanation: The source describes intracranial lipoma as the most classic association with corpus callosum agenesis. It gives the interhemispheric fissure as the most common location and quadrigeminal cistern as second. CNS lipomas are described as congenital malformations rather than true neoplasms and usually do not cause symptoms or require treatment.

updates.question_text: Which MRI sequence is highlighted as most helpful for intracranial lipoma recognition?
options_before: Delayed venous angiography only
Diffusion tensor imaging only
Non-fat-saturated T1-weighted imaging
Arterial spin labelling only
Susceptibility-weighted imaging only
options_after: Delayed venous angiography
Diffusion tensor imaging
Non-fat-saturated T1-weighted imaging
Arterial spin labelling
Susceptibility-weighted imaging
updates.explanation: The source notes that non-fat-saturated T1-weighted imaging is probably the most helpful sequence for intracranial lipoma, because most non-haemorrhagic brain findings are not T1 bright. This is a practical recognition pearl for fatty congenital lesions. The other sequences are not highlighted for this diagnosis in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding Dandy-Walker variant versus classic Dandy-Walker, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hydrocephalus is more common in classic Dandy-Walker than in variant
Dandy-Walker variant has a less severely hypoplastic vermis
Classic Dandy-Walker has a normal posterior fossa and normal torcula
Classic Dandy-Walker has normal fourth ventricle and normal vermis
Variant and classic Dandy-Walker are identical if a vermis is mildly hypoplastic
options_after: Hydrocephalus is more common in classic Dandy-Walker than in variant
Dandy-Walker variant has a less severely hypoplastic vermis
Classic Dandy-Walker has a normal posterior fossa and normal torcula
Classic Dandy-Walker has normal fourth ventricle and normal vermis
Variant and classic Dandy-Walker are closely comparable if a vermis is mildly hypoplastic
updates.explanation: The comparison table places Dandy-Walker variant between Blake pouch cyst and classic Dandy-Walker, with less severe vermian hypoplasia and hydrocephalus in a minority. Classic Dandy-Walker has hypoplastic rotated vermis, markedly dilated fourth ventricle, expanded posterior fossa and high torcula with hydrocephalus in most cases. The source stresses that classic Dandy-Walker requires the full feature set. The source table has hydrocephalus in most classic cases and a high torcula/expanded posterior fossa in classic Dandy-Walker.

updates.question_text: Regarding lobar holoprosencephaly, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The thalami are completely fused in lobar holoprosencephaly
Survival into adulthood is impossible in lobar holoprosencephaly
It is the least severe form in the source spectrum
It has zero midline cleavage with one single ventricle
It has focal anterior incomplete fusion, often involving the fornix
options_after: The thalami are completely fused in lobar holoprosencephaly
Lobar holoprosencephaly is incompatible with survival into adulthood
It is the least severe form in the source spectrum
It has zero midline cleavage with one single ventricle
It has focal anterior incomplete fusion, often involving the fornix
updates.explanation: The source lists lobar holoprosencephaly as the least severe form, with focal anterior incomplete fusion, often involving the fornix, variable mild frontal horn fusion and normal thalami. Septum pellucidum and corpus callosum abnormalities may occur, but survival into adulthood is possible. A single ventricle with zero midline cleavage describes alobar disease. The table lists normal thalami and possible adult survival for lobar holoprosencephaly, so these reversed statements are incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding arhinencephaly and Kallmann syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Arhinencephaly is described as a minor HPE expression
Anosmia is not relevant because olfactory bulbs are preserved
Midline olfactory bulbs and tracts are absent
Kallmann syndrome has no hypogonadism association in the source
The key imaging finding is an enlarged fourth ventricle with high torcula
options_after: Arhinencephaly is described as a minor HPE expression
Anosmia is not relevant because olfactory bulbs are preserved
Midline olfactory bulbs and tracts are absent
Kallmann syndrome lacks hypogonadism association in the source
The key imaging finding is an enlarged fourth ventricle with high torcula
updates.explanation: The source describes arhinencephaly as a minor holoprosencephaly expression with absent midline olfactory bulbs and tracts, producing anosmia. It may be tested as Kallmann syndrome, which also has hypogonadism in the source. Enlarged fourth ventricle/high torcula belongs to Dandy-Walker malformation. Absent olfactory bulbs/tracts explain the anosmia clue, and Kallmann syndrome is associated with hypogonadism in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding Meckel-Gruber syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Polydactyly is excluded from the classic triad
Occipital encephalocele is part of the classic triad
It has no association with holoprosencephaly
Multiple renal cysts are part of the classic triad
It is defined by isolated calcification of the falx
options_after: Polydactyly is excluded from the classic triad
Occipital encephalocele is part of the classic triad
It lacks association with holoprosencephaly
Multiple renal cysts are part of the classic triad
It is defined by isolated calcification of the falx
updates.explanation: The source lists the classic Meckel-Gruber triad as occipital encephalocele, multiple renal cysts and polydactyly. It also states that Meckel-Gruber syndrome is strongly associated with holoprosencephaly. Isolated falx calcification is not the syndrome definition in this text. The classic triad includes polydactyly, and the source states a strong association with holoprosencephaly.

updates.question_text: In the source algorithm for a severely abnormal brain, which feature supports hydranencephaly rather than severe hydrocephalus or alobar holoprosencephaly?
options_before: Preserved cortical mantle with falx present
Preserved cortical mantle with falx absent
Normal cortex with isolated concha bullosa
Absent cortical mantle
Grey-matter-lined focal cleft only
options_after: Preserved cortical mantle with falx present
Preserved cortical mantle with falx absent
Normal cortex with isolated concha bullosa
Absent cortical mantle
Grey-matter-lined focal cleft
updates.explanation: The source algorithm first asks whether the cortical mantle is present. If the cortical mantle is absent, hydranencephaly is favoured. If the mantle is still present, the falx helps separate severe hydrocephalus, where the falx remains, from alobar holoprosencephaly, where the falx is absent. A focal grey-matter-lined cleft points instead to schizencephaly.

updates.question_text: Regarding the terminology of cephalocele contents, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Meningocele refers to herniation of CSF, meninges and brain
A cystocele contains CSF, meninges, brain and ventricle
A myelocele contains only meninges and CSF
Cystocele refers to isolated spinal cord herniation
Encephalocele is used when brain tissue is included in the herniated contents
options_after: Meningocele refers to herniation of CSF, meninges and brain
A cystocele contains CSF, meninges, brain and ventricle
A myelocele contains primarily meninges and CSF
Cystocele refers to isolated spinal cord herniation
Encephalocele is used when brain tissue is included in the herniated contents
updates.explanation: A cystocele includes ventricle in addition to CSF, meninges and brain. Encephalocele or meningoencephalocele indicates that brain is part of the sac contents. Meningocele contains CSF and meninges without brain, and myelocele is spinal cord involvement.

updates.question_text: Regarding epilepsy MRI sequences discussed in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: T1-weighted imaging is useful for cortical thickness and grey-white matter assessment
FLAIR helps detect cortical or subcortical high signal from gliosis
Diffusion-weighted imaging is the only sequence needed for evaluating cortical malformations
T2*/SWI can help identify blood-breakdown products and seizure mimics
Calcified tuberous sclerosis lesions, Sturge-Weber changes, cavernomas and gangliogliomas are examples of seizure mimics to consider
options_after: T1-weighted imaging is useful for cortical thickness and grey-white matter assessment
FLAIR helps detect cortical or subcortical high signal from gliosis
Diffusion-weighted imaging is the principal sequence needed for evaluating cortical malformations
T2*/SWI can help identify blood-breakdown products and seizure mimics
Calcified tuberous sclerosis lesions, Sturge-Weber changes, cavernomas and gangliogliomas are examples of seizure mimics to consider
updates.explanation: The described epilepsy protocol uses T1 for cortical anatomy, FLAIR for gliosis, and susceptibility-sensitive imaging for blood products and calcified or vascular mimics. The source specifically lists tuberous sclerosis, Sturge-Weber, cavernomas and gangliogliomas among mimics. Diffusion imaging alone is not sufficient for the epilepsy protocol described.

updates.question_text: Regarding the Monro-Kellie doctrine, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Brain, blood and CSF volumes are in dynamic equilibrium within a closed cranial vault
It states that skull volume is unlimited because CSF can always expand
An increase in one intracranial component must be compensated by reduction in another component
It explains venous engorgement in intracranial hypotension after CSF volume loss
It requires the fourth ventricle to be obstructed
options_after: Brain, blood and CSF volumes are in dynamic equilibrium within a closed cranial vault
It states that skull volume is unlimited because CSF can characteristically expand
An increase in one intracranial component must be compensated by reduction in another component
It explains venous engorgement in intracranial hypotension after CSF volume loss
It requires the fourth ventricle to be obstructed
updates.explanation: Monro-Kellie describes the fixed-volume cranial vault containing brain, blood and CSF in dynamic equilibrium. When CSF volume falls, venous blood can expand to compensate, explaining venous engorgement in intracranial hypotension. Fourth ventricular obstruction is a hydrocephalus mechanism, not a requirement for this doctrine.

updates.question_text: Which ventricular pattern best matches non-communicating hydrocephalus from aqueductal stenosis?
options_before: Dilatation of all ventricles including the fourth ventricle
Dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles with a normal fourth ventricle
Small ventricles with posterior scleral flattening
Isolated enlargement of the fourth ventricle only
Diffuse atrophy with proportionate sulcal enlargement
options_after: Dilatation of most ventricles including the fourth ventricle
Dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles with a normal fourth ventricle
Small ventricles with posterior scleral flattening
Isolated enlargement of the fourth ventricle
Diffuse atrophy with proportionate sulcal enlargement
updates.explanation: Aqueductal stenosis obstructs CSF flow between the third and fourth ventricles, so the lateral and third ventricles enlarge while the fourth ventricle remains normal. Communicating hydrocephalus usually enlarges all ventricles. Proportionate sulcal enlargement suggests ex-vacuo change rather than obstructive hydrocephalus.

updates.question_text: Regarding over-shunting and distal shunt complications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hydrothorax is always clinically insignificant and never requires revision
Over-shunting may lead to slit ventricles
Subdural hygroma or haematoma may occur with excessive CSF drainage
Ascites is the main imaging sign of proximal shunt obstruction
A pseudocyst can form around the distal catheter tip
options_after: Hydrothorax is characteristically clinically insignificant and will not require revision
Over-shunting may lead to slit ventricles
Subdural hygroma or haematoma may occur with excessive CSF drainage
Ascites is the main imaging sign of proximal shunt obstruction
A pseudocyst can form around the distal catheter tip
updates.explanation: Excessive shunting can produce slit ventricles and predispose to subdural collections through intracranial volume shifts. Distal catheter problems include pseudocyst or loculated fluid collection, and distal migration may occur. Hydrothorax may be trivial when small but can be symptomatic when large and may require revision.

updates.question_text: Regarding PRES and treatment-related leukoencephalopathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: PRES classically produces bilateral posterior vasogenic oedema without restricted diffusion
PRES is always perfectly symmetric and limited to the occipital lobes
Chemotherapy-related PRES may have atypical distribution involving basal ganglia, brainstem or cerebellum
Treatment-induced leukoencephalopathy can produce bilateral confluent periventricular T2/FLAIR white matter abnormality
Disseminated necrotising leukoencephalopathy is a benign normal variant after trauma
options_after: PRES classically produces bilateral posterior vasogenic oedema without restricted diffusion
PRES is characteristically perfectly symmetric and limited to the occipital lobes
Chemotherapy-related PRES may have atypical distribution involving basal ganglia, brainstem or cerebellum
Treatment-induced leukoencephalopathy can produce bilateral confluent periventricular T2/FLAIR white matter abnormality
Disseminated necrotising leukoencephalopathy is a benign normal variant after trauma
updates.explanation: PRES is a vasogenic oedema pattern that is often posterior and bilateral but may be asymmetric or atypically distributed, especially after chemotherapy. Treatment-induced leukoencephalopathy can produce confluent periventricular white matter signal abnormality and later atrophy. Disseminated necrotising leukoencephalopathy is a severe treatment-related complication rather than a benign post-traumatic variant.

updates.question_text: Regarding post-radiation brain changes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: T2-bright white matter change and atrophy may correspond to the radiation portal
Imaging findings typically appear immediately during the first hours after treatment
Early delayed change may show high T2/FLAIR signal in the periventricular white matter
Late delayed change may appear mass-like and expansile with a mosaic pattern
Radiation change always selectively involves only the cortex
options_after: T2-bright white matter change and atrophy may correspond to the radiation portal
Imaging findings typically appear immediately during the first hours after treatment
Early delayed change may show high T2/FLAIR signal in the periventricular white matter
Late delayed change may appear mass-like and expansile with a mosaic pattern
Radiation change characteristically selectively involves primarily the cortex
updates.explanation: Post-radiation injury can produce T2-bright white matter change and atrophy matching the radiation field. The source describes a latent period of around two months, with early delayed periventricular white matter signal and later delayed deep white matter change that can look mass-like. A purely cortical pattern is not the expected description here.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiation-induced primary CNS neoplasms, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Radiation-induced meningiomas usually occur within the first 24 hours after treatment
Prior radiation therapy is described as an important risk factor for primary CNS neoplasm
More aggressive radiation-induced gliomas and sarcomas have no latency period
Radiation-induced tumours are excluded if mineralising microangiopathy is present
Meningioma is described as the commonest radiation-induced tumour type
options_after: Radiation-induced meningiomas usually occur within the first 24 hours after treatment
Prior radiation therapy is described as an important risk factor for primary CNS neoplasm
More aggressive radiation-induced gliomas and sarcomas lack latency period
Radiation-induced tumours are excluded if mineralising microangiopathy is present
Meningioma is described as the commonest radiation-induced tumour type
updates.explanation: The source emphasises radiation therapy as a major risk factor for later primary CNS neoplasm and states that meningioma is the most common type. Meningiomas tend to occur many years later, while more aggressive tumours have a shorter but still delayed window. Microangiopathy does not exclude a separate radiation-induced tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding toxic leukoencephalopathy and the inhalational heroin pattern, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Many toxic leukoencephalopathies produce widespread high T2/FLAIR signal in supra- and infratentorial white matter
The pattern is pathognomonic and never overlaps with other toxic leukoencephalopathies
The described inhalational heroin pattern can include symmetric centrum semiovale involvement
Deep cerebellar white matter may be involved with relative dentate nucleus sparing
The expected abnormality is isolated cortical haemorrhage without white matter signal change
options_after: Many toxic leukoencephalopathies produce widespread high T2/FLAIR signal in supra- and infratentorial white matter
The pattern is pathognomonic and will not overlap with other toxic leukoencephalopathies
The described inhalational heroin pattern can include symmetric centrum semiovale involvement
Deep cerebellar white matter may be involved with relative dentate nucleus sparing
The expected abnormality is isolated cortical haemorrhage without white matter signal change
updates.explanation: The source presents inhalational heroin leukoencephalopathy as a memorable but non-specific toxic white matter pattern. Symmetric centrum semiovale, posterior limb internal capsule and deep cerebellar white matter involvement with dentate sparing are described. The pattern is not pathognomonic and is not an isolated cortical haemorrhage syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding the McDonald diagnostic criteria concepts discussed for MS, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Dissemination in time requires all lesions to enhance at the same time
A single basal ganglia lacune is sufficient for the imaging criteria
Dissemination in space can be shown by lesions in more than one typical location
Typical locations include periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial and spinal cord regions
The criteria are based on skull-base foraminal measurements
options_after: Dissemination in time requires most lesions to enhance at the same time
A single basal ganglia lacune is sufficient for the imaging criteria
Dissemination in space can be shown by lesions in more than one typical location
Typical locations include periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial and spinal cord regions
The criteria are based on skull-base foraminal measurements
updates.explanation: The source summarises dissemination in space using typical MS locations, with involvement of more than one region. Dissemination in time is illustrated by lesions in different activity phases, such as enhancing and non-enhancing lesions together. A solitary vascular lacune or skull-base measurement does not establish MS criteria.

updates.question_text: Regarding additional MS imaging pearls, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: T2 is less useful than FLAIR for infratentorial lesions according to the source
Periventricular oval lesions perpendicular to the ventricles are classic
Calloso-septal interface involvement is highly specific for MS compared with vascular lesions and ADEM
MS plaques always show gross calcification
FLAIR is useful for juxtacortical and periventricular plaques
options_after: T2 is less useful than FLAIR for infratentorial lesions according to the source
Periventricular oval lesions perpendicular to the ventricles are classic
Calloso-septal interface involvement is highly specific for MS compared with vascular lesions and ADEM
MS plaques characteristically show gross calcification
FLAIR is useful for juxtacortical and periventricular plaques
updates.explanation: Classic MS imaging includes oval periventricular lesions oriented perpendicular to the ventricles and calloso-septal interface involvement. FLAIR is highlighted for juxtacortical and periventricular plaques, while T2 is more sensitive than FLAIR for infratentorial lesions. Calcification is not the defining feature of MS plaques.

updates.question_text: Regarding FDG PET in dementia evaluation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bright visual stimulation can never affect the study
FDG PET assesses cerebral glucose metabolism, which is used as a surrogate for functional activity
High serum glucose improves FDG uptake in abnormal brain regions
FDG PET is primarily a test for acute subarachnoid haemorrhage
The motor strip is typically preserved in degenerative dementias
options_after: Bright visual stimulation will not affect the study
FDG PET assesses cerebral glucose metabolism, which is used as a surrogate for functional activity
High serum glucose improves FDG uptake in abnormal brain regions
FDG PET is primarily a test for acute subarachnoid haemorrhage
The motor strip is typically preserved in degenerative dementias
updates.explanation: The source describes FDG PET as a metabolism study, with preserved motor strip as a useful pattern in degenerative dementia. External factors such as bright lights and high blood glucose can affect uptake patterns. FDG PET is not the primary test for acute subarachnoid haemorrhage.

updates.question_text: Regarding multi-infarct or vascular dementia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The motor strip is always preserved even if a stroke involves it
MRI may show cortical infarcts and lacunar infarcts
Generalised brain atrophy may be advanced for age
It is the most common cause of dementia according to the source
FDG PET may show scattered areas of decreased activity without a specific lobar predominance
options_after: The motor strip is characteristically preserved even if a stroke involves it
MRI may show cortical infarcts and lacunar infarcts
Generalised brain atrophy may be advanced for age
It is the most common cause of dementia according to the source
FDG PET may show scattered areas of decreased activity without a specific lobar predominance
updates.explanation: Vascular dementia is associated with cortical and lacunar infarcts, often with advanced atrophy for age and scattered FDG defects. Unlike degenerative dementias, the motor strip can be involved if the infarcts involve that region. Alzheimer disease is described as the most common dementia cause.

updates.question_text: Which FDG PET pattern is most characteristic of frontotemporal dementia in the source?
options_before: Low lateral occipital uptake with cingulate island sign
Scattered decreased activity without lobar predominance
Low posterior temporoparietal uptake
Globally increased uptake in the motor strip only
Low uptake in the frontal and temporal lobes
options_after: Low lateral occipital uptake with cingulate island sign
Scattered decreased activity without lobar predominance
Low posterior temporoparietal uptake
Globally increased uptake in the motor strip
Low uptake in the frontal and temporal lobes
updates.explanation: Frontotemporal dementia is associated with low frontal and temporal uptake, matching the structural pattern of predominant frontal atrophy with milder temporal volume loss. Posterior temporoparietal uptake is Alzheimer disease, lateral occipital reduction with cingulate island sign is Lewy body dementia, and scattered defects fit vascular dementia.

updates.question_text: Regarding Huntington disease, Leigh disease, MELAS and Hurler syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MELAS characteristically spares cortical grey matter and only affects deep white matter
Huntington disease causes caudate atrophy with enlargement and outward convexity of the frontal horns
Leigh disease may show T2/FLAIR bright lesions in brainstem, basal ganglia and cerebral peduncles
MELAS may produce cortical grey matter strokes in a non-vascular distribution, often occipital and parietal
Hurler syndrome can show enlarged perivascular spaces and inferior anterior beaking of L1
options_after: MELAS characteristically spares cortical grey matter and primarily affects deep white matter
Huntington disease causes caudate atrophy with enlargement and outward convexity of the frontal horns
Leigh disease may show T2/FLAIR bright lesions in brainstem, basal ganglia and cerebral peduncles
MELAS may produce cortical grey matter strokes in a non-vascular distribution, often occipital and parietal
Hurler syndrome can show enlarged perivascular spaces and inferior anterior beaking of L1
updates.explanation: The source links Huntington disease with caudate atrophy and characteristic frontal horn enlargement, Leigh disease with brainstem/basal ganglia/peduncle lesions, and MELAS with non-vascular cortical strokes. Hurler syndrome is associated with enlarged perivascular spaces and inferior anterior vertebral beaking. MELAS is not described as a purely deep white matter process.

updates.question_text: Regarding Parkinson disease imaging and nuclear medicine, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: DaT scan with ioflupane I-123 is discussed as a nuclear medicine study used in parkinsonian syndromes
Parkinson disease is straightforward to diagnose on routine CT or MRI alone
MIBG cardiac/mediastinal ratio is used to stage Alzheimer disease
Parkinson disease may show mild midbrain volume loss, but this is subtle
Parkinson disease always causes hot-cross-bun sign
options_after: DaT scan with ioflupane I-123 is discussed as a nuclear medicine study used in parkinsonian syndromes
Parkinson disease is straightforward to diagnose on routine CT or MRI alone
MIBG cardiac/mediastinal ratio is used to stage Alzheimer disease
Parkinson disease may show mild midbrain volume loss, but this is subtle
Parkinson disease characteristically causes hot-cross-bun sign
updates.explanation: The source discusses DaT imaging as relevant to parkinsonian syndromes and notes that routine CT/MRI alone is not a reliable way to diagnose Parkinson disease, although subtle midbrain volume loss may be described. MIBG is discussed for differentiating Parkinson disease from MSA, not Alzheimer staging. Hot-cross-bun sign belongs to MSA-C.

updates.question_text: Regarding lactate, lipid and NAA peaks on MR spectroscopy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lipid is a marker of necrotic tissue and membrane breakdown
NAA is normally absent from healthy brain spectroscopy
Lactate reflects anaerobic metabolism and is absent under normal conditions
Lactate and lipid peaks cannot be separated by changing echo time
NAA is primarily a marker of blood-brain barrier permeability
options_after: Lipid is a marker of necrotic tissue and membrane breakdown
NAA is normally absent from healthy brain spectroscopy
Lactate reflects anaerobic metabolism and is absent under normal conditions
Lactate and lipid peaks will not be separated by changing echo time
NAA is primarily a marker of blood-brain barrier permeability
updates.explanation: Lipid and lactate are discussed as markers of necrosis and anaerobic metabolism respectively. NAA is a neuronal marker and is usually tall in normal brain, but this question's selected pair emphasises the necrosis/metabolism distinction. NAA is not a marker of blood-brain barrier permeability.

updates.question_text: Regarding choline and myoinositol on MR spectroscopy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Myoinositol is decreased in Alzheimer disease according to the source
Choline rises with increased cell membrane turnover
Myoinositol is reduced in progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
Choline is absent from all tumours
Choline may be elevated in high-grade tumour, demyelination and inflammation
options_after: Myoinositol is decreased in Alzheimer disease according to the source
Choline rises with increased cell membrane turnover
Myoinositol is reduced in progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
Choline is absent from most tumours
Choline may be elevated in high-grade tumour, demyelination and inflammation
updates.explanation: Choline reflects membrane turnover and is elevated in processes with active membrane synthesis or injury such as high-grade tumour, demyelination and inflammation. Myoinositol is discussed in dementias and PML, but this question's selected pair focuses on choline. Choline is not absent from tumours.

updates.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes demyelinating disease from dysmyelinating disease in the source?
options_before: Demyelinating disease is always congenital and dysmyelinating disease is always traumatic
Demyelinating disease is defined by basal ganglia calcification
Demyelinating disease destroys normal myelin, while dysmyelinating disease disrupts normal formation and turnover of myelin
Dysmyelinating disease means a post-radiation vascular malformation
Demyelinating and dysmyelinating diseases are identical terms
options_after: Demyelinating disease is characteristically congenital and dysmyelinating disease is characteristically traumatic
Demyelinating disease is defined by basal ganglia calcification
Demyelinating disease destroys normal myelin, while dysmyelinating disease disrupts normal formation and turnover of myelin
Dysmyelinating disease means a post-radiation vascular malformation
Demyelinating and dysmyelinating diseases are closely comparable terms
updates.explanation: The source makes a direct distinction: demyelinating disease destroys previously normal myelin, while dysmyelinating disease disrupts formation or turnover of myelin. Multiple sclerosis is the demyelinating example, and metachromatic leukodystrophy is the dysmyelinating example.

updates.question_text: Which pattern best supports multiple sclerosis rather than small-vessel vascular disease?
options_before: Periventricular and juxtacortical ovoid lesions with calloso-septal interface involvement
Basal ganglia lacunes with no corpus callosum involvement
Calcified dentate nuclei and thalami
Low frontal FDG uptake only
Central pontine demyelination after rapid sodium correction
options_after: Periventricular and juxtacortical ovoid lesions with calloso-septal interface involvement
Basal ganglia lacunes without corpus callosum involvement
Calcified dentate nuclei and thalami
Low frontal FDG uptake
Central pontine demyelination after rapid sodium correction
updates.explanation: MS is favoured by periventricular and juxtacortical ovoid lesions, especially with calloso-septal interface involvement. Basal ganglia lacunes suggest vascular disease, dentate/thalamic calcification suggests Fahr-type calcinosis, low frontal FDG uptake suggests frontotemporal dementia, and central pontine demyelination fits osmotic demyelination.

updates.question_text: Which MR spectroscopy pattern best supports a high-grade glial tumour in the source?
options_before: Normal ascending choline-creatine-NAA peaks with no abnormal metabolites
Super-high NAA peak as the dominant abnormality suggesting Canavan disease
Isolated alanine peak with dural tail as the only abnormality
Reversed Hunter's angle with reduced NAA and increased choline/lactate-lipid abnormality
Absent choline in a necrotic mass
options_after: Normal ascending choline-creatine-NAA peaks without abnormal metabolites
Super-high NAA peak as the dominant abnormality suggesting Canavan disease
Isolated alanine peak with dural tail as the principal abnormality
Reversed Hunter's angle with reduced NAA and increased choline/lactate-lipid abnormality
Absent choline in a necrotic mass
updates.explanation: A high-grade glial tumour is supported by loss of normal Hunter's angle, reduced NAA from neuronal destruction, increased choline from turnover, and lactate/lipid from anaerobic metabolism or necrosis. Canavan disease is associated with very high NAA, alanine favours meningioma, and choline is not absent in high-grade tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding enhancement and blood-brain barrier logic, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Extra-axial lesions enhance because they are outside the blood-brain barrier
Low-grade tumours always enhance more than high-grade tumours
High-grade tumours and infections can enhance after disrupting the blood-brain barrier
Low-grade ganglioglioma and pilocytic astrocytoma are named exceptions that may enhance
Enhancement proves a lesion is intraventricular
options_after: Extra-axial lesions enhance because they are outside the blood-brain barrier
Low-grade tumours characteristically enhance more than high-grade tumours
High-grade tumours and infections can enhance after disrupting the blood-brain barrier
Low-grade ganglioglioma and pilocytic astrocytoma are named exceptions that may enhance
Enhancement proves a lesion is intraventricular
updates.explanation: Enhancement occurs when a lesion is outside the blood-brain barrier or has disrupted it. The source gives meningioma as an extra-axial example and high-grade tumour/infection as barrier-disrupting examples. Ganglioglioma and pilocytic astrocytoma are low-grade exceptions that can enhance.

updates.question_text: Regarding signs of extra-axial location, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A CSF cleft between mass and cortex is a reliable sign
Interposed/displaced subarachnoid vessels can support extra-axial origin
Extra-axial masses always narrow rather than widen the CSF space
Broad dural base or dural tail favours extra-axial location
Bony reaction may support extra-axial location
options_after: A CSF cleft between mass and cortex is a reliable sign
Interposed/displaced subarachnoid vessels can support extra-axial origin
Extra-axial masses characteristically narrow rather than widen the CSF space
Broad dural base or dural tail favours extra-axial location
Bony reaction may support extra-axial location
updates.explanation: The source lists CSF cleft, displaced subarachnoid vessels, cortical grey matter between mass and white matter, expanded subarachnoid spaces, dural base/tail and bony reaction as extra-axial signs. Extra-axial masses tend to widen rather than obliterate the CSF space.

updates.question_text: Regarding multiple intracranial masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Multiple masses always exclude primary CNS tumours
Metastases and infection are key adult differentials for multiple masses
Diffusion restriction helps separate abscess/infection from metastases
A solitary adult mass is always more likely a primary CNS neoplasm than metastasis
Metastases most often occur at the grey-white junction
options_after: Multiple masses characteristically exclude primary CNS tumours
Metastases and infection are key adult differentials for multiple masses
Diffusion restriction helps separate abscess/infection from metastases
A solitary adult mass is characteristically more likely a primary CNS neoplasm than metastasis
Metastases most often occur at the grey-white junction
updates.explanation: Multiple masses raise metastases and infection first, and diffusion is a key discriminator when infection is in the differential. Metastases favour the supratentorial grey-white junction because of flow and vessel calibre change. Primary CNS tumours can be multifocal, and a solitary adult mass can still be metastatic.

updates.question_text: Regarding brain metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Metastases may be solitary in approximately half of cases according to the source
Melanoma, renal, choriocarcinoma/carcinoid and thyroid are listed as bleeding metastases
Brain metastases are always infratentorial in adults
Metastases often have more surrounding oedema than primary tumours of similar size
In an adult with a suspicious intra-axial mass, searching for a systemic primary is a common next step
options_after: Metastases may be solitary in approximately half of cases according to the source
Melanoma, renal, choriocarcinoma/carcinoid and thyroid are listed as bleeding metastases
Brain metastases are characteristically infratentorial in adults
Metastases often have more surrounding oedema than primary tumours of similar size
In an adult with a suspicious intra-axial mass, searching for a systemic primary is a common next step
updates.explanation: The source stresses that metastases are not always multiple and may be solitary. The MRCT mnemonic is used for haemorrhagic metastases, and metastases often have disproportionate oedema. Because metastasis is the common adult intra-axial mass consideration, work-up for a primary is a standard next-step concept.

updates.question_text: Regarding cortically based tumours, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All cortically based tumours are intraventricular choroid plexus lesions
Cortically based tumours always cause massive vasogenic oedema
PXA, DNET, oligodendroglioma and ganglioglioma form the P-DOG group in the source
Cortical tumour location excludes seizure presentation
Small cortical metastases may have little oedema and can be occult without contrast
options_after: Most cortically based tumours are intraventricular choroid plexus lesions
Cortically based tumours characteristically cause massive vasogenic oedema
PXA, DNET, oligodendroglioma and ganglioglioma form the P-DOG group in the source
Cortical tumour location excludes seizure presentation
Small cortical metastases may have little oedema and can be occult without contrast
updates.explanation: The source groups PXA, DNET, oligodendroglioma and ganglioglioma as P-DOG cortical tumours. It also notes that cortical tumours or cortical metastases may have little oedema, making small cortical metastases easy to miss without contrast. Cortical location does not imply choroid plexus origin or exclude seizures.

updates.question_text: Regarding pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is superficial and always supratentorial in the source
It is a neonatal posterior fossa tumour by definition
It usually involves the temporal lobe
It can be a cyst-with-nodule tumour and may invade leptomeninges
It never enhances
options_after: It is superficial and always supratentorial in the source
It is a neonatal posterior fossa tumour by definition
It usually involves the temporal lobe
It can be a cyst-with-nodule tumour and may invade leptomeninges
It will not enhance
updates.explanation: PXA is described as a superficial supratentorial tumour, often temporal, and often in the cyst-with-nodule category. Leptomeningeal invasion is a listed feature. A neonatal posterior fossa definition and lack of enhancement are not the source pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding oligodendroglioma and ganglioglioma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Oligodendroglioma commonly calcifies
Oligodendroglioma commonly involves the frontal lobe and expands the cortex
Ganglioglioma is always a non-enhancing bubbly lesion with a FLAIR rim
Oligodendroglioma is associated with 1p/19q deletion in the source
Ganglioglioma classically can be mixed cystic and solid with focal calcification in a young seizure patient
options_after: Oligodendroglioma commonly calcifies
Oligodendroglioma commonly involves the frontal lobe and expands the cortex
Ganglioglioma is characteristically a non-enhancing bubbly lesion with a FLAIR rim
Oligodendroglioma is associated with 1p/19q deletion in the source
Ganglioglioma classically can be mixed cystic and solid with focal calcification in a young seizure patient
updates.explanation: Oligodendroglioma is the cortical tumour that commonly calcifies, often frontal, and is linked to cortical expansion and 1p/19q. Ganglioglioma can present in a young patient with seizures as a temporal mixed cystic/solid lesion with focal calcification. The bubbly lesion with FLAIR rim is more characteristic of DNET.

updates.question_text: Regarding SEGA and subependymal nodules in tuberous sclerosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: An enhancing partially calcified lesion at the foramen of Monro smaller than 2 mm favours SEGA over SEN
SEGA can calcify but SEN never calcifies
SEGA arises near the foramen of Monro and can cause hydrocephalus
SEN is expected to grow progressively while SEGA remains stable
SEGA enhances homogeneously
options_after: An enhancing partially calcified lesion at the foramen of Monro smaller than 2 mm favours SEGA over SEN
SEGA can calcify but SEN will not calcify
SEGA arises near the foramen of Monro and can cause hydrocephalus
SEN is expected to grow progressively while SEGA remains stable
SEGA enhances homogeneously
updates.explanation: SEGA is a tuberous-sclerosis-associated paediatric tumour near the foramen of Monro that enhances and can obstruct CSF. A lesion larger than 5 mm, enhancement and growth favour SEGA over SEN. Both SEN and SEGA can calcify, while SENs tend to remain stable.

updates.question_text: Regarding colloid cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are found almost exclusively in the anterior third ventricle behind the foramen of Monro
They usually arise in the cerebellopontine angle and widen the internal auditory canal
They are always T1 dark and T2 bright regardless of contents
They can be hyperdense on CT
They can cause acute hydrocephalus with transependymal oedema
options_after: They are found almost exclusively in the anterior third ventricle behind the foramen of Monro
They usually arise in the cerebellopontine angle and widen the internal auditory canal
They are characteristically T1 dark and T2 bright despite variation in contents
They can be hyperdense on CT
They can cause acute hydrocephalus with transependymal oedema
updates.explanation: Colloid cyst is the round anterior third ventricular lesion behind the foramen of Monro, often dense on CT and capable of causing acute obstructive hydrocephalus with transependymal oedema. Signal depends on contents; cholesterol-rich lesions may be T1 bright and T2 dark. CPA/IAC widening is a vestibular schwannoma pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding cerebellopontine angle masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Vestibular schwannoma is the commonest CPA mass
Colloid cyst is the third common CPA mass in the source
Meningioma is the second most common CPA mass in the source
CPA masses are always paediatric posterior fossa tumours
Colloid cyst is the commonest CPA mass
options_after: Vestibular schwannoma is the commonest CPA mass
Colloid cyst is the third common CPA mass in the source
Meningioma is the second most common CPA mass in the source
CPA masses are characteristically paediatric posterior fossa tumours
Colloid cyst is the commonest CPA mass
updates.explanation: The source gives the CPA ranking as vestibular schwannoma first and meningioma second, with epidermoid third. Colloid cyst is an anterior third ventricular lesion rather than a CPA mass.

updates.question_text: Regarding vestibular schwannoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It usually calcifies more often than meningioma
Bilateral vestibular schwannomas should suggest NF2
It never involves the internal auditory canal
It may widen the porus acousticus/internal auditory canal with an ice-cream-cone or trumpet appearance
It enhances strongly but less homogeneously than meningioma in the source comparison
options_after: It usually calcifies more often than meningioma
Bilateral vestibular schwannomas should suggest NF2
It will not involve the internal auditory canal
It may widen the porus acousticus/internal auditory canal with an ice-cream-cone or trumpet appearance
It enhances strongly but less homogeneously than meningioma in the source comparison
updates.explanation: Vestibular schwannoma accounts for most CPA masses and bilateral lesions point to NF2. It can expand the internal auditory canal and has the classic ice-cream-cone/trumpet morphology. Compared with meningioma it tends to enhance less homogeneously and invades the IAC more often.

updates.question_text: Regarding CPA meningioma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It can calcify
It usually invades the internal auditory canal and produces an ice-cream-cone morphology
A dural tail strongly favours meningioma when present
Head radiation is unrelated to meningioma risk in the source
It follows CSF on all sequences and restricts diffusion like an epidermoid
options_after: It can calcify
It usually invades the internal auditory canal and produces an ice-cream-cone morphology
A dural tail strongly favours meningioma when present
Head radiation is unrelated to meningioma risk in the source
It follows CSF on most sequences and restricts diffusion like an epidermoid
updates.explanation: CPA meningioma is the second common CPA mass, can calcify, and may have a dural tail. Internal auditory canal invasion and ice-cream-cone morphology favour vestibular schwannoma. Head radiation is a recognised risk factor for meningioma, while CSF-like signal with diffusion restriction describes epidermoid.

updates.question_text: In an adult with a solitary intra-axial brain mass where metastasis is a major consideration, what next-step concept is emphasised by the source?
options_before: Assume it is always a benign arachnoid cyst
Avoid contrast because cortical metastases are always obvious
Diagnose NF2 before considering metastasis
Search for a systemic primary malignancy
Proceed directly to whole-spine imaging for every solitary adult mass
options_after: Assume it is characteristically a benign arachnoid cyst
Avoid contrast because cortical metastases are characteristically obvious
Diagnose NF2 before considering metastasis
Search for a systemic primary malignancy
Proceed directly to whole-spine imaging for most solitary adult masses
updates.explanation: Because metastasis is the major adult intra-axial mass consideration and may be solitary, the source emphasises looking for a systemic primary such as lung, breast or colon. NF2, arachnoid cyst and routine whole-spine staging are not the general next-step rule for this scenario.

updates.question_text: Regarding epidermoid versus arachnoid cyst, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Arachnoid cyst contains fat droplets after rupture
Epidermoid restricts diffusion
Epidermoid is always a calcified dural-based mass
Arachnoid cyst enhances homogeneously
Arachnoid cyst does not restrict diffusion
options_after: Arachnoid cyst contains fat droplets after rupture
Epidermoid restricts diffusion
Epidermoid is characteristically a calcified dural-based mass
Arachnoid cyst enhances homogeneously
Arachnoid cyst does not restrict diffusion
updates.explanation: The key discriminator is diffusion: epidermoid restricts and arachnoid cyst does not. Arachnoid cyst is a benign CSF-containing subarachnoid-space lesion. Fat droplets after rupture belong to dermoid, while homogeneous dural enhancement points more toward meningioma.

updates.question_text: Regarding diffuse pontine glioma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is seen in children, classically age 3-10 in the source
Biopsy is always required because imaging is non-specific
The pons is the most common location
It is T2 bright with subtle or no enhancement and flattens the fourth ventricle
It is a benign choroid plexus tumour of the trigone
options_after: It is seen in children, classically age 3-10 in the source
Biopsy is characteristically required because imaging is non-specific
The pons is the most common location
It is T2 bright with subtle or no enhancement and flattens the fourth ventricle
It is a benign choroid plexus tumour of the trigone
updates.explanation: Diffuse pontine glioma is described in children aged 3-10, centred on the pons, with T2 hyperintensity, subtle or absent enhancement and fourth ventricular flattening. The imaging pattern is presented as sufficiently classic that biopsy is not needed. A trigonal choroid plexus tumour is a different paediatric ventricular differential.

updates.question_text: Regarding astrocytoma grade and enhancement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: T2/FLAIR mismatch is described as the defining feature of WHO grade 1 pilocytic astrocytoma
Diffuse grade 2 astrocytoma typically does not enhance
Pilocytic astrocytoma never enhances because it is WHO grade 1
Grade 3 anaplastic astrocytoma may enhance mildly
Grade 4 GBM may show ring or heterogeneous enhancement
options_after: T2/FLAIR mismatch is described as the defining feature of WHO grade 1 pilocytic astrocytoma
Diffuse grade 2 astrocytoma typically does not enhance
Pilocytic astrocytoma will not enhance because it is WHO grade 1
Grade 3 anaplastic astrocytoma may enhance mildly
Grade 4 GBM may show ring or heterogeneous enhancement
updates.explanation: The source presents increasing enhancement with grade: grade 2 usually none, grade 3 mild, and grade 4 GBM ring or heterogeneous enhancement. T2/FLAIR mismatch is discussed for grade 2 and 3 astrocytoma, but this question's selected set focuses on grade-enhancement behaviour. Pilocytic astrocytoma is a low-grade exception that may enhance.

updates.question_text: Regarding gliomatosis cerebri and metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Metastases are always multiple and never solitary
Gliomatosis cerebri involves at least three lobes and is often bilateral
Gliomatosis cerebri typically appears as a calcified anterior third ventricular cyst
Gliomatosis cerebri may show extensive T2 hyperintensity with little mass effect
Preservation of underlying architecture is a buzzword for gliomatosis cerebri
options_after: Metastases characteristically present as multiple rather than solitary lesions
Gliomatosis cerebri involves at least three lobes and is often bilateral
Gliomatosis cerebri typically appears as a calcified anterior third ventricular cyst
Gliomatosis cerebri may show extensive T2 hyperintensity with little mass effect
Preservation of underlying architecture is a buzzword for gliomatosis cerebri
updates.explanation: Gliomatosis cerebri is a diffuse infiltrating glioma involving at least three lobes, often bilateral, with extensive T2 signal but relatively little mass effect and preservation of architecture. Metastases may be solitary, and a calcified anterior third ventricular cyst is a colloid cyst pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding primary CNS lymphoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is seen in end-stage AIDS and post-transplant patients
It is thallium negative on SPECT in the source's toxoplasmosis comparison
It is classically an intensely enhancing homogeneous solid periventricular mass
Restricted diffusion is a key imaging clue
It never enhances
options_after: It is seen in end-stage AIDS and post-transplant patients
It is thallium negative on SPECT in the source's toxoplasmosis comparison
It is classically an intensely enhancing homogeneous solid periventricular mass
Restricted diffusion is a key imaging clue
It will not enhance
updates.explanation: Primary CNS lymphoma is linked to immunosuppression and EBV, and the classic imaging pattern is homogeneous enhancement in a periventricular mass with restricted diffusion. The source also notes thallium positivity as a test distinction from toxoplasmosis. Lack of enhancement would argue against the classic lymphoma pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding desmoplastic infantile ganglioglioma/astrocytoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a WHO grade 4 posterior fossa tumour with poor prognosis by definition
It usually presents before the first birthday
It always arises in the pineal gland
It is the same entity as AT/RT
It is a large cystic supratentorial tumour involving superficial cortex and leptomeninges
options_after: It is a WHO grade 4 posterior fossa tumour with poor prognosis by definition
It usually presents before the first birthday
It characteristically arises in the pineal gland
It is the same entity as AT/RT
It is a large cystic supratentorial tumour involving superficial cortex and leptomeninges
updates.explanation: DIG is described as a large cystic WHO grade 1 tumour, usually before the first birthday, involving superficial supratentorial cortex and leptomeninges. It differs from AT/RT, which is the aggressive WHO grade 4 posterior fossa paediatric tumour in the adjacent discussion.

updates.question_text: Regarding dural-based masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Renal cell carcinoma is described as the most common dural metastasis source
Meningioma commonly enhances homogeneously and may cause hyperostosis
Haemangiopericytoma is defined by no skull invasion and no vascularity
Dural metastases always arise in the lateral ventricle trigone
Haemangiopericytoma can mimic aggressive meningioma but tends not to calcify or cause hyperostosis
options_after: Renal cell carcinoma is described as the most common dural metastasis source
Meningioma commonly enhances homogeneously and may cause hyperostosis
Haemangiopericytoma is characterised by absent skull invasion and low vascularity
Dural metastases characteristically arise in the lateral ventricle trigone
Haemangiopericytoma can mimic aggressive meningioma but tends not to calcify or cause hyperostosis
updates.explanation: Meningioma is a homogeneously enhancing dural mass and may cause hyperostosis. Haemangiopericytoma can mimic meningioma but is more aggressive, lacks typical calcification/hyperostosis and can invade skull. Breast cancer is a dural metastasis source in the text, but this question's selected pair focuses on differentiating meningioma from haemangiopericytoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding pineal region tumours, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Germinoma is the most common of the main pineal region tumours in the source
All pineal region tumours are exclusively adult lesions
Pineal tumours cannot present with vertical gaze palsy
Pineoblastoma is invasive and associated with retinoblastoma/trilateral disease
Pineocytoma is well circumscribed and non-invasive
options_after: Germinoma is the most common of the main pineal region tumours in the source
Most pineal region tumours are predominantly adult lesions
Pineal tumours will not present with vertical gaze palsy
Pineoblastoma is invasive and associated with retinoblastoma/trilateral disease
Pineocytoma is well circumscribed and non-invasive
updates.explanation: The source lists germinoma as the most common pineal-region tumour, pineoblastoma as invasive and associated with retinoblastoma, and pineocytoma as well circumscribed/non-invasive. Pineal region lesions can present with vertical gaze palsy due to dorsal midbrain involvement.

updates.question_text: Regarding pineal calcification patterns and cysts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pineal cysts are always aggressive enhancing solid tumours
Germinoma can engulf pineal calcification
Pineal cysts never calcify
Calcification pattern cannot help at all in pineal lesion characterisation
Pineoblastoma and pineocytoma can expand pineal calcification
options_after: Pineal cysts are characteristically aggressive enhancing solid tumours
Germinoma can engulf pineal calcification
Pineal cysts will not calcify
Calcification pattern will not help at most in pineal lesion characterisation
Pineoblastoma and pineocytoma can expand pineal calcification
updates.explanation: The source contrasts engulfed calcification for germinoma with expanded calcification for pineoblastoma/pineocytoma. Pineal cysts are usually incidental cystic lesions and may have thin enhancement; calcification can occur in a minority.

updates.question_text: Regarding T1-bright intracranial lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fat-containing lesions such as dermoid and lipoma can be T1 bright
Melanin in melanoma can be T1 bright
Blood products in haemorrhagic metastasis or pituitary apoplexy can be T1 bright
Cholesterol-rich colloid cyst can be T1 bright
All T1-bright tumours must be low-grade gliomas
options_after: Fat-containing lesions such as dermoid and lipoma can be T1 bright
Melanin in melanoma can be T1 bright
Blood products in haemorrhagic metastasis or pituitary apoplexy can be T1 bright
Cholesterol-rich colloid cyst can be T1 bright
Most T1-bright tumours must be low-grade gliomas
updates.explanation: The source groups T1-bright causes as fat, melanin, blood and cholesterol: dermoid/lipoma, melanoma, haemorrhagic metastasis or pituitary apoplexy, and cholesterol-rich colloid cyst. Low-grade glioma is not the unifying diagnosis for T1-bright lesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRS distinction between GBM and metastasis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: GBM may be underestimated if only the enhancing solid tumour is considered
Metastatic vasogenic oedema always contains infiltrative tumour on spectroscopy
MRS should only sample cystic or necrotic parts of the mass
Elevated choline in surrounding T2 signal supports infiltrating glioma rather than metastasis
GBM never has abnormality outside the enhancing component
options_after: GBM may be underestimated if only the enhancing solid tumour is considered
Metastatic vasogenic oedema characteristically contains infiltrative tumour on spectroscopy
MRS should primarily sample cystic or necrotic parts of the mass
Elevated choline in surrounding T2 signal supports infiltrating glioma rather than metastasis
GBM is confined to the enhancing component on imaging
updates.explanation: The source explains that GBM can infiltrate surrounding T2 hyperintensity beyond the enhancing solid tumour. Elevated choline in that surrounding T2 signal supports infiltrating glioma rather than pure metastatic vasogenic oedema. Sampling necrosis or cystic components is discouraged.

updates.question_text: For brain tumour MR spectroscopy, what voxel-selection principle is emphasised in the source?
options_before: Always place the voxel entirely in the lateral ventricle
Choose only the densest calcified portion on CT
Choose enhancing tumour and avoid cystic parts, calcification, blood and frank necrosis
Avoid enhancing tumour because it is never diagnostic
Use only the scalp as the reference voxel
options_after: Characteristically place the voxel predominantly in the lateral ventricle
Choose primarily the densest calcified portion on CT
Choose enhancing tumour and avoid cystic parts, calcification, blood and frank necrosis
Avoid enhancing tumour because it is not diagnostic
Use primarily the scalp as the reference voxel
updates.explanation: The source explicitly warns that voxel selection matters: choose enhancing tumour and avoid cystic regions, calcification, blood or frank necrosis. Sampling non-representative tissue can make spectroscopy misleading.

updates.question_text: Regarding toxoplasmosis versus lymphoma in AIDS, which of the following statements are correct?

Toxoplasmosis always restricts diffusion like a typical bacterial abscess
Toxoplasmosis is thallium cold and PET cold in the source comparison
Lymphoma is thallium hot and PET hot in the source comparison
options_after: Toxoplasmosis is the most common opportunistic infection in AIDS
Toxoplasmosis can show ring-enhancing T1-dark/T2-bright lesions with lots of oedema
Toxoplasmosis characteristically restricts diffusion like a typical bacterial abscess
Toxoplasmosis is thallium cold and PET cold in the source comparison
Lymphoma is thallium hot and PET hot in the source comparison
updates.explanation: The source contrasts toxoplasmosis and lymphoma using metabolism/perfusion and diffusion clues. Toxoplasmosis is common in AIDS, ring enhancing with oedema, and thallium/PET cold, while lymphoma is thallium/PET hot. Toxoplasmosis does not reliably restrict diffusion despite being infectious.

updates.question_text: Regarding TB meningitis and its mimic, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: TB meningitis has a predilection for basilar meningeal enhancement

TB meningitis characteristically presents as an isolated IAC lipoma
Obstructive hydrocephalus and vasculitic infarcts are recognised complications
TB meningitis excludes dystrophic calcification

Sarcoid will not mimic the basal meningeal enhancement pattern
TB meningitis characteristically presents as an isolated IAC lipoma
Obstructive hydrocephalus and vasculitic infarcts are recognised complications
TB meningitis excludes dystrophic calcification
updates.explanation: TB meningitis is classically basilar, with hydrocephalus and vasculitic infarction as complications. Sarcoid can look very similar, so the statement that it cannot mimic the pattern is false. IAC lipoma and fat-saturation behaviour are unrelated to TB meningitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding HSV encephalitis, limbic encephalitis and West Nile, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Negative HSV testing excludes limbic encephalitis and no malignancy screening is needed
Adult HSV-1 preferentially involves the limbic/medial temporal region

Adult HSV-1 preferentially involves the limbic/medial temporal region
Diffusion is described as the earliest and more sensitive imaging sign than T2 in HSV
West Nile classically spares the basal ganglia and thalami
HSV tends to spare the basal ganglia, helping distinguish it from MCA infarct
updates.explanation: Adult HSV-1 classically involves swollen T2-bright medial temporal lobes, with restricted diffusion as an early sensitive sign and basal ganglia sparing. Limbic encephalitis is an important mimic associated with malignancy, but this question's selected set focuses on HSV imaging. West Nile can involve basal ganglia and thalami.

updates.question_text: Which CJD subtype is described as accounting for approximately 80-90% of cases?
options_before: Variant CJD
Familial CJD
Sporadic CJD
Iatrogenic CJD only
Congenital CJD
options_after: Variant CJD
Familial CJD
Sporadic CJD
Iatrogenic CJD
Congenital CJD
updates.explanation: The source lists sporadic CJD as the commonest subtype, accounting for around 80-90% of cases. Variant and familial forms are less common. Imaging clues include cortical gyriform diffusion restriction and thalamic signs in variant disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding CJD imaging signs, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cortical gyriform restricted diffusion is a sensitive early sign
Basal ganglia may be involved
CJD is defined by a smooth ring-enhancing abscess capsule
Pulvinar and hockey-stick thalamic signs are described in variant CJD
CJD always presents as a calcified intraventricular mass

Basal ganglia may be involved
CJD is defined by a smooth ring-enhancing abscess capsule
Pulvinar and hockey-stick thalamic signs are described in variant CJD
CJD characteristically presents as a calcified intraventricular mass
updates.explanation: The source emphasises diffusion as a sensitive sign, especially cortical gyriform restriction, and notes basal ganglia involvement. Pulvinar and hockey-stick signs are thalamic signs described in variant CJD. Ring-enhancing abscess and calcified intraventricular mass belong to other differentials.

updates.question_text: Regarding neurocysticercosis, which of the following statements are correct?

Calcified/involution stage lacks calcification on CT and has no blooming on SWI/T2*
The commonest location is the pituitary gland

The vesicular stage is cyst plus scolex without enhancement

Calcified/involution stage lacks calcification on CT and lacks blooming on SWI/T2*
The commonest location is the pituitary gland
Basal cistern involvement carries the worst outcome in the source
The vesicular stage is cyst plus scolex without enhancement
updates.explanation: Neurocysticercosis is due to pork tapeworm infection, and basal cistern involvement has the worst outcome. The vesicular stage is a cyst with scolex and no enhancement. The calcified stage shows calcification and blooming, but this question's selected set focuses on cause, outcome location and early-stage appearance.

updates.question_text: Regarding leptomeningeal and pachymeningeal enhancement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fungal and carcinomatous meningitis are always thinner and smoother than bacterial meningitis
Leptomeningeal enhancement fills subarachnoid spaces and extends into sulci and cisterns
Pachymeningeal enhancement is synonymous with intraventricular abscess rupture
Leptomeningeal enhancement never occurs in bacterial meningitis
Pachymeningeal enhancement is dural and does not extend into the sulci
options_after: Fungal and carcinomatous meningitis are characteristically thinner and smoother than bacterial meningitis
Leptomeningeal enhancement fills subarachnoid spaces and extends into sulci and cisterns
Pachymeningeal enhancement is synonymous with intraventricular abscess rupture
Leptomeningeal enhancement will not occur in bacterial meningitis
Pachymeningeal enhancement is dural and does not extend into the sulci
updates.explanation: Leptomeningeal enhancement involves the pia-arachnoid/subarachnoid spaces and extends into sulci and cisterns. Pachymeningeal enhancement is dural and does not extend into the sulci. Thick/lumpy carcinomatous or fungal patterns are discussed, but this question's selected pair focuses on the core anatomical distinction.

updates.question_text: Regarding cerebral abscess, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Abscess usually appears as a hyperdense solid homogeneous tumour on CT
Haematogenous spread is the most common route in the source
Abscess always lacks surrounding vasogenic oedema
Right-to-left shunts and pulmonary AVMs are important associations to consider
Typical bacterial abscess restricts diffusion
options_after: Abscess usually appears as a hyperdense solid homogeneous tumour on CT
Haematogenous spread is the most common route in the source
Abscess characteristically lacks surrounding vasogenic oedema
Right-to-left shunts and pulmonary AVMs are important associations to consider
Typical bacterial abscess restricts diffusion
updates.explanation: Cerebral abscess may arise from several infections but haematogenous spread is emphasised, with right-to-left shunts and pulmonary AVMs as key associations. Typical bacterial abscess restricts diffusion. Abscess tends to have low-density centre and vasogenic oedema rather than a homogeneous solid hyperdense tumour pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding abscess versus tumour/metastasis ring-enhancement clues, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Smooth ring margin favours abscess but does not exclude metastasis

Abscesses are often smaller, commonly less than 10 mm in the source
Abscess ring may be thicker on the grey-matter/oxygen side and thinner toward the ventricle
Ring enhancement always proves toxoplasmosis

Irregular or shaggy inner lip may suggest necrosis
Abscesses are often smaller, commonly less than 10 mm in the source
Abscess ring may be thicker on the grey-matter/oxygen side and thinner toward the ventricle
Ring enhancement characteristically proves toxoplasmosis
updates.explanation: Smooth rings and small size favour abscess, and the ring may be thicker toward the oxygenated grey matter side. A shaggy inner lip is discussed as necrosis, but this selected set focuses on abscess-versus-metastasis clues. Ring enhancement remains a broad pattern and does not prove toxoplasmosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding cerebritis and ventriculitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ventriculitis cannot show ventricular enhancement or intraventricular fluid-fluid levels
Cerebritis is an early intra-axial infection that can progress to abscess
Ventriculitis excludes hydrocephalus if septa form
Intraventricular extension of abscess is a reassuring benign finding
Cerebritis may show vasogenic oedema without a well-defined central enhancing lesion

Cerebritis is an early intra-axial infection that can progress to abscess
Ventriculitis excludes hydrocephalus if septa form
Intraventricular extension of abscess is a reassuring benign finding
Cerebritis may show vasogenic oedema without a well-defined central enhancing lesion
updates.explanation: Cerebritis is the early parenchymal infection stage, often with oedema before a mature ring-enhancing abscess develops. Ventriculitis can enhance and show fluid-fluid levels, but this question's selected pair focuses on cerebritis. Septations can produce obstructive hydrocephalus, and intraventricular abscess rupture is ominous.

updates.question_text: Regarding enhancement patterns in stroke, tumour, abscess and MS plaque, which of the following statements are correct?

Abscess classically has a ring-enhancement pattern

Low-grade tumours always enhance intensely

Subacute stroke will not produce gyriform cortical ribbon enhancement
Abscess classically has a ring-enhancement pattern
MS plaque classically has incomplete ring enhancement
Low-grade tumours characteristically enhance intensely
updates.explanation: The source's enhancement strategy maps high-grade tumour to homogeneous/heterogeneous enhancement, abscess to ring, MS to incomplete ring, and subacute stroke to gyriform cortical ribbon enhancement. This selected set focuses on the tumour/abscess/MS triad; low-grade tumours usually do not enhance apart from named exceptions.

updates.question_text: Regarding traumatic parenchymal contusion and diffuse axonal injury, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Contusions commonly occur in anterior temporal and inferior frontal lobes

Diffuse axonal injury favourite sites include posterior corpus callosum and grey-white junction in frontal/temporal lobes
DAI grading progresses from grey-white interface to corpus callosum to brainstem
DAI is defined by calcified basal ganglia and thalamic lesions

Initial CT in DAI is characteristically grossly abnormal
Diffuse axonal injury favourite sites include posterior corpus callosum and grey-white junction in frontal/temporal lobes
DAI grading progresses from grey-white interface to corpus callosum to brainstem
DAI is defined by calcified basal ganglia and thalamic lesions
updates.explanation: Traumatic contusions occur where the brain contacts rough skull base, especially anterior temporal and inferior frontal regions. DAI involves shear injury with favourite sites at grey-white junction and posterior corpus callosum, and grading extends to brainstem. CT can be normal early, but this selected set focuses on location and grading.

updates.question_text: On CT, what density is expected for acute blood between approximately 1 hour and 3 days?
options_before: Hypodense
