options_after: Congenital hepatic fibrosis is always present in ARPKD in the source
In ARPKD, severe kidney cystic disease and severe liver fibrosis characteristically progress together
Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is autosomal recessive in the source
Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is characterised by multiple liver and lung AVMs
Lung AVMs in hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia can predispose to brain abscess
updates.explanation: The source states that congenital hepatic fibrosis is always present in ARPKD and that liver severity is inversely related to the renal cystic disease burden. Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is described as autosomal dominant with multiple AVMs in the liver and lungs, massively dilated hepatic artery, cirrhosis, and lung AVMs predisposing to brain abscess.

updates.question_text: Regarding the source's top paediatric GI reminders, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Biliary atresia is treated primarily by pyeloplasty
Malrotation places the duodenum left of the midline
Malrotation increases risk of midgut volvulus and internal hernia
VACTERL is diagnosed only when all listed anomalies are present
Biliary atresia scintigraphy shows no tracer excretion into bowel by 24 hours
options_after: Biliary atresia is treated primarily by pyeloplasty
Malrotation places the duodenum left of the midline
Malrotation increases risk of midgut volvulus and internal hernia
VACTERL is diagnosed primarily when most listed anomalies are present
Biliary atresia scintigraphy shows no tracer excretion into bowel by 24 hours
updates.explanation: The top-things summary reiterates that malrotation has the duodenum to the right of midline and increases risk of midgut volvulus and internal hernia. Biliary atresia is treated with Kasai procedure, not pyeloplasty, and scintigraphy shows no bowel excretion by 24 hours. VACTERL requires three or more component anomalies, not all of them.

updates.question_text: In women with unilateral renal agenesis, which association is emphasised in the source?
options_before: Associated genital tract anomalies such as unicornuate uterus or rudimentary horn
Bilateral pulmonary sling
Absent vas deferens on the contralateral side only
Aortic coarctation as the defining association
Pancreatic lipomatous pseudohypertrophy
options_after: Associated genital tract anomalies such as unicornuate uterus or rudimentary horn
Bilateral pulmonary sling
Absent vas deferens on the contralateral side
Aortic coarctation as the defining association
Pancreatic lipomatous pseudohypertrophy
updates.explanation: The source states that most women with unilateral renal agenesis have associated genital anomalies, usually unicornuate uterus or rudimentary horn. In men, ipsilateral absence of epididymis and vas deferens plus ipsilateral seminal vesicle cyst are described. Pulmonary sling, coarctation, and pancreatic lipomatous pseudohypertrophy belong to other topics.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal agenesis and Potter sequence, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bilateral renal agenesis is linked to Potter sequence
Potter sequence involves absent kidneys, absent urine, oligohydramnios, and pulmonary hypoplasia
The lying-down adrenal sign helps distinguish congenital absence from surgical absence
Unilateral renal agenesis has no reproductive associations in men
Men may have ipsilateral absence of epididymis and vas deferens with ipsilateral seminal vesicle cyst
options_after: Bilateral renal agenesis is linked to Potter sequence
Potter sequence involves absent kidneys, absent urine, oligohydramnios, and pulmonary hypoplasia
The lying-down adrenal sign helps distinguish congenital absence from surgical absence
Unilateral renal agenesis lacks reproductive associations in men
Men may have ipsilateral absence of epididymis and vas deferens with ipsilateral seminal vesicle cyst
updates.explanation: Bilateral renal agenesis is Potter-sequence related: no kidneys, no urine, oligohydramnios, and pulmonary hypoplasia. The lying-down or pancake adrenal sign reflects an adrenal not moulded by an adjacent kidney and helps separate congenital from surgical absence. In men, unilateral renal agenesis is associated with ipsilateral absence of the epididymis and vas deferens plus ipsilateral seminal vesicle cyst.

updates.question_text: Regarding ARPKD and neonatal renal vascular thrombosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: ARPKD kidneys are smoothly enlarged and diffusely echogenic with loss of corticomedullary differentiation
Congenital hepatic fibrosis is always present in ARPKD in the source
Neonatal renal vein thrombosis is associated with maternal diabetes, sepsis, and dehydration
Renal artery thrombosis from an umbilical artery catheter presents with renal enlargement rather than hypertension
Neonatal renal vein thrombosis is typically bilateral and never causes renal atrophy
options_after: ARPKD kidneys are smoothly enlarged and diffusely echogenic with loss of corticomedullary differentiation
Congenital hepatic fibrosis is always present in ARPKD in the source
Neonatal renal vein thrombosis is associated with maternal diabetes, sepsis, and dehydration
Renal artery thrombosis from an umbilical artery catheter presents with renal enlargement rather than hypertension
Neonatal renal vein thrombosis is typically bilateral and will not cause renal atrophy
updates.explanation: ARPKD produces big echogenic kidneys with loss of corticomedullary differentiation and always has congenital hepatic fibrosis in the source. Neonatal renal vein thrombosis is associated with maternal diabetes, sepsis, and dehydration, is usually unilateral, often left-sided, acutely enlarges the kidney and chronically causes atrophy. Renal artery thrombosis is associated with UAC and presents with severe hypertension rather than renal enlargement.

updates.question_text: Regarding prenatal hydronephrosis work-up in baby boys, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Most persistent postnatal hydronephrosis is managed with no anatomical evaluation in the source algorithm
Persistent hydronephrosis should be followed by VCUG to evaluate anatomy
MAG3 can evaluate function and drainage
VCUG is not used when posterior urethral valves are suspected
MR urography can provide function and structure but may require sedation in small children
options_after: Most persistent postnatal hydronephrosis is managed without anatomical evaluation in the source algorithm
Persistent hydronephrosis should be followed by VCUG to evaluate anatomy
MAG3 can evaluate function and drainage
VCUG is not used when posterior urethral valves are suspected
MR urography can provide function and structure but may require sedation in small children
updates.explanation: The source algorithm begins with repeat ultrasound after birth. If hydronephrosis persists, VCUG evaluates anatomy and is the gold standard for posterior urethral valves, while MAG3 evaluates function and drainage. MR urography can combine structure and function but often requires sedation in little children. Persistent cases therefore require anatomical and functional assessment rather than simple dismissal.

updates.question_text: Regarding secondary VUR and Hutch diverticula, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A Hutch diverticulum occurs at or adjacent to the UVJ
Hutch diverticula are best seen on ultrasound and never on VCUG
Secondary VUR causes exclude ureteroceles and posterior valves in the source
If associated with VUR, Hutch diverticula are usually managed only with reassurance in the source
They are dynamic and best seen during the voiding phase
options_after: A Hutch diverticulum occurs at or adjacent to the UVJ
Hutch diverticula are best seen on ultrasound and not on VCUG
Secondary VUR causes exclude ureteroceles and posterior valves in the source
If associated with VUR, Hutch diverticula are usually managed primarily with reassurance in the source
They are dynamic and best seen during the voiding phase
updates.explanation: Hutch diverticula are congenital muscular defects at or just above the UVJ. They can be difficult to see on ultrasound, are better seen on VCUG, and are dynamic, best seen during voiding. If associated with VUR they are often surgically resected. Ureteroceles, posterior valves, and neurogenic bladder are secondary VUR causes.

updates.question_text: Regarding urachal anomalies and bladder exstrophy, which of the following statements are correct?

Cloacal malformation occurs primarily in males in the source
Infection is the most common complication of urachal remnants
Bladder exstrophy has unfused pubic bones producing the manta ray sign on pelvic radiograph
updates.explanation: The source states that infection is the commonest urachal remnant complication and urachal anomalies are twice as common in boys. Bladder exstrophy is bladder herniation through an infra-umbilical anterior abdominal wall defect, with unfused pubic bones producing a very wide pubic symphysis or manta ray sign. Cloacal malformation occurs only in females.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric neurogenic bladder and cloacal malformation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cloacal malformation is a male-only posterior urethral obstruction
Tethered cord and sacral agenesis are listed in the paediatric neurogenic bladder context
Cloacal malformation keeps GU and GI drainage completely separate
Paediatric neurogenic bladder should first suggest isolated bladder carcinoma
Cloacal malformation is the classic male obstructive urethral fold
options_after: Cloacal malformation is a male-predominant posterior urethral obstruction
Tethered cord and sacral agenesis are listed in the paediatric neurogenic bladder context
Cloacal malformation keeps GU and GI drainage completely separate
Paediatric neurogenic bladder should first suggest isolated bladder carcinoma
Cloacal malformation is the classic male obstructive urethral fold
updates.explanation: Cloacal malformation is described as GU and GI drainage into a common opening and occurs only in females. Posterior urethral valves are the male posterior urethral obstructing fold. For paediatric neurogenic bladder, the source advises thinking of spinal dysraphism, including tethered cord and sacral agenesis.

updates.question_text: Regarding Wilms-associated syndromes and variants, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Beckwith-Wiedemann is associated with macroglossia, omphalocele, hemihypertrophy, and Wilms
WAGR includes Wilms, aniridia, genital anomalies, and growth delay

options_after: Beckwith-Wiedemann is associated with macroglossia, omphalocele, hemihypertrophy, and Wilms
WAGR includes Wilms, aniridia, genital anomalies, and growth delay
Rhabdoid Wilms variant is associated with excellent prognosis without brain tumour association
Drash includes Wilms, pseudohermaphroditism, and progressive glomerulonephritis
Clear cell Wilms variant is associated with bone metastases
updates.explanation: The source lists Beckwith-Wiedemann and Sotos among overgrowth syndromes and WAGR and Drash among non-overgrowth associations. Beckwith-Wiedemann is also linked to omphalocele and hepatoblastoma. Clear cell Wilms variant likes bone metastases. Rhabdoid variant has poor prognosis and is associated with aggressive rhabdoid brain tumours.

updates.question_text: Regarding paratesticular rhabdomyosarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is primarily a benign vascular malformation
It is expected only after direct scrotal trauma
It is by far the most common extratesticular mass in young men in the source
It is synonymous with hydrocele
A scrotal mass that is definitely outside the testicle should raise this diagnosis if it is a true mass
options_after: It is primarily a benign vascular malformation
It is expected primarily after direct scrotal trauma
It is by far the most common extratesticular mass in young men in the source
It is synonymous with hydrocele
A scrotal mass that is definitely outside the testicle should raise this diagnosis if it is a true mass
updates.explanation: The source states that paratesticular rhabdomyosarcoma is by far the most common extratesticular mass in young men and is the key diagnosis when a true mass is not definitely intratesticular. Trauma may produce haematoma, but a true mass should not be dismissed as trauma. Hydrocele is a fluid collection rather than a solid tumour.

updates.question_text: Which feature favours neuroblastoma over Wilms tumour in the source comparison?
options_before: Usually around age 4 and never before 2 months
Rare calcification, less than 10%
Well circumscribed renal mass
Lung metastases as the usual pattern
Encasement rather than invasion of vessels
options_after: Usually around age 4 and not before 2 months
Rare calcification, less than 10%
Well circumscribed renal mass
Lung metastases as the usual pattern
Encasement rather than invasion of vessels
updates.explanation: The source contrasts neuroblastoma with Wilms tumour. Neuroblastoma is usually under age 2, can occur in utero, commonly calcifies, is poorly marginated, metastasises to bone, and encases vessels. Wilms is usually around age 4, rarely calcifies, is well circumscribed, tends to invade vessels, and usually metastasises to lung.

updates.question_text: Regarding hydrometrocolpos and paediatric ovarian torsion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A lateral neck branchial cleft cyst is the most common cause listed in the source
Paediatric ovarian torsion always requires an ovarian malignancy as a lead mass
Hydrometrocolpos is an expanded fluid-filled vaginal cavity with uterine distension
It may present as a midline pelvic mass causing hydronephrosis
In children, an ovary at least three times the contralateral side suggests torsion
options_after: A lateral neck branchial cleft cyst is the most common cause listed in the source
Paediatric ovarian torsion characteristically requires an ovarian malignancy as a lead mass
Hydrometrocolpos is an expanded fluid-filled vaginal cavity with uterine distension
It may present as a midline pelvic mass causing hydronephrosis
In children, an ovary at least three times the contralateral side suggests torsion
updates.explanation: Hydrometrocolpos is described as obstructed drainage of the vagina/uterus with expanded fluid-filled vagina and distended uterus. Imperforate hymen is the most common cause, and it can present as a midline pelvic mass causing hydronephrosis. In children, torsion can occur without a mass due to excessive ovarian mobility, and comparison with the contralateral ovary is key; threefold enlargement is suspicious.

updates.question_text: Regarding hydrocele, varicocele, and idiopathic scrotal oedema, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hydrocele is the most common cause of painless scrotal swelling in the source
Congenital hydrocele results from closure of the processus vaginalis with no peritoneal communication
Septated hydrocele implies haematocele or pyocele, distinguished clinically
Isolated right-sided varicocele requires only scrotal follow-up in the source
HSP is the most common cause of idiopathic scrotal oedema in the source
options_after: Hydrocele is the most common cause of painless scrotal swelling in the source
Congenital hydrocele results from closure of the processus vaginalis without peritoneal communication
Septated hydrocele implies haematocele or pyocele, distinguished clinically
Isolated right-sided varicocele requires primarily scrotal follow-up in the source
HSP is the most common cause of idiopathic scrotal oedema in the source
updates.explanation: Hydrocele is described as the most common cause of painless scrotal swelling, with congenital hydroceles due to patent processus vaginalis. A complicated septated hydrocele represents haematocele or pyocele, separated clinically. Isolated right varicocele should raise abdominal pathology and lead to abdominal CT, while HSP is listed as the most common cause of idiopathic scrotal oedema.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric testicular and extratesticular masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ultrasound can localise a scrotal mass as intra- or extratesticular
An extratesticular paediatric scrotal mass is most likely embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma from spermatic cord or epididymis in the source
Paratesticular rhabdomyosarcoma presents as a heterogeneous vascular extratesticular mass
Imaging features reliably distinguish all intratesticular tumour histologies
Testicular microlithiasis is a large solitary calcified testicular mass
options_after: Ultrasound can localise a scrotal mass as intra- or extratesticular
An extratesticular paediatric scrotal mass is most likely embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma from spermatic cord or epididymis in the source
Paratesticular rhabdomyosarcoma presents as a heterogeneous vascular extratesticular mass
Imaging features reliably distinguish most intratesticular tumour histologies
Testicular microlithiasis is a large solitary calcified testicular mass
updates.explanation: The source separates paediatric scrotal masses into intra- and extratesticular locations. Ultrasound localises the mass, but intratesticular tumour histology is not reliably distinguished by imaging alone. Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma is the key extratesticular diagnosis and is described as a heterogeneous vascular extratesticular mass. Microlithiasis consists of multiple tiny echogenic foci.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric testicular germ cell tumours, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Germ cell tumours account for only a small minority of testicular cancers in the source
Pure testicular teratomas are primarily an adolescent tumour rather than a tumour of very young children in the source
Seminoma is the dominant first-decade tumour
The two germ cell tumours seen in the first decade are yolk sac tumour and teratoma
Yolk sac tumour usually has elevated AFP
options_after: Germ cell tumours account for primarily a small minority of testicular cancers in the source
Pure testicular teratomas are primarily an adolescent tumour rather than a tumour of very young children in the source
Seminoma is the dominant first-decade tumour
The two germ cell tumours seen in the first decade are yolk sac tumour and teratoma
Yolk sac tumour usually has elevated AFP
updates.explanation: The source states that germ cell tumours account for most testicular cancers, but first-decade germ cell tumours are yolk sac tumour and teratoma. Yolk sac tumour is described in children under 2 years and usually has elevated AFP. Pure testicular teratoma is also described in very young children, whereas seminoma is more typical of the fourth decade.

updates.question_text: Regarding choriocarcinoma, Sertoli cell tumour, and testicular lymphoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Choriocarcinoma is aggressive, highly vascular, and associated with bleeding metastases
Beta-hCG is usually elevated in choriocarcinoma in the source
Testicular lymphoma can appear as multiple hypoechoic vascular testicular masses
Sertoli cell tumours are usually unilateral and never calcify
No Sertoli cell tumour subtype is associated with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome in the source
options_after: Choriocarcinoma is aggressive, highly vascular, and associated with bleeding metastases
Beta-hCG is usually elevated in choriocarcinoma in the source
Testicular lymphoma can appear as multiple hypoechoic vascular testicular masses
Sertoli cell tumours are usually unilateral and will not calcify
Peutz–Jeghers syndrome lacks a recognised Sertoli-cell tumour association
updates.explanation: Choriocarcinoma is described as an aggressive, highly vascular tumour with bleeding metastases and usually elevated beta-hCG. Sertoli cell tumours are usually bilateral, can have burned-out calcified scar-like foci, and one subtype is linked with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Testicular lymphoma may replace normal echogenic tissue with focal or diffuse hypoechoic vascular tissue, including multiple hypoechoic masses.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric fractures and physeal injury, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The major concern with physeal injury is immediate joint dislocation rather than growth arrest
Repeat radiographs in 7-10 days can reveal periosteal reaction after occult fracture
A physeal bar is an early bony bridge crossing the growth plate
Physeal bars can follow trauma or prior infection
Children rarely remodel and usually keep permanent fracture deformity
options_after: The major concern with physeal injury is immediate joint dislocation rather than growth arrest
Repeat radiographs in 7-10 days can reveal periosteal reaction after occult fracture
A physeal bar is an early bony bridge crossing the growth plate
Physeal bars can follow trauma or prior infection
Children rarely remodel and usually keep long-term fracture deformity
updates.explanation: Children may bend or sustain subtle fractures, so repeat radiographs after 7-10 days can reveal periosteal reaction. The major concern of physeal injury is growth arrest, often represented by a physeal bar crossing the growth plate. Prior trauma is the classic context, although previous infection can also produce a bar. Children often remodel well rather than preserving a permanent deformity.

updates.question_text: Regarding Salter-Harris classification, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Type 2 involves the metaphysis and is the most common type
Type 1 is primarily a metaphyseal fracture away from the physis
Type 3 is a metaphyseal fracture and is the commonest Salter-Harris injury
Type 4 involves only the metaphysis and has no growth-arrest risk
Type 5 is compression of the growth plate with poor prognosis
options_after: Type 2 involves the metaphysis and is the most common type
Type 1 is primarily a metaphyseal fracture away from the physis
Type 3 is a metaphyseal fracture and is the commonest Salter-Harris injury
Type 4 involves primarily the metaphysis and lacks growth-arrest risk
Type 5 is compression of the growth plate with poor prognosis
updates.explanation: The source uses the classic Salter-Harris pattern: type 1 through the physis, type 2 above or away into the metaphysis and most common, type 3 into the epiphysis, type 4 through metaphysis and epiphysis, and type 5 as compression injury. Types 3 and 4 can require surgery and have growth-arrest risk, while type 5 has poor prognosis and may be subtle.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric elbow trauma lines and fat pads, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A visible posterior fat pad is abnormal and suggests effusion
The radiocapitellar line should intersect the middle of the capitellum on every view
The anterior humeral line on a true lateral should pass through the middle third of the capitellum
A thin anterior fat pad is always pathologic
With supracondylar fracture, the anterior humeral line may pass through the anterior third
options_after: A visible posterior fat pad is abnormal and suggests effusion
The radiocapitellar line should intersect the middle of the capitellum on every view
The anterior humeral line on a true lateral should pass through the middle third of the capitellum
A thin anterior fat pad is characteristically pathologic
With supracondylar fracture, the anterior humeral line may pass through the anterior third
updates.explanation: Posterior fat pad visibility is abnormal and suggests effusion or occult fracture, while a thin anterior fat pad can be normal. The radiocapitellar line should intersect the capitellum on every view. The anterior humeral line should pass through the middle third of the capitellum on a true lateral, but may pass through the anterior third with supracondylar fracture.

updates.question_text: Regarding lateral condyle and medial epicondyle elbow injuries, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A fracture through the capitello-trochlear groove is unstable in the source
Displaced lateral condyle fracture requires surgery in the source
A missing medial epicondyle after dislocation should prompt search for an incarcerated fragment
External rotation oblique views are the source-listed method for excluding lateral condyle displacement
Medial epicondyle avulsion is intra-articular and must always cause effusion
options_after: A fracture through the capitello-trochlear groove is unstable in the source
Displaced lateral condyle fracture requires surgery in the source
A missing medial epicondyle after dislocation should prompt search for an incarcerated fragment
External rotation oblique views are the source-listed method for excluding lateral condyle displacement
Medial epicondyle avulsion is intra-articular and must characteristically cause effusion
updates.explanation: Lateral condyle fractures through the capitello-trochlear groove are unstable, and displacement matters because displaced fractures require surgery. The source stresses internal rotation oblique views for displacement assessment. Medial epicondyle avulsion is extra-articular, so effusion is not obligatory, and the fragment can be incarcerated in the joint, especially after dislocation.

updates.question_text: Regarding Caffey disease and physiologic periostitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Caffey disease is self-limiting soft-tissue swelling, periosteal reaction, and irritability in the first 6 months
Physiologic periostitis occurs around 3 months and should resolve by 6 months
The metatarsal is the most common location for Caffey disease in the source
Physiologic periostitis always spares the diaphysis
Physiologic periostitis is expected if seen before 1 month of age
options_after: Caffey disease is self-limiting soft-tissue swelling, periosteal reaction, and irritability in the first 6 months
Physiologic periostitis occurs around 3 months and should resolve by 6 months
The metatarsal is the most common location for Caffey disease in the source
Physiologic periostitis characteristically spares the diaphysis
Physiologic periostitis is expected if seen before 1 month of age
updates.explanation: Caffey disease is described as a self-limiting disorder with soft-tissue swelling, periosteal reaction, and irritability in the first 6 months. The mandible is the most common location, with clavicle and ulna also classic. Physiologic periostitis occurs around 3 months, resolves by 6 months, and involves the diaphysis; before 1 month is not physiologic.

updates.question_text: Regarding limb-shortening terminology, which of the following pairings are correct?
options_before: Mesomelic - short forearm or lower leg
Acromelic - short forearm or lower leg
Rhizomelic - short hands or feet
Micromelic - absence of a single limb
Amelia - distal hands and feet are short but all limbs present
options_after: Mesomelic - short forearm or lower leg
Acromelic - short forearm or lower leg
Rhizomelic - short hands or feet
Micromelic - absence of a single limb
Amelia - distal hands and feet are short but most limbs present
updates.explanation: Mesomelic shortening involves the middle limb segments such as forearm or lower leg. Acromelic refers to distal hands or feet, rhizomelic to proximal femur or humerus, and micromelic to generalized limb shortening. Amelia means limb absence rather than isolated distal shortening.

updates.question_text: Regarding mucopolysaccharidoses imaging patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Clavicles and ribs can be thick and narrow medially, like a canoe paddle
The pelvis may have tall flared iliac wings, described as opposite to achondroplasia
The source says these disorders have no spinal manifestations
Hand radiographs commonly show wide metacarpals with proximal tapering
Morquio bony changes progress during the first few years of life
options_after: Clavicles and ribs can be thick and narrow medially, like a canoe paddle
The pelvis may have tall flared iliac wings, described as opposite to achondroplasia
The source says these disorders lack spinal manifestations
Hand radiographs commonly show wide metacarpals with proximal tapering
Morquio bony changes progress during the first few years of life
updates.explanation: Mucopolysaccharidoses are described with oval vertebral bodies and anterior beaking, thick ribs and clavicles narrowing medially, tall flared iliac wings, and hand radiographs showing wide metacarpals with proximal tapering. Morquio bony changes progress during early life and cervical myelopathy is an important risk. The no-spine statement is false.

updates.question_text: Regarding miscellaneous paediatric skeletal conditions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: NF1 can cause anterior tibial bowing and distal fibular pseudoarthrosis
Gaucher disease is described as the most common lysosomal storage disease
Gaucher disease classically produces a small spleen and no skeletal signs
Caudal regression syndrome is unrelated to VACTERL or Currarino associations in the source
NF1 scoliosis is specifically excluded by the source
options_after: NF1 can cause anterior tibial bowing and distal fibular pseudoarthrosis
Gaucher disease is described as the most common lysosomal storage disease
Gaucher disease classically produces a small spleen without skeletal signs
Caudal regression syndrome is unrelated to VACTERL or Currarino associations in the source
NF1 scoliosis is specifically excluded by the source
updates.explanation: The source briefly lists NF1 as a cause of anterior tibial bowing, distal fibular pseudoarthrosis, and scoliosis. Gaucher disease is described as the commonest lysosomal storage disease and may show hepatosplenomegaly, femoral head AVN, H-shaped vertebrae, bone infarcts, and Erlenmeyer flask femurs. Caudal regression is associated with VACTERL and Currarino syndromes.

updates.question_text: Regarding radial dysplasia, sickle-cell dactylitis, and Blount disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Blount disease is valgus deformity at the distal femur
Blount disease is often seen before age 1 and is almost always unilateral in the source
Radial dysplasia usually includes absence or hypoplasia of the radius and often a missing thumb
TAR syndrome can have radial abnormality while preserving the thumb
Hand-foot syndrome in sickle cell disease is dactylitis related to ischaemia
options_after: Blount disease is valgus deformity at the distal femur
Blount disease is often seen before age 1 and is typically unilateral in the source
Radial dysplasia usually includes absence or hypoplasia of the radius and often a missing thumb
TAR syndrome can have radial abnormality while preserving the thumb
Hand-foot syndrome in sickle cell disease is dactylitis related to ischaemia
updates.explanation: Radial dysplasia is absence or hypoplasia of the radius, usually with thumb abnormality; TAR is the notable exception where the thumb is present. Hand-foot syndrome is sickle-cell dactylitis causing hand or foot pain and swelling in infants. Blount disease is tibia vara, with varus angulation at the medial proximal tibial metaphysis, often bilateral and not typically before age 2.

updates.question_text: Regarding congenital flat foot and tarsal coalition, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Congenital flat foot has hindfoot valgus
Tarsal coalition is always unilateral and purely osseous
Calcaneonavicular coalition occurs at the middle facet
Flexible flat foot can improve on plantar-flexion stress views
Rigid flat foot subtypes include tarsal coalition and vertical talus in the source
options_after: Congenital flat foot has hindfoot valgus
Tarsal coalition is characteristically unilateral and purely osseous
Calcaneonavicular coalition occurs at the middle facet
Flexible flat foot can improve on plantar-flexion stress views
Rigid flat foot subtypes include tarsal coalition and vertical talus in the source
updates.explanation: Congenital flat foot is a hindfoot valgus condition. Flexible flat foot improves with plantar-flexion stress, whereas rigid flat foot includes tarsal coalition and vertical talus. Tarsal coalition can be talocalcaneal or calcaneonavicular, is bilateral in about half, and fibrous/cartilaginous forms are more common than osseous forms. Talocalcaneal coalition involves the middle facet, while calcaneonavicular involves the anterior facet.

updates.question_text: Regarding developmental dysplasia of the hip, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is never bilateral in the source
Measurements in the first week of life are always reliable because neonatal laxity is absent
It is more common in females and breech infants
Oligohydramnios is a source-listed risk factor
Ultrasound is useful after physical examination until ossification limits assessment
options_after: It is not bilateral in the source
Measurements in the first week of life are characteristically reliable because neonatal laxity is absent
It is more common in females and breech infants
Oligohydramnios is a source-listed risk factor
Ultrasound is useful after physical examination until ossification limits assessment
updates.explanation: DDH is more common in females, breech infants, and oligohydramnios. Physical examination may show asymmetric folds, leg length discrepancy, palpable clunk, or delayed ambulation. Ultrasound is excellent until ossification, after which radiographs are used. The source cautions that first-week laxity from maternal hormones can distort measurements, and bilateral involvement occurs in about one third.

updates.question_text: Regarding Kocher criteria and workup for painful paediatric hip, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI is presented as the first test before radiographs or ultrasound in typical cases
Fever, inability to walk, raised ESR or CRP, and high white cell count are the four criteria in the source
A negative CRP and ability to bear weight argue against septic arthritis in the source
Initial imaging workup includes hip radiographs followed by ultrasound for effusion
Joint aspiration is never considered once ultrasound shows an effusion
options_after: MRI is presented as the first test before radiographs or ultrasound in typical cases
Fever, inability to walk, raised ESR or CRP, and high white cell count are the four criteria in the source
A negative CRP and ability to bear weight argue against septic arthritis in the source
Initial imaging workup includes hip radiographs followed by ultrasound for effusion
Joint aspiration is not considered once ultrasound shows an effusion
updates.explanation: The Kocher criteria in the source include fever, inability to walk, raised ESR or CRP, and WBC greater than 12K. Negative CRP and ability to bear weight argue against septic arthritis. Typical workup begins with AP/lateral/frog-leg radiographs, then ultrasound for effusion, then clinical decision about aspiration. MRI is reserved for situations where aspiration cannot or has not been performed.

updates.question_text: Regarding lipomyelocele, lipomyelomeningocele, and terminal myelocystocele, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lipomyelomeningocele has the placode-lipoma interface inside the canal in the source
These lipomatous lesions are never associated with tethered cord
Lipomyelocele and lipomyelomeningocele are lipomas with a dural defect
The expected presentation is a subcutaneous fatty mass above the gluteal crease
Terminal myelocystocele is a solid fibrous spur splitting the cord
options_after: Lipomyelomeningocele has the placode-lipoma interface inside the canal in the source
These lipomatous lesions are not associated with tethered cord
Lipomyelocele and lipomyelomeningocele are lipomas with a dural defect
The expected presentation is a subcutaneous fatty mass above the gluteal crease
Terminal myelocystocele is a solid fibrous spur splitting the cord
updates.explanation: Lipomyelocele and lipomyelomeningocele are lipomas with dural defects, distinguished by whether the neural placode-lipoma interface is inside or outside the canal. The expected presentation is a subcutaneous fatty mass above the gluteal crease, and the source states these lipomatous lesions are always associated with tethered cord. Terminal myelocystocele is herniation of a terminal syrinx into a posterior meningocele, not a solid split-cord spur.

updates.question_text: Regarding closed spinal dysraphism without a subcutaneous mass, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Intradural lipomas are most common in the thoracic spine along the dorsal aspect
Fibrolipoma of the filum terminale may be an incidental linear T1-bright fatty filum
Intradural lipomas always require posterior element defects in the source
A fatty filum always means the conus is low and the filum is thickened
Dermal sinus is an epithelial-lined tract that can extend from skin to deeper tissues
options_after: Intradural lipomas are most common in the thoracic spine along the dorsal aspect
Fibrolipoma of the filum terminale may be an incidental linear T1-bright fatty filum
Intradural lipomas characteristically require posterior element defects in the source
A fatty filum characteristically means the conus is low and the filum is thickened
Dermal sinus is an epithelial-lined tract that can extend from skin to deeper tissues
updates.explanation: The source lists intradural lipomas, fibrolipoma of the filum terminale, tight filum, dermal sinus, diastematomyelia, and caudal regression under closed dysraphism without a subcutaneous mass. Intradural lipomas are most common dorsally in the thoracic spine and do not necessarily require posterior element defects. Fatty filum can be incidental with normal conus and non-thickened filum. Dermal sinus is an epithelial tract that may extend deeply.

updates.question_text: Regarding tight filum terminale and tethered cord syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A normally located conus with non-thickened fatty filum is the definition of tight filum in the source
Tight filum cannot have an associated terminal lipoma
Tight filum is thickened greater than 2 mm with low conus below the inferior endplate of L2
Tethered cord syndrome can include low back pain, leg pain, and bladder dysfunction
Tethered cord syndrome results from shortening of the spinal canal rather than cord stretching during growth
options_after: A normally located conus with non-thickened fatty filum is the definition of tight filum in the source
Tight filum will not have an associated terminal lipoma
Tight filum is thickened greater than 2 mm with low conus below the inferior endplate of L2
Tethered cord syndrome can include low back pain, leg pain, and bladder dysfunction
Tethered cord syndrome results from shortening of the spinal canal rather than cord stretching during growth
updates.explanation: Tight filum terminale is a thickened filum greater than 2 mm with a low conus below the inferior endplate of L2, sometimes with terminal lipoma. Tethered cord syndrome is clinical, with low back pain, leg pain, and urinary bladder dysfunction from cord stretching as the canal grows.

updates.question_text: Regarding caudal regression and Currarino triad, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Currarino triad includes posterior sacral meningocele
The classic cord termination is low and tapered below the sacrum
Maternal diabetes is not associated in the source
Currarino triad includes anterior sacral meningocele, anorectal malformation, and sacrococcygeal osseous defect
Caudal regression cannot involve coccygeal or lumbosacral agenesis
options_after: Currarino triad includes posterior sacral meningocele
The classic cord termination is low and tapered below the sacrum
Maternal diabetes is not associated in the source
Currarino triad includes anterior sacral meningocele, anorectal malformation, and sacrococcygeal osseous defect
Caudal regression will not involve coccygeal or lumbosacral agenesis
updates.explanation: Caudal regression ranges from partial coccygeal agenesis to lumbosacral agenesis and is associated with maternal diabetes, VACTERL, and Currarino triad. The source describes a blunted high-terminating cord and shield sign from opposed iliac bones. Currarino triad consists of anterior sacral meningocele, anorectal malformation, and sacrococcygeal osseous defect.

updates.question_text: Regarding poor-quality or non-diagnostic bone scans, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Poor renal function improves skeletal conspicuity by clearing soft-tissue tracer faster
Encouraging hydration between injection and imaging may improve clearance
A 24-hour delayed image may be used as a problem-solving delayed phase
Absent renal clearance always proves diffuse skeletal metastases
High soft-tissue background can degrade bone scan interpretation
options_after: Poor renal function improves skeletal conspicuity by clearing soft-tissue tracer faster
Encouraging hydration between injection and imaging may improve clearance
A 24-hour delayed image may be used as a problem-solving delayed phase
Absent renal clearance characteristically proves diffuse skeletal metastases
High soft-tissue background can degrade bone scan interpretation
updates.explanation: The source lists poor renal function as a major cause of difficult bone scan interpretation because tracer is not cleared from soft tissue. Hydration can improve clearance, and delayed imaging can sometimes be used for problem solving. Absent renal visualisation can be seen in a superscan, but poor renal function and technical/contextual factors must also be considered.

updates.question_text: Regarding focal breast uptake on a bone scan, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It is always normal if bilateral
It proves renal osteodystrophy
It is the expected appearance of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
It can represent breast cancer when focal
It is diagnostic of an adrenal lesion
options_after: It is characteristically normal if bilateral
It proves renal osteodystrophy
It is the expected appearance of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
It can represent breast cancer when focal
It is diagnostic of an adrenal lesion
updates.explanation: The source notes that mild diffuse breast uptake can be physiological, especially in younger women, but focal breast uptake can represent cancer. This distinction is a clinical pattern-recognition point rather than a skeletal-metastasis-only interpretation. Renal osteodystrophy and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy have different scan patterns.

updates.question_text: Regarding abnormal non-osseous or unexpected uptake on bone scans, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Marked skull suture uptake can suggest renal osteodystrophy
Renal cortical uptake colder than adjacent lumbar spine is the haemochromatosis clue in the source
Asymmetric renal tracer activity may reflect obstruction or altered renal function
The urinary bladder is normally excluded from bone scan images
Focal soft-tissue uptake should always be ignored
options_after: Marked skull suture uptake can suggest renal osteodystrophy
Renal cortical uptake colder than adjacent lumbar spine is the haemochromatosis clue in the source
Asymmetric renal tracer activity may reflect obstruction or altered renal function
The urinary bladder is normally excluded from bone scan images
Focal soft-tissue uptake should characteristically be ignored
updates.explanation: The source highlights several non-osseous pattern traps: marked skull suture activity can suggest renal osteodystrophy, and asymmetric renal activity may reflect renal tract pathology or function. The haemochromatosis clue is renal cortex hotter than adjacent lumbar spine, not colder. Bladder activity is expected, and focal soft-tissue uptake can be clinically meaningful.

updates.question_text: Regarding bone scan evaluation of fractures in older patients, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bone scans can be negative for several days after fracture in older patients
A bone scan at about one week can help exclude fracture in the source
All acute fractures are immediately intensely hot in elderly patients
Delayed positivity is a recognised limitation
A negative early scan always excludes fracture
options_after: Bone scans can be negative for several days after fracture in older patients
A bone scan at about one week can help exclude fracture in the source
Most acute fractures are immediately intensely hot in elderly patients
Delayed positivity is a recognised limitation
A negative early scan characteristically excludes fracture
updates.explanation: The source warns that bone scans in older patients can be negative for several days after fracture. A scan obtained about one week later can be used to help exclude fracture. This is why a negative very early scan must be interpreted cautiously rather than treated as definitive.

updates.question_text: Regarding primary bone tumours on bone scan, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Both benign and malignant bone tumours can be hot
Hot uptake proves malignancy
Fibrous dysplasia may be hot
Osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma may be hot
Aneurysmal bone cyst is always invisible on bone scan
options_after: Both benign and malignant bone tumours can be hot
Hot uptake proves malignancy
Fibrous dysplasia may be hot
Osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma may be hot
Aneurysmal bone cyst is characteristically invisible on bone scan
updates.explanation: The source emphasises that increased bone scan uptake reflects bone turnover, so both benign and malignant bone tumours can be hot. Fibrous dysplasia, osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma are included among hot lesions. Hot uptake alone therefore does not prove malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding the donut sign on bone scan, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It is pathognomonic for osteoid osteoma
It excludes cystic bone lesions
It is never seen outside the hip
It describes a hot rim with a cold centre and is not specific
It proves metastatic prostate cancer
options_after: It is pathognomonic for osteoid osteoma
It excludes cystic bone lesions
It is not seen outside the hip
It describes a hot rim with a cold centre and is not specific
It proves metastatic prostate cancer
updates.explanation: The source describes the donut sign as a hot circle with a cold centre and explicitly notes that it is not specific. It can be seen with cystic bone lesions including aneurysmal bone cyst, simple bone cyst, giant cell tumour and telangiectatic osteosarcoma. The sign should therefore guide pattern recognition rather than be treated as a single diagnosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding bone metastasis patterns in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Prostate cancer commonly metastasises to bone
A solitary sternal lesion is relatively specific for breast cancer in the source
Lung cancer metastases may involve the appendicular skeleton
Neuroblastoma never metastasises to bone
A bone island should be intensely hot like a prostate metastasis
options_after: Prostate cancer commonly metastasises to bone
A solitary sternal lesion is relatively specific for breast cancer in the source
Lung cancer metastases may involve the appendicular skeleton
Neuroblastoma will not metastasise to bone
A bone island should be intensely hot like a prostate metastasis
updates.explanation: The source lists prostate, breast, lung and neuroblastoma patterns. Prostate cancer commonly metastasises to bone, breast cancer often involves the spine with solitary sternal involvement being relatively specific, and lung cancer can involve the appendicular skeleton. A bone island is expected to be cold or only faintly warm, unlike a hot prostate metastasis.

updates.question_text: Regarding uptake in bone on non-bone nuclear medicine studies, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bone uptake on MIBG should raise concern for metastases
Bone uptake on iodine imaging is always normal physiologic biodistribution
Bone uptake on octreotide imaging is always normal physiologic biodistribution
Skeletal uptake on MIBG is always normal biodistribution
MIBG is useful for neuroblastoma bone metastases
options_after: Bone uptake on MIBG should raise concern for metastases
Bone uptake on iodine imaging is characteristically normal physiologic biodistribution
Bone uptake on octreotide imaging is characteristically normal physiologic biodistribution
Skeletal uptake on MIBG is characteristically normal biodistribution
MIBG is useful for neuroblastoma bone metastases
updates.explanation: The source warns that visible skeletal uptake on MIBG, iodine or octreotide studies is abnormal and concerning for metastatic disease. It also states that MIBG is useful for detecting neuroblastoma bone metastases. Treating skeletal uptake on these non-bone studies as normal biodistribution would miss disseminated disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding metabolic superscans, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hyperparathyroidism is excluded from metabolic superscan causes in the source
Renal osteodystrophy can produce a metabolic superscan
Paget disease and severe thyrotoxicosis are excluded from metabolic superscan causes in the source
Metabolic superscans tend to have relatively uniform uptake with more distal appendicular extension
The skull is always cold in a metabolic superscan
options_after: Hyperparathyroidism is excluded from metabolic superscan causes in the source
Renal osteodystrophy can produce a metabolic superscan
Paget disease and severe thyrotoxicosis are excluded from metabolic superscan causes in the source
Metabolic superscans tend to have relatively uniform uptake with more distal appendicular extension
The skull is characteristically cold in a metabolic superscan
updates.explanation: The source lists hyperparathyroidism, renal osteodystrophy, Paget disease and severe thyrotoxicosis as metabolic causes of superscan. Compared with metastatic superscan, the metabolic pattern tends to be more uniform and extends more distally into the appendicular skeleton. The skull may be relatively hot rather than cold.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteoid osteoma on bone scan, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A normal bone scan excludes osteoid osteoma in the source
It can be three-phase hot
It is defined by diffuse absent skeletal uptake
A central hot nidus may create a double-density appearance
It is always cold because the nidus is too small
options_after: A normal bone scan excludes osteoid osteoma in the source
It can be three-phase hot
It is defined by diffuse absent skeletal uptake
A central hot nidus may create a double-density appearance
It is characteristically cold because the nidus is too small
updates.explanation: The source states that osteoid osteoma is focal and three-phase hot, often with a central hot nidus creating a double-density pattern. It also says a normal bone scan excludes the entity. Diffuse absent uptake or a consistently cold nidus would contradict the source pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding Paget disease on bone scan, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It is primarily a neonatal adrenal disorder
It is classically considered in older patients and can be very hot on bone scan
It is always cold and focal
It excludes super scan patterns
It is diagnosed by MIBG uptake in adrenal tissue
options_after: It is primarily a neonatal adrenal disorder
It is classically considered in older patients and can be very hot on bone scan
It is characteristically cold and focal
It excludes super scan patterns
It is diagnosed by MIBG uptake in adrenal tissue
updates.explanation: The source describes Paget disease as a condition of older patients that can be very hot on bone scan and can mimic other high-turnover processes. It is not a neonatal adrenal disease or an MIBG diagnosis. The important skill is recognising high bone turnover rather than assuming malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding heterotopic ossification and MDP bone scans, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Heterotopic ossification means bone formation within soft tissues
It never follows muscular trauma
Bone scan activity may help identify active ectopic bone formation
It is defined by absence of mineralisation
Mature cortical bone always develops from the centre outward in the source
options_after: Heterotopic ossification means bone formation within soft tissues
It will not follow muscular trauma
Bone scan activity may help identify active ectopic bone formation
It is defined by absence of mineralisation
Mature cortical bone characteristically develops from the centre outward in the source
updates.explanation: The source defines heterotopic ossification as bone forming in soft tissues, often after muscular trauma. It can mature from outside inward, eventually producing cortical bone, and MDP uptake reflects active mineralisation. Absence of mineralisation or centre-out maturation does not match the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding cold lesions on bone scan in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Early osteonecrosis may be cold
Late radiation therapy change or osteitis must always be intensely hot
Every osteosarcoma is cold
Very early or late infarction can be cold
A cold lesion can still represent clinically important disease
options_after: Early osteonecrosis may be cold
Late radiation therapy change or osteitis must characteristically be intensely hot
Routine osteosarcoma is cold
Very early or late infarction can be cold
A cold lesion can still represent clinically important disease
updates.explanation: The source lists late radiation therapy change/osteitis, early osteonecrosis and very early or late infarction among cold lesion patterns. A cold lesion can still be clinically important. Osteosarcoma is discussed as generally hot for staging rather than as an invariably cold tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric osteomyelitis on bone scan, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Whole-body imaging may be performed to evaluate disease extent
Subperiosteal pus or oedema can sometimes make early phases appear cold
Delayed phase uptake can still become clearly hot
A cold early phase always excludes infection in children
MRI remains an important alternative for spinal infection assessment
options_after: Whole-body imaging may be performed to evaluate disease extent
Subperiosteal pus or oedema can sometimes make early phases appear cold
Delayed phase uptake can still become clearly hot
A cold early phase characteristically excludes infection in children
MRI remains an important alternative for spinal infection assessment
updates.explanation: The source notes that paediatric whole-body bone scanning may be used to assess extent. Subperiosteal pus or oedema can reduce early vascularity so the early phases may be cold, while delayed images become hot. For spinal infection, MRI or gallium combined with bone scan is discussed as a problem-solving approach.

updates.question_text: Regarding the timing limitation of sulphur colloid marrow imaging in infection, which of the following statements are correct?

The combined test is positive primarily when both studies are exactly congruent

Renal activity helps interpretation because loss of renal visualisation can signal altered biodistribution
updates.explanation: The source expects renal activity on MDP bone scans and uses absent renal visualisation as a major clue to superscan physiology. It also describes unusually hot renal cortex relative to lumbar spine as a clue to haemochromatosis. updates.question_text: Regarding malignancy staging with bone scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?

Sclerotic metastases and bone islands may need functional correlation

updates.question_text: Regarding normal paediatric skeletal uptake on MDP bone scans, which of the following statements are correct?

Symmetric growth plate uptake should ordinarily be called multifocal metastases
Paediatric bone scans will not show physiological skeletal uptake
MDP uptake at growth plates reflects active bone formation
updates.explanation: The source specifically notes tracer deposition at epiphyseal growth plates and osteochondral junctions in growing skeletons. This reflects physiological bone formation and mineralisation. Symmetric growth plate uptake should not be mistaken for multifocal metastatic disease without supporting clinical or imaging evidence.

updates.question_text: Regarding a practical interpretation checklist for skeletal scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?

Use combined white-cell and marrow imaging when infection versus marrow distribution is the key problem
updates.explanation: The source repeatedly frames bone scan interpretation as pattern recognition: renal visualisation, diffuse versus focal uptake, three-phase behaviour and combined marrow/white-cell imaging all matter. Hot lesions are non-specific and can be benign, malignant, traumatic or inflammatory. This checklist keeps the focus on interpretation rather than memorising decay data.

updates.question_text: Regarding tracer in the brain on a perfusion lung scan, which of the following statements is correct?

It is expected in most patients with COPD

Thyroid or stomach activity may raise free technetium as a possibility, but brain activity is needed to call the shunt pattern. It is not normal lung perfusion biodistribution.

updates.question_text: Regarding a unilateral whole-lung perfusion defect with preserved ventilation, which of the following statements are correct?

updates.explanation: The source states that a unilateral whole-lung perfusion defect without a ventilation defect should prompt CT or MRI, with differential diagnoses including central obstructing mass, fibrosing mediastinitis and central PE. It notes that this pattern is technically low probability rather than automatically high probability PE. Air trapping is a ventilation washout phenomenon.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal gallium biodistribution, which of the following statements is correct?

Renal activity is the principal normal site
updates.explanation: The source lists normal gallium uptake in liver, marrow, spleen, salivary glands, lacrimal glands and breast tissue in appropriate settings. Bowel activity can be seen after 24 hours, and early renal/bladder activity can occur. Normal gland uptake alone is not diagnostic of sarcoidosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding gallium in sarcoidosis, which of the following statements are correct?

The choice depends on clinical site and background activity.

updates.question_text: Regarding Graves disease on thyroid scintigraphy, which of the following statements is correct?

It is defined by a single hot nodule in a cold gland
It has low uptake closely comparable to De Quervain thyroiditis
It excludes pyramidal lobe visualisation
The typical pattern is homogeneous increased thyroid uptake
updates.explanation: The source describes Graves disease as autoimmune hyperthyroidism with homogeneous increased thyroid uptake, often with increased uptake at both early and delayed time points. A single hot nodule or multinodular pattern suggests toxic nodular disease instead. Low uptake in a hyperthyroid patient points toward thyroiditis rather than Graves disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding toxic multinodular goitre and non-toxic multinodular goitre, which of the following statements are correct?

Toxic multinodular goitre is characteristically homogeneous like Graves disease
The typical clinical setting is an elderly patient with hyperthyroid symptoms
Toxic multinodular goitre has no scintigraphic distinction from thyroiditis
updates.explanation: The source describes toxic multinodular goitre as heterogeneous, with hot nodules against a relatively cold gland, often in an elderly patient with hyperthyroid symptoms. Non-toxic multinodular goitre has nodules on a more normal thyroid background. Low uptake thyroiditis is a different pattern, so uptake patterns help distinguish thyroiditis from toxic nodular disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding hot, warm and cold thyroid nodules, which of the following statements are correct?

All cold thyroid nodules are malignant

Most cold thyroid nodules are malignant
updates.explanation: The source notes that most thyroid nodules are cold and most are benign, but cold nodules are more concerning than functional nodules. A solitary cold nodule is more concerning than a cold nodule in multinodular goitre. Discordance between technetium and iodine matters because some cancers trap tracer but fail to organify iodine.

updates.explanation: The source describes I-131 as a treatment for hyperthyroidism such as Graves disease and multinodular goitre, but notes that acute severe hyperthyroidism can be medically controlled rather than treated emergently with I-131. updates.question_text: Regarding HMPAO and ECD brain SPECT tracers, which of the following statements are correct?

DTPA is the source's preferred ictal parenchymal tracer

Delayed injection risks imaging the interictal state instead. HMPAO or ECD, not DTPA, are used for parenchymal seizure SPECT.

Thallium uptake can be considered a viability marker
updates.explanation: The source describes thallium as a potassium analogue entering cells by active transport through the sodium-potassium pump. Because living cells are required for this transport, it functions as a viability marker. Higher-grade tumours tend to show more uptake, whereas necrosis is cold.

Thallium has negligible role in this differential
updates.explanation: The source highlights thallium as useful for the classic CNS lymphoma versus toxoplasmosis problem: lymphoma is thallium-positive and toxoplasmosis is thallium-negative. It also notes that several CNS infectious/tumour processes can be gallium-positive, so gallium alone is not the discriminator. The imaging skill is identifying viable tumour uptake.

updates.question_text: Regarding abnormal cisternography and normal-pressure hydrocephalus, which of the following statements are correct?

Delayed ascent over the convexities is abnormal

It also states that radionuclide cisternography cannot distinguish communicating from non-communicating hydrocephalus. Ventricular tracer is therefore abnormal in this context, not normal.

updates.question_text: Regarding radionuclide shunt patency studies, which of the following statements are correct?

The tracer is characteristically administered orally

Tracer reaching the peritoneum supports distal patency, while distal limb occlusion can force reflux into the ventricles to assess proximal patency. Delayed peritoneal flow can suggest partial distal obstruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding gastric emptying scintigraphy, which of the following statements is correct?

It uses labelled meal protocols rather than MAA, and preparation includes fasting. Meckel diverticulum, brain death and pulmonary embolism use different nuclear medicine logic.

updates.question_text: Regarding positive GI bleeding scan criteria, which of the following statements are correct?

Distal colonic activity may move less, but fixed vascular or organ activity is a common mimic. Gastric activity may be free technetium rather than true bleeding.

updates.question_text: Regarding GI bleeding scan localisation by vascular territory, which of the following statements are correct?

Celiac territory includes distal oesophagus, stomach and first duodenum; SMA includes distal duodenum through bowel to the splenic flexure; IMA includes distal transverse colon to proximal rectum. updates.question_text: Regarding Meckel scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?

A positive focus often appears in the pelvis or right lower quadrant around the same time as the stomach
H2 blockers can improve sensitivity by retaining tracer in gastric mucosal cells
Recent barium study will not affect the examination
updates.explanation: The source describes Meckel scan as a test for ectopic gastric mucosa, using pertechnetate uptake by gastric mucosal cells. The typical positive focus is pelvic or right lower quadrant activity appearing around the same time as stomach activity. Active bleeding should prompt a bleeding scan instead, and recent barium can cause false-negative attenuation.

updates.question_text: Regarding HIDA physiology and preparation, which of the following statements are correct?

options_after: HIDA tracers mimic bilirubin uptake, transport and excretion
The patient should ideally have eaten nothing for several days before the scan
The patient should be fasting for several hours so the gallbladder is ready to fill
CCK may be used if prolonged fasting has left the gallbladder overly full
Prompt hepatic uptake is abnormal in routine HIDA examination
updates.explanation: The source describes HIDA tracers as bilirubin analogues assessing hepatobiliary uptake, transport and excretion. Preparation balances fasting long enough for gallbladder filling but not so long that the gallbladder becomes overdistended and refuses tracer; CCK may be used after prolonged fasting. Prompt hepatic uptake is normally expected.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute cholecystitis on HIDA scanning, which of the following statements are correct?

Persistent non-visualisation up to delayed imaging supports cystic duct obstruction
The rim sign is always a benign normal variant
A cystic duct sign can appear as a small nub of activity with distal obstruction
options_after: Cystic duct obstruction is the usual mechanism
Failure of gallbladder filling within the expected time supports the diagnosis
Persistent non-visualisation up to delayed imaging supports cystic duct obstruction
The rim sign is characteristically a benign normal variant
A cystic duct sign can appear as a small nub of activity with distal obstruction
updates.explanation: The source states that acute cholecystitis is usually due to cystic duct obstruction, with failure of gallbladder filling on HIDA as the central pattern. The cystic duct sign is a nub of activity in the cystic duct with the remainder obstructed. The rim sign reflects pericholecystic hepatic hyperaemia and suggests more severe inflammation rather than normality.

updates.question_text: Regarding narcotics, CCK and morphine in HIDA scanning, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Narcotics can delay bowel visualisation by increasing sphincter of Oddi tone
Narcotics alone should not necessarily prevent gallbladder visualisation
Morphine can be used as a tool to promote gallbladder visualisation in selected scenarios

options_after: Narcotics can delay bowel visualisation by increasing sphincter of Oddi tone

Morphine can be used as a tool to promote gallbladder visualisation in selected scenarios
CCK and morphine should not be injected close together in the source
Morphine is not used in hepatobiliary scintigraphy
updates.explanation: The source notes that narcotics can delay bowel visualisation through sphincter of Oddi contraction and mimic biliary obstruction, but narcotics alone do not necessarily prevent gallbladder visualisation. Morphine can be used intentionally when tracer dumps into bowel without gallbladder activity. CCK and morphine should not be given close together.

updates.question_text: Regarding rapid HIDA pattern recognition and bilirubin effects, which of the following statements are correct?

options_after: No bowel activity with persistent blood pool suggests hepatocyte dysfunction
