Absent bowel activity with persistent blood pool supports common duct obstruction rather than hepatocyte dysfunction
Elevated bilirubin improves HIDA performance and reduces false-negative examinations
Increased renal activity can suggest elevated bilirubin
updates.explanation: The source's rapid HIDA summary separates hepatocyte dysfunction from common duct obstruction by blood-pool persistence versus normal clearance. Persistent gallbladder non-visualisation is the acute cholecystitis pattern, while chronic disease can show delayed filling or reduced ejection fraction. Elevated bilirubin worsens test performance and may increase renal activity; alternative agents can be preferred.

updates.question_text: Regarding Tc-sulphur colloid liver scans, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They primarily assess biliary excretion like HIDA
Sulphur colloid is taken up by the reticuloendothelial system
All liver lesions are hot on sulphur colloid
Metastases are usually hot on sulphur colloid
Focal nodular hyperplasia may be hot because it contains functioning reticuloendothelial elements
options_after: They primarily assess biliary excretion like HIDA
Sulphur colloid is taken up by the reticuloendothelial system
Most liver lesions are hot on sulphur colloid
Metastases are usually hot on sulphur colloid
Focal nodular hyperplasia may be hot because it contains functioning reticuloendothelial elements
updates.explanation: The source describes sulphur colloid as rapidly taken up by the liver reticuloendothelial system, allowing hot and cold liver lesion assessment. FNH is the classic lesion that can be hot, although not always. Many lesions, including metastases, adenoma, haemangioma, cholangiocarcinoma and abscess, are typically cold on sulphur colloid.

updates.question_text: Regarding colloid shift and abnormal sulphur colloid biodistribution, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Diffuse hepatic dysfunction can shift uptake toward spleen and marrow
Colloid shift means that all colloid must go exclusively to the lungs
Diffuse pulmonary activity is normal sulphur colloid localisation
Renal activity on sulphur colloid is diagnostic of HCC
Diffuse liver disease is one context in which altered biodistribution may be seen
options_after: Diffuse hepatic dysfunction can shift uptake toward spleen and marrow
Colloid shift means that most colloid must go predominantly to the lungs
Diffuse pulmonary activity is normal sulphur colloid localisation
Renal activity on sulphur colloid is diagnostic of HCC
Diffuse liver disease is one context in which altered biodistribution may be seen
updates.explanation: The source describes colloid shift as altered uptake away from normal liver-dominant distribution toward spleen and marrow in settings such as diffuse hepatic dysfunction, portal hypertension and hypersplenism. Diffuse pulmonary activity is abnormal and non-specific, with excess aluminium in the colloid an important testable cause. Renal activity has other associations such as CHF or transplant rejection, not HCC diagnosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding a labelled RBC haemangioma scan, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Immediate flow activity alone proves haemangioma
The lesion must be sulphur-colloid hot
The classic pattern is delayed blood-pool activity with little immediate hot spot
Small haemangiomas are the easiest lesions to detect
Angiosarcoma is never hot on flow images
options_after: Immediate flow activity alone proves haemangioma
The lesion must be sulphur-colloid hot
The classic pattern is delayed blood-pool activity with little immediate hot spot
Small haemangiomas are the easiest lesions to detect
Angiosarcoma is not hot on flow images
updates.explanation: The source describes haemangioma confirmation with labelled RBC imaging, classically showing marked delayed blood-pool activity without a strong immediate flow/pool hot spot. Small size is a common false-negative reason. Angiosarcoma may also become hot on delays but tends to be hot on flow as well, helping separate it from haemangioma.

updates.question_text: Regarding spleen and fatty liver scintigraphic patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Heat-damaged RBCs cannot be used for splenic localisation
Sulphur colloid cannot localise ectopic splenic tissue
Tc-sulphur colloid or heat-damaged labelled RBCs may be used for splenic tissue localisation
Fatty liver always increases sulphur colloid uptake above splenic uptake
Fatty liver can reduce sulphur colloid uptake in liver and alter liver-to-spleen distribution
options_after: Heat-damaged RBCs will not be used for splenic localisation
Sulphur colloid will not localise ectopic splenic tissue
Tc-sulphur colloid or heat-damaged labelled RBCs may be used for splenic tissue localisation
Fatty liver characteristically increases sulphur colloid uptake above splenic uptake
Fatty liver can reduce sulphur colloid uptake in liver and alter liver-to-spleen distribution
updates.explanation: The source describes Tc-sulphur colloid and heat-damaged labelled RBCs as splenic localisation approaches, for example when searching for ectopic spleen. Fatty liver can reduce liver sulphur colloid uptake and even reverse the normal liver-greater-than-spleen pattern. FDG liver uptake is described as not being altered by background steatosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding dynamic renal scintigraphy tracers, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: DTPA is primarily secreted and estimates effective renal plasma flow
DTPA is filtered and is useful for GFR assessment
MAG3 is primarily filtered and is the best pure GFR tracer in the source
MAG3 is secreted by proximal tubules and estimates effective renal plasma flow
All renal dynamic tracers are primarily cortical binding agents
options_after: DTPA is primarily secreted and estimates effective renal plasma flow
DTPA is filtered and is useful for GFR assessment
MAG3 is primarily filtered and is the best pure GFR tracer in the source
MAG3 is secreted by proximal tubules and estimates effective renal plasma flow
Most renal dynamic tracers are primarily cortical binding agents
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes renal dynamic tracers by renal handling. DTPA is mostly filtered and used for GFR assessment, while MAG3 is secreted by proximal tubules and estimates effective renal plasma flow. DMSA is the cortical binding tracer, not the standard dynamic renal function tracer.

updates.question_text: Regarding basic dynamic renography phases and indications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Dynamic exams typically include blood-flow, cortical and clearance phases
Posterior imaging is typical for native kidneys
Anterior imaging may be useful for transplant or horseshoe kidneys
Dynamic renography cannot assess suspected obstruction
Dynamic renography has no role in transplant complications
options_after: Dynamic exams typically include blood-flow, cortical and clearance phases
Posterior imaging is typical for native kidneys
Anterior imaging may be useful for transplant or horseshoe kidneys
Dynamic renography will not assess suspected obstruction
Dynamic renography has negligible role in transplant complications
updates.explanation: The source describes dynamic renal scans as having flow, cortical and clearance phases. Posterior imaging is usual for native kidneys, while anterior imaging is used for transplants or horseshoe kidneys. Indications include differential function, obstruction, renal artery stenosis, transplant complications and urine leak.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal blood-flow patterns on dynamic renography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: ATN, interstitial nephritis and cyclosporin toxicity always have absent perfusion
A poor bolus causes isolated increased asymmetric renal flow
Asymmetric decreased flow can be seen with renal artery thrombosis, renal vein thrombosis, severe obstruction, acute rejection or pyelonephritis
Increased asymmetric flow is the classic pattern of chronic rejection
Renal flow should normally reach the kidneys symmetrically after the aorta
options_after: ATN, interstitial nephritis and cyclosporin toxicity characteristically have absent perfusion
A poor bolus causes isolated increased asymmetric renal flow
Asymmetric decreased flow can be seen with renal artery thrombosis, renal vein thrombosis, severe obstruction, acute rejection or pyelonephritis
Increased asymmetric flow is the classic pattern of chronic rejection
Renal flow should normally reach the kidneys symmetrically after the aorta
updates.explanation: The source gives practical flow-pattern interpretation: poor bolus can make flow symmetrically reduced, while several unilateral pathologies can reduce flow asymmetrically. ATN, interstitial nephritis and cyclosporin toxicity are specifically noted as having normal perfusion. Normal renal flow should be symmetric and similar to the aortic arrival timing.

updates.question_text: Regarding the Lasix renogram, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: True obstruction should rapidly clear after Lasix
The study is used only for renal artery stenosis
Reservoir effect proves acute transplant rejection
A dilated but non-obstructed system should wash out after diuretic challenge
Lasix renography requires a sulphur colloid liver tracer
options_after: True obstruction should rapidly clear after Lasix
The study is used primarily for renal artery stenosis
Reservoir effect proves acute transplant rejection
A dilated but non-obstructed system should wash out after diuretic challenge
Lasix renography requires a sulphur colloid liver tracer
updates.explanation: The source explains the Lasix renogram as distinguishing true obstruction from a dilated but non-obstructed collecting system. A non-obstructed dilated system should empty after diuretic challenge, while true obstruction does not. Reservoir effect from a very dilated pelvis can produce an indeterminate or false-positive pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding false-positive obstruction on diuretic renography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Poor renal function can impair Lasix response
A full or neurogenic bladder can create back pressure and delay drainage
Hydration status has no effect on test interpretation
A Foley catheter can help when bladder back pressure is a concern
Reservoir effect from a very dilated pelvis is irrelevant
options_after: Poor renal function can impair Lasix response
A full or neurogenic bladder can create back pressure and delay drainage
Hydration status lacks effect on test interpretation
A Foley catheter can help when bladder back pressure is a concern
Reservoir effect from a very dilated pelvis is irrelevant
updates.explanation: The source lists false-positive obstruction causes including poor Lasix response from poor renal function or dehydration, reservoir effect, and back pressure from a full or neurogenic bladder. A Foley catheter can resolve the bladder back-pressure issue. These pitfalls prevent overcalling obstruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal transplant scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: ATN usually has poor perfusion with prompt excretion
Acute rejection has poor perfusion with delayed excretion
Cyclosporin toxicity is typically immediate post-operative only
ATN is commonly seen in the early post-transplant period
Chronic rejection always shows increased tracer uptake
options_after: ATN usually has poor perfusion with prompt excretion
Acute rejection has poor perfusion with delayed excretion
Cyclosporin toxicity is typically immediate post-operative
ATN is commonly seen in the early post-transplant period
Chronic rejection characteristically shows increased tracer uptake
updates.explanation: The source differentiates ATN from rejection using flow and excretion. ATN is early, especially with cadaveric donors, and shows preserved perfusion with delayed excretion. Acute rejection shows poor perfusion with delayed excretion, while cyclosporin toxicity can mimic ATN but is not the immediate post-operative pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding DMSA renal cortical defects, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute pyelonephritis can produce focal, multifocal or diffuse decreased uptake
Renal scars can show focal decreased uptake with volume loss
Clinical history helps distinguish acute pyelonephritis from chronic scar or mass
All focal DMSA defects are benign columns of Bertin
DMSA cannot show cortical defects
options_after: Acute pyelonephritis can produce focal, multifocal or diffuse decreased uptake
Renal scars can show focal decreased uptake with volume loss
Clinical history helps distinguish acute pyelonephritis from chronic scar or mass
Most focal DMSA defects are benign columns of Bertin
DMSA will not show cortical defects
updates.explanation: The source notes that acute pyelonephritis can appear as focal, multifocal or diffuse decreased cortical uptake, while scars and masses can also be cold. Scarring usually has volume loss, and the acute versus chronic clinical setting changes the differential. A column of Bertin should take up tracer.

updates.question_text: Regarding testicular nuclear medicine in acute scrotal pain, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Acute torsion shows focal absence of flow to the affected testis
Acute epididymitis shows absent flow
Delayed torsion and abscess can never mimic each other
The study evaluates biliary excretion
Pertechnetate cannot be used for this blood-flow study
options_after: Acute torsion shows focal absence of flow to the affected testis
Acute epididymitis shows absent flow
Delayed torsion and abscess will not mimic each other
The study evaluates biliary excretion
Pertechnetate will not be used for this blood-flow study
updates.explanation: The source describes the testicular scan as a blood-flow study for torsion versus epididymitis. Early torsion shows focal absent flow, while epididymitis shows increased flow and blood pool. Delayed torsion can resemble abscess with a hot rim and central photopenia.

updates.question_text: Regarding FDG PET/CT technique and interpretation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The CT component provides anatomy and attenuation correction
The CT component eliminates all possible PET artefacts
Metallic devices can produce attenuation-correction artefacts
Uncorrected source images should be reviewed when attenuation artefact is suspected
PET is always superior to CT/MRI for local invasion assessment
options_after: The CT component provides anatomy and attenuation correction
The CT component eliminates most possible PET artefacts
Metallic devices can produce attenuation-correction artefacts
Uncorrected source images should be reviewed when attenuation artefact is suspected
PET is always superior to CT/MRI for local invasion assessment
updates.explanation: The source states that PET/CT fusion adds anatomy and attenuation correction, but correction can create artefacts such as apparent uptake near dense metallic devices. Reviewing uncorrected/source images is the solution when artefact is suspected. PET is useful for extent and distant disease, while CT or MRI is often better for local invasion and characterisation.

updates.question_text: Regarding timing of FDG PET after cancer therapy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: FDG PET should always be performed immediately after radiotherapy
Therapy timing is irrelevant because FDG cannot show inflammation
Waiting after chemotherapy helps avoid false-negative stunning
Waiting after radiotherapy helps avoid inflammatory false positives
PET can be used for treatment response assessment
options_after: FDG PET should characteristically be performed immediately after radiotherapy
Therapy timing is irrelevant because FDG will not show inflammation
Waiting after chemotherapy helps avoid false-negative stunning
Waiting after radiotherapy helps avoid inflammatory false positives
PET can be used for treatment response assessment
updates.explanation: The source recommends waiting after chemotherapy and radiotherapy to avoid treatment-related false negatives and inflammatory false positives. FDG PET can be valuable for response assessment, but timing matters. Immediate post-treatment PET can be misleading.

updates.question_text: Regarding brown fat on FDG PET, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Brown fat uptake is commonly seen at the base of the neck and shoulders
Brown fat uptake is increased by warm rooms and deep sedation in every patient
Cold rooms and anxiety can increase brown fat uptake
Keeping the room warm and selected medications can reduce brown fat uptake
Brown fat uptake is diagnostic of lymphoma
options_after: Brown fat uptake is commonly seen at the base of the neck and shoulders
Brown fat uptake is increased by warm rooms and deep sedation in most patients
Cold rooms and anxiety can increase brown fat uptake
Keeping the room warm and selected medications can reduce brown fat uptake
Brown fat uptake is diagnostic of lymphoma
updates.explanation: The source describes brown fat uptake at the base of the neck, shoulders and paraspinal thoracic fat. It is more common with cold rooms and anxious patients, and can be reduced by warming and medications such as propranolol or reserpine. Brown fat is a physiologic/pitfall pattern rather than lymphoma by itself.

updates.question_text: Regarding hibernoma on FDG PET/CT, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hibernoma is a malignant renal tumour in the source
Hibernoma is a benign brown fat tumour
It can be very FDG-avid
It may be well circumscribed on CT with density between fat and muscle
It is never considered against liposarcoma
options_after: Hibernoma is a malignant renal tumour in the source
Hibernoma is a benign brown fat tumour
It can be very FDG-avid
It may be well circumscribed on CT with density between fat and muscle
It is not considered against liposarcoma
updates.explanation: The source describes hibernoma as a benign brown fat tumour, often very hot on PET, with CT density between fat and muscle. Liposarcoma is the main differential, which is why these lesions are often removed. It is not a renal carcinoma pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding tumours or processes that may be PET-cold or PET-hot, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Low- or intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumours may be relatively FDG-cold
Mucinous tumours can be FDG-cold
RCC may be FDG-cold
Infection and inflammation are always FDG-cold
Brown fat and thymus can be PET-hot non-malignant mimics
options_after: Low- or intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumours may be relatively FDG-cold
Mucinous tumours can be FDG-cold
RCC may be FDG-cold
Infection and inflammation are characteristically FDG-cold
Brown fat and thymus can be PET-hot non-malignant mimics
updates.explanation: The source lists several PET-cold tumour patterns, including low/intermediate neuroendocrine tumours, RCC, mucinous lesions and some peritoneal/bowel/liver implants. Non-malignant PET-hot mimics include infection, inflammation, brown fat, muscle, ovaries in functional phases and thymus. FDG avidity is therefore not synonymous with malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding focal thyroid uptake on FDG PET, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It should always be ignored as physiological
It proves Hashimoto thyroiditis
It is diagnostic of Graves disease
It excludes malignancy
It requires further work-up because it may represent malignancy or benign disease
options_after: It should characteristically be ignored as physiological
It proves Hashimoto thyroiditis
It is diagnostic of Graves disease
It excludes malignancy
It requires further work-up because it may represent malignancy or benign disease
updates.explanation: The source states that focal thyroid uptake on FDG PET requires further work-up because it may be cancer or may be benign. Diffuse thyroid uptake more often suggests autoimmune thyroiditis such as Hashimoto disease. Focal uptake should therefore not be dismissed.

updates.question_text: Regarding FDG PET special tumour scenarios, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A cold ground-glass nodule can still be cancer in the source
A hot ground-glass nodule is always adenocarcinoma in situ
HCC is often FDG-cold
Seminoma tends to be FDG-hot compared with non-seminomatous testicular cancer
Metformin can cause intense diffuse bowel uptake, often favouring colon
options_after: A cold ground-glass nodule can still be cancer in the source
A hot ground-glass nodule is characteristically adenocarcinoma in situ
HCC is often FDG-cold
Seminoma tends to be FDG-hot compared with non-seminomatous testicular cancer
Metformin can cause intense diffuse bowel uptake, often favouring colon
updates.explanation: The source gives several practical PET traps: a cold ground-glass nodule can be cancer, while a hot one may be infection; HCC is often cold; seminoma is typically hotter than non-seminomatous testicular cancer; and metformin can cause intense diffuse bowel uptake. These are pitfalls in interpreting FDG avidity.

updates.question_text: Regarding pelvic and genitourinary FDG PET pitfalls, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Physiological endometrial uptake can occur during menstruation and around ovulation
Physiological ovarian uptake can occur during ovulation
Postmenopausal endometrial or ovarian FDG uptake is suspicious and should prompt ultrasound
Small peritoneal disease and small nodes can be missed because of size or adjacent bowel uptake
Perivesical disease is always easy to see because bladder FDG excretion is low
options_after: Physiological endometrial uptake can occur during menstruation and around ovulation
Physiological ovarian uptake can occur during ovulation
Postmenopausal endometrial or ovarian FDG uptake is suspicious and should prompt ultrasound
Small peritoneal disease and small nodes can be missed because of size or adjacent bowel uptake
Perivesical disease is characteristically easy to see because bladder FDG excretion is low
updates.explanation: The source describes physiological endometrial and ovarian uptake in premenopausal phases, but postmenopausal endometrial or ovarian uptake is suspicious and ultrasound is the next step. Small peritoneal disease and small nodes may be missed because of size or adjacent bowel uptake. Perivesical disease can be hidden by intense bladder activity.

updates.question_text: Regarding misregistration and urinary activity on pelvic FDG PET/CT, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ureteric or bladder activity cannot simulate disease
Misregistration can make ureteric or bladder activity look like pathology
Reviewing uncorrected or source images can help
Minimising the time between PET and CT acquisitions helps reduce misregistration
Vesicovaginal fistula can falsely elevate SUV because urinary FDG spills into the vagina
options_after: Ureteric or bladder activity will not simulate disease
Misregistration can make ureteric or bladder activity look like pathology
Reviewing uncorrected or source images can help
Minimising the time between PET and CT acquisitions helps reduce misregistration
Vesicovaginal fistula can falsely elevate SUV because urinary FDG spills into the vagina
updates.explanation: The source warns that urinary FDG in the ureter or bladder can simulate disease if mapped incorrectly. Source or uncorrected images help solve this, and minimising the PET-to-CT interval reduces misregistration. Vesicovaginal fistula can elevate apparent vaginal activity because urinary FDG spills into the vagina.

updates.question_text: Regarding In-111 pentetreotide/octreotide imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is primarily a bone mineralisation tracer
It targets somatostatin receptor expression
It is used only for renal obstruction
It is the preferred tracer for routine V/Q perfusion imaging
Classic uses include carcinoid, gastrinoma, paraganglioma, medullary thyroid cancer and meningioma
options_after: It is primarily a bone mineralisation tracer
It targets somatostatin receptor expression
It is used primarily for renal obstruction
It is the preferred tracer for routine V/Q perfusion imaging
Classic uses include carcinoid, gastrinoma, paraganglioma, medullary thyroid cancer and meningioma
updates.explanation: The source describes In-111 pentetreotide as a somatostatin receptor imaging agent. It is used for several neuroendocrine or receptor-expressing tumours including carcinoid, gastrinoma, paraganglioma, medullary thyroid cancer and meningioma. It is not a bone mineralisation, renal obstruction or V/Q perfusion tracer.

updates.question_text: Regarding indium labelling in nuclear medicine, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All indium studies are labelled white-cell studies
Indium cannot be attached to octreotide or DTPA
Indium can be used to label white cells
Indium can be attached to octreotide or DTPA when chelated appropriately
Indium is the source's standard tracer for MDP bone scan
options_after: Most indium studies are labelled white-cell studies
Indium will not be attached to octreotide or DTPA
Indium can be used to label white cells
Indium can be attached to octreotide or DTPA when chelated appropriately
Indium is the source's standard tracer for MDP bone scan
updates.explanation: The source warns against equating all indium scans with white-cell imaging. Indium is commonly used for labelled white cells, but it can also be attached to octreotide or DTPA using chelation chemistry. MDP bone scanning is a technetium-labelled phosphate analogue study, not an indium study.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal octreotide scan biodistribution and timing, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal octreotide uptake excludes abdominal organs such as liver, spleen, kidneys, bladder and GI tract
Early imaging is useful because bowel activity is absent or less problematic
Delayed imaging can clarify whether abdominal activity is bowel related
Normal uptake excludes thyroid activity
Physiological GI activity should never be considered
options_after: Normal octreotide uptake excludes abdominal organs such as liver, spleen, kidneys, bladder and GI tract
Early imaging is useful because bowel activity is absent or less problematic
Delayed imaging can clarify whether abdominal activity is bowel related
Normal uptake excludes thyroid activity
Physiological GI activity should not be considered
updates.explanation: The source lists normal octreotide uptake in thyroid, liver, gallbladder, spleen, kidneys, bladder and GI tract. Early imaging is useful because bowel activity is absent, while delayed imaging helps clarify whether abdominal tracer is of GI origin. Physiological GI activity is therefore a key interpretive pitfall.

updates.question_text: Regarding meningioma uptake in this section, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Meningioma is always cold on octreotide imaging
Meningioma is diagnostic of renal transplant rejection
Meningioma can take up octreotide and Tc-MDP in the source
Meningioma is the classic use of MAA perfusion imaging
Meningioma excludes somatostatin receptor expression
options_after: Meningioma is characteristically cold on octreotide imaging
Meningioma is diagnostic of renal transplant rejection
Meningioma can take up octreotide and Tc-MDP in the source
Meningioma is the classic use of MAA perfusion imaging
Meningioma excludes somatostatin receptor expression
updates.explanation: The source notes the testable point that meningiomas can take up octreotide and Tc-MDP. This reflects receptor or lesion-specific uptake rather than renal, V/Q or transplant imaging. The point is clinically useful because meningioma can be encountered on non-neuroendocrine nuclear studies.

updates.question_text: Regarding thyroid blocking and normal MIBG biodistribution, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Thyroid blockade is unnecessary before radioiodinated MIBG
Lugol iodine or perchlorate can be used for thyroid blockade
The kidneys are normally prominently seen on MIBG imaging
Normal MIBG biodistribution includes liver, spleen, colon and salivary glands
Thyroid blockade is unnecessary because unbound iodine has no thyroid effect
options_after: Thyroid blockade is unnecessary before radioiodinated MIBG
Lugol iodine or perchlorate can be used for thyroid blockade
The kidneys are normally prominently seen on MIBG imaging
Normal MIBG biodistribution includes liver, spleen, colon and salivary glands
Thyroid blockade is unnecessary because unbound iodine lacks thyroid effect
updates.explanation: The source states that the thyroid should be blocked for radioiodinated MIBG to prevent unintended thyroid radiation from unbound iodine. Lugol iodine, perchlorate or saturated potassium iodide can be used. Normal MIBG biodistribution includes liver, spleen, colon and salivary glands, while kidneys are not normally seen.

updates.question_text: Regarding MIBG pitfalls and medication interactions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Certain medications can interfere with MIBG and should be held
Labetalol is listed among interacting medications
Brown fat can be seen with MIBG because of sympathetic innervation
Brown fat uptake on MIBG always proves neuroblastoma metastases
Seeing a skeleton on MIBG suggests diffuse bone metastases in the source
options_after: Certain medications can interfere with MIBG and should be held
Labetalol is listed among interacting medications
Brown fat can be seen with MIBG because of sympathetic innervation
Brown fat uptake on MIBG characteristically proves neuroblastoma metastases
Seeing a skeleton on MIBG suggests diffuse bone metastases in the source
updates.explanation: The source lists several MIBG medication interactions, including labetalol, calcium-channel blockers, reserpine, tricyclic antidepressants and sympathomimetics. It also describes brown fat as a common MIBG biodistribution variant due to sympathetic innervation. Diffuse skeletal MIBG uptake suggests bone metastases rather than benign brown fat.

updates.question_text: Regarding ProstaScint in this source, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It localises bone metastases better than a bone scan
It is a gallbladder ejection fraction test
It is used as routine screening in all men
It is considered when PSA is rising and bone scan is negative to look for soft-tissue metastases
Its critical organ is the bladder in the source
options_after: It localises bone metastases better than a bone scan
It is a gallbladder ejection fraction test
It is used as routine screening in most men
It is considered when PSA is rising and bone scan is negative to look for soft-tissue metastases
Its critical organ is the bladder in the source
updates.explanation: The source describes ProstaScint as an indium-labelled antibody study considered with rising PSA and negative bone scan, aiming to identify soft-tissue metastases outside the prostate bed. It does not localise bone metastases. The source lists the critical organ for ProstaScint as liver.

updates.question_text: Regarding sentinel lymph node scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A sentinel node receives afferent drainage directly from a primary cancer
The study is used only in renal artery stenosis
Melanoma and breast cancer are excluded uses in the source
The tracer is injected intravenously to opacify the pulmonary arteries
Small enough particles must travel through lymphatics to the sentinel node
options_after: A sentinel node receives afferent drainage directly from a primary cancer
The study is used primarily in renal artery stenosis
Melanoma and breast cancer are excluded uses in the source
The tracer is injected intravenously to opacify the pulmonary arteries
Small enough particles must travel through lymphatics to the sentinel node
updates.explanation: The source defines the sentinel node as the lymph node receiving afferent drainage directly from the primary tumour. Melanoma and breast cancer are classic indications, and tracer particle size matters because particles must travel through lymphatics. This is lymphoscintigraphy rather than V/Q perfusion imaging.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast-specific gamma imaging with sestamibi, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Breast density is the dominant determinant of uptake distribution in the source
Sestamibi can concentrate in breast cancer above background breast tissue
Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic change and inflammation cannot cause false-positive uptake
False negatives can occur with small, deep or medial lesions
Lymph node uptake on a MIBI breast study is normal and should be ignored
options_after: Breast density is the dominant determinant of uptake distribution in the source
Sestamibi can concentrate in breast cancer above background breast tissue
Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic change and inflammation will not cause false-positive uptake
False negatives can occur with small, deep or medial lesions
Lymph node uptake on a MIBI breast study is normal and should be ignored
updates.explanation: The source describes sestamibi uptake in breast cancer and lists fibroadenoma, fibrocystic change and inflammation as false positives. Small, deep or medial lesions and overlap with heart activity can cause false negatives. Breast density does not determine uptake distribution, and lymph node uptake is concerning.

updates.question_text: Regarding myocardial perfusion stress testing, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stress increases sensitivity for haemodynamically significant coronary stenosis
A reversible defect is seen on stress and improves at rest
A fixed defect is seen only on stress and completely normalises at rest
Transient ischaemic dilatation suggests high-risk diffuse subendocardial hypoperfusion
Stress testing makes left-main disease impossible to detect
options_after: Stress increases sensitivity for haemodynamically significant coronary stenosis
A reversible defect is seen on stress and improves at rest
A fixed defect is seen primarily on stress and completely normalises at rest
Transient ischaemic dilatation suggests high-risk diffuse subendocardial hypoperfusion
A negative stress test excludes detectable left-main coronary disease
updates.explanation: The source explains that stress improves sensitivity because a lesser stenosis can create a perfusion defect during stress. Reversible defects indicate ischaemia, while fixed defects are present on stress and rest and suggest scar. Transient ischaemic dilatation correlates with high-risk disease such as left main or three-vessel disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding left bundle branch block and myocardial perfusion imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: LBBB can produce a false-positive reversible septal or anteroseptal defect
Vasodilator stress is favoured over dobutamine in the source
Dobutamine reduces LBBB-related septal false positives because it slows the heart rate
LBBB makes ECG stress testing non-diagnostic, so imaging is often used
LBBB artefact always involves isolated apical uptake
options_after: LBBB can produce a false-positive reversible septal or anteroseptal defect
Vasodilator stress is favoured over dobutamine in the source
Dobutamine reduces LBBB-related septal false positives because it slows the heart rate
LBBB makes ECG stress testing non-diagnostic, so imaging is often used
LBBB artefact characteristically involves isolated apical uptake
updates.explanation: The source highlights LBBB as a cause of false-positive septal or anteroseptal defects, especially with exercise or dobutamine stress. Vasodilator stress is favoured because increased heart rate worsens the septal relaxation artefact. ECG stress testing is non-diagnostic in known LBBB, making perfusion imaging relevant.

updates.question_text: Regarding stunned and hibernating myocardium, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stunned myocardium has normal perfusion but abnormal contractility after ischaemia/reperfusion
Hibernating myocardium is chronically hypoperfused but viable
Hibernating myocardium can show FDG uptake or delayed thallium redistribution
Scar is expected to recover on delayed thallium imaging
Stunning is a chronic resting perfusion defect identical to scar
options_after: Stunned myocardium has normal perfusion but abnormal contractility after ischaemia/reperfusion
Hibernating myocardium is chronically hypoperfused but viable
Hibernating myocardium can show FDG uptake or delayed thallium redistribution
Scar is expected to recover on delayed thallium imaging
Stunning is a chronic resting perfusion defect closely comparable to scar
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes stunned from hibernating myocardium. Stunned myocardium has normal perfusion but impaired contractility after ischaemia/reperfusion and can recover, while hibernating myocardium is chronically hypoperfused but viable, with FDG uptake or delayed thallium redistribution. Scar lacks viable uptake and does not redistribute.

updates.question_text: Regarding MUGA scanning, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It uses gated labelled-RBC blood-pool imaging to calculate ejection fraction
It is a sulphur colloid liver scan
It is used to diagnose acute PE by ventilation-perfusion mismatch
It cannot assess ejection fraction
It is the standard Meckel diverticulum study
options_after: It uses gated labelled-RBC blood-pool imaging to calculate ejection fraction
It is a sulphur colloid liver scan
It is used to diagnose acute PE by ventilation-perfusion mismatch
It will not assess ejection fraction
It is the standard Meckel diverticulum study
updates.explanation: The source describes MUGA as a gated equilibrium radionuclide angiogram using labelled RBC blood-pool images to calculate ejection fraction and assess wall motion. It is especially useful for monitoring potentially cardiotoxic chemotherapy. It is not a liver, V/Q or Meckel study.

updates.question_text: Regarding myocardial perfusion artefacts, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Breast attenuation can reduce anterior wall activity
Left hemidiaphragm attenuation can reduce inferior wall activity
Subdiaphragmatic tracer activity cannot affect myocardial interpretation
Patient motion can create artefacts and may require repeat imaging
Normal apical thinning should be considered when stress/rest pattern and wall function support a variant
options_after: Breast attenuation can reduce anterior wall activity
Left hemidiaphragm attenuation can reduce inferior wall activity
Subdiaphragmatic tracer activity will not affect myocardial interpretation
Patient motion can create artefacts and may require repeat imaging
Normal apical thinning should be considered when stress/rest pattern and wall function support a variant
updates.explanation: The source lists breast attenuation, diaphragmatic attenuation, subdiaphragmatic activity, motion, misregistration, LBBB and apical thinning as artefact patterns. Breast attenuation can affect anterior activity, and motion may require repeat imaging. Subdiaphragmatic activity can mask or alter apparent inferior wall activity, so it cannot be ignored.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiopharmaceutical therapy for painful bone metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: External beam radiation is always an absolute contraindication
Pregnancy and breastfeeding are absolute contraindications for strontium/samarium therapy in the source
Strontium and samarium target areas of high bone turnover
Renal failure is an absolute contraindication for strontium/samarium therapy in the source
These therapies are used for bone pain related to metastatic breast or prostate cancer
options_after: External beam radiation is characteristically an absolute contraindication
Pregnancy and breastfeeding are absolute contraindications for strontium/samarium therapy in the source
Strontium and samarium target areas of high bone turnover
Renal failure is an absolute contraindication for strontium/samarium therapy in the source
These therapies are used for bone pain related to metastatic breast or prostate cancer
updates.explanation: The source describes bone pain therapies for metastatic breast and prostate cancer, with strontium and samarium complexing at areas of high bone turnover. Pregnancy, breastfeeding and severe renal failure are listed as absolute contraindications for strontium/samarium. External beam radiation is not an absolute contraindication and can be used with therapy.

updates.question_text: Regarding altered biodistribution before radioimmunotherapy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Excessive lung uptake can be an altered biodistribution pattern
Excessive kidney uptake can be an altered biodistribution pattern
Fixed bowel uptake greater than liver is always safe normal biodistribution
Bone marrow uptake above the source threshold can be concerning
Altered biodistribution is irrelevant before therapy
options_after: Excessive lung uptake can be an altered biodistribution pattern
Excessive kidney uptake can be an altered biodistribution pattern
Fixed bowel uptake greater than liver is characteristically safe normal biodistribution
Bone marrow uptake above the source threshold can be concerning
Altered biodistribution is irrelevant before therapy
updates.explanation: The source lists altered biodistribution patterns for radioimmunotherapy, including excessive lung, kidney, bowel or marrow uptake. Fixed bowel uptake greater than liver can be concerning rather than automatically safe. The diagnostic study exists to identify unsafe or inappropriate biodistribution before treatment.

updates.question_text: Regarding critical organ versus target organ, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: They are always the same organ
The critical organ is always the organ being intentionally imaged
The target organ is the organ that limits administered dose
The critical organ is irrelevant to radiopharmaceutical selection
The critical organ is the organ that limits dose because of radiation susceptibility or residence time
options_after: They are characteristically the same organ
The critical organ is characteristically the organ being intentionally imaged
The target organ is the organ that limits administered dose
The critical organ is irrelevant to radiopharmaceutical selection
The critical organ is the organ that limits dose because of radiation susceptibility or residence time
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes target organ from critical organ. The target organ is the desired site of tracer accumulation or the organ of clinical interest, while the critical organ limits dose because it receives or retains enough radiation to constrain administration. They may differ for the same radiopharmaceutical.

updates.question_text: Regarding cardiac nuclear medicine study selection and pitfalls, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Use myocardial perfusion SPECT to distinguish reversible ischaemia from fixed scar
Use MUGA when accurate ejection fraction monitoring is the key question
Attenuation, motion, misregistration and LBBB artefacts can be ignored before calling disease
Select vasodilator stress rather than dobutamine when LBBB artefact is a major concern
Subdiaphragmatic activity never affects inferior wall interpretation
options_after: Use myocardial perfusion SPECT to distinguish reversible ischaemia from fixed scar
Use MUGA when accurate ejection fraction monitoring is the key question
Attenuation, motion, misregistration and LBBB artefacts can be ignored before calling disease
Select vasodilator stress rather than dobutamine when LBBB artefact is a major concern
Subdiaphragmatic activity will not affect inferior wall interpretation
updates.explanation: The source frames myocardial perfusion SPECT around reversible ischaemia, scar and high-risk patterns, while MUGA is used for ejection fraction monitoring. Artefacts from attenuation, motion, misregistration, subdiaphragmatic activity and LBBB must be considered before calling disease. Vasodilator stress is favoured over dobutamine in LBBB because dobutamine worsens septal false positives.
